Kick off your Zurich exploration at the Grossmünster, with its familiar twin towers. The climb up one of the towers, named the Karlstrum, is worth every step for the jaw-dropping view at the top.

For more breathtaking views, take the train or hike up to Uetliberg. The lookout offers an unparalleled panorama of Zurich, with Lake Zurich and the snow-capped Alps in the distance.

Opera enthusiasts will be delighted by the Zurich Opera House, a must-visit for its world-class performances year-round.

Spend a day exploring the charming streets of Old Town, especially the Niederdorf area. It’s a delightful maze of cobblestone streets, bespoke shops, and cosy cafés.
CH.ZRH.leisureActivitiesText:
Make your way to Lindenhof Park, a historical and cultural oasis dating back 2000 years. The site of a Roman fort and a medieval castle in the past, now it’s perfect for walks and an outlook of the city. Board a scenic boat cruise on Lake Zurich for beautiful views followed by a coffee at one of the lakeside cafés.

For more scenic escapades, take a day trip to explore the picture-perfect Schwyz region, home to traditional Swiss villages.

Dive into Switzerland’s history at the National Museum of Zurich, or view the works inside Kunsthaus Zurich, if art is more your cup of tea. Then marvel at the public art installations dotted all around the city.

Don’t miss a day trip to the Swiss Alps. Ascend to the highest train station in Europe and wander through an Ice Palace in Jungfraujoch – the ‘Top of Europe’. From here you can ride a cable car to Grindelwald for skiing.
CH.ZRH.shoppingText:
Exchange your Swiss francs and begin your retail adventure on one of the most indulgent shopping streets in the world – Bahnhofstrasse. Here you can find fine chocolatiers, exquisite Swiss watches, and dazzling jewellery.

If you’re looking for something more on trend, Viadukt is the place to go. Nestled under the old railway arches, this hip area is abundant with boutiques, quirky stores, and food markets. Zurich’s Old Town is another must-do to hunt for vintage finds.

Summer in Zurich brings weekly markets brimming with fresh flowers, local produce, and handmade goods. Come winter, Zurich transforms into a magical wonderland with its festive markets. Enjoy the spirit of the season under twinkling lights, the scent of roasted chestnuts and stalls filled with gifts and decorations.
CH.ZRH.destinationPageIntro: Zurich, a place of opulence, adventure, and the very best chocolate. Admire the view from the Grossmünster, cruise on Lake Zurich and marvel at Jungfraujoch’s Ice Palace.
CH.ZRH.overviewText:
Zurich is a place of picturesque scenery and quaint old-world elegance. This Switzerland-based city is alive with the buzz of bustling marketplaces, cosy cafés, and opulent boutiques. Nestled beside the legendary Swiss Alps, this area buzzes with thrilling adventures and endless activities.

Zurich offers the best of both worlds: for the leisurely traveller, it tempts with locally-made truffles and pralines, while thrill-seekers can conquer the ‘Top of Europe’ and ski to their heart’s content.
CH.ZRH.eatingImageText:
Zurich is home to many food favourites, so dedicate a day to your belly with a food tour of Zurich’s best. Start off with a hearty bowl of birchermüesli, a Zurich-born classic. This mix of oats, fruits, nuts and yoghurt can be found in the snug cafés of the Niederdorf district.

For lunch, savour Zürich Gescnetzeltes, a creamy veal dish typically served with rösti – crispy, Swiss potato pancakes.

For an afternoon treat, sample Zurich’s world-famous chocolates. Indulge in a selection of truffles and pralines that melt in your mouth.

As the evening sets in, gather your travel companions for a cheese fondue, where you dip bread into a pot of melted cheese. Or try raclette, when melted cheese is scraped over boiled potatoes, pickles, and onions.

AT.VIE.touristAttractionsText:
Schönbrunn Palace is one of the most popular places to see in Vienna – a stunning Baroque masterpiece with sprawling gardens of manicured lawns and ornate fountains. Visit the Old Town, where Vienna’s charm unfolds with each cobblestone street. Wander through the narrow alleys and admire the elaborate architecture. Nearby, the Hofburg Palace stands as a symbol of imperial power, with lavish rooms that housed the Habsburg dynasty.

Ready for some art? The Belvedere Complex holds a treasure trove of it. You’ll find masterpieces by Klimt, Schiele and other renowned artists. Just a short stroll away, you’ll spot the grand dome of Karlskirche – another architectural marvel. 

St. Stephen’s Cathedral is another must-see – its towering Gothic spires are a landmark of the city. Climb to the top for panoramic views of the skyline.
AT.VIE.leisureActivitiesText:
Head to the Kunsthistorisches Museum, home to one of the world’s finest art collections. Discover masterpieces by Titian, Velázquez, and Caravaggio. And don’t miss the ancient Egyptian artefacts – they’re fascinating.

Next, get lost in the MuseumQuartier. This vibrant hub is where modern art meets old-world charm. It’s a playground for culture lovers, filled with galleries, cafés, and a buzz of inspiration.

For a truly unique experience,  catch a concert at the Mozarthaus. This is where the legendary Mozart lived and worked. Sit in the same room where he composed his masterpieces, while the sound of his music fills the amphitheatre – a once-in-a-lifetime experience that you can’t miss.

Need a day of rejuvenation? Head to the Amalienbad, a magnificent art deco swimming pool and spa. Take a deep breath and get ready to unwind – Vienna-style!
AT.VIE.shoppingText:
Vienna is a luxury shopper’s dream, with glamorous streets lined with upscale boutiques, like Kärntner Straße, Graben, and Kohlmarkt. Here, you’ll find everything from luxury fashion to exquisite jewellery.

But Vienna isn’t just about designer brands, it’s a city steeped in rich craftsmanship. From hand-carved wooden treasures to delicate porcelain painted with intricate details, you’re sure to find the perfect souvenir to take back home.
AT.VIE.destinationPageIntro: Take in Vienna’s ostentatious Schönbrunn Palace before picking one of its many Mozart attractions. Sip on a coffee and marvel at the pure beauty of this Baroque-inspired city.
AT.VIE.overviewText:
Imagine strolling down cobblestone streets lined with majestic buildings, the air filled with melodies of classic music and the scent of freshly brewed coffee. This is Vienna – where imperial grandeur and modern charm waltz hand-in-hand. 

This enchanting Austrian capital is a feast for the senses. Art isn’t just confined to galleries in Vienna, it’s everywhere – woven into old-world buildings and contemporary establishments. 

Whether you’re a history, music and arts enthusiast or simply seeking a touch of European elegance, Vienna has something special in store for you.
AT.VIE.eatingImageText:
Begin your culinary adventure at the Naschmarkt, a true haven for foodies. Stalls overflow with pickled delights, artisanal cheeses, stuffed olives, fragrant spices, and exotic fruits. 

No trip to Vienna is complete without indulging in a classic wiener schnitzel – a crispy, golden veal cutlet served typically with a potato salad or lingonberries.

Vienna’s café culture is just as legendary. Make sure to cosy up in one of the iconic coffee houses and sip on a velvety brew paired with a slice of apple strudel or a buttery spekulatius biscuit.

Looking for something a bit more trendy? Head over to the Freihaus district, where you’ll find modern eateries and traditional coffee spots. There’s something for everyone here, so get ready to discover your own Viennese favourites!

GR.ATH.touristAttractionsText:
History is seeping out of every nook in Athens, with much to learn about its storied past. Start out at the iconic Acropolis, where the Parthenon stands tall. Before ascending, stop by the Acropolis Museum to gain a deeper understanding of this ancient marvel.

Delve further into Athen’s rich history by visiting the theatre ruins of Odeon of Herodes Atticus and Ancient Agora. Check out the Hadrian’s Library, a grand structure that once housed vast collections of scrolls, as well as the Temple of Olympian Zeus, Roman Forum of Athens, and the Benizelos Mansion.

Embrace the Olympic spirit at the Panathenaic Stadium, the birthplace of the modern Olympic Games. Nearby, the Dromeas statue commemorates the legendary feat of the first runner from the Battle of Marathon.
GR.ATH.leisureActivitiesText:
Athens is a great place to explore on foot, with many walking tours that take you around the city. Wander through Anafiotika, a charming neighbourhood nestled beneath the Acropolis. Its narrow, winding streets, whitewashed houses and vibrant colours create a stunning backdrop.

Athens also boasts lush green spaces throughout the city, with Zappeion Garden and Athens National Garden being popular retreats. You’ll find parks for children, hidden ruins, and plenty more once inside.

Ascend Lycabettus Hill – the highest point of Athens – for the most spectacular views of the city, especially at sunset.
GR.ATH.shoppingText:
Athens has a vibrant mix of traditional markets, stylish boutiques, and contemporary shopping streets. Browse whimsical boutiques in the historic district of Plaka, and the latest fashion trends and accessories in Ermou Street.

Monastiraki Flea Market is a must-visit, if you’re looking for antiques, vintage items and souvenirs. For a taste of local life, head to Varvakios Central Market. This bustling marketplace is the heart of Athens’ food scene, packed with varieties of meats, spices and seafood. Pick some snacks for the road, or some preserved treats to take home.

Throughout the city, you can find all sorts of souvenirs. Browse stalls of Greek pottery, olive oil, accessories and more for the perfect memento of your trip.
GR.ATH.destinationPageIntro: From the ancient ruins of the Acropolis to the vibrant, trendy street atmosphere in Plaka, Athens is sure to delight visitors with a plethora of things to see and do.
GR.ATH.overviewText:
Explore a city so steeped in history, you’ll stumble upon an ancient ruin at every corner. Stroll through picturesque neighbourhoods where winding lanes are lined with neoclassical buildings and vibrant street art. The air is filled with the lively chatter of al fresco cafés, the melodies of street musicians and the warm greetings of friendly locals.

The city’s arts and culture scene bursts with festivals, concerts, film screenings and even culinary delights. And when you need a quick escape from the hustle and bustle, the green spaces throughout the city offer idyllic spots for relaxation and recreation.

Whether you are wandering through its historic streets or savouring divine Greek delicacies, Athens promises an unforgettable holiday.
GR.ATH.eatingImageText:
Head to Plaka for the best local eateries and charming tavernas. Sample Greek favourites such as moussaka – a hearty casserole of layered eggplant, a meaty tomato sauce and creamy béchamel. Or, savour some souvlaki – grilled meat and vegetable skewers – with a signature Greek salad.

Look out for quaint bakeries offering a variety of baked goods, and make sure to try spanakopita – a crispy phyllo dough with a rich filling of spinach and feta cheese.

While exploring around, grab yourself a gyro to enjoy on the go. This popular favourite consists of thinly sliced meat served in pita bread and topped with tzatziki sauce. Don’t forget dessert! Finish your meal with loukoumades – delicious bite-sized doughnuts that are soaked in honey and sprinkled with cinnamon.

PT.LIS.touristAttractionsText:
Fado is a traditional music style that’s central to Portuguese culture. Daily shows at the Cine Theatro Gymnasio introduce you to Fado, a style that’s been given World Heritage status by UNESCO.

Explore Alfama, the city’s oldest district and a twisted maze of streets and alleyways lined with historic architecture. Be sure to stop at the Santa Luzia viewpoint for some great views of the city.

Portuguese food is delicious and unique, so why not learn to create your own dishes with a cooking class? It’s an ideal way to immerse yourself in the culture of the city.

The stunning gardens of the Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation are peaceful, and the foundation is also home to museums housing modern art and countless artefacts. The gardens host summer music concerts in the open-air theatre.
PT.LIS.leisureActivitiesText:
With an average of 290 days of sunshine a year, it’s no surprise that Lisbon’s beaches are hugely popular with families. Head south out of the city centre towards Arrábida and you’ll find some of Portugal’s most beautiful and family-friendly beaches. The 25-mile journey is worth it for a day trip exploring gorgeous beaches such as Galapinhos, Galápos, Coelhos and Creiro.

Portugal is famous for its championship golf courses, and there are plenty to choose from around Lisbon, including Belas Clube de Campo, a challenging 19-hole course.

The region is also home to plenty of family attractions including theme parks and zoos. Tours guide you through Lisbon’s unique historic legacy, take a helicopter flight over the city, or cruise down the river Tejo and see old Lisbon from a different viewpoint.
PT.LIS.shoppingText:
For a shopping experience in pedestrianised comfort, Baixa district’s Rua Augusta is a favourite retail area filled with major chain stores. Browse a selection of independent shops and famous brands in the dedicated shopping area of Armazéns do Chiado where you’ll find plenty of bookstores, cafés and restaurants. For a touch of luxury, visit Avenida Liberdade for high-end fashion boutiques.

Lisbon has several large malls that combine retail with entertainment such as multiplex cinemas, funfairs and bowling alleys.

For a more relaxed market atmosphere, the Feira da Ladra market is held on Tuesdays and Saturdays and is a busy antique market full of fascinating stalls and trinkets. There are also artisan’s markets such as the Benfica Handicrafts Market for handmade leatherwork, jewellery and ceramics.
PT.LIS.destinationPageIntro: Lisbon is a friendly, relaxed city where narrow cobbled streets are lined with colourful buildings and cafés. History, art and culture all meet in Portugal’s capital city.
PT.LIS.overviewText:
Winding cobbled streets, ancient ruins and magnificent cathedrals teamed with bustling markets and a thriving arts scene make Lisbon a perfect city break destination. This enchanting city is full of personality, where the narrow streets are lined with boutiques and family restaurants.

Head out of the city centre and you’re instantly surrounded by seven hills overlooking the Rio Tejo, covered in lush forests and with miles of incredible hiking and cycling trails.

Lisbon’s easy-going, relaxed charm makes it a perfect summer destination, with some beautiful beaches nearby for a lazy day by the sea. Art and music play a key role in the character of Portugal’s capital, with festivals celebrating the culture, food and spirit of Portugal. One visit is never enough.
PT.LIS.eatingImageText:
Food in Lisbon ranges from light and sweet egg custard pastries to hearty rich stews and freshly fried sardines. Make sure your morning coffee comes with a Pastel De Nata, a flaky pastry with a creamy egg custard filling.

Bacalhau is deeply rooted in Portuguese culture. This salted cod is served with crispy fried potatoes or a rich cream sauce.

Chicken is a common feature on menus, and the region’s unique Peri Peri spice blend makes the simplest grilled chicken taste delicious.

Thanks to its proximity to the sea, Lisbon is renowned for its seafood, including fresh lobsters and jumbo prawns cooked simply with lemon and pepper. Cataplana de Marisco is a seafood stew served with rice. Hop across the river to the village of Porto Brandão to taste the best example of this Lisbon favourite!

DK.CPH.touristAttractionsText:
The castles and palaces to be found in Copenhagen are like something out of a fairytale. Visit the Amalienborg Palace to see where the Danish royal family live and watch the changing of the guard. For another royal excursion, make your way to Kronborg Castle, a UNESCO World Heritage site. Best known as Elsinore in Shakespeare’s Hamlet, this fortress exudes a sense of grandeur and mystery.

Get a unique view of Copenhagen by climbing the spiral ramp of The Round Tower. With sweeping views of Copenhagen’s rooftops and spires, it’s the perfect spot to take in the city’s beauty. Don’t miss out on paying a visit to The Little Mermaid, Copenhagen’s beloved bronze icon. Perched by the water, this famous statue embodies the city and was inspired by the fairy tale written by Danish author Hans Christian Anderson.
DK.CPH.leisureActivitiesText:
Venture to the world’s oldest amusement park, Bakken, where the echoes of excitement have been bountiful since 1583. Located in the woodlands, the park consists of historic rides in a magical setting and makes for a great day out for the whole family.

Visit Glyptoteket, a haven for art lovers. Classical sculptures stand alongside modern masterpieces in its beautiful ‘Winter Garden’. To learn more about Denmark’s past, head to the National Museum, where exhibits showcase Viking treasures, medieval artefacts, and cultural relics.

A walk around Copenhagen is an experience in itself. The city’s streets are lined with colourful townhouses, cosy cafés, and discrete courtyards. Stroll through King’s Garden, an urban oasis consisting of sculptures, floral gardens and manicured lawns ideal for picnics.
DK.CPH.shoppingText:
For your shopping fix, stroll down the famous Strøget Street. One of Europe’s longest pedestrian streets, you’ll find plenty of luxury brands, high street fashion, cafés and even street performers.

Another pedestrian shopping street is Købmagergade. Here you’ll find traditional Danish designs alongside contemporary fashion, and is the kind of place where you’re bound to find one-of-a-kind pieces. Nearby, Pilestræde beckons with its boutiques and hidden gems, offering everything from tasteful jewellery to chic Scandinavian home décor.

Known for its creativity and diversity, Vesterbro is a hip and happening neighbourhood. The main street, Istegade, is packed with edgy boutiques, restaurants and bespoke shops that guarantee authentic finds.
DK.CPH.destinationPageIntro: Explore Copenhagen via its canals or on foot. There are just as many cultural sites to discover as there are culinary delights to indulge in, in this chic and cosmopolitan Scandi city.
DK.CPH.overviewText: Explore Copenhagen, one of the world’s greenest cities. Why drive when you can cycle? Copenhagen boasts 546 kilometres of bicycle paths, limitless eco-friendly hotels and a food culture fueled by sustainable dining. This chic yet quaint city has just as many cultural sites to discover as it has culinary delights to indulge in. Imagine exploring ancient castles and the birthplace of fairytales, shopping for the latest Scandi fashion, and taking your taste buds on a modern-day culinary adventure. Whether you’re a first-time visitor or returning traveller, Copenhagen is always a good idea.
DK.CPH.destinationHighlightsH1: Copenhagen: Experience Scandinavian charm at its best
DK.CPH.eatingImageText:
Nørrebro neighbourhood is known for its diverse culinary scene, with the streets around Jaegersborggade housing a plethora of eclectic eateries. Tuck into everything from Michelin-star cuisine, to authentic Nordic cuisine – think pickled vegetables, smoked fish, and foraged herbs, all presented with an artistic flair. 

A must-try is smørrebrød, Denmark’s famous open-faced sandwich. This simple yet sophisticated sandwich consists of rye bread topped with anything from pickled herring to roast beef, and garnished with fresh dill or crispy onions.

Another street food staple is a Danish hot dog – served in a soft bun with remoulade, crispy onions, and pickles. To satisfy your sweet tooth, nothing beats a freshly made Danish pastry – a buttery, flaky treat filled with custard, jam, or marzipan.

SE.ARN.touristAttractionsText:
Explore royal grandeur and historic beauty in the vibrant city of Stockholm. Visit the official residence of Sweden’s King, the Royal Palace and relish in its majestic halls and chambers. For more royal residences, visit Drottningholm, Rosendal or Ulriksdal Palace – each look like they were plucked straight out of a fairytale.

Back in the city, visit Stockholm Cathedral in Stockholm Old Town. Then walk along its cobblestone streets past charming cafés and shops providing a glimpse into the past. Visit Stockholm City Hall to admire its architecture and the intricate murals inside. Get your steps in and climb the tower for panoramic views of the city below.
SE.ARN.leisureActivitiesText:
Make your way to the island of Djurgården, where culture and amusement collide. Music enthusiasts can lose themselves in the ABBA Museum while history buffs can enjoy the Vasa Museum, home to a fascinating 17th-century ship. For a more immersive experience, head to Skansen, the world’s oldest open-air museum – here you can find old Swedish farmhouses and watch folk performances.

When you’re ready to escape the bustling city, island-hop your way through the wider Stockholm Archipelago, made up of over 30,000 islands. Start with Fjäderholmarna for handicrafts and seafood, or relax on the beaches of Grinda. For a more adventurous day, go to Utö which is famous for its cycling paths. Vaxholm is another interesting island, where you can explore Sweden’s maritime history.
SE.ARN.shoppingText:
Blending chic Scandinavian design with quirky vintage finds, Stockholm has something for every kind of shopper. Södermalm is sprinkled with trendy boutiques that showcase the best of Swedish high street fashion, from cutting-edge designs and minimalist clothing, to unique accessories that exude an effortlessly cool Scandinavian vibe.

Embark on a treasure hunt at Hornsgatan for second-hand items. Packed with vintage gems, there is an abundance of retro clothing and trinkets to browse. Scout the antique shops in Vasastan, where you may find rare collectibles, furniture and detailed art pieces. Look out for a Dala horse, a hand-painted wooden figure that is the perfect Swedish keepsake.
SE.ARN.destinationPageIntro: Stockholm is a picturesque city with quaint streets, museums, castles and royal residences. Beyond is the wider Stockholm archipelago, a true wonder waiting to be explored.
SE.ARN.overviewText:
The Swedish capital of Stockholm is a well sought destination in Europe. It’s a city of history, culture and stunning natural scenes that thrill and excite the senses. Made up of 14 islands connected by more than 50 bridges, the city is a sight to behold. Wander along its picturesque streets, crossing from island to island, each creating a breathtaking backdrop to the city’s elegant architecture.

Relish in long days of endless sunshine in the summer while winters in the city are best spent indoors in a cosy atmosphere. Known as the food capital of Sweden, Stockholm is rich with traditional Swedish delicacies to indulge in and international flavours to try. With its captivating mix of nature, creativity and urban allure, Stockholm offers an enchanting experience for all.
SE.ARN.eatingImageText:
Östermalms Saluhall is a historic food market brimming with fresh produce, Swedish delicacies and artisanal treats. Here’s where you can savour the true essence of Swedish gastronomy, from the finest cheeses to lingonberry jams.

For a typical Swedish snack, try sill, a beloved Swedish staple of pickled herring. It’s often served with crispbread, potatoes and topped with a variety of sauces for unique flavour combinations. While Sweden is famous for its meatballs, don’t miss out on ordering a räksmörgås. Made with only one slice of bread, it’s a towering open sandwich layered with fresh prawns, boiled eggs and dill.

Of course, no Swedish food adventure is complete without indulging in a toasty, spiced cinnamon bun – found in every bakery across the city. Old Town is one of the best places to enjoy authentic dishes like these.

NO.OSL.touristAttractionsText:
The medieval stronghold, Akershus Fortress, overlooks the Oslofjord and transports you back in time. Walking along its ancient walls, one can imagine knights and battles from centuries ago. The Rose Castle – an outdoor installation commemorating Norway’s resistance during World War II – offers a more modern take on history.

For a touch of art, head to Ekebergparken Sculpture Park, where contemporary sculptures blend in with the surrounding greenery.

Oslo has more than 50 museums to explore. Start with the Polar Exploration Museum, where tales of brave explorers like Roald Mundsen come to life. To learn about Norway’s past, browse the Norwegian Museum of Cultural History. And don’t miss MUNCH, an iconic museum dedicated to the famous Norwegian painter, Edvard Munch.
NO.OSL.leisureActivitiesText:
Pamper yourself at one of the traditional Norwegian saunas scattered along the harbor promenade, where you can sweat it out with some amazing views of the fjord. As the sun sets, the harbour turns into a buzzing hub, with plenty of restaurants and cafés waiting to be discovered.

Up for more adventure? Dive into the public seawater pool in trendy Sørenga. There’s something special about swimming in the middle of the city, with Oslo’s stunning skyline as your background.

If you are visiting in summer and looking for a beach day, the Bygdøy peninsula is the place to be. Pack a picnic, hike the trails, or simply unwind.
NO.OSL.shoppingText:
The bustling main street of Karl Johans Gate is lined with everything from luxurious stores to quirky local boutiques. It’s the shopping hub for the latest fashion finds as well as Norwegian souvenirs. Look for something Viking-inspired for a typical Norwegian memento.

The waterfront shopping district, Aker Brygge, is another top location for stylish shops featuring Nordic designs. Keep an eye out for sleek homeware, minimalist clothing, and Scandinavian knick-knacks.

For something more upscale, head to Bogstadveien, Oslo’s premier shopping street – home to high-end stores and well-known designer brands.
NO.OSL.destinationPageIntro: Discover the timeless, magnificent city of Oslo. Norway’s capital has no shortage of luxurious sauna experiences, world-class restaurants and museums.
NO.OSL.overviewText:
Oslo, Norway’s cosmopolitan capital and largest port, attracts adventurers and city dwellers alike. With a delightful mix of urban life and nature, the city is a breath of fresh air and the world’s greenest city. Stroll through lively streets, where designer boutiques are a stone’s throw away from lush forests and majestic waterways.

This historic yet artsy city has no shortage of museums and trendy neighbourhoods waiting to be explored. It’s also the perfect base to discover the majestic fjords from. Whether it’s a forest hike, boat trip, or sauna dip, Oslo will keep you coming back for more.

A city that is proud of its heritage but also embraces innovation, Oslo allows you to experience both modernity and Scandinavian charm.
NO.OSL.eatingImageText:
Nordic flavours are unlike any other, with the earthy taste of Norway’s wild environment woven throughout dishes. Sample unique meats like reindeer, or succulent lamb. For those bold enough, try lutefisk, a stockfish that has been soaked in water, placed in lye, then soaked in water again. You might be able to find this bespoke snack in Oslo’s Mathallen indoor food market.

Røkelaks is another famed meal in Oslo, otherwise known as smoked salmon. The harbour is the best place to go as the quality here is top-notch. There’s nothing quite like fresh Norwegian salmon.

Brunost, sweet brown cheese on bread, is the ideal meal to enjoy during kveldsmat, which is essentially a second dinner or an evening meal. Explore the streets of Grünerløkka for kveldsmat – this hip neighbourhood is brimming with delectable finds.

FI.HEL.touristAttractionsText:
Start at Senate Square, the epicentre of neoclassical beauty. The square is home to many of the city’s must-see sights, including the Helsinki Cathedral. Its gleaming white façade and towering green domes are a symbol of Helsinki. Next, make your way to the National Library of Finland – an architectural gem, packed with history and fascinating collections. 

The Ateneum Art Museum is another must-visit. It houses a collection of Finnish and European art, showcasing traditional and modern pieces, interactive art wall and special exhibitions. 

Get a taste of Helsinki’s vibrant social scene at Esplanadi Park. Lined with trees and sculptures, it’s the perfect place for leisurely strolls, picnics, eateries and cultural events.   

Close by is the bustling Market Square, where you can find fresh-caught salmon, caviar and other local delicacies. You’ll also be able to spot the Uspenski Cathedral as it stands tall over the city, showcasing its Greek architecture, golden domes and red brick walls.
FI.HEL.leisureActivitiesText:
Visiting Helsinki in the summer? Then, dive right into the Allas Sea Pool, where you can swim in the refreshing waters while soaking in amazing views of the Helsinki skyline. For a more tranquil escape, immerse yourself in the Finnish tradition of sauna and spa, where relaxation reaches a new level. 

When winter rolls around, get ready to meet some reindeer at Nuuksio National Park – a wild experience you won’t want to miss. The park also boasts spectacular scenery with beautiful lakes, hiking trails and diverse flora and fauna.

Looking for a day trip? Suomenlinna is just a short boat ride away. This UNESCO World Heritage site is a a testament to the city’s fascinating history. Wander through its impressive walking trails and enjoy panoramic views of the Baltic Sea.
FI.HEL.shoppingText:
Helsinki is a haven for design-centric shopping. Journey through the Design District – a lively area full of innovative shops showcasing the best of Finnish creativity. You’ll find everything from sleek furniture to unique homewares, exquisite textiles, handmade accessories and more. 

Wander through the boutiques and admire the local artisans’ creations. You can even pop into galleries and studios to experience the true sense of Finland’s creative culture.

And don’t forget the sauna goodies. Besides homewares, Finland is famous for its sauna culture, so be sure to check out sauna related goods. Look out for robes, soothing oils and authentic wooden accessories (like those adorable handcrafted birch whisks!).
FI.HEL.destinationPageIntro: Helsinki, known for its creativity and innovation, is a hub of bespoke things to see and do. Marvel at impressive buildings, relax in a Finnish spa and connect with nature.
FI.HEL.overviewText:
If you’re looking for a city that effortlessly blends contemporary cool with a love for nature, then Helsinki is the answer. The capital of Finland has a charming and laid-back vibe that gives it a distinct character. 

Being by the sea is a big part of its charm. Delicious seafood is everywhere, and you can’t miss out on the sauna culture – especially by the water. And the best part? You’re never far from nature, with surrounding national parks and lush green islands. Explore the city’s iconic landmarks, unwind in traditional Finnish cafés and just enjoy being outdoors. 

Helsinki is a hotspot of creativity, with a fascinating mix of history, art, and innovation. It’s a place that invites you to slow down, soak in the atmosphere and truly experience the heart of Finland.
FI.HEL.eatingImageText:
The classical Old Market Hall is a great place to start. It’s filled with traditional Finnish treats and coastal flavours. Grab a karjalanpiirakka while you’re there – it’s a warm pastry filled with rice porridge or mashed potatoes.

Next, wander over to Kauppatori Salutorget which offers one of Helsinki’s favourite dishes of fish soup. It’s creamy, hearty, and packed with fresh seafood – the perfect comfort food.

Looking to try something new? Make your way to the Hernesaari area by the docks and bite into a Finnish delicacy – a reindeer burger.

Classic Finnish snacks are quite unique. Pickled herring with traditional ruisleipä (rye bread) is a must. And for those with a bold palate, try some salmiakki – Finland’s infamous salty liquorice.

IE.DUB.touristAttractionsText:
Much like its European neighbours, Dublin is a historic city with many ancient landmarks. Start your Dublin exploration at Dublin Castle. The medieval and Georgian architecture is a must-see. Discover Ireland’s regal heritage and admire the classical design of the majestic corridors and manicured gardens. 

For a look into some of Dublin’s centuries-old architecture, check out the iconic Trinity College Dublin, St. Patrick’s Cathedral and other spiritual sites. The incredible Gothic elements evoke the rich Irish heritage that the city is known for.

The Kilmainham Gaol Museum is another popular attraction to tour, presenting a sobering glimpse of Ireland’s struggle for independence. The museum provides guided tours that lead visitors through the former prison’s halls and often offer captivating stories by the prisoners themselves.
IE.DUB.leisureActivitiesText:
Dublin is passionate about providing accessible culture for all, therefore admission to many museums is free of charge. Be sure to visit the extensive National Museum of Ireland – it has four different branches: Archaeology, Natural History, Decorative Arts & History, and Country Life. The National Gallery of Ireland is also a great choice, with an impressive collection of Irish and European masterpieces.

Another museum to add to the list is the Little Museum of Dublin, which presents an overview of the city’s past century. For an immersive historical experience, visit EPIC The Irish Emigration Museum.

Take a day trip to the Wicklow Mountains and explore its rugged peaks and lush valleys or trek the scenic trails and marvel at the panoramic landscape. You can also find solace in one of Dublin’s many city parks to enjoy a light stroll or afternoon picnic.
IE.DUB.shoppingText:
Begin your retail adventure on Grafton Street, where you can find a plethora of high-end boutiques, flagship stores and entertaining street performers. A short walk from there, you’ll find Henry Street with a few more popular shops.

If vintage shopping is more your style, spend the morning browsing Liberty Market. It’s a treasure trove of second-hand finds, handmade crafts and souvenirs.

Treat yourself to the finest Irish tea or pick up some fancy chocolates to take home with you. Or, for a touch of Irish elegance, purchase a piece of Waterford Crystal, which is renowned around the world for its beautiful designs and artistry.
IE.DUB.destinationPageIntro: Dublin is a city bursting with energy, ingrained history, and artistic expression. Rich culture , wild mountains, friendly locals and majestic architecture – Dublin has it all.
IE.DUB.overviewText:
Dublin, the vibrant heart of Ireland, is a city steeped in history, culture and warm Irish charm. With its cobblestone streets, historic landmarks, lively arts scene and cosy eateries, this Irish capital offers a unique blend of old-world elegance and modern-day energy. 

Dublin is incredibly picturesque, with many parks and waterfront areas offering a leisurely escape within the city. The scenic mountains surrounding the city are perfect for trekking, biking and exploring nature. 

With its variety of attractions, a holiday to Dublin is perfect for families, solo travellers, couples and friends. Embrace the warm and friendly hospitality of the Irish and discover why Dublin captivates everyone who visits.
IE.DUB.destinationHighlightsH1: Dublin: The heart and soul of Ireland
IE.DUB.eatingImageText:
Weekends in Dublin can be spent exploring the Temple Bar Food Market. Nestled in the heart of the city, this gastronomic haven is bustling with local and international delicacies. Sample artisanal cheeses, fresh produce and gourmet street food.

Dublin has restaurants from near and far, and a stroll down Camden Street or South William Street demonstrates how diverse the culinary scene is. Parliament street is another must-do in the summer as it transforms into a pedestrian-only space, providing al fresco dining in a lively atmosphere.

Try colcannon to really get a taste of that traditional Irish flavour. It’s a dreamy dish of buttery mashed potato with cabbage. Or indulge in a bowl of Irish stew – a hearty comfort food made with tender meat and root vegetables.

Once you’re on board our modern, spacious aircraft, settle into your seat with generous legroom, and an ergonomic design that ensures complete comfort. Ambient lighting lets your body adjust to your destination time zone, and high-speed Wi-Fi (available on our A380, A350, B787 and select B777 aircraft) keeps you connected to family and colleagues. 

During the flight, you can indulge your love of fine cuisine with a selection of dishes from our à la carte menu, meticulously prepared by our award-winning chefs. After your meal, sit back and enjoy a film, TV show or game from our entertainment selection, or stretch out on a lie-flat bed and drift off to sleep. Arrive at your destination rejuvenated and ready to do business or explore the cultural attractions of the city. 

Book a Business or First Class flight to Amsterdam with Qatar Airways for an exceptional experience.
NL.AMS.touristAttractionsText:
A mosaic of culture and history awaits in Amsterdam, starting with an exploration of the Museumplein. It’s home to three major museums, most notably the Van Gogh Museum which has the world’s largest collection of his masterpieces. Step into Rijksmuseum, where centuries of Dutch history unfold before your eyes, including Rembrandt’s works. Nearby is the Concertgebouw which offers one of the best classical concert experiences you can find globally.

Naturally, a visit to the Anne Frank House is a must – a place where echoes of the past resonate through its walls. Close by, Amsterdam’s golden age prestige is still present in the grand merchant houses that sit along the Herengracht canal.
NL.AMS.leisureActivitiesText:
Amsterdam’s spirit is best felt on two wheels. Hop on a bike and join the locals on the extensive network of bike lanes across the city. Take your bike on one of the ferries across the IJ to Amsterdam-Noord where expansive green spaces and beautiful local neighbourhoods make for a relaxing day out.

Vondelpark also beckons with its lush greenery and lively atmosphere. During the summer months, the park transforms into an exciting location offering free live music, theatre and cabaret from June to August.

For a quintessential Dutch experience, glide along the canals on a leisurely cruise. If you’re visiting in winter, the canal in Prinsengracht usually freezes over – creating a magical ice-skating scene.
NL.AMS.shoppingText:
Amsterdam has something for every kind of shopper, from unique produce and souvenir items, to the latest in fashion. 

Explore the outdoor market of Albert Cuypstraat to find everything from fresh produce to souvenirs. Bloemenmarkt is stocked with a dazzling array of flowers and is the world’s only Floating Flower Market, located on the Singel canal.

For something unique, visit the Fashion for Good Museum where you can learn more about Amsterdam’s sustainable values and eco-friendly practices. You can even create your own sustainable t-shirt.

Browse De 9 Straatjes (The 9 Streets) to ensure your suitcases are filled with European fashion, souvenirs or anything your heart desires. Its cobbled lanes are lined with independent boutiques, vintage stores and cosy cafés.
NL.AMS.destinationPageIntro: Discover a laid-back pace of life in Amsterdam. Cycle through the city or enjoy boat-cruises drifting serenely up and down picturesque canals.
NL.AMS.overviewText:
Explore Amsterdam, a city of weaving canals and picturesque streets that is constantly buzzing with energy. Spend your days walking through its cobblestone alleys, where the scent of coffee and patat (chips) intertwine with the laughter of locals gathered at quaint corner cafés. The canals are like a living postcard, with boats lazily drifting by and cyclists pedalling alongside.

Art isn’t confined to galleries here, it spills onto the streets, making everywhere quirky and inviting. There is culture on every corner, with its plethora of museums and historic landmarks to discover. Explore the canals, savour its flavours and indulge in the upbeat rhythm of Amsterdam.
NL.AMS.destinationHighlightsH1: Amsterdam: A city of bikes and bridges
NL.AMS.eatingImageText:
Leidseplein is a hub for gastronomical adventures, with bustling restaurants and street performers creating an incredible vibe. There are plenty of restaurants serving international favourites as well as local Dutch cuisine. 

For Dutch street foods, head over to Dam Square. Grab some patat on the go – Dutch fries served in a paper cone. To enjoy traditional Dutch cuisine, try raw herring fish, typically served with diced onions and pickles.

Discover Foodhallen, an indoor food market. With over 20 pop-up restaurants under one roof, it’s a paradise for foodies. For a more avant-garde experience, make your way to Westergasfabriek. This converted industrial building is now a cultural hotspot with hip restaurants and fair-trade food stores.

PL.WAW.touristAttractionsText:
The Palace of Culture and Science stands as a testament to Warsaw’s resilience and modern spirit. Its sleek silhouette dominates the skyline, offering a breathtaking panoramic view from the 30th floor. Here, the city’s past and present collide and a captivating blend of old and new worlds spread out before you. 

Step back in time as you wander the charming cobblestone streets of Old Town, meticulously rebuilt after World War II. Follow the winding path to the majestic Royal Castle, where you can uncover Poland’s rich royal heritage and admire lavish interiors.

Pay homage to the brave at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier, where an eternal flame burns in solemn tribute to Poland’s fallen heroes. The tranquillity of this ground offers a poignant contrast to the grandeur of Wilanów Palace. This regal estate transports you back to the time of kings and queens. Lose yourself in its opulent halls and wander through its magnificent gardens.
PL.WAW.leisureActivitiesText:
Want something a bit different? Then get ready for a Chopin concert. This isn’t just any performance either, it’s a tribute to Poland’s beloved composer, who was born just outside the city.

Escape to Łazienski Park for a breath of fresh air. You can admire peacocks, meander through beautiful pavilions, and maybe even catch another live Chopin recital by the lake.

Immerse yourself in a vast collection of Polish and international art at the Warsaw National Museum. Explore masterpieces of paintings, sculpture and decorative art spanning centuries. Ready for a pop of colour? Explore the Neon Museum – Europe’s first and only museum that showcases the vibrant history of neon signs, from vintage advertising to dazzling contemporary installations.
PL.WAW.shoppingText:
Zlote Tarasy is the city’s shimmering jewel – a shopping precinct with breathtaking architecture, and a glass dome cascading over high-end boutiques and trendy stores. The sleek, futuristic design alone is worth a visit, but the array of international brands and local designers will have you dreaming for a shopping spree.

For a more traditional experience, head to Rynek Starego Miasta, also known as Old Town Market Square. It’s lined with colourful buildings and filled with stalls selling all sorts of treasures. Don’t miss the beautiful Polish amber jewellery. These glowing gems, pulled from the Baltic Sea, are crafted into stunning necklaces, bracelets and rings. For a piece of heritage, be sure to check out the hand-painted ceramics. Each piece is uniquely made and makes for the perfect souvenir to take home.
PL.WAW.destinationPageIntro: There's no shortage of attractions in Warsaw, from the opulent Royal Castle and Chopin’s tribute concerts, to Łazienki Park’s and the city’s unique dining scene.
PL.WAW.overviewText:
Experience the wonder of Poland’s cultural capital, Warsaw. Wander down cobblestone avenues, stumble upon quirky cafés, or venture to one of the contemporary districts buzzing with energy. The city is a playground for visitors of every age, with pop-up food markets, street performers and plenty of things to see and do.

If you’re looking for relaxation, kick back in one of Warsaw’s lush parks where locals unwind with picnics and paddle boating. As the sun sets, the city comes alive. Rooftop venues offer skyline views, jazz clubs fill the air with soulful melodies and quaint restaurants invite you to savour delicious flavours. Creativity, culture and an eclectic spirit pulse through every corner of this city, making it a truly unique experience.
PL.WAW.destinationHighlightsH1: Warsaw: The cultural capital of Poland
PL.WAW.eatingImageText:
Warsaw isn’t just about history and culture – it’s a city that knows how to satisfy your cravings. 

Start your culinary adventure on Nowy Świat Street in the charming Old Town, where you can savour traditional dishes in cosy restaurants. Taste the local bigos, an authentic Polish stew of tender meat and tangy cabbage served in a rustic, bread bowl.

Feeling peckish for a snack? Indulge in the city’s famed pierogi. These soft, doughy dumplings come filled with all sorts of deliciousness, from savoury cheese and potatoes to sweet fruit.

Up for dessert? Nowy Świat Street has a dedicated cheesecake corner! You’ll find creamy, rich cheesecakes with just the right amount of sweetness. 

If you’re seeking international flavours, head to Hala Koszyki. This vibrant market is a foodie’s haven – a hip dining spot serving everything from sushi to Italian pasta and more.

CZ.PRG.touristAttractionsText:
Down the cobblestone streets and quaint alleyways, there are many sights to see in the city of Prague. Walk over Charles Bridge, with statues watching over the Vltava River. Continue walking towards the Old Town Square where you’ll be charmed by the historic ambience of the city. Spot the Prague Astronomical Clock that strikes each hour with a mesmerising show.

Head up to Prague Castle, perched on a hill with panoramic views of the city’s spires and rooftops. Experience what it feels like to be royalty as you meander through its courtyards and gardens.

At Wenceslas Square, the pulse of modern Prague comes alive with shops and cafés. Make sure to visit the nearby Lucerna Palace, it’s not just a shopping complex, it’s an Art Nouveau wonder with striking architecture and a quirky hanging horse statue. Equally, it’s home to the Lucerna Music Bar – a spot you don’t want to miss, especially in the evenings, for live music and entertainment.
CZ.PRG.leisureActivitiesText:
Letna Park has sweeping views of the city and is ideal for walks along tree-lined paths. It’s even more perfect for relaxing and watching the world go by. Another option is to hop on a bike and cycle through the park, followed by a picnic along the banks of the Vltava River. Otherwise, venture to the Vrtba Garden, a hidden Baroque masterpiece. The garden is abundant with fountains, statues and pathways weaved through hedges and plantations. It’s a hidden gem in the middle of the city.

For a truly rejuvenating experience, sink into one of Prague’s many saunas. Imagine the stress melting away as you relax in the soothing heat of a traditional steam sauna. It’s the perfect escape from the cold if you’re visiting during the winter.
CZ.PRG.shoppingText:
Stroll down the pedestrianised streets of Na Příkopě and 28 Října. These lively avenues are the place to browse high-end boutiques and locally-owned stores stocked with everything from the latest fashion to Czech souvenirs.

A must-buy while in Prague is Czech glass and crystal. Known for its exceptional quality and artistry, these stunning pieces make for an elegant keepsake or gift. From intricate vases to shimmering jewellery, the craftsmanship is unmatched.

Head to Prague Markets, where the locals shop. This bustling bazaar offers a bespoke mix of goods, from vintage finds to handmade treasures. Whether you’re hunting for handcrafted items or simply wanting to people-watch with a cup of coffee, Prague’s markets deliver an authentic taste of the Czech Republic.
CZ.PRG.destinationPageIntro: With all the places to visit in Prague, it's easy to see why it has taken centre stage as one of the world’s most popular holiday destinations.
CZ.PRG.overviewText:
Prague, the capital of the Czech Republic, is full of places to visit from historical landmarks to beautifully manicured gardens and parks. Wander through the cobblestone streets and admire the incredible architecture, from Gothic spires to Baroque facades – each telling their own story.

The city buzzes with life in the day, with cafés and markets brimming with local treats, and the hum of street performers creating an atmosphere like no other. The Vltava River becomes a spectacle in the evening, as the city’s lights cast a golden glow across the water.

Whether you’re a history enthusiast, an adventurer or someone seeking a quiet moment of serenity, Prague has it all, with its old-world allure.
CZ.PRG.eatingImageText:
The Žižkov Farmers Market and the Dejvice Farmers Market are some of the best places to relish fresh, local produce. Stalls are filled with everything from artisanal cheeses to freshly baked bread and sweets giving you a true taste of Czech life.

One dish you have to try is Czech goulash. This meaty stew is packed with beef simmered in a paprika-spiced sauce, often served with dumplings or bread. It’s rich, hearty and deeply satisfying. 

Make sure to try kulajda, a creamy soup made with mushrooms, dill and a touch of sour cream.

If you’re craving something sweet, you will adore ‘trdelník’ or chimney cake – a doughy delight baked to perfection on a cylindrical spit and topped with cinnamon sugar to serve. 

Finally, don’t forget to snack on ‘bramboraky’ whilst you’re there – these are crispy potato pancakes seasoned with garlic and marjoram.

HR.ZAG.touristAttractionsText:
Gather in the bustling main square, Trg Bana Jelačića, to discover the vibrancy and culture of the city of Zagreb. Stroll the streets to the Stone Gate, a historic archway-turned-shrine where candles flicker in homage to Zagreb’s patron saint. Further along, you can spot the Zagreb Cathedral, with gothic spires soaring into the sky – making it the tallest building in Croatia.

Head over to Lotrščak Tower for sweeping views of the city. Don’t miss the daily cannon firing at noon – it’s a local tradition. There is also a museum inside with fascinating facts about the tower.

A fun thing to do is hop onto the shortest funicular in the world on Ilica Street – the minute-long ride connects the lower and upper town, and has been in operation for over a century.
HR.ZAG.leisureActivitiesText:
Take a look around Lenuci Horseshoe – a series of lush, horseshoe-shaped parks and squares dotted with statues, flowerbeds, and fountains, that surround the city centre.

For a true natural retreat that’s a favourite among city dwellers, make your way to Jarun Lake. Often named the Zagreb Sea, Jarun boasts relaxing shores, paddle boats, and cycling paths all around – perfect for a tranquil day outdoors. A little further along you’ll find Maksimir Park, where towering oaks and winding paths have made it a beloved spot for nearly two centuries.

If you’re looking for more of an adventure, take a day trip to Plitvice Lakes National Park, one of Croatia’s most awe-inspiring treasures. With its cascading waterfalls and turquoise lakes, Plitvice is a natural paradise.
HR.ZAG.shoppingText:
Ilica Street is Zagreb’s main hub of retail excitement, where boutiques, artisan shops, and local designers line the sidewalks. From modern fashion to intricate jewellery, here you can browse handcrafted pieces that celebrate Croatian heritage.

No holiday to Zagreb is complete without taking home some Croatian lace. The intricate, delicate lace is more than fabric – it’s a symbol of artistry passed down through generations. Alongside the pretty lace pieces, you’ll often find bundles of lavender, grown in Croatia’s sun-drenched fields and sold in small, hand-tied sachets.

If you’re shopping for little ones, Croatia is abundant with traditional wooden toys. Often shaped and painted by hand, these toys reflect the playful side of Croatian folk art.
HR.ZAG.destinationPageIntro: The medieval Lotrščak Tower and Stone Gate introduce you to the old-world glamour of Croatia’s capital, while Zagreb’s greener side can be seen in and around the city.
HR.ZAG.overviewText:
Zagreb is a whirlwind of sights, sounds and surprises. The cobblestone streets invite you to explore its many landmarks and attractions, including quaint cafés and colourful street art. The city has an easygoing charm, where locals sip their coffee as though they have all the time in the world, and street musicians play melodies that travel through the alleyways.

Zagreb feels like a blend of small-town warmth with big-city energy. One minute you’re appreciating a cultural statue or landmark in a busy square, the next you’re in a quiet park. It’s a city that invites you to explore without a map in order to uncover all its hidden nooks – a delightful mix of history, personality, and pure Croatian flair.
HR.ZAG.eatingImageText:
A top attraction and destination to indulge in is Dolac Market – a hub of fresh produce, artisan cheeses, and local spices. Make your way through the stalls, sampling seasonal fruits and chatting with the locals – it’s where everyone goes for their grocery shopping and a real local gem.

Tkalčićeva Street is a popular strip buzzing with lively cafés. Slurp on a coffee while watching the world go by, indulging in the city’s rich café culture. For a taste of Zagreb’s heartwarming cuisine, try štrukli, a delicious baked pastry layered with cheese. For something heartier, try sarma, a comforting dish of cabbage rolls stuffed with minced meat and rice.

Traditional fare like this can be found in Konoba Didov, or along the main street, Ilica Street.

RS.BEG.touristAttractionsText:
Begin your Serbian holiday at the iconic Belgrade Fortress, where ancient walls tell tales of the past. Overlooking the Danube and Sava Rivers, the fortress is also an idyllic spot for scenic strolls.

Ready for a bit of nature? Just a short drive away lies Mt Avala, offering lush forest trails leading up to the impressive Avala Tower. Once there, prepare to be awed by panoramic vistas of the city. Don’t forget to explore the Danube River – hop aboard a boat ride, grab a coffee at one of the riverside cafés, or simply take a stroll along the banks. 

Explore beyond Belgrade at the Petrovaradin Fortress in Novi Sad – just an hour outside the city. This 17th century landmark boasts stunning architecture and houses several art galleries inside.
RS.BEG.leisureActivitiesText:
Ready for a sun-soaked day? Head over to Ada Ciganlija, known as the “Belgrade Sea”. This lively man-made peninsula is perfect for swimming, cycling and relaxing by the lake. 

If you’re eager to learn more about Serbia’s fascinating history, then the Museum of Yugoslavia is a great place to start. It brings the country’s rich and intricate past vividly to life. Don’t miss the House of Flowers, the peaceful resting place of former leader Josip Broz Tito.

If you’re up for an adventure, consider a trip beyond the city to Eastern Serbia, where you’ll find stunning nature and historical sites. The Manasija Monastery, also known as Resava, is an icon of culture and history dating back to the 15th century. Stop by the Resavska Cave nearby to admire unique rock formations such as stalactites and stalagmites. And make sure to see the Lisine Waterfall nestled within the serene Serbian forests – it’s a hidden gem worth exploring.
RS.BEG.shoppingText:
In addition to the many malls in Belgrade, Knez Mihailova Street is a popular choice for shoppers. This bustling pedestrian avenue is lined with boutique shops, international brand stores and local designer displays. It’s the perfect place to spend an afternoon window shopping and soaking in the vibrant Serbian retail scene. 

For a more authentic shopping adventure, go to Kalenic Market. As the largest and most colourful market in Belgrade, this bustling hub is where locals come to buy fresh produce, handmade goods and artisanal treasures. You’ll find exquisite pieces of locally made pottery and jewellery that make for the perfect souvenirs. 

Keep an eye out for the famous licitar heart-shaped gingerbread cookies too – they’re a cherished tradition throughout Serbia and other Balkan countries.
RS.BEG.destinationPageIntro: Belgrade, the heart of Serbia, is a city of historical sights. Marvel at the old architecture of fortresses, or venture to the outskirts for a slice of Balkan nature.
RS.BEG.overviewText:
Belgrade is a city that’s always telling a story – the heart of Serbia, where culture and history blend seamlessly. This dynamic city is calling you to explore its vibrant streets – where every corner holds a piece of history. Delve into its captivating past, soak up the café culture, or venture into the stunning landscapes of the region. 

In the warmer months, Belgrade comes alive with outdoor festivals, bustling open-air markets and riverside relaxation. As the seasons shift, the city transforms into a cosy haven. Think warm, hearty Serbian meals, captivating cultural events and a winter buzz that’s truly one-of-a-kind. Whether it’s your first trip or your tenth, Belgrade always has something new to offer.
RS.BEG.destinationHighlightsH1: Belgrade: Historical hub in the Balkans
RS.BEG.eatingImageText:
Kickstart your mornings like a true local with burek – a flaky pastry stuffed with cheese or meat that’s a great breakfast on the go. For a taste of homemade goodness, try gibanica – this melt-in-your-mouth layered cheese pie will have you coming back for seconds.

Belgrade is bursting with comforting classics to dine on. Cosy up with gulaš – a hearty meat stew that’s as flavourful as it is filling. It’s typically made with vegetables and various spices, and served alongside mashed potatoes. 

To truly immerse yourself in the authentic culinary scene, head to Skadarlija, Belgrade’s charming bohemian quarter. Cobblestone streets lined with traditional eateries provide the perfect setting to savour classic dishes. Or, for a more contemporary twist with international flair, dine at one of the restaurants on the Belgrade waterfront.

GE.TBS.touristAttractionsText:
Spend a day in Tbilisi Old Town, a maze of cobblestone streets lined with colourful balconies, charming courtyards, and cafés. Soar up to the iconic Mother of Georgia statue by cable car. She watches over the city with her sword and bowl – a symbol of Georgia’s welcoming yet proud nature.

Beyond Old Town, the Sameba Cathedral rises majestically, offering a glimpse into Georgia’s rich history. For something quirky, head to the Chronicles of Georgia, known as the country’s ‘Stonehenge’. These colossal stone pillars depict scenes from Georgia’s ancient past.

Cross the Bridge of Peace for a contemporary masterpiece. The bow-shaped glass and steel structure weaves over the Mtkvari River, leading you toward the Narikala Fortress where you can climb its magnificent ruins and take in the beauty of the skyline.
GE.TBS.leisureActivitiesText:
Pop your history hat on and explore the Georgian National Museum. Walk through the exhibits of ancient artefacts and fascinating archaeology. The National Gallery is another lovely museum where you can observe the works of Niko Pirosmani, Georgia’s most beloved painter.

Need a day of rejuvenation? A visit to Tbilisi’s famous sulfur baths is a must. Let the waters relax your muscles as the steam wraps around you and experience the benefits of this ancient Georgian pampering technique.

For family fun and thrills, ride the funicular railway to Mtatsminda Park – perched high above the city. With amusement rides and beautiful views, it’s a fun escape from the hustle and bustle of the city below. 

If you crave more nature, venture beyond the city to hike near Tbilisi in the stunning Georgian landscapes of the Rkoni Monastery or the verdant Algeti National Park.
GE.TBS.shoppingText:
Stroll down Rustaveli Avenue, the bustling heart of Tbilisi, where you can scout modern boutiques alongside stores brimming with local Georgian craftsmanship. For something more thrifty, the vibrant chaos of the Dry Bridge Flea Market won’t disappoint. You can find relics from the Soviet era, like kitschy memorabilia and antique treasures – each carrying their own story.

If you’re looking for the perfect souvenir, seek out lurji supra, a striking blue tablecloth often adorned with intricate patterns that embodies the aura of Georgian hospitality. And don’t miss the chance to discover Georgia’s renowned pottery and ceramics. The tradition of hand-crafted plates and vases have been passed down through generations, and offer a glimpse into the country’s rich cultural tapestry.
GE.TBS.destinationPageIntro: With its delectable cuisine, 4th-century citadel of Nariqala Fortress, and hiking hotspot, Tblilisi is a holiday dream come true.
GE.TBS.overviewText:
Tbilisi, the charming central hub of Georgia, is nestled between dramatic hills and winding rivers. The city is a captivating blend of cultures, with a rich tapestry of history woven into its landmarks and atmosphere. The aromatic spices of Georgian cuisine are present almost everywhere you go, matching the city’s lively and welcoming vibe.

Wind your way through its old-world streets, uncover traditional courtyards overflowing with flowers, and marvel at the variety of architectural styles. The colours, flavours and sounds around the city provide a mix of life and creativity at every turn.

Whether you’re browsing local art, or soaking up the luxury of a sulfur bath, Tbilisi has many hidden gems to unveil – it’s a destination for the curious and the adventurous.
GE.TBS.eatingImageText:
Head down Shardeni Street, which is filled with cafés and buzzing Georgian restaurants. Order khinkali, Georgia’s infamous dumplings generously filled with spiced meat, cheese or vegetables. Master the art of eating them – pinch, slurp, and savour every bite. 

For a taste of everything Georgian, make sure you also try gobi – a delicious platter of diverse Georgian appetisers.

Indulge in khachapuri, a gooey, cheesy bread that’s so comforting you’ll want seconds. For a vegetarian delight, try some flavourful pkhali, a mix of minced vegetables such as spinach, beetroot, and eggplant mixed with walnut paste and vinegar – best enjoyed with fresh Georgian bread.

The Bazari Orbeliani food hall is worth visiting for the full Georgian culinary experience, with local treats like dried fruits, and fresh honey tempting you everywhere you look.

AM.EVN.touristAttractionsText:
Make your way to the 572-step Yerevan Cascade, an architectural marvel that begins with a Sculpture Garden at its base and culminates with The October Revolution Memorial at the top. The view will leave you in awe, with the majestic Mount Ararat in sight. Beyond the Cascade, you’ll find the towering Mother Armenia Monument in Victory Park.

In the heart of Yerevan, Republic Square pulses with life. Its stunning fountains and grand buildings offer a taste of Yerevan’s vibrant culture. Wander through streets lined with murals, adding a splash of creativity to every alleyway. 

Don’t miss the Blue Mosque for a cultural awakening – it’s the last mosque standing in the city.
AM.EVN.leisureActivitiesText:
Visit Matenadaran, home to the world’s largest collection of ancient manuscripts. It’s a treasure trove for book lovers and history buffs, filled with texts that chronicle Armenia’s rich past.

Take a moment to reflect at the Tsitsernakaberd Memorial, an architectural masterpiece that stands as a powerful symbol of resilience and remembrance. Its striking design and serene surroundings will leave a lasting impression. 

For a change of pace, retreat to Lover’s Park, a green oasis in the heart of the city. Perfect for a quiet stroll, the park features romantic bridges and flowing streams. In the winter months, swap your stroll for skis and head to Mount Teghenis. Known as Armenia’s winter wonderland, it offers fantastic skiing and winter sports for all skill levels.
AM.EVN.shoppingText:
Every purchase in Yerevan feels like stepping into a museum of Armenian culture. Start your shopping adventure at the famed Vernissage Market, where Carpet Row unfolds in a kaleidoscope of colours and designs. These handwoven Armenian rugs, with their intricate patterns, each tell a tale of tradition and artistry. While you’re there, keep an eye out for unique Soviet memorabilia and be sure to stock up on dried fruits. You’ll find stalls brimming with apricots, figs, walnuts and more.

For high-end stores and chic boutiques, head to Northern Avenue. Meanwhile, the Gold Market is home to delicate jewellery, often crafted with local motifs by skilled Armenian goldsmiths.
AM.EVN.destinationPageIntro: Yerevan is not short on attractions: hit the slopes on Mount Teghenis or admire a panoramic view of the city atop the 572-step Cascade Complex.
AM.EVN.overviewText:
The Armenian city of Yerevan is alive with energy, blending ancient tales with a modern vibe that you can feel in every corner. Locals lounge in outdoor cafés, sharing laughs against the backdrop of picturesque mountains. Here, history isn’t tucked away – it’s woven into the walls, the art and even the food.

Markets burst with colour and stories, and the people of Yerevan are quick to share them with a warm smile. There are countless sights to see and natural wonders to discover. It’s a city that pulls you in with its charm and promise of adventure.
AM.EVN.eatingImageText:
The bustling Gum Market is the place to be to watch Armenian chefs in action. Marvel at them making delicious lavash, Armenia’s traditional flatbread, baked fresh in clay ovens. Tolma (also known as dolma) is another must-try dish that features minced meat and rice, wrapped in grape leaves or cabbage.

Every city seems to have its own twist on dumplings and Yerevan is no different with its mante – crispy, bite-sized snacks filled with spiced lamb and served with a tangy yogurt sauce. For a sweet treat, try gata – a buttery Armenian cake that is meant to be served with tea or coffee.

Taste many of these delights on Tumanyan Street, where local vendors serve up everything from grilled meat mains to bite-sized snacks.

AZ.GYD.touristAttractionsText:
The Baku Boulevard is the most enchanting place to spend an afternoon, as you stroll along the Caspian Sea coast. Stop halfway for a delicious ice cream, or head to the walkway in the evening when it comes alive with street food vendors, entertainers and lively crowds.

The UNESCO World Heritage site of the Old Town is Baku’s oldest quarter. Cobbled streets wind their way around the inner citadel, surrounded by the stone walls of the fortress, and look out for landmarks such as the Maiden’s Tower and the Palace of the Shirvanshahs.

One charming place to discover is the Miniature Book Museum, nestled against the western wall of the inner city. Baku’s museums and galleries, including the Museum of Modern Art, are filled with local artwork and fascinating exhibitions.
AZ.GYD.leisureActivitiesText:
For some of the best views of the city, take the funicular lift to the top of the dramatic Flame Towers, where the observation deck gives you stunning panoramic vistas, especially during the evening.

A half-hour drive out of the city takes you to Ateshgah, the Fire Temple. This sacred Zoroastrian site is beautifully preserved and well worth a day trip to see where the eternal flame, fuelled by natural gas, has burned for centuries. Or drive for an hour and a half along the coast to the Qobustan National Park. This UNESCO World Heritage site is a truly unique landscape filled with ancient petroglyphs and incredible mud volcanoes.

For a great family day out, a trip on the Baku Ferris wheel is a must, followed by a trip to the delights of Baku Zoological Park.
AZ.GYD.shoppingText:
While Baku may have plenty of modern malls and department stores to explore, nothing quite beats the energy and buzz of a Bazar. Baku has several to discover, including Taza Bazar and Yasil Bazar, also known as the Green Market. Remember that haggling is mandatory, especially if you want to take an authentic Azerbaijani carpet home as a memento!

For a more leisurely shopping experience, the most popular retail area is Nizami Street. This 3km-long street is the Downtown area of the city and is pedestrianised so you can shop at your leisure. You’ll find boutiques and independent stores as well as plenty of cafés and restaurants where you can stop and refuel before wandering around a few more galleries or shops. It’s just as lively in the evening, when it’s a little cooler.
AZ.GYD.destinationPageIntro: Baku is an architecture lover’s dream filled with historic marvels. This beautiful and romantic summer destination is perfect for an affordable and unforgettable city break.
AZ.GYD.overviewText:
Baku is one of the most eclectic and vibrant cities in the world, where east meets west, and a merging of cultures gives it a unique character. Azerbaijan’s capital is wrapped around the UNESCO World Heritage-listed Old City, surrounded by ancient fortress walls that speak of the capital’s strategic importance through the centuries.

Take a stroll through its winding cobbled streets and you’ll discover exclusive boutiques and coffee bars, restaurants and stores selling international brands.

Wooded parks and lush gardens make Baku a truly green capital, surrounded by the desert on one side and the Caspian Sea on the other. A walk along the promenade as the sun sets is the perfect way to finish a busy day in Baku, followed by some fine dining in one of its many restaurants.
AZ.GYD.destinationHighlightsH1: Baku: A summer destination for everyone
AZ.GYD.eatingImageText:
For some of the best views of the city, take the funicular lift to the top of the dramatic Flame Towers, where the observation deck gives you stunning panoramic vistas, especially during the evening.

A half-hour drive out of the city takes you to Ateshgah, the Fire Temple. This sacred Zoroastrian site is beautifully preserved and well worth a day trip to see where the eternal flame, fuelled by natural gas, has burned for centuries. Or drive for an hour and a half along the coast to the Qobustan National Park. This UNESCO World Heritage site is a truly unique landscape filled with ancient petroglyphs and incredible mud volcanoes.

For a great family day out, a trip on the Baku Ferris wheel is a must, followed by a trip to the delights of Baku Zoological Park.

BH.BAH.touristAttractionsText:
A UNESCO World Heritage Site, the Bahrain Fort is a sight to behold. Wander through the sprawling 16th-century fort and admire views of the Arabian Gulf. For a glimpse of Bahrain’s grandeur, discover the Al Fateh Grand Mosque at the capital of Manama. One of the largest mosques in the world, you can appreciate the intricate architecture, marble domes and chandeliers.

Venture into the desert to see the Tree of Life, a natural wonder that has survived the barren landscape for over 400 years. Alternatively, visit the Royal Camel Farm to interact with the gentle creatures and learn about their cultural significance to Bahrain.

For even more breathtaking views, catch the sunset at Arad Fort. This beautifully preserved 15th-century structure is a prime example of Omani military architecture.
BH.BAH.leisureActivitiesText:
Discover ancient artefacts and the origin stories of Bahrain at the Bahrain National Museum. Explore the exhibits that reveal Bahrain’s pearl diving heritage, Islamic art and archaeological finds.

For a brush with nature, go to the Al Areen Wildlife Park and Reserve, a sanctuary where endangered Arabian species like oryxes and gazelles roam freely. Keep your eyes peeled – it’s a rare opportunity to witness these creatures in their natural habitat.

Explore Bahrain’s history with a walk through the Pearling Path, a UNESCO site that showcases its rich pearl-diving legacy. It takes you past historic homes, merchant shops and ancient coastlines.

Bahrain is also renowned for its beaches. Rent a kayak, pedal boat or a sea bike to glide across the tranquil waters.
BH.BAH.shoppingText:
Explore the vibrant Manama Souq. It’s not only a destination for food but also a must-visit for shopping. Make your way through the lively alleys, letting the scent of exotic spices entice you in to colourful stalls selling saffron, cardamom and cinnamon. Shop for something special like handwoven fabrics – intricately embroidered, making the most beautiful souvenir. There are plenty of pearl jewellery, perfumes and pottery to purchase too.

For an authentic artisanal experience head to the Al Jasra Handicrafts Centre. Watch skilled artisans weave palm leaves into baskets, carve wood into authentic dhow boats or shape clay into spectacular pottery pieces. It’s a place of timeless traditions and meticulous crafting that has been passed down through generations.
BH.BAH.destinationPageIntro: Explore the vibrant energy of Bahrain. From archaeological wonders to traditional souqs, delicious cuisine and beaches lined with date palm – there’s much to see and do.
BH.BAH.overviewText:
Bahrain is one of the Middle East’s most visited countries, known for its energy, warm hospitality and plethora of things to do. Stroll along the sunny white-sand beaches, explore the bustling souqs that sit alongside sleek skyscrapers or tour the nearby desert landscapes. Bahrain’s diversity is something to marvel.

Located along the Arabian Gulf and abundant with date palms, this coastal gem has a unique rhythm within the Middle East. Locals are eager to share their traditions, culture and flavours with all who visit, and the city is filled with unexpected treasures to uncover. Travel to Bahrain, where the island’s spirit is one of adventure.
BH.BAH.destinationHighlightsH1: Bahrain: A modern oasis in the Arabian Gulf
BH.BAH.eatingImageText:
Stroll through the Manama Souq, where the delightful aroma of spices and fresh tandoor bread fills the air. The souq is the heart of Bahraini cuisine, where street stalls and cafés offer up local delights. Try baid tamat, a traditional breakfast dish of scrambled eggs with tomatoes and spices. Pair this with balaleet, a combination of sweet vermicelli and savoury eggs. It’s a breakfast treat that can also double as a dessert.

Give samak safi a try. Freshly fried Safi fish marinated in a blend of aromatic spices is best paired with basmati rice and a side of vegetables. Wash it down with a hot cup of gahwa, a traditional Bahraini spiced coffee. Don’t leave without indulging your sweet tooth with halwa, a sticky, rose-flavoured dessert.

KW.KWI.businessClassSummary:
Fly to Kuwait in Business or First Class with Qatar Airways and enjoy a journey with exceptional service and attention to detail from start to finish.

Your trip begins with priority check-in and fast-tracked immigration procedures. Then make the most of your time before departure in one of our Business Class lounges, where you can savour a delectable light meal, use private workstations, or refresh with a shower.

Once on board, settle into a seat designed for both productivity and relaxation, with ample space to stretch out. Ambient lighting helps you adjust to a different time zone, while high-speed Wi-Fi keeps you connected to colleagues and loved ones on our A380, A350, B787 and select B777 aircraft.

Choose a dish from the à la carte menu crafted by our award-winning chefs and served when it suits you, followed by a movie from our in-flight entertainment selection. When you’re ready to rest, enjoy a restorative sleep on a lie-flat bed with a soft blanket. Arrive at your destination feeling rejuvenated and prepared for business meetings, family gatherings or cultural exploration.

Book a Business or First Class flight to Kuwait with Qatar Airways for an unrivalled travel experience.
KW.KWI.touristAttractionsText:
Kick off your Kuwait getaway at the iconic Kuwait Towers. The futuristic spires aren’t just landmarks, they’re your gateway to a breathtaking outlook of the city and the Arabian Gulf. 

Not far away lies the majestic Grand Mosque, where you can step into a spectacular space filled with intricate patterns, soaring domes and ornate halls, all surrounded by peaceful gardens.

Make your way to the Sheikh Jaber Al Ahmad Cultural Centre and explore the richness of Kuwaiti culture and history. Wander through the lush park in the centre, watch the water fountains and grab a snack at one of the eateries. It’s a great spot for a family picnic or an evening stroll.

Round off your trip with a day at Al Shaheed Park, an urban oasis of lush gardens, art installations and peaceful pathways for walks.
KW.KWI.leisureActivitiesText:
If you’re on a family trip, a great way to cool off and have some fun together is at the water park near the Kuwait Towers. There are rides, pools and plenty of cold drinks to keep everyone happy and hydrated.

One of the city’s landmarks is the Mirror House, a dazzling display of artwork by Lidia Al Qattan. Adorned with glittering mirror mosaics both inside and out, it’s a never-to-be-forgotten experience.

For a taste of Middle Eastern luxury, unwind at one of Kuwait’s opulent resorts. Lounge by an infinity pool, indulge in a spa treatment, and dine at a restaurant serving mouth-watering Kuwaiti food. The city’s resorts offer a perfect blend of relaxation and sophistication.
KW.KWI.shoppingText:
Your shopping journey should start at Souk Al-Mubarakiya, where the winding alleys and local bazaars overflow with treasures. Browse through stalls selling beautiful carpets, woven with patterns that tell stories of Turkish and Egyptian craftsmanship. There are piles of rare spices on offer and perfumes to smell, each bottle offering a unique Middle Eastern fragrance. 

There’s lots of hand-carved wood to admire too, from furniture pieces to delicate trinkets that make great souvenirs.

Head to the marina to discover the modern Kuwait City. You'll find yourself in a stylish shopping destination where high-end boutiques meet stunning seaside views. Shop for fashion, dine in chic cafés and enjoy the lively atmosphere. Then visit one of the biggest malls in the GCC along Sheikh Zayed Bin Sultan Al Nahyan road for a vast array of shopping, dining and entertainment experiences.
KW.KWI.destinationPageIntro: Visit the Kuwait Towers for a spectacular view before touring the Grand Mosque and tantalize your tastebuds with traditional Kuwaiti food in a welcoming family restaurant.
KW.KWI.overviewText:
Take off on an adventure and discover the rich culture of Kuwait City. Wander around this ancient city and immerse yourself in its old-world charm, and sleek, contemporary vibes. The streets are lined with quaint cafés serving local treats, and traditional markets are bursting with the aroma of spices and freshly brewed coffee.

From family-friendly water parks to the sparkling beauty of the Mirror House, Kuwait City is a surprising and delightful destination.
