World-class food and shopping locations stand alongside ancient souqs and charming tea shops. It’s a breath of fresh air no matter how you experience it. Kuwait City is a place that’s both captivating and diverse.
KW.KWI.eatingImageText:
Thanks to it being located near the sea, fish is a staple in Kuwaiti cuisine. A classic fish dish is mutabbaq samak, made from zubaidi (a silver pomfret fish that’s abundant in the sea around Kuwait) and served with rice cooked in a well-seasoned fish stock.

No visit to Kuwait is complete without trying machboos, the nation’s signature dish of spiced rice and tender meat. Finish your meal with some sweet delicacies that the city is famous for, including syrup-soaked doughnut balls (luqaimat) or a spiced wheat flour pudding served with ghee and walnuts (asida).

Street food enthusiasts can’t miss out on a juicy shawarma, where marinated meat is grilled and wrapped in soft bread. It’s often served with a side of garlic sauce and pickles, too. In Kuwait, every bite tells a story that will leave you craving more.

OM.MCT.businessClassSummary:
Fly to Muscat in Business or First Class with Qatar Airways and embark on a journey where impeccable attention to detail and renowned hospitality create a memorable experience. Begin at a dedicated check-in counter, then unwind in one of our exclusive Business Class lounges. Here, you can refresh with a shower, savour a light meal, or finish off a few last-minute tasks in one of the private workstations. 

On board, relax in your ergonomically designed seat with ample space to stretch out. Ambient lighting gently adjusts your body clock, while high-speed Wi-Fi on our A380, A350, B787 and select B777 aircraft keeps you connected. Be sure to discover thousands of entertainment options including the latest movies, TV shows and games. 

Then choose an exquisite meal from the à la carte menu, prepared by our award-winning chefs, and enjoy the flexibility of dining whenever you wish. For complete relaxation, recline in a lie-flat bed for a restful sleep. With premium personal care kits, you’ll feel refreshed and ready to explore Oman’s capital.  

Book a Business or First Class flight to Muscat with Qatar Airways and begin your Arabian adventure in unrivalled luxury.
OM.MCT.touristAttractionsText:
Visit the most iconic attraction in Muscat, the Sultan Qaboos Grand Mosque. The mosque’s beauty is awe-inspiring, particularly at dusk when the golden dome glows softly against the sky. Not far from the mosque sits Al Alam Palace – an architectural masterpiece that presents a modern twist on traditional Omani design.

Discover Muscat’s rich history at the Bait Al-Zubair Museum, where Omani heritage comes alive in the intricate artefacts and collections on display. The Oman National Museum offers an even deeper insight into the country’s past, from its maritime legacy to its vibrant cultural tapestry.

Travel back in time in Muscat’s Old Quarter, with its 16th century forts, narrow alleyways and historic whitewashed buildings.
OM.MCT.leisureActivitiesText:
Adventure and culture go hand-in-hand in Muscat. Climb up to Mutrah Fort, a historic gem built in the 1580s. Reach the top for sweeping views of the harbour below — setting the scene for the ultimate photoshoot. After your climb, relax at the charming café where you can soak up the history that surrounds you.

For a more refined experience in Muscat, the elegant Royal Opera House is a must. This architectural beauty hosts world-class performances, from ballet and opera to world-renowned shows. 

When it’s time to unwind, head to Qurum Beach for a walk along the water’s edge, or a blissful sunset swim.
OM.MCT.shoppingText:
Mutrah Souk is at the heart of shopping in Muscat. Step into the bustling marketplace, where the air is thick with the smell of spices like saffron, cinnamon, and cardamom. A treasure trove of delights, you’ll find everything from handcrafted silver and gold jewellery to intricately designed marquetry boxes – each piece a testament to Omani craftsmanship.

Stumble upon stalls selling leather sandals that are soft, durable and made with the precision of skilled artisans. Stop by the antique shops, where Omani lanterns, authentic khanjars, and trinkets can be found.

Coffee enthusiasts can stock up on fragrant Omani blends, known locally as ‘kahwa’. Another fragrant favourite to shop for is frankincense – which was once worth its weight in gold and is known for its healing properties.
OM.MCT.destinationPageIntro: From Bait Al-Zubair Museum’s vast collection of artefacts to the grandeur of the Sultan Qaboos Grand Mosque, Muscat is a cultural treasure trove waiting to be unearthed.
OM.MCT.overviewText:
Steeped in history and ancient traditions, the port city of Muscat captures the imaginations of visitors with its Arabian charm. Set against the backdrop of rugged mountains and the Gulf of Oman, there’s plenty to explore in Oman’s capital. 

Enjoy the scent of frankincense lingering in the air, and experience the famed Omani hospitality that’s bound to make you feel right at home. Whether you are sipping Omani coffee in a quiet café, soaking up the coastal sun, or exploring one of its many cultural wonders, Muscat is a traveller’s dream.
OM.MCT.eatingImageText:
The streets of Muscat are filled with the enticing aroma of Omani spices. This once-famous ancient trading hub is also influenced by the rich and fragrant flavours from countries such as Yemen, Türkiye and India.

For a true local taste, one cannot talk about Omani cuisine without mentioning shuwa. Succulent meat is marinated in spices, wrapped in banana leaves, and slow-cooked in an underground oven. For an even more adventurous feat, why not sample some camel meat? Often served with rice, this hearty dish provides a glimpse into the Bedouin way of life.

Seafood lovers will have a field day in Muscat, with an abundance of fresh fish dishes available from the Gulf of Oman, seasoned with local treasures like Omani dried limes.

SA.RUH.businessClassSummary:
Fly to Riyadh in Business or First Class with Qatar Airways to arrive in Saudi Arabia’s capital in style. As soon as you check in, our world-renowned team are on hand to ensure that you enjoy unmatched comfort during every moment. With our impeccable attention to detail, your trip will be one to remember from take-off to landing. 

Begin in one of our exclusive Business Class lounges, where you can relax in peace and quiet. Take a hot shower, sip on a refreshing drink or unwind with a good book until the aircraft is ready for boarding. Once our courteous cabin crew welcome you onboard, you’re free to settle into your seat, complete with generous legroom giving you the space stretch out.  

During the flight, connect to high-speed Wi-Fi on our A380, A350, B787 and select B777 aircraft, or watch a film from our extensive entertainment selection. When you’re craving a mouth-watering meal, explore our à la carte menu, featuring dishes freshly prepared by our award-winning chefs. Then drift off into a restful sleep on a lie-flat bed, while ambient lighting resets your body to your destination’s time zone. 

Book a flight to Riyadh in Business or First Class with Qatar Airways and revel in a luxurious travel experience.
SA.RUH.touristAttractionsText:
Begin your journey at the Al Murabba Historical Palace and the Al Masmak Palace, both of which provide fascinating insights into the country’s cultural evolution. Then, make your way to the King Abdullah Financial District, an architectural marvel known for its impressive skyline and cutting-edge infrastructure.

Riyadh boasts numerous museums that offer a comprehensive look into the past, and the Saudi National Museum is a great place to start, with a treasure trove of historical artefacts. Be sure to check out Saudi’s emerging art scene at Naila Art Gallery, Al Ajlan Art Gallery and the Abstract Art Gallery.

Visit Diriyah for an authentic outdoor experience – you'll get to enjoy seasonal events, folk performances, markets and traditional restaurants.

Don’t miss Riyadh Season, featuring entertainment venues like Boulevard City and the Riyadh Zoo.
SA.RUH.leisureActivitiesText:
Riyadh’s surrounding natural landscapes, from the rugged desert dunes to the serene mountain ranges, offer endless opportunities for exploration.

Spend a day at Al Kharrarah National Park, an idyllic spot for hiking, picnicking and admiring the scenic views. Wadi Namar also offers a serene escape with its tranquil streams and lush surroundings.

Feeling adventurous? Take on a desert safari to experience the vast desert landscapes. Or, travel an hour outside the city to the Edge of the World – a dramatic cliff overlooking the Tuwaik Mountain range. The views are particularly breathtaking at sunset. While in the area, check out Heet Cave, a limestone cave with an eye-like entrance and an underground lake.
SA.RUH.shoppingText:
Shopping in Riyadh offers a blend of traditional markets and souqs, alongside luxurious and contemporary retail experiences. The city’s malls provide a cosmopolitan atmosphere with a diverse selection of luxury brands, international retailers and high-quality dining. Take a stroll down Roshn Front, a high-end development featuring upscale boutiques, restaurants and entertainment venues.

For a more traditional shopping experience, head to Farmer’s Day, where local vendors present fresh produce and crafts, showcasing Saudi Arabia’s agricultural heritage. Immerse yourself in the cultural richness at Souq Al-Zal, a bustling marketplace filled with spices, textiles, and handmade goods – a perfect venue for finding a souvenir to take back home.
SA.RUH.destinationPageIntro: Visit the heart of Saudi Arabia. Discover the cultural evolution of Riyadh at its many museums, then venture further out of the city to enjoy some spectacular natural wonders.
SA.RUH.overviewText:
The dynamic capital of Saudi Arabia, Riyadh, is rapidly emerging as a must-see tourist destination with attractions that range from urban sightseeing to stunning natural wonders. Historically renowned for its ancient landmarks and rich cultural heritage, the city is also embracing a modern transformation, particularly in its flourishing arts scene.

Explore art galleries and museums or stroll through traditional souqs and savour the unique flavours of local cuisine, to fully embrace the city’s cultural essence. Venture beyond the bustling urban landscapes to uncover the serene beauty of oases, wadis (valleys) and national parks. With so much to do and see, Riyadh promises a captivating experience in the heart of Saudi Arabia.
SA.RUH.destinationHighlightsH1: Riyadh: Where timeless tradition meets modernity
SA.RUH.eatingImageText:
Set about your gastronomic journey in Riyadh on Tahliyah Street, a vibrant hub of Arabic eateries and chic cafés. Savour a plate of kabsa, Saudi Arabia’s signature dish, featuring flavourful rice and meat infused with aromatic spices.

Find your way to the Addoho neighbourhood and grab yourself a shawarma – a popular street food featuring thinly sliced meat wrapped in tender bread and savoury sauces. If you’re a vegetarian, freshly made falafel is a must-try. These deep-fried balls or patties, made from ground chickpeas or fava beans and mixed with herbs and spices, are a middle-eastern favourite.

Up for dessert? Make sure to try luqaimat – crispy and fluffy dough balls that are deep fried and dunked into sugar syrup.

JO.AMM.touristAttractionsText:
Discover the Ancient Roman Amphitheatre, a magnificent 2,000-year old structure that once hosted grand performances, and is now a historic marvel. Stand on the same stage where gladiators once fought and imagine the roar of the crowds.

Make your way to the Amman Citadel, where the Temple of Hercules awaits – there’s no better place for a panoramic view of Amman. The colossal hand of Hercules still rests here as a reminder of the global hero’s strength.

Don’t miss the King Abdullah I Mosque while exploring within the city too – its striking blue dome is visible from almost anywhere in the city.
JO.AMM.leisureActivitiesText:
Uncover ancient treasures that tell tales of lost civilisations at the Jordan Archaeological Museum. Browse exhibits of artefacts that date from the 15th century to as far back as prehistoric times. Or lose yourself in the artsy vibes of Darat al Funun, a hidden gem tucked away in Amman’s streets.

If you’re up for a desert adventure, head about an hour out of Amman to the stunning Umayyad Palace at Qasr al-Kharaneh. This massive desert castle, a UNESCO gem, feels like something out of a fairytale, with its towering walls and mysterious past.

Venture even further to the famous site of Petra. This legendary city carved into rose-coloured cliffs is one of the seven wonders of the world and an absolute must-see.
JO.AMM.shoppingText:
Your one-stop shop for your Amman retail journey is Souk Jara – a weekly market nestled near the famous Rainbow Street. Rainbow Street is lined with shops of locally crafted clothing and souvenirs. Picture a maze of stalls dotted with colourful crafts, handmade jewellery, and eclectic antiques.

For a touch of tradition and your own piece of Jordanian opulence, get your hands on some of the exquisite gold jewellery. The souk is the place to be for reasonably priced gold. You may also slip into handcrafted leather sandals, or pick up beautiful beads and mosaics that perfectly capture Amman’s artistic flair.
JO.AMM.destinationPageIntro: Explore Amman, where you can marvel at the Ancient Roman Amphitheatre and Temple of Hercules, or venture to the spectacular wonder of the world, Petra.
JO.AMM.overviewText:
Amman is a city of culture and excitement, with wonders of the world not far from the centre and dazzling experiences at its heart. Wander through the urban tapestry that is truly a treasure trove of surprises – from a spectacular bazaar where the stalls are bursting with spices, crafts and trinkets, to one of the world’s most iconic landmarks.

Unveil a new facet of this lively city, and dive into the rhythm of Amman where its charm will sweep you off your feet.
JO.AMM.eatingImageText:
Delve into the soul of Levantine cuisine, where each dish tells a story. Stroll down Rainbow Street, where cosy cafés and dessert spots create a sugary parade of knafeh, with its gooey cheese and crisp pastry, and baklava, dripping with honey and nuts. If you’re on the go, falafel is the best snack – a crispy, spiced chickpea ball.

Indulge in a plate of mansaf – Jordan’s beloved national dish. Tender lamb is slow-cooked in a creamy yoghurt sauce and served with fluffy rice. It’s often enjoyed during festive gatherings, where friends and family enjoy it together.

If you end up in the desert, taste the Bedouin tradition of zarb. Cooked in an underground oven, meat and vegetables are infused with a smoky, earthy flavour that narrates Jordan’s nomadic past.

LB.BEY.touristAttractionsText:
The Museum and Urban Cultural Center of Beirut, also known as ‘Yellow House’, is as much art as it is history. Its walls bear the marks of Beirut’s past, particularly the Lebanese Civil War.

The Roman Baths are just a stone’s throw away – now just ruins and a peaceful city oasis, they invite you to imagine what life was like centuries ago.

Martyrs’ Square is one of the most significant attractions in Beirut. Gather at the square with a bag of takeaway falafel and take in this historic landmark.

There are a number of spots for art lovers to relish, including the Sursock Museum and the National Museum of Beirut. Delve into the artistic evolution and collective memory of Beirut as you stroll through the galleries.
LB.BEY.leisureActivitiesText:
Experience the coastal charm of Beirut while admiring the art at the Corniche. The murals dotted along the strip give you a true taste of the creativity that runs through this Lebanese city. For a glimpse of nature’s artistry, head to the Rocks of Raouche, also known as ‘Pigeon Rocks’. Find a spot along the coast to gaze at the sunset between these towering rock formations.

If the beach is on your agenda, the Sporting Club Beach is calling your name. It’s a popular spot for locals to relax and soak up the sun. If skiing is more your scene, the mountains near Beirut offer an incredible ski opportunity. Trails are varied, providing everything from gentle slopes to more challenging descents. The après-ski scene is one to revel in too, with its touch of warming Lebanese hospitality.
LB.BEY.shoppingText:
Shopping in Downtown Beirut offers a unique blend of luxury, tradition and modernity. At the heart of the experience lies the Beirut Souks, home to high end brands, local boutiques and artisanal crafts. From luxury fashion to handmade jewellery and souvenirs, there’s something for everyone.

Lose yourself in the vibrant neighbourhoods of Bourj Jammoud and Hamra. Wander through local shops selling gold, traditional clothing, spices, perfume and much more. Every item tells a story of Beirut’s rich history. Friendly shop owners are eager to share the passion behind their trade, making your shopping experience as special as the gifts you take home.
LB.BEY.destinationPageIntro: Beirut is perfect for a relaxed city break featuring great coffee and leisurely strolls along the Corniche or a more active getaway exploring the sights and maybe even skiing.
LB.BEY.overviewText:
Beirut is a city that refuses to be defined by its past, yet proudly showcases its rich heritage at every corner. From the wholesome cafés with the aroma of freshly brewed coffee, to historical landmarks – it’s a mosaic of ancient and modern history, resilience and creativity.

Beirut is a city where you can swim in the Mediterranean Sea and ski in the snowcapped mountains of Faraya, all in the same day. Make sure to wander through a vibrant souk, savour traditional Lebanese mezze and visit the Roman baths.

Every moment is a chance to discover something new, beautiful and unique in Beirut.
LB.BEY.eatingImageText:
Dive into the Lebanese culture with a delectable mezze spread of hummus, tahini, lemon, tabbouleh and crispy falafel. Try a classic shawarma served with pickles and garlic sauce.

On Thursdays, the Souk El Akel is the place to be for Lebanese street food and live cooking stations – it’s a feast for the eyes and the palate. Delight in fresh, seasonal produce at the Beirut Farmer’s Market where you’ll find handmade cheeses, olives and fruit jams that capture the city’s agricultural bounty.

For a culinary surprise, venture to Little Armenia, where you can order dishes like sujuk (a spicy, garlic sausage) and lahmajoun (a thin, crispy flatbread with mince, tomatoes and herbs).

IQ.BGW.touristAttractionsText:
Explore the Al-Kadhimayn Shrine, the final resting place of two Imams, known for its serene atmosphere. The architectural grandeur and intricate detailing here is something to marvel at. Wander through Al-Mutanabbi Street, the heartbeat of Baghdad’s literary scene. The famous Al-Mutanabbi Statue stands as a tribute to the celebrated 10th-century poet. Surrounding book markets and cafés invite you to experience the city’s literary heritage.

For a moment of quiet remembrance, visit the Al-Shaheed Monument, a stunning symbol of Iraq’s fallen soldiers. Its striking blue dome against the skyline is quite iconic. The Al-Kadhimayn Mosque is another architectural wonder, with glittering golden domes that narrate Baghdad’s rich history.
IQ.BGW.leisureActivitiesText:
The Iraqi National Museum houses fascinating treasures of the historical region of Mesopotamia. Ancient artefacts, relics from the dawn of civilisation, and pottery works tell stories of empires long gone. Feel connected to a time when Baghdad was the centre of the world’s knowledge and culture.

For a change of pace from the history, head to Al-Zawraa Park, the city’s green oasis. There is a zoo, gardens and an amusement park to enjoy inside. Take a leisurely stroll or hop on a boat across the lake – you can easily spend a day there.

Baghdad Island is another slice of serenity within the city, located on the Tigris River. Walk down palm-lined paths, picnic on the grassy plains, and admire views of the city skyline.
IQ.BGW.shoppingText:
Revisit Al-Mutanabbi Street, where the scent of old books fills the air. The street is dotted with bookshops and teahouses, a haven for literary enthusiasts. Browse rare books, poetry collections, and writings that have shaped Iraqi culture.

Make your way to the vibrant Alsafafeer Market, where the charm of Baghdad’s craftsmanship comes alive. Artisans and craftsmen sell handmade items like copperware, jewellery, and beautifully woven rugs. It’s a glimpse into Baghdad’s traditional mercantile traditions.

No trip to Baghdad would be complete without wandering through the colourful spice stalls in the market, where the scent of cumin, cardamom and cinnamon lingers. You can also find authentic local clothing here – flowing abayas and uniquely embroidered fabrics provide the perfect keepsake.
IQ.BGW.destinationPageIntro: Iraq's fascinating capital and a significant cultural hub Baghdad is home to a plethora of historic museums and shrines.
IQ.BGW.overviewText:
Once the heart of the Islamic Golden Age, Baghdad weaves together a tapestry of old-world mystique and modern vitality. Walking its streets can feel like stepping into a living museum, where centuries of culture are reflected in its many landmarks of shrines and museums.

The sounds of bustling souqs fill the air, where artisans craft by hand and the scent of spiced dishes draws you in. Delve into the stories of ancient civilisations and poets as you meander through the winding city alleyways and along the riverbanks.

Whether you are an adventurer or a seeker of knowledge, Baghdad’s historical and cultural essence will leave you feeling inspired and enchanted.
IQ.BGW.eatingImageText:
Baghdad cuisine is a fusion of Persian, Turkish and Arab influences. Start your culinary journey with a breakfast dish of kahi and geymar. Kahi are flaky, buttery pastries served with geymar, a rich clotted cream often drizzled with honey or syrup.

Al Rasheed Street is the place to be – whether you’re looking for street food snacks or restaurant meals. Biryani is one of the most popular dishes to try in Baghdad – tender meat and vegetables atop fragrant rice infused with spices and saffron. For a truly local specialty, try Iraq’s renowned grilled fish dish ‘masgouf’: fish is slow-cooked over an open flame and seasoned with olive oil, tamarind and lemon.

Looking for a sweet treat? Dive into the world of baklava – a sugary filo pastry, and halwa – a sesame-based dessert.

PK.KHI.touristAttractionsText:
For a slice of history, discover Frere Hall. This colonial relic is a multipurpose landmark – a museum, art gallery, gardens and a historical wonder. Delve deeper into Karachi’s past at the Mohatta Palace Museum and uncover the influences of Mughal and Rajasthani eras.

Witness the final resting place of Pakistan’s founder, Mazar-e-Quaid. This iconic white, marble mausoleum is right in the city’s core.

Step back in time to a forgotten era at the Chaukhandi Tombs. These ancient, intricately carved sandstone tombs are surreal – they’re worth the short journey outside of the city to see.
PK.KHI.leisureActivitiesText:
Karachi is home to picturesque beach scenes, just a short drive from the city centre. There are many spots to enjoy, including Port Grand. This promenade is a real feast for the senses, with its waterfront views, lively eateries, and entertainment. Stroll down the boardwalk as the sea breeze cools you down, sample street food, and listen the melodies of live music – all with the city skyline as your backdrop.

Escape to the beaches of Clifton, where the sand meets the Arabian Sea. Whether you choose the tranquil sands of Sandspit, or the rugged beauty of Paradise Point with its natural rock formations, each beach offers a unique glimpse of Karachi’s coastal charm. Hawksbay is the perfect location for a relaxing day under the sun, with golden sands, azure waters and even camels to ride.
PK.KHI.shoppingText:
While you’re at Port Grand soaking up its history, wander through the stalls filled with artisanal crafts, fashion, and bespoke souvenirs. Similarly, if you visit Frere Hall on the weekend, local artisans gather to showcase their products. Browse the handmade jewellery, artwork, and more. The historic setting adds an element of prestige, as you walk through the gardens discovering one-of-a-kind pieces.

Immerse yourself in the vibrant energy of Zainab Market, a treasure trove of textiles where you can discover everything from colorful fabrics to exquisitely crafted garments. Hunt for Pakistani textiles to take home, or even a handwoven carpet.
PK.KHI.destinationPageIntro: Mohatta Palace Museum and Quaid-e-Azam's Mausoleum are the perfect introduction into Karachi’s culture. Or amble along Port Grand’s promenade, and head for the beaches.
PK.KHI.overviewText:
Karachi, a city where the Arabian Sea meets the shore, is a tapestry of cultures. It’s a place where every street hums with life, and the aroma of spicy street food mingles with the salty sea air. Wander through its bustling neighbourhoods, where the people of Karachi are as diverse as the city itself.

Whether you’re a first-time visitor, or someone who has explored this city countless times, this city in Pakistan always has something new to offer.
PK.KHI.eatingImageText:
A street food tour is a great way to taste your way around Karachi. Make your way to Burns Road Food Street for a plate of nihari – a rich, slow-cooked stew simmered in spices. Often enjoyed for breakfast, this national dish warms the heart and soul. For a mid-morning treat, savour kulfi – Karachi’s traditional ice cream made from condensed milk, flavoured with cardamom and garnished with nuts.

Explore the streets near Mohatta Palace and Zainab Market in search of the famous bun kebab. This meat patty is fried and sandwiched between soft buns, with chutney and fresh onions – it’s a burger with a Karachi twist. Of course, no trip to Karachi is complete without a bowl of biryani – a fragrant rice dish with layers of meat, spices, and saffron. Scoop it up with a buttery, pan-fried paratha flatbread.

LK.CMB.businessClassSummary:
Fly to Colombo in Business or First Class with Qatar Airways and make your journey to Sri Lanka’s bustling capital as memorable as the destination itself. From entering the airport to landing at your destination, our team ensures that you experience optimal comfort during every moment of your trip.

Enjoy priority check-in and a quick route through immigration, then relax in one of our Business Class lounges. Here, you can indulge in freshly prepared cuisine, make use of the workstations, or take a hot shower to prepare for the flight ahead.

Once on board, sit back in an ergonomically designed seat, with generous personal space that makes it easy to work, dine or unwind. Ambient lighting helps you adjust naturally to a different time zone, while high-speed Wi-Fi keeps you connected on our A380, A350, B787 and select B777 aircraft.

Then savour gourmet cuisine from the à la carte menu, created by our award-winning chefs, and explore a wide range of entertainment options. When it’s time to sleep, transform your seat into a lie-flat bed for quality rest. Arrive at your destination feeling refreshed and ready to dive into dynamic business hubs, coastal scenery and rich cultural heritage.

Book a flight to Colombo in Business or First Class with Qatar Airways and travel in unmatched luxury.
LK.CMB.touristAttractionsText:
Explore Colombo’s spiritual sites, starting with Gangaramaya Temple – Colombo’s most important temple and place of education. Just outside the city lies Kelaniya Raja Maha Viharaya Temple, an iconic site in the country’s history. 

Immerse yourself in Sri Lanka’s culture with a visit to the Colombo National Museum to admire paintings, sculptures and sketches dating back to the 4th century B.C.

If you are transiting through Colombo, make sure to take a trip to the incredible rock fortress of Sigiriya. Consider setting off early to watch the sunrise from atop the ancient ruins and witness the jungle below come to life.

Do not miss the opportunity to go to Galle Fort, a UNESCO World Heritage Site in the southern town of Galle. It’s the largest remaining colonial-era fortress in Asia and a great location for restaurants, shopping and seaside views.
LK.CMB.leisureActivitiesText:
Get a breathtaking bird’s eye view of Colombo by ascending to the observation deck of Lotus Tower – the tallest self-supported structure in South Asia. Then, relax on the golden sands of Mount Lavinia Beach and treat yourself to some local seafood. For an authentic Sri Lankan experience, travel around the city on a trishaw – a motorised three-wheeled chariot.

Upgrade from three to four wheels for a day trip to the Wilpattu National Park. Embark on a safari through the untamed wilderness and look out for elephants and elusive leopards. 

Book a scenic train ride from Colombo into the tea plantations and marvel at the beauty of Sri Lanka’s countryside. Travel up hills, through the jungle and arrive at tea country where the production of Ceylon varieties takes place.
LK.CMB.shoppingText:
Colombo has numerous premier shopping destinations, boasting upscale boutiques, international brands and gourmet cuisine.

For a historic twist on your shopping trip, wander through the charming cobblestone streets of the Dutch Hospital Shopping Precinct. This landmark has been transformed into a dynamic shopping and dining precinct, now bursting with unique handicrafts.

Find locally sourced products and artisanal goods at Good Market, a community-focused marketplace offering live music, workshops and cultural events. Weave your way through the stalls to find an authentic Sri Lankan souvenir such as native tea leaves or cinnamon.
LK.CMB.destinationPageIntro: A picturesque city, nestled along the western coast of Sri Lanka, boasts an abundance of history, culture and extraordinary beach and wilderness landscapes.
LK.CMB.overviewText:
Fly to Colombo – the beating heart of Sri Lanka. This picturesque city acts as a central hub for exploration and adventure around the Sri Lankan countryside, while the city itself boasts an abundance of history, culture and extraordinary landscapes.

Colombo stands as a testament to Sri Lanka’s rich heritage, with various contrasting activities and sights to see. You can venture through temples, stroll along pristine beaches, relax in luscious gardens and indulge in delicious local cuisine.

Outside of the city, the country landscapes are well worth the few hours journey by car or train. You can discover ruins, spot elephants in the jungle or take a train through the tea plantations.

This gateway city has something for every kind of traveller to enjoy.
LK.CMB.eatingImageText:
Colombo’s culinary scene is a feast for the taste buds. Sample the world-famous Singapore chilli crab, which is actually caught in Sri Lanka. Whether steamed, grilled or cooked in a spicy sauce, these crustaceans are a must-try. 

Savour the flavours of Sri Lankan cuisine with a hearty plate of Sri Lankan rice and curry or embrace the street food markets. Order kottu roti – sliced roti blended with your choice of meat, egg, vegetables and spices. Another delectable dish to try is Sri Lankan hoppers – a crispy, fermented coconut milk pancake topped with an egg.

If you are a dedicated food enthusiast, travel a few hours south to Ganduwa Island where you can taste the world’s finest cinnamon. Learn about the production and enjoy its aromatic flavours in traditional dishes and desserts.

BD.DAC.touristAttractionsText:
Kick off your Dhaka adventure at Lalbagh Fort. Imagine the grandeur of Mughal-era courts as you stroll through its majestic halls, gardens and ancient tombs. Continue the historical journey onward to Old Dhaka, to the Ahsan Manzil. This iconic Pink Palace is a photographer's dream – as you walk through the opulent rooms, capture a taste for royal extravagance.

Step into the serene ambiance of Dhakeshwari Temple, a peaceful retreat that has stood for over 800 years. Just a stone’s throw away, discover the hidden gem of Shan Mohammad Mridha, showcasing exquisite Mughal-era architecture with its delicate arches and ornate carvings. Conclude your journey at the Star, a spectacular site adorned with star-shaped mosaics and tiles, offering a visual feast for the eyes.
BD.DAC.leisureActivitiesText:
Let the bustling, colourful Sadarghat Riverfront sweep you away as you set sail on a boat ride. This kaleidoscope of boats, vendors, and locals provide a glimpse of the lively tapestry of daily life in Dhaka.

Hop on a rickshaw, one of the most popular forms of transport in Dhaka, and ride through the classical area of Sonargon. It’s dotted with some of the oldest buildings in Dhaka, where narrow streets reveal stories etched in ancient bricks.

Take a thrilling detour to the Sundarbans National Park, home to the incredible Bengal tiger. The UNESCO World Heritage Site is worth the trek out of the city to cruise through the mangroves, and spot this wildlife wonder with many exotic species
BD.DAC.shoppingText:
Dive in to the liveliness of Dhaka New Market. This shopping haven has been around since the 1950s and is a treasure trove for bargain hunters. This maze of stalls sells everything from fashionable clothing to quirky, household items. Haggling is the name of the game here, and scoring a great deal is all part of the fun.

The rainbow labyrinths of Banga Bazar or Shankharia Bazar are sensory delights, providing a shopping trip that is quintessentially Dhaka. The narrow lanes are packed with stalls of shimmering silk, bamboo crafts, and intricately designed bangles – keep a look out for Dhaka’s infamous pink pearls too. These pearls are cultivated in local waters and have a meticulous culturing process that result in the stunning, pinkish tones.
BD.DAC.destinationPageIntro: Explore the splendid Lalbagh Fort, and the pink hues of Ahsan Manzil to experience the pride of Bangladesh. Don’t forget to pick up some pink pearls at the Banga Bazar!
BD.DAC.overviewText:
Discover a city where the rickshaw bells ring and the streets pulse with energy and vibrancy – explore the Bangladesh capital of Dhaka. The city is a melting pot of cultures, celebrated for its diverse heritage. You can explore a variety of historical and cultural landmarks, all harmoniously coexisting in this vibrantly energetic cityscape.

Throughout the year, Dhaka comes alive with a myriad of festivals that paint the town in every colour imaginable. From dazzling lights and fireworks, to traditional music and dance – there’s always something to enjoy. Experience the rhythm and warmth of the heart of Bangladesh.
BD.DAC.eatingImageText:
Allow your senses to guide you to Dhaka’s street food scene, where you can wander through markets and order crispy fritters and spicy chaats – wafers made from chickpeas and potatoes. Indulge in a heartier dish like a kebab, where tender meat is marinated over an open flame and served with a variety of stuffed breads.

Roast meats in general are a must-try in Dhaka, often cooked slowly to perfection. One of these dishes is Kachi biryani – made up of fragrant rice, mutton, spices and saffron, and typically paired with sweetened coconut and jaggery (cubes of unrefined cane sugar).

For something upscale, venture to the district of Gulshan. Renowned for its finest restaurants, gourmet chefs craft dishes that blend local ingredients with international flair.

TH.HKT.businessClassSummary:
Fly to Phuket with Qatar Airways in Business or First Class and travel the world in style. Whether you’re flying for work or leisure, every element of your journey is perfect from start to finish with one of the world’s leading airlines. 

Start by unwinding in one of our Business Class lounges, designed with flawless attention to detail to create a soothing ambience. Take a refreshing shower or catch up on emails in a quiet zone where you’ll be undisturbed. When your flight is called, our professional cabin crew welcome you onboard with a smile and show you to your spacious seat. Stretch out comfortably thanks to extra legroom, or relax under ambient lighting that helps your body synchronise with your destination’s time zone.  

During the flight, indulge in one of the delectable meals on our à la carte menu, prepared daily by our award-winning chefs. Then immerse yourself in a film from our in-flight entertainment selection, or enjoy a peaceful slumber on a lie-flat bed. If you have a video meeting scheduled, take advantage of the high-speed Wi-Fi on our A380, A350, B787 and select B777 aircraft. 

Book a flight to Phuket with Qatar Airways Business and First Class and enjoy the most luxurious way to travel.
TH.HKT.touristAttractionsText:
Head straight into Phuket’s historic atmosphere and take a stroll through Phuket Old Town. Enjoy a stroll along Soi Romanee – a captivating street lined with colourful buildings and historic temples.

Phuket is abundant with incredible beaches where you can spend your days lounging on the golden sands and swimming in crystal-clear waters. Discover one or many of the beaches around the island, from the long bay of Hat Bang Thao to the stunning shores of Kata Noi Beach and the tranquil waters of Freedom Beach.

Uncover Phuket’s culture and heritage and take a day trip to the renowned Big Buddha statue, by sunrise or sunset. This spiritual site is a symbol of peace and serenity, and the location offers breathtaking views of the island below.
TH.HKT.leisureActivitiesText:
Embark on a snorkelling trip by taking a boat to Ko Phi Phi to explore the alluring beauty of Pileh Lagoon. Home to one of the world’s most thriving coral reef systems, you are almost guaranteed to swim with all kinds of marine life.

There are many more picturesque islands to venture to by boat, including James Bond Island. If visiting a famous movie location isn’t enough to draw you in, the tranquility of the island will persuade you. Known for its limestone karst towers, caves and lagoons – it’s the perfect place for spotting marine life on the coral reefs below. 

For a truly memorable encounter, visit the Phuket Elephant Nature Reserve for a day. This park prides itself on being an ethical sanctuary and provides the opportunity to educate yourself about these majestic creatures.
TH.HKT.shoppingText:
Investigate the best of Phuket’s shopping, with the bustling Phuket Walking Street Night Market in Old Town Phuket being your first stop. Immerse yourself in a kaleidoscope of colours, scents and sounds as you browse through stalls brimming with handicrafts, clothing and souvenirs. In the surrounding retail stores of Old Town, you can find unique handmade items crafted by local artisans and a wide selection of t-shirts, fabrics, batik and more.

Next, head to the Phuket Weekend Market, where vendors display an eclectic mix of goods ranging from locally produced garments and accessories to rare artworks and antiques. Whether you’re hunting for gifts or simply indulging in some affordable retail therapy, Phuket has a multifaceted shopping experience that suits any budget.
TH.HKT.destinationPageIntro: Thailand’s largest island allures you with its sun-kissed beaches, cultural richness, vibrant markets and delectable cuisine.
TH.HKT.overviewText:
Set out on an unforgettable journey to Thailand’s biggest island, Phuket. Experience the mesmerising mix of tropical beaches, sacred temples, lively markets and mouthwatering cuisine that makes Phuket a must-visit destination in Thailand.

Check out awe-inspiring temples and ornate shrines and walk along the charming streets of Old Town lined with Sino-Portuguese architecture. Or relax on one of the island’s pristine beaches as you delight your taste buds with Phuket’s multifarious fare.

With its diverse attractions, tropical weather and alluring scenery, Phuket promises an adventure at every turn.
TH.HKT.eatingImageText:
Phuket’s food scene is a vibrant tapestry of flavours. Indulge in local delights like mee sua, a comforting noodle soup and roti with banana, a sweet Thai dessert. Savour the rich spices of a massaman curry and the iconic taste of Thailand’s best-known noodle dish, Pad Thai.

While there are many restaurants and cafés to dine at, surround yourself with the buzz of street food and night markets that bring Phuket alive with atmosphere. Chillva Market and Kata Night Market are popular places to visit, with a contrasting array of dishes and snacks on offer.

For something a little different, learn the art of Thai cooking in a traditional cooking class – the perfect end to your culinary expedition in Phuket.

VN.HAN.touristAttractionsText:
Immerse yourself in the vibrant energy of Hanoi's Old Quarter. Picture the bustling streets filled with the enticing scent of street food, and the thrill of Le Duan Street, where trains pass so close to the buildings that you can almost touch them.

Step into a world of ancient legends at the One Pillar Pagoda, a unique structure perched above a lotus pond, said to be inspired by a dream. This charming pagoda offers a glimpse into Vietnam's storied past.

As the day unfolds, take a whimsical stroll around Hoan Kiem Lake. Arrive early to see locals gracefully practicing tai chi, or join the lively weekend night markets. While you're there, cross the iconic red bridge to Ngoc Son Temple, a serene sanctuary perfect for reflection.

For book lovers, wander through the classical courtyards of the Temple of Literature, where the echoes of scholars from centuries past seem to whisper through the air.
VN.HAN.leisureActivitiesText:
Explore the exhibits at the Vietnamese Women’s Museum, celebrating the remarkable contributions of Vietnamese women throughout history. You'll leave feeling inspired and awestruck.

For a touch of cultural enrichment, watch a show at the Water Puppet Theatre. Prepare to be enchanted by this ancient art form – it's quirky, entertaining, and pure Hanoi joy.

After the city's hustle and bustle, stretch your legs with a trip to Sapa. Spend a few days trekking through terraced rice fields, meeting the friendly locals, and soaking in the spectacular mountain views.

Tick off a bucket-list item with a quick getaway to the picturesque Halong Bay. Opt for a day trip or an overnight cruise through waters dotted with limestone islands. It’s truly an unforgettable experience!
VN.HAN.shoppingText:
In the Old Quarter, each street is dedicated to a specific trade, making it a shopper’s dream. The most popular streets for souvenirs are Hang Bac (Silver Street), Hang Dau (Shoe Street), and Hang Gai (Silk Street). These stores are brimming with handcrafted products, perfect for taking home.

For a more local vibe, visit Long Bien Market. This night market buzzes with activity as vendors sell produce and flowers, offering a true taste of Hanoi’s vibrant trade scene.

But the real magic of Hanoi lies in its markets. At Dong Xuan Market in the Old Quarter, you can weave through stalls packed with colourful clothing, freshly harvested produce, and bespoke souvenirs. And remember, haggling is part of the fun!
VN.HAN.destinationPageIntro: From the museums of Trang Tien and Tong Dan Street, to the eerie Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum, Hanoi is the home of heritage in Vietnam.
VN.HAN.overviewText:
Hanoi is a city that dances to its own rhythm. Imagine the hum of motorbikes weaving through narrow streets, shopkeepers calling out their wares, and the tantalising aroma of street food in the air. The city is a vibrant kaleidoscope where every corner tells a story and every turn offers an adventure.

Discover the bustling markets, indulge in the delightful culinary scene, or admire the intricate designs of local temples – Hanoi’s charm is undeniable. There’s also plenty to explore outside the city, from the mesmerising Sapa region to the picture-perfect surroundings of Halong Bay.
VN.HAN.destinationHighlightsH1: Hanoi: A mesmerising tapestry of delights
VN.HAN.eatingImageText:
Get your caffeine fix at Hoan Kiem Lake where the Vietnamese coffee is robust and the egg-yolk coffee – a delightful blend of egg yolks and sugar – is practically a dessert.

The sizzle of bun cha on street grills will lure you into the Old Quarter. This dish, featuring grilled meat patties with a mountain of fresh herbs and noodles, will inspire your taste buds.

Join the locals in slurping down bowls of pho. Pho isn’t just a soup; it’s a way of life. Although it’s primarily a breakfast staple, the Vietnamese enjoy it at all times of day and night. This nourishing beef or chicken broth is filled with rice noodles, meat, and crisp herbs.

In the French Quarter, seek out banh mi stands. These baguette sandwiches are a delicious fusion of French and Vietnamese flavours – crispy bread stuffed with meats, pickled vegetables, and herbs.

ID.DPS.businessClassSummary:
Fly to Bali in Business or First Class with Qatar Airways and arrive rejuvenated and ready to explore this beautiful island. From the moment you check in, all your needs are taken care of by our world-class team, who are committed to making your experience one to remember. 

Begin your trip to Bali by relaxing in one of our elegant Business Class lounges. Here, you can escape the hustle and bustle of the airport and find your own peaceful space to unwind. Why not take a refreshing shower before sipping on a beverage or checking your emails? 

When your flight is called, it's just a few minutes' walk to your Qatar Airways aircraft. You're welcomed aboard by friendly cabin crew who are there to take care of your every need throughout the journey. Cabins are spacious and luxurious, with ergonomic seats that offer complete support and comfort. Generous legroom gives you the freedom to stretch out, while ambient lighting helps your body adjust to the local time zone.  

During your flight, indulge your love of fine cuisine with our à la carte menu, where award-winning chefs freshly prepare every dish. Then select a film from our wide variety of entertainment options or get a restful sleep on a lie-flat bed. Wherever you’re off to, you can connect to the world with high-speed in-flight Wi-Fi on our A380, A350, B787 and select B777 aircraft. 

Book a flight to Bali in Business or First Class with Qatar Airways and take to the skies in style.
ID.DPS.touristAttractionsText:
Calling all beach lovers – Bali’s coastline is studded with a lineup of the world’s most breath-taking sandy beaches, each offering a unique experience. Relax on the pristine sands of Nusa Dua, surf the waves at Canggu, or enjoy the bohemian vibes of Seminyak.

Bali is home to countless ancient temples, each showcasing the island's rich culture and heritage. Immerse yourself in the picturesque Uluwatu Temple overlooking the Indian Ocean, witness the sunset at Tanah Lot Temple perched majestically on a rock, or explore the sites of the Besakih Temple.

Nature enthusiasts will love Bali’s diverse landscapes. Hike through the picturesque rice terraces of Tegalalang or Jatiluwih, trek to the summit of Mount Batur Volcano, or marvel at the cascading Gitgit waterfalls to really enjoy the splendour of nature.
ID.DPS.leisureActivitiesText:
Bali’s extensive coastline isn’t just a sight to behold – it’s a surfer’s dream destination. From beginner-friendly breaks to legendary swells in Uluwatu and Padang Padang, there’s a perfect wave waiting for every surfer. Learn the ropes at a surf school or challenge yourself at renowned spots and feel the thrill of the waves. 

Bali’s beauty extends beyond the surface. Discover a vibrant underwater world and explore coral reefs brimming with colourful marine life. Popular scuba diving sites include Nusa Penida, Nusa Lembongan and Tulamben. Take the plunge and get ready to explore shipwrecks, underwater temples and encounter manta rays and other fascinating creatures. 

Bali is also a renowned destination for yoga and wellness retreats. Immerse yourself in a tranquil environment, practice yoga and meditation, or indulge in spa treatments and traditional massages.
ID.DPS.shoppingText:
Unleash your inner shopper in Bali. From busy street markets overflowing with handcrafted treasures to chic boutiques boasting international brands, Bali offers a one-of-a-kind shopping experience.

Visit the Ubud Art Market, Seminyak Flea Market or Sukawati Art Market for unique souvenirs, intricate wood carvings, vibrant batik fabrics and exquisite jewellery – all while immersing yourself in the island's vibrant culture. Make sure to bring your haggling skills with you.

There is also an abundance of night markets around the island, where you can find spices, teas and quirky trinkets.
ID.DPS.destinationPageIntro: Your recipe for the ultimate Bali experience: stroll the sandy beaches with crystal clear water, shop the artisanal markets, and indulge in authentic Balinese massages.
ID.DPS.overviewText:
Seeking adventure, relaxation, or a taste of local culture? Look no further than Bali – an island treasure trove overflowing with new and exciting experiences at every turn. 

From sun-drenched beaches and volcanic peaks, to ancient temples and lush rice paddies, this Indonesian jewel promises unforgettable memories. 

Let’s delve into the heart of Bali and discover what makes this iconic island Indonesia’s most popular destination.
ID.DPS.destinationHighlightsH1: Bali: An island of beauty and culture
ID.DPS.eatingImageText:
Bali's vibrant food scene caters to every palate, from bustling night markets serving diverse street food to trendy cafés with international flavours.  

Savour iconic dishes like nasi goreng, Indonesia’s national fried rice dish, or sate lilit, lemongrass-infused meat skewers. Another must-try is bebek betutu, which is slow-cooked duck infused with fragrant spices. Don't miss the refreshing rujak bulung, a salad made with young coconut leaves and a sweet-spicy dressing.

For seafood lovers, beachfront restaurants offer grilled fish, lobster and more. For a truly local experience, venture into warungs for authentic favourites like mie goreng, gado-gado and satay. No matter your taste, Bali’s food scene has something waiting for you.

PH.CEB.touristAttractionsText:
Fort San Pedro is a centuries-old fortress standing proudly along the waterfront. Step back into the Spanish colonial era as you explore its stone walls and gardens. 

A stroll around the Sirao Flower Garden is a perfect chance to relax. Known as the ‘Little Amsterdam’ of Cebu, it’s renowned for its brightly-coloured flower beds.

A visit to Kawasan Falls is a chance to escape the hustle and bustle of the city and sit next to one of the island’s most beautiful natural wonders. The waterfall is famous for its turquoise water and serene ambience. 

Visit Museo Sugbo, where even the building has its own tale to tell. Built from coral stone, it was the island’s jail for over 130 years. The museum is filled with well-preserved artefacts that take you on a journey through the island’s history.
PH.CEB.leisureActivitiesText:
Explore the other nearby islands – each island has its own charm. Nature lovers will relish spending time on Olango Island, a sanctuary for migratory birds, as the shores are idyllic for bird watching. For divers, Moalboal town is the gateway to an underwater world. Witness the great sardine run, or swim alongside graceful turtles in the sparkling waters.

Adrenaline seekers can head to Kawasan Falls for an unforgettable canyoneering encounter. Imagine leaping off cliffs, sliding down waterfalls, and swimming through streams amidst jungle landscapes. Or hike up Osmeña Peak, the highest point in Cebu – for stunning vistas of the island’s jagged cliffs and endless horizons.
PH.CEB.shoppingText:
Embark on a shopping day within the city’s many markets. Taboan Public Market is a bustling hub famous for its dried mangoes, one of Cebu’s beloved exports. For a more traditional vibe, stroll through the Carcar Market, where Cebuano craftsmanship comes alive. From handwoven baskets to intricately designed jewellery, each piece exemplifies the island’s rich heritage.

As the sun sets, the Colon Night Market transforms Cebu’s oldest street into a lively bazaar. Here you can find everything from clothing to quirky trinkets. Look for Cebuano guitars, a popular souvenir from Cebu that are handcrafted by local artisans.
PH.CEB.destinationPageIntro: The Philippines island of Cebu is abundant with beaches, diving spots, historical landmarks and local delicacies to enjoy.
PH.CEB.overviewText:
Cebu is a hub of relaxation and blissful scenes. Step off the plane and feel the warmth of the island breeze as you’re whisked into a land of pristine beaches, lush mountains, and intriguing city streets. Wander through colourful markets where the scent of grilled seafood mingles with tropical fruits. Go scuba diving in some of the world’s best diving locations. Discover hidden gems tucked in quiet corners, from charming mountain trails to street stalls offering handcrafted treasures.

Whether you are seeking thrilling adventures, soaking in the island’s natural beauty, or mingling with friendly locals who greet you with warm smiles, Cebu promises a holiday like no other.
PH.CEB.eatingImageText:
Larsian BBQ is the first culinary stop you should make in Cebu. These market-style stalls offer an open-air feast of smoky barbecue. Indulge in dampa-style dining where you can choose your fresh seafood or meat, and watch as it is grilled or cooked to perfection.

Another Cebuano dish to try is larang – a deliciously savoury fish stew simmered with local herbs and spices. For a hearty meal, tuck in to pochero, Cebu’s take on beef stew, slow-cooked with vegetables in a rich broth. If you’re feeling up for it, don’t miss tasting kinilaw – a refreshing dish of fresh fish marinated in vinegar, with a zing of onions, ginger and chilli.

Craving a sweet treat? Snack on pintos, a local delicacy made of corn wrapped in husk – ideal for on the go.

When your flight is called, our professional cabin crew give you a warm welcome as you board our modern aircraft.  

Settle into your ergonomically designed seat with plenty of legroom, and connect to the super-fast Wi-Fi. It’s available on our A380, A350, B787 and select B777 aircraft, so that you can join that important video call with no interruptions. Then choose a mouth-watering meal from our à la carte menu, followed by a film or TV show from our in-flight entertainment options. To get some rest, relax on a lie-flat bed while soft ambient lighting gently acclimatises you to your destination's time zone. 

Fly to Hong Kong with Qatar Airways in Business or First Class to indulge in unparalleled luxury above the clouds.
HK.HKG.touristAttractionsText:
Lace up your boots and get ready for a scenic hike through the lush rolling hills of Tai Lam Country Park. Once ancient village paths, these trails now lead you past peaceful temples, rugged rock formations and gentle streams winding their way into the Tai Lam Chung Reservoir – also known as Thousand Island Lake. Visiting during the winter months? Don’t miss the real showstopper, nestled within the park – Sweet Gum Woods starts bursting with a breathtaking display of fiery red and golden yellows as the temperature drops.

If you are chasing views, ride the Hong Kong Observation Wheel at Central Harbourfront. The Sky100 Hong Kong Observation Deck is also a must-see, offering a 360-degree view of the city from the 100th floor.

Stroll down the Avenue of Stars, Hong Kong’s own Hollywood Walk of Fame. This iconic promenade celebrates the city’s cinematic heritage, showcasing Hong Kong’s biggest entertainment stars via handprints and statues.
HK.HKG.leisureActivitiesText:
If you’re travelling with family, the Hong Kong Space Museum is an entertaining activity for adults and children alike, with interactive exhibits and a state-of-the-art planetarium. Additionally, visit the world-renowned theme park for an enchant, one-of-a-kind experience.

Nature enthusiasts can find solace in the Hong Kong Wetland Park just an hour outside of the city, and abundant with serene landscapes and diverse wildlife. Ride the Ngong Ping 360 cable car for a breathtaking view of the city. It takes you up to Ngong Ping Village, where you can uncover other cultural landmarks.

Make sure to ascend Hong Kong Island's Victoria Peak for some spectacular views of the city, skyline, harbour and lush surroundings. You can choose to hike up the mountain or take the bus or tram.
HK.HKG.businessClassTitle: Business Class flights to Hong Kong
HK.HKG.shoppingText:
From traditional markets to luxurious malls, Hong Kong has it all. Explore Ko Shing Street or ‘Medicine Street’, filled with stores that feature herbs and remedies steeped in centuries-old traditions and provide a look at holistic health practices.

Themed markets are abundant in Hong Kong, including Flower Market, Goldfish Market, Sneakers Street, Jade Market and Toy Street. Don’t miss the Ladies’ Market in Mong Kok, a busy bazaar of clothing, accessories and souvenirs. Temple Street Night Market is another must-visit, especially for souvenirs and handcrafted trinkets.

No trip to Hong Kong is complete without a visit to the vibrant shopping centre and tourist spot – Times Square. It’s the ultimate shopping landmark with more than 230 world-renowned brands on 16 floors. Harbour City is another one-stop shopping haven with a range of dining, entertainment and sightseeing options.
HK.HKG.touristAttractionsTabHeading: Things to do in Hong Kong
HK.HKG.destinationPageIntro: Whether it’s the mountain summits and tranquil parks of Hong Kong Island or Kowloon’s museums and galleries, you will never be bored in Hong Kong.
HK.HKG.overviewText: Travel to Hong Kong to explore a city known across the world for its dynamic energy. This vibrant metropolis has an incredible culinary scene, unparalleled shopping spots, majestic natural attractions, and inspirational arts and cultural heritage. The city has reasonable weather all year round, making it the perfect destination for various activities. Embark on an adventure to Hong Kong’s mountainous region, admire historical landmarks and immerse yourself in the energetic atmosphere of the city’s markets. Experience the rhythm of Hong Kong and discover a city that never ceases to excite.
HK.HKG.eatingImageText:
Hong Kong’s culinary scene is diverse with cuisines to try and dining precincts to explore. Begin your gastronomic journey in Soho, where chic restaurants offer both international and local cuisines.

Venture to Temple Street, a bustling night market dotted with an array of street food. Sample local delights such as curry fish balls, roasted sweet potatoes and roasted chestnuts.

Kowloon City is renowned for its authentic Thai food and is home to many hidden hole-in-the-wall eateries. While in Tsim Sha Tsui, you can scout luxury dining options, as well as street vendors serving siu mai – Chinese steamed dumplings, and cheung fun – steamed rice noodle rolls.

Explore popular cha chaan tengs or ‘tea restaurants’ and indulge in some signature specialties like milk tea, egg tarts and pineapple buns.

CN.CAN.touristAttractionsText:
Step back in time at the Museum of the Mausoleum of the Nanyue King. Discover treasures and relics from one of the largest and best-preserved stone tombs from the Han Dynasty in the Lingnan region. Whether you love history or just want to explore ancient dynasties, it’s a must-visit. 

Head to the Chen Clan Ancestral Hall. Brimming with intricate carvings, it’s a sight to behold. Plus, discover the deep history and stories of this ancient city. For even more beautiful architecture, visit the Flower Pagoda – one of the oldest landmarks in the city. 

The Sun Yat-sen Memorial Hall is another masterpiece, dedicated to the great revolutionary, with its grand dome and elegant gardens. For a slice of serenity in Guangzhou, venture to Shamian Island – a riverside town with charming, colonial buildings and tree-lined streets.
CN.CAN.leisureActivitiesText:
Also known as the City of Flowers, Guangzhou’s Flower City Square is a fitting place to begin your sightseeing. It’s a burst of colour and art, where tall skyscrapers cut across lush, green spaces. Ascend to the top of Canton Tower for impressive views of the cityscape below.

Encounter serenity in Yuexiu Park for a picnic or a leisurely stroll. Look for the Five Rams Statue – legend has it these mystical creatures saved the city from famine.

Feeling wild? Make your way to the Chimelong Safari Park, for thrilling close encounters with lions, pandas, and even koalas. It’s the perfect family activity. End your day with a Pearl River night cruise for a breathtaking perspective of Guangzhou’s skyline by night.
CN.CAN.shoppingText:
Enjoy a shopping spree at Beijing Road. Stroll past age-old stone pavements as you browse international brands, boutiques and glittering jewellery stores. Its modern and exciting atmosphere makes for a fun shopping experience.

For a more eclectic and local vibe, stroll along Shangxiajiu Pedestrian Street. Sample local snacks while enjoying some clothes shopping. Whether you’re looking for an edgy jumper or something minimal and chic, this lively street is abundant with Japanese and Korean-inspired clothing stores.

For those seeking the ultimate retail therapy, Guangzhou’s malls will dazzle you. Towering high above the city, these hubs house high-end fashion and designer brands with architecture that’s out of this world. It’s worth a visit even if you don’t plan to buy anything in particular.
CN.CAN.destinationPageIntro: Venture to the legendary city of Guangzhou in Southern China. Discover ancient traditions, indulge in delicious Cantonese snacks and enjoy the colourful surrounds.
CN.CAN.overviewText:
Guangzhou, the heart of Southern China, is a city where legends meet modern wonders. Known amongst locals as the City of Five Rams, this bustling metropolis’ origin story is steeped in an enchanting tale of five celestial rams that brought prosperity and eternal abundance. The legend lives on, as Guangzhou continues to charm all who holiday there.

It’s a city where bursts of colourful flowers adorn every corner, as beauty seems to grow effortlessly in its parks and avenues. Wander through Guangzhou’s dynamic streets, learn old-world traditions, admire cutting-edge architecture and be swept up in its delicious culinary scene.
CN.CAN.destinationHighlightsH1: Guangzhou: A dynamic city in Southern China
CN.CAN.eatingImageText:
Embark on a food adventure at Shangxiajiu Pedestrian Street, where the air is thick with the aroma of sizzling Cantonese snacks. Sample some crispy spring rolls, rice noodle rolls, fluffy egg tarts and steaming hot buns.

Explore Qingping Market for an experience like no other. It’s traditional for Cantonese households to make soup each day, and this is where you’ll find the freshest produce. Discover a unique ingredient or two, from earthy herbs and plump mushrooms to exotic seafood. 

For something slow-paced, head to an authentic tea house where the delicate scent of jasmine will entice you. One of the best ways to enjoy tea is with dim sums. The perfect brunch meal, these freshly-made dumplings with all kinds of fillings are served alongside fragrant tea in a relaxed setting.

JP.KIX.touristAttractionsText:
Osaka Castle is a must-visit when you’re in the city. A proud symbol of resilience, the castle was rebuilt in 1931 and is now surrounded by sprawling gardens and ancient moats. Walk through its halls and step back into Japan’s feudal era. Discover its significance in the unification of Japan during the shogunate era.

Explore Sumiyoshi Taisha’s distinctive architecture, found nowhere else in Japan. Take a stroll across the Sorihashi Bridge and admire the tranquility of your surroundings. Alternatively, visit Shitennō-ji, one of Japan’s oldest buildings, dating back to the 6th century. Don’t miss out on the Gokuraku-jodo Garden, where you can roam on the pebble-covered courtyard to soak in the reverent atmosphere.

For a truly awe-inspiring sight, head to the Mozu Tombs, a UNESCO World Heritage site, and one of Japan’s largest ancient burial grounds. These massive mounds are marvels of engineering.
JP.KIX.leisureActivitiesText:
Step back in time at the Osaka Museum of History, where immersive exhibits whisk you through the city’s journey. From its transformative past to the bustling metropolis of today. Head to the upper floors where you can catch panoramic views of Osaka Castle.

For a day of thrills for the whole family, visit the aquarium or theme park for ultimate play. In the summer, Osaka comes alive with Tenjin Matsuri, one of Japan’s oldest festivals. Join the locals as they don traditional yukata and kimono. After sunset, watch the fireworks and elaborately decorated boats light up the river.

For nature lovers, Minoo Park is a natural sanctuary just a short trip from the city. Follow winding trails through dense forest foliage leading to a magnificent waterfall, surrounded by greenery or autumn hues depending on when you visit.
JP.KIX.shoppingText:
For Osaka’s largest shopping districts, head to Umeda and Namba. Discover towering malls full of luxury brands, high-end fashion and stylish boutiques, as well as underground shopping arcades filled with unique gems, from Japanese accessories to chic clothing. Namba is also where all the tech stores are located, if you’re looking for the latest technology or gadget.

Head south to Shinsaibashi for trendy streetwear and vintage treasures. Dotted with independent stores, this is the area for quirky finds. From manga and anime memorabilia, to local fashion and custom-made gadgets, you won’t want to miss this. To end your shopping trip, remember to snap a photo with the iconic neon lights along the Dotonbori River by night.
JP.KIX.destinationPageIntro: From Japan’s rich feudal past to exciting attractions, neon lights and tantalising street food, Osaka is a destination for the senses.
JP.KIX.overviewText:
Osaka is a Japanese city that is as lively as its neon lights. Known as Japan’s kitchen, this dynamic metropolis is renowned for its bold flavours, quirky neighbourhoods and rich history. Nestled along the country’s western coast, Osaka has it all. Roam through its busy city streets or discover the serene beauty of ancient sites and parks.

Explore iconic landmarks that symbolise Japan’s feudal past or lose yourself in modern districts that thrive on retail. Devour street food in Kita, soak in the electrifying atmosphere of Dotonbori, enjoy the thrill at a theme park or experience a unique summer festival during Tenjin Matsuri. Osaka is a treasure trove of places to eat and shop, sprinkled with a touch of adventure.
JP.KIX.eatingImageText:
Make your way to Shinsekai, a district known for kushikatsu, skewers of meat, seafood and vegetables coated in a batter and deep-fried. Alternatively, the Kita, Minami and Tennoji districts are also hubs for street food and restaurants, whether you’re looking for Japanese curry or bowls of ramen.

No trip to Japan is complete without seafood. Head to Kuromon Market, which is packed with the fresh catches of the day. If you’re craving for a light snack, have some takoyaki, octopus-filled dough balls topped with a sweet, savoury sauce and bonito flakes.

For something truly iconic to Osaka, try okonomiyaki, a savoury pancake filled with cabbage, meat and seafood, grilled to perfection. For dessert, don’t miss Rikuro’s cheesecake. A fluffy, jiggly delight that melts in your mouth.

Book a Business or First Class flight to Tokyo with Qatar Airways, and begin your Japanese adventure in unparalleled luxury.
JP.NRT.touristAttractionsText:
For panoramic views of the city that is breathtaking both day and night, visit the iconic Tokyo Tower observatory. Enjoy a different perspective of the tower from Zōjō-ji. It’s an Edo-period landmark known for traditional architecture and the Tokugawa family mausoleum. 

Make your way to the famous Shibuya crossing to experience the hustle and bustle of Tokyo. Witness thousands of pedestrians crossing simultaneously across the world’s busiest intersection. 

For a slice of slow Japanese life, Nakameguro is the place to be. Explore quaint cafés, bookstores below train tracks and hipster shopping. Crowds gather in the spring as cherry blossoms, sakura, bloom over the Meguro River, creating a tunnel of soft pink petals. Tokyo is a city that offers a symphony of experiences for the senses.
JP.NRT.leisureActivitiesText:
Discover a world of history and tranquillity at Meiji Jingū, accessible through Yoyogi Park. Dedicated to the Emperor Meiji and Empress Shoken, it is a sight to behold. Walk through its torii gates to admire stunning traditional architecture and serene gardens. 

Immerse yourself in contemporary art at one of the many museums in Roppongi, an upscale neighbourhood in central Tokyo. Explore world-class collections at the Mori Art Museum, the National Art Centre Tokyo, the Suntory Museum of Art and more. 

For a relaxing day out of the city, embark on a scenic day trip to Mount Fuji. Experience the thrill of travelling by bullet train, Shinkansen, from Tokyo Station. Views of Mount Fuji can be enjoyed by many surrounding towns, including Lake Fujikawaguchiko, Gotemba and Hakone, to name a few.
JP.NRT.shoppingText:
Discover traditional crafts, Japanese-made goods and global brands all in Tokyo. The vibrant area of Harajuku is popular for its quirky and cute shops. Explore the world of anime and electronics at Akihabara to find the latest manga, anime merchandise and technology. 

Experience the epitome of luxury in Ginza. Shop at high-end boutiques and flagship stores for the latest fashion, jewellery and Japanese sweets, wagashi. The streets of Omotesandō are lined with vintage boutiques and contemporary designer brands. Find unique pieces and hidden gems in Cat Street to add to your wardrobe. 

Don’t leave Japan without visiting a convenience store. Shop for local snacks and merchandise to bring home as souvenirs. It’s an experience so quintessentially Japanese, it can’t be missed.
JP.NRT.destinationPageIntro: Discover a futuristic city while embracing the past in Japan’s capital. Fly with us via Narita Airport to explore Tokyo’s modern architecture, ancient landmarks and more.
JP.NRT.overviewText:
Tokyo, the vibrant capital of Japan is a mesmerising blend of age-old tradition and cutting-edge modernity. While stylish skyscrapers fill its skyline, lush gardens and historical landmarks offer a balance of tranquility. 

From the bustling Shibuya Crossing to the serenity of Meiji Jingū and the quirky vibes of Harajuku, every day is an adventure. Indulge in fresh, high-quality ingredients incorporated into Japanese and international cuisine. Explore the eclectic energy of Akihabara and charm of Roppongi. 

Whether you enjoy discovering the rich history of ancient Edo or wanting to experience life as a local, Tokyo is a destination for the senses. There’s truly something special for every traveller. Fly with us to Tokyo via Narita Airport and unlock a holiday of a lifetime.
JP.NRT.destinationHighlightsH1: Tokyo: A discovery of modern Japan
JP.NRT.eatingImageText:
Tokyo's diverse culinary landscape is unparalleled. The freshest seafood in the city can be found at the Toyosu Fish Market. Score coveted spots to witness the tuna auction but be prepared to be there before dawn. If you prefer sleeping in, you can still visit one of the many seafood restaurants there. 

For an elevated sushi experience, enjoy a chef-curated meal of seasonal ingredients at an omakase restaurant. Then, savour Japan’s world-famous beef, wagyu, best enjoyed teppanyaki style where A5 grade steaks are grilled to perfection or cooked in a rich soy sauce, sukiyaki style. 

Explore the streets of Nakameguro for trendy restaurants and quaint cafés. It’s the perfect location for relaxing brunch, handcrafted coffee, fruit sandwiches or local eats overlooking the Meguro River.

KZ.ALA.touristAttractionsText:
Ride the cable car to get your bearings and take in the sweeping views from atop Kok Tobe, the highest point in this city surrounded by mountains. It feels like you’re in a postcard. Down below in the city lies the Golden Quarter – Almaty’s most prestigious district lined with cafés, upscale boutiques and grand buildings. Spend a day or two exploring the area for a taste of the luxurious Almaty lifestyle. A short walk away stands the Ascension Cathedral, a pastel marvel built entirely of wood and with intricate frescoes.

While in the city, don’t miss the towering Golden Man Independence Monument in Republic Square – a warrior from ancient Kazakhstan, symbolising the nation’s resilience and heritage. A stroll to the Square of Kazakhstan’s national poet brings you to the Republic Palace, where cultural events and open-air performances animate the summer months.
KZ.ALA.leisureActivitiesText:
Visit the Central Museum, as it traces Kazakhstan’s roots back to the Silk Road. The Almaty City Museum and the Kasteyev Museum of Arts are also worth a visit, with collections that span the nation’s cultural evolution.

In the evening, let the Abey Opera and Ballet Theatre mesmerise you with performances that honour the rich heritage of Kazakh music and storytelling. For an authentic folk experience, listen to local musicians play soulful tunes of the two-stringed dombra.

Almaty’s natural beauty is right on the city’s doorstep and is well worth the adventure. Head to the Shymbulak ski resort for some winter fun. In summer, it’s perfect for mountain biking amongst its lush trails. The Kolsai and Kaindy Lakes offer the perfect backdrop of nature – ideal for scenic picnics framed by the mountains.
KZ.ALA.shoppingText:
There are plenty of luxury boutiques that cater to high-end shoppers in Almaty, particularly around the Golden Quarter. A visit to Esentai Mall is a must – it’s known for being one of the best malls in the city, with plenty of luxury brands on offer. If you’re looking for some traditional treasures, head to Arbat shopping street, where artists sell paintings and street vendors showcase handcrafted works. 

Keep an eye out for the beautifully crafted Kazakh carpets around the city, as well as kalpak hats (called ‘Takiya’), that mirror the peaks of the surrounding mountains. More keepsakes include handmade felted items. Often made in earthy tones and adorned with folk motifs, they’ll add a touch of Kazakhstan to your home.
KZ.ALA.destinationPageIntro: From historical architecture and a lively café culture, to spectacular mountain peaks, there is something for everyone in Almaty.
KZ.ALA.overviewText:
Nestled against the dramatic backdrop of the Tian Shan mountains, Almaty is Kazakhstan’s cultural heart. Once the nation’s capital, this lively metropolis is where traditional yurt-studded landscapes meet cosmopolitan streets filled with cafés, museums, and iconic attractions.

Browse the city’s streets for a glimpse of Soviet-era architecture, take in the views from atop the city’s hills, or indulge in interesting local cuisine. Hikers venture to Almaty’s mountains for spectacular trails and adventures, and there is good reason why.

Whether you’re drawn by the allure of its colourful bazaars or the serenity of its nearby lakes and peaks, Almaty is a city that enchants every traveller who visits.
KZ.ALA.eatingImageText:
Explore the Green Bazaar, a foodie paradise where rows of stalls brim with Kazakh culinary wonders. Then, make your way down Zhibek Zholy Street, abundant with local eateries and cafés. The food in Kazakhstan offers plenty of unique dishes that reflect the country’s rich culture. Sample kazy, delicately smoked horsemeat with an intense flavour. Or, grab handfuls of freshly roasted nuts and dried fruits, perfect for a sweet snack.

The highlight of Kazakh cuisine is beshbarmak, the national dish and a hearty feast. Thin slices of horse meat rest on wide pasta noodles, all steeped in a meaty broth. Then there’s baursak, golden doughy balls, fried until puffy and served with kurt – tangy, dried yoghurt balls. For the bold, slurp a cup of kumis, a drink made from fermented mare’s milk – it’s a Kazakh staple.
