NZ.AKL.touristAttractionsText:
Start your adventure by ascending the city’s most iconic landmark, the Sky Tower. If you’re up for the thrill, challenge yourself to walk the edge or skydive from 192 metres high. If you’d prefer to stay on the ground, make your way to Waitemata Harbour to see the sea gateway to Auckland. Cross the Auckland Harbour Bridge for mesmerising views, and perhaps a daring bungee jump.

Delve into Auckland’s rich history and vibrant art scene at its many museums. The Auckland War Memorial Museum, the Auckland Art Gallery Toi o Tåmaki and the Auckland Museum all offer unique insights into the city’s past and creative spirit. Stroll through the picturesque Albert Park, a green oasis in the heart of the city, and make your way to One Tree Hill for panoramic views of the city and its treasured historic monuments.
NZ.AKL.leisureActivitiesText:
While Auckland’s city centre is bustling with things to do, the surrounding areas are equally captivating. Set sail across the Hauraki Gulf to explore Auckland’s enchanting islands. Whale safaris are a popular attraction, with orcas spotted from December to March and humpbacks from June to July.

Hop on a ferry to Waiheke Island to savour exquisite vineyards and bespoke dining experiences. Kayak to Rangitoto Island and hike its volcanic summit for breathtaking views. A trip to Great Barrier Island is a must for spectacular hiking trails and prime fishing spots.

West Auckland’s beaches, Piha or Muriwai are perfect for a day trip – just an hour outside of the city. These beaches are renowned for their rugged beauty, black sand and great surfing conditions.
NZ.AKL.shoppingText:
Begin your shopping adventure on Queen Street, the bustling heart of Auckland’s retail district. This trendy strip is lined with fashion and lifestyle boutiques, offering everything from international brands to unique local stores. For a quirky mix of vintage shops and independent boutiques, head to Karangahape Road. If you’re looking for garments designed and created in New Zealand, then head over to Ponsonby Road to explore some top-fashion talent.

Take home a piece of New Zealand’s natural heritage with jade jewellery and luxurious merino wool products. Don’t forget to pick up some manuka honey too, cherished for its numerous health benefits.
NZ.AKL.destinationPageIntro: Boat through the Hauraki Gulf, soar up the Sky Tower, or travel to the famous Hobbiton. Auckland is a place where you can experience adventure, culture and nature all in one city.
NZ.AKL.overviewText:
Auckland, a city where adventure, culture and nature converge, offers something for everyone – from adrenaline chasers to culture enthusiasts and nature lovers. Experience the rush of bungee jumping, explore volcanic landscapes on foot, or simply immerse yourself in the authentic New Zealander lifestyle. Auckland will leave you with memories that’ll last a lifetime.

A nature’s playground, Auckland offers endless opportunities to connect with the natural world. Its diverse population enriches the city with a vibrant array of cultural experiences, from world-class museums and art galleries to international dining. In Auckland, you can enjoy the dynamic energy of city life while being surrounded by breathtaking landscapes.
NZ.AKL.eatingImageText:
SkyCity offers a dynamic dining experience with a collection of premium restaurants. Viaduct Harbour is the place to go for fresh seafood – enjoy oysters, whitebait, and classic fish and chips while overlooking the waterfront.

Savour the finest local produce at the Matakana Farmers Market. Just a 45-minute drive from the city, it’s the perfect spot to grab organic produce, artisanal cheeses, and much more.

Auckland is also renowned for its diverse cuisine. Stroll down Dominion Road to indulge in authentic Asian food, from Thai curries to Japanese sushi.

Tantalise your taste buds with New Zealand’s national dish, hangi – a traditional cooking method that uses heated rocks buried in a pit oven to cook meat, vegetables and sometimes seafood.

Fly to Melbourne Business or First Class with Qatar Airways and enjoy international travel in style.
AU.MEL.touristAttractionsText:
Immerse yourself in the true essence of Melbourne city life – stroll down Flinders and Hosier Lane to uncover impressive street art, unique installations and trendy cafés. 

For a dose of culture, visit the National Gallery of Victoria, Australia’s oldest art museum. Develop an understanding of Australia’s significant indigenous history with the Aboriginal Heritage Walk at the Royal Botanical Gardens and the Bunjilaka Aboriginal Cultural Centre.

If you are travelling with children, a trip to Melbourne Zoo is a must. They’ll love getting up close to the kangaroos and koalas – Australian icons of the animal kingdom. Then, enjoy some family fun and activities, while admiring the city from a bird’s eye view at Melbourne Skydeck.
AU.MEL.leisureActivitiesText:
For a unique perspective of Melbourne, board a self-skippered boat and cruise down the Yarra River. Gaze at the sights of Melbourne’s skyline from the water – including the Royal Exhibition Building and Federation Square.

Enjoy a day at one of Melbourne’s famous golden beaches. Head to St. Kilda or Brighton Beach by train to bask in the sun, stroll down palm-lined boardwalks and sip some coffee at beachside cafés.

For a day out of the city, embark on the ultimate road trip along the Great Ocean Road. Prepare to be dazzled by breathtaking views of the coastline and spot the majestic Twelve Apostles – Australia’s iconic limestone rock formations.

If the rainforest is on your bucket list, climb aboard the Puffing Billy steam train to roam through the picturesque Dandenong Ranges.
AU.MEL.shoppingText:
Melbourne’s shopping scene is a vibrant mix of bustling markets and independent boutiques.

Hunt for souvenirs and gourmet treats at the Queen Victoria Market and the stalls of Prahran Market. Don’t miss the weekend craft market at Federation Square – explore this cultural hub while shopping for artisanal handicrafts.

Bourke Street is renowned for local brands and handmade goods. Scout Chapel Street’s boutiques to find high-end fashion pieces and vintage treasures.
AU.MEL.destinationPageIntro: Get your fill of sports at Melbourne Cricket Ground, relax on stunning Brighton Beach, and admire the laneway street art. There's something for everyone in lively Melbourne.
AU.MEL.overviewText:
Melbourne is the dynamic cultural capital of Australia, where hidden gems await. Discover every corner of its famous ‘laneways’, or pedestrian-friendly alleys. With its iconic street art, world-class museums, and vibrant food scene – Melbourne is a playground for the curious and the adventurous.

Immerse yourself in the spirit of the city and explore its art-adorned lanes while enjoying artisan coffee. Head a few kilometres outside city limits to unwind at one of the tropical beaches or venture to the Australian rainforest for a peaceful hike.

Book flights to Melbourne and fall in love with one of Australia’s most diverse cities.
AU.MEL.destinationHighlightsH1: Melbourne: The cultural capital of Australia
AU.MEL.eatingImageText:
Melbourne is a melting pot of culinary delights, with each neighbourhood offering distinctly unique dining experiences.

Revel in modern eateries in Fitzroy or sample multifarious cultural cuisines in Richmond. If you’re looking for a cosmopolitan vibe, dine in Prahran.

For an idyllic Australian morning snack, savour a delicious pastry and perfectly brewed coffee in one of Melbourne’s cafés. Did you know that avocado toast originated in Australia? Grab yourself this perfectly Instagram-worthy brunch staple.

AU.BNE.touristAttractionsText:
No matter where you are in Brisbane, you’re likely to catch a glimpse of the Story Bridge, which connects the north to the south. Take a climbing tour to the top at sunset for jaw-dropping views.

Spend an afternoon soaking up the sun at South Bank, a man-made beach area set on the Brisbane River. The lush parklands and swimming lagoon make it an idyllic location for a taste of Brisbane’s relaxed lifestyle.

Close by, there are numerous museums to visit such as the Gallery of Modern Art and the Queensland Museum. Both have interactive spaces and exhibits, providing a great day out for the whole family.

Experience Australia’s unique fauna and flora by taking a boat from South Bank to Lone Pine Koala Sanctuary. Here you can see koalas, kangaroos and a number of other Australian wildlife.
AU.BNE.leisureActivitiesText:
Board a CityCat ferry down the Brisbane River over to New Farm Park. Enjoy the view from the water and explore one of Brisbane’s most popular parklands when you arrive. Not only is it the perfect location for picnics and walks, it’s also an entertainment hub with the nearby Brisbane Powerhouse hosting cultural events and weekend markets.

Explore Mount Coot-tha Reserve and enjoy panoramic views of the city from the top. This natural area also has walking trails, the Brisbane Botanic Gardens and a Planetarium.

Expand your adventure with a day trip to the beach on the Sunshine or Gold Coast, easily accessible by car or train. The Sunshine Coast is known for its divine beaches, while the Gold Coast has a reputable surf culture.

On the way to the Sunshine Coast, stop at Australia Zoo. Founded by the legendary Steve Irwin, this world-renowned zoo is a must-visit.
AU.BNE.shoppingText:
Australia’s shopping scene is gaining global attention, with many local designers and boutiques creating unique pieces that attract the international market.

Begin your retail journey on Queen Street, which has retail stores, luxury boutiques and souvenir shops. Take a walk down James Street, a premier lifestyle precinct that’s full of designer boutiques, artisanal stores and trendy eateries.

In the city suburb of Paddington, you can find a blend of shopping and history. Browse small boutiques and antique stores that are often within beautifully preserved Queenslander homes. They offer a unique insight into Brisbane’s suburban old-world charm.

Don’t miss the city’s markets for locally crafted and artisanal goods, including the Collective Markets and the West End Markets.
AU.BNE.destinationPageIntro: From koala sanctuaries and city beaches, to lush parklands and bespoke shopping – there's plenty to see and do in sunny Brisbane.
AU.BNE.overviewText:
Australia’s third-largest city and the capital of Queensland, Brisbane offers a welcoming and laid-back atmosphere with a plethora of opportunities from city to coast.

Brisbane is abundant with things to do in and around the city centre, with spectacular beaches and rainforest treks just a short trip away. The diversity of Brisbane’s attractions is renowned, and its warm climate provides a pleasant stay any time of the year. Brisbane is more than just a destination. It’s a blend of experiences that captivate and inspire. Explore, discover and create memories in this breathtaking Australian city.
AU.BNE.eatingImageText:
Brisbane is a delight for food enthusiasts with its vibrant café culture, multicultural cuisine and high-quality eateries.

Go to Howard Smith Wharves – a riverside precinct offering impressive views of the Story Bridge, packed with both upscale and casual establishments.

Teneriffe is an upscale suburb known for its chic cafés and boutique restaurants. Located near New Farm Park, it’s an ideal spot for a leisurely brunch after a walk around the park. West End is also known for having an eclectic mix of cafés and restaurants.

Venture to Eat Street Northshore – a bustling night market featuring an array of global cuisines and entertainment. Various city suburbs also host farmers markets on the weekend – try the Jan Powers Farmers Market and the Collective Markets.

AU.PER.businessClassSummary:
Fly to Perth in Business or First Class with Qatar Airways and reach Australia’s thriving west coast in style. From the moment you arrive at the airport, every element of your journey is designed to make travelling effortless. Enjoy fast check-in at a dedicated counter, so you can spend more time unwinding in one of our Business Class lounges. Freshen up with a shower, nibble on a light snack, or use one of the private workstations to check your emails.

Once on board, attentive cabin crew welcome you to your spacious seat. With generous legroom and an ergonomic design, you can relax in comfort while ambient lighting helps you adapt to your destination’s time zone. Stay connected with high-speed Wi-Fi on our A380, A350, B787 and select B777 aircraft, or explore thousands of entertainment options.  

Then savour a meal from our à la carte menu, prepared by our award-winning chefs, and experience premium service as you dine. When it’s time to rest, recline in a lie-flat bed to ensure a soothing sleep. With sophisticated personal care kits, you’ll feel refreshed and ready to explore the wonders of your destination, from its flourishing arts scene to its pristine beaches. 

Book a Business or First Class flight to Perth with Qatar Airways and experience unparalleled luxury.
AU.PER.touristAttractionsText:
Make your way to Kings Park and Botanic Garden, one of the largest inner-city parks in the world. Stroll through greenery and delight in panoramic views of the city’s skyline. You can even explore the parkland’s Aboriginal history on a guided tour.

For a deeper understanding of the region’s Aboriginal history, visit the WA Museum Boola Bardip and city monument, Yagan Square, traditionally an important meeting place for Indigenous people. Stop by the Perth Mint to discover the city’s opulent past and golden heritage or admire an impressive collection of artworks in the Art Gallery of WA. For a dazzling view of the surrounding Swan River, spend an evening basking in the lively Elizabeth Quay.
AU.PER.leisureActivitiesText:
Perth is known for its stunning beaches. Cottesloe Beach, located approximately 20 minutes from the city, is a favoured spot for swimming, snorkelling, surfing and unwinding. The closest beach to the centre of Perth is City Beach, which is also a prime location for relaxing in the sunshine and appreciating the view.

Head to Hillarys Boat Harbour, a supreme precinct for dining, shopping and more beaches. Catch a ferry for a day trip to Rottnest Island to enjoy adventurous hikes, incredible Australian scenery and the most adorable wildlife. Snap a photo with the quokka, a small macropod that’s famous for its big smile.

If you’re visiting between September and December, set off on a whale watching tour for an opportunity to witness humpback whales migrating past the state.
AU.PER.shoppingText:
There are numerous malls, outlets and boutiques in the city centre, as well as Australian souvenir shops for your gifting needs. Look for Aboriginal artwork to take home and cherish.

On the weekend, head to Market City – a market of over 300 stalls filled with fresh produce, takeaway snacks, garments, artisanal gifts and even furniture. The Perth Home Grown Market is worth a visit if you’re interested in the produce farmed within Western Australia. Baked goods, handmade gifts and homeware are some of the items you will find at this sustainable living market.

Board a train to Fremantle to explore markets and small-scale boutiques. This historic part of Perth is an idyllic place for shoppers to scout unique clothing and unique accessories.
AU.PER.destinationPageIntro: Say g’day to the sun-soaked city of Perth. Embark on one-of-a-kind experiences, relax on breathtaking beaches and embrace the cultural history of Western Australia.
AU.PER.overviewText:
Perth has an array of attractions that blend the natural, urban and historical elements this cosmopolitan city has to offer. Nestled along the Swan River, Perth boasts breathtaking beaches, lush parklands and a thriving cultural scene. This sun-soaked city offers more sunshine than any other city of Australia, providing a warm climate for most of the calendar year.

Immerse yourself in Perth’s colourful history, relish in its culinary scene and embrace the great outdoors of Western Australia. Meet friendly locals and embark on a one-of-a-kind experience. Perth is an outstanding destination for adventure, curiosity and ultimate relaxation.
AU.PER.eatingImageText:
A plethora of dining experiences await in Perth. Enjoy a fine-dining meal overlooking the Swan River, tuck into fish and chips by the beach or sip on a warm cup of coffee in an al fresco café in Fremantle. 

Perth is renowned for its fresh seafood caught on the coastline. For a taste of the city’s finest, order Western Rock lobster, Fremantle octopus and Akoya oysters. If a simple fillet of fish with chips is your preference, try a local barramundi, and dust your chips with chicken salt – the seasoning of choice in Australia.

Cuisines such as Vietnamese, Chinese and Thai are also plentiful in Perth. With its multicultural population, you can uncover the most delectable Asian dishes, from affordable dumplings to generous bowls of Vietnamese pho.

AU.ADL.touristAttractionsText:
While Adelaide is the capital of South Australia, it has a small city atmosphere, with quaint streets and hidden nooks to explore.

Start by immersing yourself in the multicultural heritage and natural history at the South Australian Museum, showcasing Australian, European, and Asian art. Then, take a guided tour of the Adelaide Gaol, for a fascinating insight into the city’s history.

The Adelaide Botanic Garden is a lovely morning activity, with a lush oasis of plant species, walking paths and landscaped gardens. If you’re visiting with the family, go to Adelaide Zoo where you can witness exotic wildlife, including giant pandas.

Sports fans shouldn’t miss the opportunity to visit the Adelaide Oval, home to cricket, the Australian Football League and other sports. You can even climb the oval’s roof.
AU.ADL.leisureActivitiesText:
Continue your city exploration at MOD, a futuristic museum where art meets science and innovation.

For a coastal escape, make your way to Glenelg Beach, just a short drive from the city. It’s a picturesque beach with a jetty, shops and restaurants. Another option for a seaside getaway further along the coast is Port Noarlunga, especially if you’re into water sports. It’s home to the iconic Port Noarlunga Aquatic Reef Reserves, a popular spot for snorkelling and diving enthusiasts. Port Noarlunga is just one of the many townships with stunning seafront sceneryalong the Fleurieu Peninsula.

A ferry trip to Kangaroo Island is a must for nature lovers. The island is pristine, abundant with rugged landscapes, unique wildlife and unspoiled beaches.

Alternatively, a scenic drive inland will take you to the charming town of Harhndorf in the Adelaide Hills. It’s Australia’s oldest surviving German settlement, where you can wander through charming streets and try German cuisine.
AU.ADL.shoppingText:
The outdoor precinct in the centre of Adelaide, Rundle Mall, is a premier shopping destination. Boasting over 700 retail stores, you’ll find international brands, local boutiques and arcades. The East End neighbourhood beckons shoppers with Australian designer stores and up-and-coming boutiques.

Adelaide is home to the nation’s oldest family-owned chocolate maker, so be sure to take some home with you. Another popular souvenir is opals. Many beautiful pieces of jewellery showcasing this local, precious gemstone.

The Adelaide Riverbank area is also a great retail space, featuring various crafts and artisanal products. For a taste of the city’s rich food scene, head to the Adelaide Central Market, one of the largest produce markets in the Southern hemisphere.
AU.ADL.destinationPageIntro: With a thriving cultural scene, exquisite dining and the most beautiful natural scenery, Adelaide will be sure to blow you away.
AU.ADL.overviewText:
Adelaide, the capital of South Australia, is a city of culture, natural allure and relaxed lifestyle. The city’s streets are idyllic for a leisurely stroll to see the sights and immerse yourself in the urban atmosphere. With festivals taking place year-round, there’s always something to marvel at in this vibrant city.

Known for its gourmet restaurants and fresh produce, your Adelaide culinary experience will be exceptional. Art and culture enthusiasts also find themselves captivated by its thriving arts scene and creative spirit.

The city is surrounded by natural beauty, providing numerous locations for adventure and wildlife discovery.

Whether you’re indulging in dining delights, exploring the arts, or enjoying outdoor activities, the city promises to be a memorable one.
AU.ADL.eatingImageText:
Adelaide is celebrated for its culinary excellence, with gourmet restaurants and contemporary cafés on every corner. Rundle Street, in Adelaide’s East End district, is known for its top-quality cafés, bakeries and restaurants. Try a freshly brewed coffee while you’re there – it’s a rite of passage in Australian culture.

North Adelaide’s O’Connell Street and Melbourne Street are hotspots for international cuisine. You’ll find everything from authentic Asian dishes to Mexican street food, Irish taverns and elegant Italian eateries. If you’re looking for more Asian flavours, Chinatown and Gouger Street are the places to go.

Next, enjoy the Adelaide catch of the day which often includes Coffin Bay oysters and king prawns.

Just a 30-minute drive from the city centre is Adelaide Hills, known for some of the best farm-to-table produce in the region. Take in the breathtaking views over mouth-watering local cuisine.

AU.CBR.touristAttractionsText:
Some of Australia’s most important museums and cultural attractions are in Canberra, including the National Gallery of Australia. Here you’ll find the largest collection of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander art on the continent. 

The city is renowned for glassmaking, and you can watch the masters at work at Canberra Glassworks. If you’ve always wanted to try your hand at glassmaking, the centre holds classes and workshops that will help unleash your creativity.

Canberra’s Lake Burley Griffin is a wonderful day out for the whole family. Here, you can sail on the lake or sit underneath a shady tree for a picnic.

A 10-minute drive takes you to Majura Pines Park, where you’ll find a plethora of treetop obstacles to enjoy including zip lines and aerial walkways. Try to spot some of the, native birds like kookaburras.
AU.CBR.leisureActivitiesText:
Hire a bicycle and cycle the classic ‘Bridge to Bridge’ around Lake Burley Griffin, a 5-kilometre trail that gives you some amazing views of the city. Along the way, stop and enjoy the lakeside galleries and grab an ice cream from one of the vendors. Make sure to hop over to Aspen Island and visit one of Canberra’s most important landmarks, the National Carillion. This tower was gifted to the Australian people and houses 57 bronze bells that are often rung to celebrate special occasions. 

Just 6 kilometres from the city centre is the National Arboretum, filled with over 44,000 rare trees. You can even take a horse ride through the forest or hop on a bus tour.

To embrace the café culture of Canberra, take a stroll around Braddon, a cool suburb filled with coffeehouses, a lively farmer’s market and plenty of boutiques to browse.
AU.CBR.shoppingText:
Love shopping? Canberra’s the city for you. For some trendy boutique shopping, Manuka is your go-to. It has everything from big brands to fashion labels exclusive to Canberra, as well as jewellery and ceramics.

Canberra’s weekend markets are filled with stalls offering artisanal crafts, deli delights, and more. The Hall Showground is home to the monthly Hall Markets, held on the first Sunday of every month. Be sure to check out Braddon, where you’ll not only find the hugely popular Lonsdale Street (popular for its boutiques and craft stores), but you can also wander the Haig Park Village Markets, hosted here every Sunday. 

Canberra is also home to many modern malls, where you can browse retail, dining and entertainment options in air-conditioned comfort.
AU.CBR.destinationPageIntro: Canberra is the sunshine capital of Australia, where history and heritage sit alongside a vibrant café culture and the natural beauty of the Bush is just a short drive away.
AU.CBR.overviewText:
Canberra is one of Australia’s gems. It feels surprisingly relaxed and laid-back for a capital city. It’s packed full of historical buildings, parks and open spaces. And there’s natural beauty just a 45-minute drive from the city centre with waterfalls and snow-capped mountains.

Canberra’s museums and galleries are crammed with internationally renowned exhibits, while the culture of the local Ngunnawal people is yours to discover.

Canberra’s free-spiritedness is celebrated in festivals and events, and the food is a gastronome’s dream. There are restaurants serving dishes from all around the world and a bustling street food scene. And for retail lovers, there’s no shortage of markets, malls, antique stores and boutiques to visit.
AU.CBR.eatingImageText:
Like any capital city, Canberra is filled with dining options. Canberra’s large Asian community makes it one of the best places in Australia to find Chinese, Thai, Vietnamese and Korean food. You’ll find some of the best Vietnamese food in the suburb of Griffith, while many of the most popular Chinese restaurants are situated in the Dickson area and Northbourne Avenue. 

Griffith is also known for its high-end dining, with everything from Turkish and classic Italian, to French cuisine on offer. For dinner with a view, head to the shores of Lake Burley Griffin in time for sunset.

If you want the best burger in Canberra, head to Wentworth Avenue, just behind Canberra Glassworks, and look out for a little red caravan with a very long queue!

Prepare for an extraordinary Business or First Class experience when flying to the Seychelles with Qatar Airways.
ZA.CPT.touristAttractionsText:
Make your way up Table Mountain on a clear day via cableway or on foot – if you’re feeling extra energetic. The scenery from the top is nothing short of spectacular, with panoramic views of the city and ocean. For a different perspective, head to Bloubergstrand to enjoy an incredible view of Table Mountain from across the bay.

Experience the best of Cape Town’s beaches at the pristine Clifton Beach, or along the lively Camps Bay strip. Or, make your way to Boulders Beach (about an hour outside the city) for a chance to see African penguins in their natural habitat.

Up for a little adventure? Take a day trip to Franschhoek and Stellenbosch to take in the picturesque vistas, and enjoy world-renowned vineyards and charming produce farms.
ZA.CPT.leisureActivitiesText:
If you are up for a hike, trek up to Lion’s Head for some breathtaking outlooks of the city and coastline. Find serenity amidst the botanical wonders of Kirstenbosch National Botanical Garden. To encounter some African wildlife, venture to Aquila Private Game Reserve for a local safari experience – it’s a great opportunity to witness the majestic Big 5 of South Africa.

Take a short ferry to Robben Island for a profound journey into history. This island is famously known as the place where Nelson Mandela was imprisoned, offering a poignant glimpse into the past.
ZA.CPT.shoppingText:
Looking for souvenirs? The Watershed at the V&A Waterfront is the perfect spot – you’ll find stalls filled with everything from authentic, traditional fabrics to handmade trinkets and more. The Old Biscuit Mill is another creative hub, where local artisans showcase their talents in fashion, art and cooking.

The Oranjezicht City Farm Market offers a delightful farm-to-table shopping experience. Pick up some fresh organic produce and gourmet treats!
ZA.CPT.touristAttractionsTabHeading: Things to do in Cape Town
ZA.CPT.destinationPageIntro: A laid-back city with dazzling scenery and within arm's reach of some of the world's most beloved wildlife, Cape Town is truly the beating heart of South Africa.
ZA.CPT.overviewText:
Nestled between the iconic Table Mountain and the meeting point of the Atlantic and Indian Ocean lies Cape Town – a city of unparalleled beauty and cultural diversity. From the famous mountainscape to the stunning beaches and nearby nature reserves, Cape Town’s natural scenery is sure to captivate.

Adding to its charm, Cape Town’s bespoke atmosphere and cosmopolitan vibe offers visitors a plethora of things to see and do. Wander through historical streets, indulge in fresh seafood on the waterfront and satisfy your inner shopping enthusiast at the bustling markets. Cape Town’s warm hospitality ensures an unforgettable experience for every traveller.
ZA.CPT.destinationHighlightsH1: Cape Town: A gem at the tip of Africa
ZA.CPT.eatingImageText:
For your first culinary stop, head to the V&A Waterfront to savour freshly caught seafood and international cuisine. Whether you choose to dine at a trendy market or an upscale waterfront café, you’ll be treated to unbeatable views of the harbour and Table Mountain.

Next, explore the vibrant Bree Street, where chic bistros and hidden gems offer a variety of gastronomic delights. Be sure to try Cape Malay curry, or the popular dish of bunny chow – a flavourful curry served in a bread loaf. Take a leisurely stroll down Kloof Street, and explore the boutiques and coffee shops while you snack on some biltong – a dried meat delicacy.

Embrace South Africa’s love for outdoor cooking with a traditional braai (barbeque) – meats are grilled to perfection and often paired with a spicy vegetable relish called chakalaka.

ZA.DUR.touristAttractionsText:
Get up close and personal with Durban’s marine wildlife. Shark adventures take you out to the blue water and introduce you to some of the world’s largest marine predators, including the Great White.

For a less adrenaline-pumping experience, take the family to uShaka Marine World, home to one of the largest aquariums in the world and a water park that younger visitors will love.

Experience the thrill of a South African football game at the Moses Mabhida stadium, built for the 2010 World Cup and seating 56,000 passionate soccer fans.

Learn more about the culture of the tribes of South Africa with a visit to Phansi Museum, where you’ll find thousands of artefacts on display. Or take a peaceful stroll and stop for a picnic in Durban Botanic Gardens, filled with rare plants and shady trees.
ZA.DUR.leisureActivitiesText:
Durban celebrates with festivals all year round, from music and dance to food and poetry. A large Indian community means that there are plenty of Hindu events including demonstrations of walking on hot coals and celebrations such as Diwali, as well as Muslim celebrations for Eid.

For a day trip with a little bit of a bite, Crocodile Creek is just half an hour from the centre of Durban. Here, you’ll find thousands of rare Nile crocodiles, alligators and other reptiles, and keepers who are passionate about conserving these incredible creatures.

Spend a day at one of South Africa’s most important racetracks and watch thoroughbred horses take on the gallops at Greyville Race Course. Or tee off on the 18-hole Zimbali Golf Course, with incredible backdrops and fiendishly tricky sand traps.
ZA.DUR.shoppingText:
Durban has a thriving retail centre, but you have to experience the huge Gateway Theatre of Shopping at least once during your visit. Reported to be the largest in the southern hemisphere, it’s also home to some great family entertainment including a skateboard park and an artificial wave centre for some surfing fun.

To dive into South Africa’s market culture, Victoria Street market is the place to go for souvenirs, while the monthly I Heart Market in People’s Park is a great spot for artisan crafts and textiles. Look out for Zulu beadwork and wickerwork, as well as fresh spices and wood carvings that capture the spirit of Africa. 

For air-conditioned comfort, the Pavilion Mall in Westville is worth a browse for branded retailing and some independent stores selling local crafts.
ZA.DUR.destinationPageIntro: From regal colonial buildings to bustling markets and waterfront restaurants, Durban has that quintessential ambience that welcomes you to South Africa with open arms.
ZA.DUR.overviewText:
Africa’s busiest port is an extraordinary mix of cultures, from the traditions of the Zulu people to influences from the UK, Netherlands and India. Its cosmopolitan nature continues, and you’ll hear a multitude of languages and traditional African dialects spoken throughout the city.

The natural wonders of this part of South Africa are there to discover, from the gentile walkways and flowerbeds of the Durban Botanical Gardens to the thousands of imposing reptiles at Crocodile Creek.

Food is a delicious fusion of classic European, Indian, and African dishes, including seafood and quirky local specialities like ‘Bunny Chow’. Shopping ranges from markets selling local handicrafts to top fashion outlets and air-conditioned malls. Durban is the perfect introduction to your South African odyssey.
ZA.DUR.eatingImageText:
With one of the largest Indian populations in the world, Durban’s cuisine is heavily influenced by Indian food, and curries are a staple throughout the city. One unique variation is ‘Bunny Chow’: a quarter of a loaf of bread hollowed out and filled with spicy curry. It’s a great on-the-go food or as a fiery lunchtime snack.

Shisa Nyama is a flavourful Zulu BBQ technique that’s usually at the heart of a social get-together with family and friends. Just about anything goes on the grill, from chicken and beef to more exotic delights such as ostrich.

If you need something cool and sweet after all those spices, a Bombay Crush is a Durban favourite. This blend of Rooh Afza syrup, milk, and basil seeds is topped with vanilla ice cream and is a favourite among the Muslim community during Ramadan.

NG.LOS.leisureActivitiesText:
Just a short drive from the city centre lies the Lekki Conservation Centre. This lush, green nature preserve is a breath of fresh air, with the longest canopy walk in Africa, suspended high above the forest floor. Capture a bird’s eye view of the stunning treetops and try to spot monkeys swinging from the branches below. The reserve is a sanctuary for wildlife, with colourful peacocks and shy crocodiles lurking in the marshes.

For a more relaxing day out, take a boat journey from the city’s waterfront, over to Tarkwa Beach. Glide across this lagoon to the soft sands of this pristine beach where you can sunbathe and indulge in freshly caught seafood from one of the beachside food stalls.
NG.LOS.shoppingText:
Immerse yourself in a tapestry of culture and inspiration at Lekki Arts and Crafts Market. Each stall tells a story, with talented artisans showcasing handcrafted canvas and leather bags, shoes, beads, woodwork and paintings. Each piece is meticulously made, with lots of character. This is the perfect place to buy your souvenirs and trinkets.

Marvel at the charming chaos of Balogun Market, Lagos Island, one of Lagos’ largest and most famous markets. Located in the heart of the city, this sprawling marketplace is a labyrinth of rainbow fabrics, sparkling jewellery and everything in between.

For a more curated shopping experience, meander through Lagos’ concept stores where local designers meet high-end fashion. Nigerian designers are at the forefront of the African fashion industry, and Lagos is the epicentre. So, if you’re a fashion-lover, make sure to visit the stylish boutiques that mix traditional Nigerian fabrics and silhouettes with modern flair.
NG.LOS.destinationPageIntro: Experience the charm of Lagos. Get acquainted with the people, the food, the creative cultural scene and experience the natural beauty of the beaches that surround this coastal city.
NG.LOS.overviewText:
In Lagos, the pulse of Africa beats strong and fast. Nigeria’s largest city and commercial capital is where the rhythm of  bustling city streets by day is matched by its lively atmosphere in the evenings. There’s always something to do in this coastal city, known for its beaches, boutiques and restaurants. It’s the perfect place for a holiday filled with fun and adventure.

Lagos is a playground of contrasts, with concept stores brimming with colourful, high-fashion pieces, nearby bustling markets filled with daily essentials. There is culture to immerse yourself in, beaches to relax on and plenty of delicious food to devour. Lagos invites you to discover its endless possibilities, where experiences are as unforgettable as they are unique.
NG.LOS.touristAttractionsText:
Don’t miss an opportunity to marvel at the thousands of pieces showcasing Nigeria’s creative ingenuity. Nike Art Foundation is a teaching institution for young performance artists and craftspeople specialising in traditional practices such as wood sculpture, beadwork, batic, adire (tie and dye) and more. Their work is then displayed across the gallery. 

Travel back in time at the National Museum. Nigeria’s rich heritage unfolds through ancient artefacts, including spectacular bronze sculptures and regal treasures that whisper stories of kingdoms of the past.

Finally, a trip to the beach is a must, and Eleko Beach is one of the most well-known. Located an hour out of town, this 60-km stretch of golden sand is an idyllic setting for unwinding in the sun.
NG.LOS.eatingImageText:
Food in Lagos reflects Nigeria’s diversity as well as its global influences. Flavours are bold and spicy to suit local palettes. 

Indulge in street food like suya – thinly sliced meat, grilled to perfection in a nutty spice blend or hail a vendor selling roasted groundnuts from the comfort of your car whilst you stop at a traffic light.

No trip to Lagos is complete without trying Abula. This dish, native to southwestern Nigeria, is as colourful as it is delicious. It’s a combination of amala, a soft, stretchy swallow made from yam flour, paired with gbegiri, a creamy soup made from black-eyed beans, ewedu – blended, seasoned jute leaves – and obe ata, a rich tomato-based meat stew.

Next, try the classic pairing of eba and okra soup. The okra is made into a stew with either meat, seafood or both. It’s served with eba, another dough-like carbohydrate made from cassava flour. This is a meal best eaten with your hands. Think of the eba as a spoon you use to scoop up the rich, velvety sauce. If you like spicy, umami flavours, you’ll love Nigerian food.

GH.ACC.touristAttractionsText:
Explore the magnificent Osu Castle, one of the Gold Coast’s most important trading posts and a key location in the history of the country. To see how the country has developed, a trip to the Kwame Nkrumah Memorial Park is essential. The museum tells you the story of the remarkable man who was Ghana’s first prime minister.

To find out about the biodiversity of the region, visit Aburi Botanical Gardens, which covers 160 acres and is about half an hour’s drive from the capital. Look out for old buildings that have been allowed to return to nature, and hooded vultures circling on the warm air currents.

Labadi Beach beckons, and is hugely popular with both locals and visitors. Here, you can go on a pony ride, or watch the street performers, acrobats and drummers, before cooling off with a paddle in the ocean.
GH.ACC.leisureActivitiesText:
If you feel like a bit of an adrenaline buzz, head to La Raceway, a go-kart circuit and entertainment centre. It’s a great destination for a family afternoon out and has an excellent child-friendly restaurant.

For the ultimate Ghanaian experience, join the heaving crowds of Makola Market. No matter what you’re looking for, you’ll find it here, and experience the excitement of an authentic market.

Go a little off the beaten track and explore Jamestown’s harbour, just down the road from the famous Jamestown lighthouse. This is where you’ll find old stone houses and hidden alleyways.

A visit to the National Museum is well worthwhile, combined with a trip to the Dubois Centre For Pan African Culture, where you can browse exhibits and find out more about this famous scholar.
GH.ACC.shoppingText:
At least one visit to Makola Market is a must, just to say you’ve been! If you prefer air-conditioned comfort when shopping, Accra Mall offers plenty of outlets, a large food court and a cinema playing the latest blockbusters.

If you want to see artisan crafts and artwork, the Centre for National Culture is a wonderfully colourful and eclectic arts and crafts market that feels a little more relaxed than Makola. Or stroll around the stalls at the Tetteh Quarshie Art Market, one of the best places to buy work from local artists and craftspeople.

For a leisurely shopping experience, Achimota Retail Centre has plenty of parking as well as lots of independent outlets selling fashion, jewellery, and electronics.
GH.ACC.destinationPageIntro: From large parks, busy markets, sandy beaches and the chance to experience the fusion of French and African culture, Accra is a charming destination with lots of personality.
GH.ACC.overviewText:
As soon as you land in Accra, you know you’re in Africa. The colours, smells and exhilarating lifestyle capture the spirit of a truly exciting city. Accra is Ghana’s capital and welcomes visitors with open arms and huge smiles. Famous for its live music and cultural complexity, it introduces you to the captivating energy of the African continent.

Accra’s an intoxicating blend of African and European cultures, and you’ll hear French spoken as often as English. The markets heave with people, while the city’s beaches remind you that Accra is also a very popular beach destination.

Discover the historic side of Ghana’s capital city with explorations of Jamestown, or dine in style on Omanye Street, where the cool sea breeze drives away the heat and dust of the day.
GH.ACC.eatingImageText:
Ghanaian food is delicious and unique, with the occasional French and even Danish influence thrown in to keep things interesting. Jollof is a spicy dish of rice, tomatoes and grilled chicken with a shrimp-pepper sauce called shito. The most common fish dishes involve tilapia, served with banku, a dumpling made from fermented corn and cassava.

If you prefer a vegan option, kontomire stew is made from the leaves of the cocoyam tuber, which tastes similar to spinach. And if you want a spicy treat on the go, look for street vendors selling kelewele, a crispy fried plantain snack.

For the trendiest restaurants, head to the suburb of Osu, where you’ll find plenty of eateries serving a wide variety of African and international food. Or visit the harbour for fresh fish caught that day.

ET.ADD.overviewTabHeading: Book your visit to Addis Ababa
ET.ADD.touristAttractionsText:
Once you’ve snapped a picture of the symbol of the city, Menelik, the Lion of Judah statue, it’s time to explore the rest of the city’s attractions. Addis Ababa has a fine selection of museums including the National Museum, with one of the most important collections of artefacts in Sub-Saharan Africa. Here you can meet ‘Lucy’, the world’s oldest hominid.

A taxi ride up to Entoto Mountain gives you some magnificent panoramic views of the capital and the surrounding lush landscape.

Embrace the culture of Abyssinian heritage with an evening of music and dance, but don’t expect to be a mere spectator, there’s a good chance you’ll be joining in with the celebrations!

Visit the splendour of Emperor Menelik II’s palace in Unity Park, including his throne room and banquet hall.
ET.ADD.leisureActivitiesText:
Coffee was discovered in Ethiopia, so taking part in a coffee ceremony is a must while you’re here. It’s a lengthy ritual, but the results are well worth the wait.

Addis Ababa is home to the Hager Fikir Theatre, the oldest in Ethiopia. A performance introduces you to the culture and music of the country and is not to be missed.

If you’re a keen golfer, the Addis Ababa Golf Club has a superb 18-hole course with some of the best backdrops in the country. The club also has an excellent restaurant after you’ve sunk that final putt on the 18th.

Horse racing is popular in Ethiopia, so a day at the Jan Meda Race Ground is an exciting diversion. The venue also holds other events including concerts.

Entoto Mountain is crisscrossed with hiking trails, with magnificent views around every corner.
ET.ADD.shoppingText:
Shopping in the city is a mix of a mix of traditional markets, modern malls, and boutiques. Merkato is reported to be the largest market in Africa where you can buy everything from spices to souvenirs, clothing and electronics, all surrounded by a bustling crowd.

If you prefer it a little less busy, Shola Market is a great alternative with handmade crafts and fresh fruit, while Chiromeda Market is famous for its authentic Ethiopian textiles. Be prepared to haggle, it’s part of the shopping experience in Addis Ababa!

The city has plenty of malls too, including Edna Mall and Dembel City Center, for a mix of stores, dining and entertainment.

Throughout the city you’ll find plenty of galleries selling work by local artists, as well as jewellery and traditional Ethiopian crafts.
ET.ADD.touristAttractionsTabHeading: Things to do in Addis Ababa
ET.ADD.destinationPageIntro: Addis Ababa, the ‘New Flower’ of Ethiopia, is surrounded by natural beauty. Warm, welcoming and friendly, it’s a delightful introduction to Africa’s unique personality.
ET.ADD.overviewText:
An enchanting city full of colour, history and wonder, Addis Ababa is a fabulous introduction to the culture and personality of Ethiopia. While the city itself is relatively new, Ethiopia is regarded as the cradle of humanity and the area around Addis Ababa has been settled for thousands of years.

Today’s metropolis is a busy, bustling city, filled with lively markets, sleek new shopping malls and retail districts, and excellent restaurants serving delicious food. It’s an affordable travel destination for adventurers who want to experience North Africa, but also works as an enjoyable city break destination for a long weekend with a difference. With museums, parks and palaces as well as mountains and hiking trails, there’s plenty to discover in Addis Ababa too.
ET.ADD.eatingImageText:
Almost every meal in Ethiopia includes the national dish of injera, a flatbread with a unique spongy texture. It’s ideal for mopping up some delicious juices from a stew such as spicy chicken Doro Wat. A popular meal is Fit-fit, which is shredded injera mixed with spices, meat and vegetables.

Don’t be surprised to see raw beef on the menu, as it’s been eaten in Ethiopia for hundreds of years. Usually served with a fiercely spicy sauce, some lime juice and of course, injera - it’s a unique dining experience.

Throughout Addis Ababa, you will also find plenty of international restaurants serving Asian, Turkish and European cuisine, as well as plenty of street vendors selling hot snacks like spicy sambusas, kolo (a bag of roasted barley or corn), and fresh fruit juices.

TZ.DAR.overviewTabHeading: Book your visit to Dar es Salaam
TZ.DAR.touristAttractionsText:
Begin your exploration at the Askari Monument, a bronze statue proudly honouring the soldiers who served in World War I. Located at the very heart of the city, it stands as one of Dar es Salaam’s most visited and significant landmarks. 

The National Museum of Dar es Salaam offers an inspiring journey through Tanzania’s past, from ancient fossils to royal regalia. Discover captivating exhibits on Swahili culture and the pre-colonial trade routes that shaped the region. For a more immersive experience, visit the Village Museum, which showcases the diverse architecture of various tribes. Wander among authentic, traditional huts and enjoy live performances that vividly narrate the country’s fascinating history.
TZ.DAR.leisureActivitiesText:
Embark on an adventure to Pugu Hills Nature Reserve, a serene escape where you can walk through ancient baobab trees, listen to the harmonious birdsong and soak in the stunning views. It’s a great spot to enjoy Tanzania’s wildlife. 

For an underwater escapade, dive into the Marine Reserve. Here, you can snorkel through vibrant coral gardens and see tropical fish swimming through the clear, turquoise waters. The coastline itself is highly recommended for its breathtaking beauty.

For a taste of local seaside life, head to Coco Beach. Weekends here burst with energy, with live music, barbecues and families picnicking along the shore. You can also take a boat ride to Mbudya Island, where palm-lined beaches offer the perfect setting for relaxing and unwinding.

Naturally, your coastal getaway wouldn’t be complete without hopping over to Zanzibar. This iconic island adds a whole new dimension to your experience with its spice markets, historic Stone Town, and pristine beaches.
TZ.DAR.shoppingText:
The Kariakoo Market is the heart of Tanzania’s trade scene, where stalls overflow with everything from fresh local produce to handcrafted goods. The market pulses with life and colour – it’s the perfect place to find unique batiks and tingatanga paintings of Tanzania’s vibrant landscapes and wildlife.

For a taste of local fashion and culture, stroll down Uhuru Street. Here, you’ll find shops full of kangas – boldly patterned fabrics frequently worn by locals. These beautiful textiles are adorned with Swahili proverbs, making them perfect to wear or to keep for home decor.

As you wander through town, make sure to check out the stalls of handicrafts, from woven baskets to Maasai beaded jewellery. Each piece is crafted with care and speaks of Tanzanian heritage.
TZ.DAR.touristAttractionsTabHeading: Things to do in Dar es Salaam
TZ.DAR.destinationPageIntro: Visit tribal homes, snorkel in crystal-clear waters and sink your teeth into juicy grilled kebabs – your experience in Dar es Salaam will be anything but bland.
TZ.DAR.overviewText:
Dar es Salaam, Tanzania’s bustling port city, is a captivating blend of African, Arab and Indian influences. This energetic metropolis pulses with life, from the azure waters of the Indian Ocean to the vibrant marketplaces and lively streets. Its laid-back atmosphere makes you feel right at home, as you stroll along the waterfront watching traditional dhow boats bobbing on the sea, hauling the freshest catch.

Venture within the city to marvel at landmarks, indulge in delectable, spiced street food and immerse yourself in the rich culture. Wander through sacred temples, haggle for treasures in the market or simply relax on one of its many pristine beaches. There’s plenty to see and do in Dar es Salaam.
TZ.DAR.socialProofQuote: Book flights to Dar es Salaam (DAR)
TZ.DAR.destinationHighlightsH1: Dar es Salaam: Swahili seaside gem
TZ.DAR.eatingImageText:
Experience the city’s vibrant culinary scene with a visit to the Dar es Salaam Fish Market. Witness the fishermen proudly hauling in their morning’s catch, ready to be cooked on the spot. Indulge in grilled fish, that’s seasoned and fire-roasted to bring out the fresh, bold flavours known to this region.

As you wander through the city streets, be sure to seek out local vendors selling mishkaki – tender, marinated beef or chicken skewers cooked over an open flame. Nearby, you’ll discover the irresistible aroma of nyama choma, a local barbecue favourite featuring slow-roasted meats that are juicy, charred and seasoned to perfection.

For a taste of the city’s rich Indian heritage, explore restaurants serving curries, freshly baked naan, and biryanis. And for an authentic street food experience, try Zanzibar mix – a chickpea soup, mixed with potatoes, crisp fritters and a tangy tamarind sauce. Don’t forget to grab some roasted maize, with zesty lime and chili for that extra kick.

RW.KGL.touristAttractionsText:
One of the grandest buildings in Kigali is the Presidential Palace, now a museum and gallery showcasing the intricate history of the country. Take a guided tour and learn why Rwanda has become one of the most forward-thinking of all the African countries.

To understand the importance of art in Rwandan culture, a visit to the Inema Arts Center is a must. As well as visual art, you’ll be able to join in art-inspired yoga classes or take in a concert of African music.

If you fancy a little pampering while you’re here, Kigali has plenty of health spas offering relaxing saunas and top-to-toe massages. If you’re a passionate golfer, Kigali Golf Club provides plenty of challenges, while football fans can experience the incredible energy of an African match at the Amahoro stadium.
RW.KGL.leisureActivitiesText:
You have to climb at least one of Rwanda’s ‘Thousand Hills’ while you’re here, and Mount Kigali is well worth the effort, with panoramic views of the city and the countryside. 

If you want to explore Mount Kigali at a more relaxed pace, a horse ride puts you right in the heart of the incredible scenery. Available for both beginner and experienced riders, you can also discover the delights of Rugende Park by horseback.

For a peaceful afternoon outside the city, fishermen can try and hook a catch at Lake Muhazi. The large lake and surrounding park are also an excellent spot for wildlife and birdwatching. 

Get some family time in: settle down with a blockbuster movie at one of the city’s multiplexes.
RW.KGL.shoppingText:
Crafts and textiles are Rwandan specialities. The best place to shop for these brightly coloured handicrafts is Kimironko Market – one of the city’s liveliest and most endearing retail experiences. 

Support the local social enterprises by shopping for souvenirs at the Nyamirambo Women’s Center. Or pick up some bespoke work from local artists at the Inema Arts Center. 

For a truly authentic African market shopping experience, the Nyabugogo Marche Market is the real deal. Expect big crowds, lots of noise, and lots of haggling.

The city centre is where you’ll find modern, air-conditioned malls and department stores, but walk around any corner and you’ll stumble cross yet another market. Things to look out for include Rwandan coffee and the local honey, which is absolutely delicious.
RW.KGL.destinationPageIntro: For eco-adventurers, Kigali is the ideal destination. This green city, surrounded by the beauty of Rwanda’s ‘Thousand Hills’ is a perfect introduction to the soul of Africa.
RW.KGL.overviewText:
Imagine a city where vibrant energy meets untamed wilderness. Often called the 'Singapore of Africa,' this city pulses with a dynamic spirit, framed by Rwanda's breathtaking tapestry of emerald forests and majestic mountains. Here, eco-tourism isn't just a buzzword – it's a way of life. Mountain gorillas thrive in protected sanctuaries, making Kigali a great starting point for safaris and the chance to see some of Africa’s greatest animals.  

Beyond its incredible landscapes, Kigali is a sleek, contemporary city centre bustling with malls, markets, and chic boutiques. Here, culinary adventures await, where European finesse meets the bold flavours of authentic African cuisine in innovative fusion dishes. And the rhythm of Rwanda never stops – vibrant music and dance festivals are around every corner throughout the year. From its dynamic city life to its awe-inspiring natural wonders, Kigali offers an unforgettable experience, a city that truly has it all.  

For eco-adventurers, Kigali is the ideal destination. This green city, surrounded by the beauty of Rwanda’s ‘Thousand Hills’ is a perfect introduction to the soul of Africa.
RW.KGL.eatingImageText:
If you want to eat like a local in Kigali, tuck into brochette, a shish kebab made with meat or fish with a unique blend of herbs and spices. A hearty meal with plenty of taste packed in is nyama choma, a Rwandan variation of barbequed meat served with a spicy tomato, onion and chilli salad.

Tilapia is the most common fish used in African cuisine. Try some ‘big fish’ (tilapia grilled and served with vegetables) in the Nyamirambo area.

While there are plenty of modern coffee bars in the city, the locals head to the nearest milk bar for a glass of fresh or fermented milk known as ikivuguto, along with a plate of snacks. 

High-end dining is also available. The city centre has some excellent restaurants serving international cuisine.

UG.EBB.touristAttractionsText:
Known as a destination for safari and gorilla spotting, the Uganda Wildlife Conservation Education Centre is a great attraction to start with. Here you can learn about wildlife and the conservation efforts made to protect it, before setting off to witness these animals in their natural habitats.

Admire Entebbe’s flora at the Entebbe Botanical Garden. Stunning blooms and towering trees provide the perfect backdrop to vistas of Africa’s largest lake, Lake Victoria – spot birds fluttering overhead and monkeys swinging between branches.

Finally, a trip to Entebbe wouldn’t be complete without standing on the Equator. With one foot in each hemisphere, this iconic landmark is an incredibly unique experience.
UG.EBB.leisureActivitiesText:
As one of the best places to embark on a safari, Entebbe has multiple options whether on foot or on wheels.

For a close encounter with primates, head to Ngamba Island Chimpanzee Sanctuary on Lake Victoria. Step into their world, set amidst lush, thriving greenery.

Entebbe is also the perfect place for a gorilla trekking tour. Hike through dense forests and feel the excitement build as you come face-to-face with a gentle gorilla family. This once-in-a-lifetime trek will leave you in awe.

For a more leisurely adventure, take a cycling tour around Lake Victoria. Or take a trip to the Sesse Islands – an archipelago of eighty-four islands covered in forest, where there are more animals than people.
UG.EBB.shoppingText:
The Entebbe crafts village is a colourful maze of market stalls brimming with handmade treasures. This makes for a truly Ugandan shopping adventure. You’ll find intricately woven baskets and beautifully carved wooden sculptures. Each piece is crafted by local artisans who pour their heart and heritage into everything they create. Whether it’s beautifully-designed fabrics, striking masks or pottery – each item will bring the essence of Uganda home with you.

Grab yourself one of the country’s most prized exports – Ugandan coffee. Whether you’re a coffee connoisseur or simply need a caffeine kick every morning, this cold brew will transport you back to Uganda’s enchanting highlands with every sip.
UG.EBB.destinationPageIntro: From the Uganda Wildlife Conservation Education Centre to trekking through gorilla-clad forests – Entebbe has plenty of attractions for both nature and animal lovers.
UG.EBB.overviewText:
Nestled along the shimmering shores of Lake Victoria, Entebbe offers a blend of nature, wildlife and history. Entebbe feels like a hidden gem – a peaceful oasis where vibrant markets buzz with life, and the lush wilderness invites you to experience adventure.

Whether you are taking in the awe-inspiring views of Africa’s largest lake, or venturing through the nearby rainforests abundant with wildlife, you’ll feel deeply connected to nature in Entebbe.

Entebbe isn’t just about tranquility, it’s also a place where Uganda’s history is told. Every corner tells a story, and the richness of Ugandan culture is alive in the people and their traditions. Entebbe provides a truly unforgettable experience to anyone seeking a journey beyond the ordinary.
UG.EBB.eatingImageText:
Stalls overflow with fresh, local produce at Kitooro Market. Bananas take centre stage here as it is the national fruit. Plantains are a popular dish across Uganda too, whether they are steamed and mashed to make matoke or fried into crisps as a moreish snack.

For a hearty meal, you must try luwombo, a traditional method of stewing meat in banana leaves. You can opt for slow-cooked chicken or beef in onions, ginger, finely chopped peanuts, spices and more. For a delightful snack, order ‘rolex’ (no, not the watch). This iconic street food derives its name from ‘rolled eggs’ – an omelette filled with tomatoes, onions and cabbage wrapped in a chapati.

MZ.MPM.touristAttractionsText:
If you’re a history and architecture enthusiast, Maputo is a real gem. The Praça dos Trabalhadores train station designed by José Ferreira da Costa is a spectacular structure of intricate iron latticework. Art lovers have a choice of superb art museums and galleries to explore such as the National Art Gallery of Mozambique, the Chissano Gallery, and Núcleo De Arte Digital.

For exhibitions, dance, music and a lovely day out, the Centro Cultural Franco-Moçambicano is the cultural centre of the city.
MZ.MPM.leisureActivitiesText:
Maputo isn’t just a great beach destination. It’s also the gateway to safari adventures. Maputo National Park is one of the most diverse in Africa, with stunning coastal sand dunes, mountain ranges and forestry.

In the heart of the city is Parque Dos Continuadores, a thriving open space filled with beds of native flora, handicraft stalls and a food fair selling delicious treats.

If you love fishing, Maputo is the gateway to some of the best deep-sea sports fishing along the coast. Hire a speedboat to take you out to catch tuna, marlin and sailfish.

To see the city from a totally different perspective, take a sunset cruise around Maputo Bay or take a day trip to Inhaca Island, home to numerous shipwrecks. Dive tours take you down to see these ancient ships and the marine wildlife.
MZ.MPM.shoppingText:
Maputo has plenty of markets, stores, boutiques and malls. One of the busiest is the Municipal Market, which is an ideal place to hunt for souvenirs. One of the most popular mementoes of a trip to Maputo is a handmade wooden mask. The best place to buy one is on Saturdays at Feira de Artesanato. These beautifully crafted pieces of art are guaranteed to be a focal point of any room. If you love to shop, Maputo Shopping Centre is a large, modern mall with high-profile brands as well as boutiques and smaller stores selling local crafts. Other authentic souvenirs to look out for include Batik fabrics, woven baskets and locally produced honey.

The main tourist shopping area is Parque dos Continuadores, where the street vendors sell trinkets and crafts.
MZ.MPM.destinationPageIntro: With beaches galore, plenty of sunshine, broad boulevards and boutique shopping, Mozambique’s elegant capital, Maputo, is the perfect destination for families and couples.
MZ.MPM.overviewText:
Maputo, the capital of Mozambique, is a fascinating mix of local culture and its colonial Portuguese heritage, showcased most notably through the city’s architecture, culture and language. Maputo is filled with wide boulevards and large parks, and a vibrant social scene.

Maputo is also an excellent beach destination for families, with easy access to some of the country’s best beaches including the Costa do Sol, Inhaca and Marracuene. The city feels young, exciting and vibrant, with a sprinkling of Portuguese-inspired buildings along broad, tree-lined streets. Shopping is a scintillating blend of markets, boutiques and malls.

The restaurants and cafés in Maputo serve a fusion of international cuisine as well as local specialities, with Portuguese, Indian and Middle Eastern influences. A warm climate makes Maputo an ideal destination year-round.
MZ.MPM.destinationHighlightsH1: Maputo: The vibrant soul of Mozambique
MZ.MPM.eatingImageText:
Cassava and rice are staples in Mozambican cuisine. Rich stews also tend to be served with xima, a maize porridge similar to polenta. When in Maputo, you have to try the national dish Mutapa, which is made by braising cassava leaves in coconut milk, seasoned with onions, tomatoes and dried shrimp. The result is a creamy, savoury sauce with a hint of that coconut flavour, served with xima or rice. You’ll also notice the Portuguese and Indian influence on local cuisine. Peri-peri seasoning is a popular marinade for grilled chicken and seafood, enhanced with birds-eye chilli for a kick.

Street food lovers must look out for chamuças, which are the Mozambique equivalent of Indian samosas stuffed with various fillings such as meat, fish and cheese and potatoes.

Maputo is a coastal city, so you’ll find plenty of fish and seafood dishes, especially prawns cooked in a curry sauce with coconut milk, knowns as caril de camaro. You’ll find street vendors throughout the city and on the beaches. For more high-end dining, the city centre is the place to go.

ZW.HRE.touristAttractionsText:
Pay a visit to the National Heroes’ Acre, a tribute of sculptures and statues that commemorate those who fought for Zimbabwe’s independence. For a glimpse of wildlife close to the city, head to Mukuvisi Woodlands – home to impalas, giraffes, crocodiles and more. It’s simply incredible.

Art enthusiasts can browse Zimbabwe’s creative heritage at the Chapungu Sculpture Park, where stone carvings capture the soul of Shona culture. Take a trip to the National Gallery of Zimbabwe for contemporary African art. Explore more history at the Zimbabwe Museum of Human Sciences, home to what is believed to be the oldest wooden sculpture in sub-Saharan Africa.

Don’t miss the Great Zimbabwe National Monument, a UNESCO World Heritage Site of stunning stone structures that tell a story of an ancient empire.
ZW.HRE.leisureActivitiesText:
For a feel-good activity in Harare, explore Wild is Life wildlife sanctuary. Learn all about their conservation efforts and dedication to protecting elephants and other wildlife.

A short drive from the city lies the Thetford Game Reserve, a huge area teeming with animals including over 150 bird species. Embark on a guided safari, where spotting a lion or a rare bird will leave you in awe.

Meander through Lake Chivero Recreational Park, spanning 6,000 hectares of land. It’s home to all kinds of animals, from rhinos and warthogs, to everything in between. Go on a game walk or try your hand at some fishing along the lake.

If you’re all safari-ed out, discover an abundance of spectacular flora species in the National Botanic Garden.
ZW.HRE.shoppingText:
Fill your shopping bags at Avondale Flea Market, a treasure trove of Zimbabwean crafts of handmade jewellery and intricately beaded trinkets. Every piece feels personal, crafted with care by local artisans. For those who adore rich textiles, Harare’s fabric markets are bursting with colourful patterns that reflect the true spirit of Zimbabwe. From daring prints to vibrant hues, these beautiful textiles are ideal mementoes to bring home and make into something beautiful.

Take home a handmade basket, a unique souvenir that reflects Zimbabwean heritage. These stunning home decor pieces will not only enhance the beauty of your living space but also serve as conversation starters.
ZW.HRE.destinationPageIntro: Harare offers a mix of bushland beauty and vibrant city life. Venture to a game reserve or browse the bustling local markets for a true taste of Zimbabwean life.
ZW.HRE.overviewText:
As soon as you arrive in Harare, Zimbabwe, you’re greeted by the eclectic hum of city life that blends effortlessly with scenes of wild beauty. The streets in the city pulse with colours, from the dazzling fabrics draped on stalls, to the bold handcrafted beads and ceramics.

Every twist and turn reveals a new adventure, from incredible wildlife safaris to old ruins that narrate the city’s history. It’s a place where you can savour earthy, soulful food, see the handiwork of artisans, and uncover the tranquil charm of the vast savanna. Harare doesn’t just invite you to visit, it dares you to dive in.
ZW.HRE.eatingImageText:
Wander through the Mbare Musika Market, where vibrant stalls overflow with exotic fruits, fragrant spices and enticing street food. Sample local delicacies like crispy fried kapenta – small fish that are fried to perfection. They are popular snacks that pack a punch of umami and are best served with a squeeze of fresh lemon.

For something hearty and comforting, indulge in a creamy peanut butter stew made with meat and vegetables, a signature dish that showcases the country’s love for peanuts. No trip to Harare is complete without trying sadza, a porridge-like side made from corn flour. Served with different kinds of stews and sauces, it’s a staple in Zimbabwean cuisine.

DZ.ALG.touristAttractionsText:
The Kasbah of Algiers is a UNESCO World Heritage site boasting exquisite buildings. As you make your way through its 17th-century streets, look out for the Dar Aziza palace, named after a princess. Once you’ve wandered around, stop by The Great Mosque of Algiers, dating back to the 11th century. Take a break in this tranquil setting situated close to the harbour.

Then discover the rest of Algiers, filled with French architectural influences. The Notre Dame d’Afrique basilica is an ornate version of its Parisian cousin, featuring colourful glass-stained windows. Don’t forget to stroll around the Bardo Museum for a deep dive into the city’s culture. This exquisite Turkish mansion houses historic artefacts and is decorated with ornate tiles.
DZ.ALG.leisureActivitiesText:
Algiers is famous for its gardens and one of the best is Le Jardin d’Essai du Hamma, located in the Mohamed Belouizdad district. This stunning botanical garden was established in the early 19th century, and is recognised as one of the most important botanical gardens in the world.

If you’re in the city with kids, spend a day at the local waterpark, a fun and family-friendly place with something for all ages: the children can have a blast playing in the pool while you get pampered at the spa. Or relax on the beach where the sand is soft, and the water is shallow and clean – just right for paddling and water sports.

Golfers will have the time of their lives on a trip to Algiers. There’s a sprawling 18-hole championship course covering over 10km, with some spectacular coastal backdrops to admire as they tee off.
DZ.ALG.shoppingText:
The Kasbah of Algiers is, of course, a must-visit when shopping in Algiers. Walk through a maze of streets lined with stalls selling everything from leatherwork, clothing and jewellery to herbs and spices.

For a more contemporary experience, browse through huge malls such as the Centre Commercial Bab Ezzouar and the Centre Commercial Al Qods. Each of these multi-level buildings has hundreds of stores along with food courts and entertainment facilities. They’re also air-conditioned and have plenty of parking for your convenience.

If you’re looking for something a little different, take a stroll down Didouche Mourad Street, which is packed with boutiques and artisan stores. For an authentic market experience, try the buzzing Marché Medina Jedida, stocking textiles, wood carvings and bags of spices.
DZ.ALG.destinationPageIntro: The Kasbah of Algiers, its 14th-century Great Mosque and the towering Maqam Echahid monument, are just a few of the treasures to be explored on a city break in Algiers.
DZ.ALG.overviewText:
At the heart of Algiers is a fusion of French and north African cultures, unlike any other. This unique destination is bathed in African sunshine, yet has wide boulevards reminiscent of the streets of Paris. 

A labyrinth of cobbled streets winds through the city, where The Kasbah of Algiers boasts a fascinating blend of sights, aromas and flavours. Elegant French-inspired architecture contrasts beautifully with ancient mosques, while coffee shops around every corner offer refreshing drinks.  

The sweeping Bay of Algiers adds a shimmering splash of cobalt blue, with breath-taking beaches and warm, clear water that’s perfect for swimming. All this and so much more can be explored in Algiers.
DZ.ALG.eatingImageText:
With a combination of African and French influences, dining in Algiers is an extraordinary experience full of surprises. From rich Tajin Zitoun served with couscous to chakchouka infused with herbs and spices, the local cuisine will delight your taste buds.

If you need something on the go, look out for Bourek. This delicacy is like a spring roll stuffed with various fillings including cheese, meat and vegetables. You can also uncover the best street food around the Kasbah of Algiers.

Prefer to indulge in fine French cuisine at high-end restaurants? Head to the Bois des Arcades neighbourhood or modern areas of the city centre. Although French dishes are plentiful in Algiers, you’ll find more familiar meals at international food halls in malls.

US.DFW.businessClassSummary:
Fly to Dallas in Business or First Class with Qatar Airways and travel cross the Atlantic in style. From check-in to arrival, every stage of your journey is curated to suit your needs. Speed through immigration formalities at a dedicated counter before you step into one of our exclusive Business Class lounges. Here, you can dine, work, or simply enjoy a quiet moment before your flight. 

On board, our professional cabin crew guide you to your seat, designed to bring you optimal comfort. Stretch out thanks to ample legroom and adjust to your destination’s time zone with ambient lighting. Once you’re settled in, connect with colleagues using the high-speed Wi-Fi, available on our A380, A350, B787 and select B777 aircraft. Between meetings, explore a selection of movies, games and TV shows from our extensive entertainment system. 

Savour a meal whenever it suits you with our à la carte menu, created by world-renowned chefs. When you’re ready to rest, pamper yourself with premium personal care products before relaxing in fully lie-flat bed. Whether you’re travelling to close business deals or discover a captivating cultural scene, you’ll arrive feeling revived and ready for your day. 

Book a Business or First Class flight to Dallas with Qatar Airways and indulge in ultimate luxury.
US.DFW.touristAttractionsText:
Dive into the city’s artistic heart by exploring its many inspiring galleries. The Dallas Museum of Art is home to an extensive collection from around the world, while the Meadows Museum of Art features a fine collaboration of Spanish art. On the cultural spectrum, the Perot Museum of Nature and Science is also worth a look – it’s perfect for families and curious minds. 

Step back in time at the Sixth Floor Museum, which chronicles the life and legacy of President John F. Kennedy. The nearby John F. Kennedy Memorial Plaza provides a reflection and tribute to the late president.

You can’t visit Dallas without embracing the spirit of the Old West by attending the Texas Cowboy Hall of Fame in Fort Worth. Here you can find legends of rodeo and the storied history of Texas cowboys.
US.DFW.leisureActivitiesText:
Spend a morning walking or running along the Katy Trail. This 2-mile urban trail weaves through the city, providing spectacular sightseeing opportunities. Minutes from downtown, you can take a boat out or simply picnic at White Rock Lake, a haven for nature lovers. There is also a 9-mile trail around the lake for running and cycling. 

Immerse yourself in the local culture with an evening of line dancing lessons. There are many country dance halls that provide a traditional Texan experience where you can learn the steps and enjoy the lively Texan atmosphere. 

Travel out of the city to the old-world town of Grapevine. Known for its historic Main Street, dining establishments and boutique shops, it presents a quaint Texan experience compared to that of the city centre.
US.DFW.shoppingText:
Much like the rest of the United States, Dallas has no shortage of malls and plazas to browse. From high-end fashion to everyday essentials, you’re sure to find what you’re looking for in this city. For a touch of sophistication, explore Highland Park Village. This classical and elegant area boasts a collection of boutiques, upscale retailers and high-end dining establishments. 

The Bishop Arts District offers an eclectic and artsy feel, with charming streets lined with artisan crafts, fashion and cafés. 

You can’t leave Texas without a visit to a Wild West store. Try on some classic cowboy boots, hats and Western attire to take a piece of Texas home with you.
US.DFW.destinationPageIntro: Immerse yourself in Texan culture and indulge your inner cowboy at the Texas Cowboy Hall of Fame, then explore the city’s famous art museums.
US.DFW.overviewText:
Embrace the warm Southern charm of Dallas and discover its dynamic blend of culture, history and nature. Located in the heart of Texas, this metropolis is renowned for its world-class museums, thriving arts scene and laidback cowboy culture. 

With an abundance of cutting-edge galleries, theatres and music venues to explore, the city’s dedication to the arts is unmatched. The culinary landscape is also not far behind, with a wide selection of classic Southern favourites like Texas-style barbecue and Tex-Mex dishes. 

Dallas also offers an opportunity for a wide range of outdoor activities with plenty of parks, green spaces, hiking and bike trails throughout the city. Whether you’re in Dallas for business or leisure, it’s sure to provide you with an experience that will leave you eager to return.
US.DFW.destinationHighlightsH1: Dallas: The cowboy heart of Texas
US.DFW.eatingImageText:
Naturally, the most popular food in Dallas is Tex-Mex cuisine, which seamlessly blends Mexican and Texan flavours. There’s a plethora of options, from casual eateries serving sizzling fajitas and juicy tacos, to fine dining eateries offering gourmet enchiladas and curated nachos. 

For those seeking American comfort food, you can also source authentic Southern dishes here. Indulge in soul-warming meals like fried chicken and buttery biscuits, with a side of Southern hospitality. 

Dallas is also famous for its steak houses, showcasing the quality and flavour of local Texan beef. If you’d like to explore more of the locally sourced food space, head to the Dallas Farmers Market. It’s a treasure trove of farm-fresh produce, unique spices and handcrafted delicacies.

US.SEA.touristAttractionsText:
Venture to the Space Needle, where panoramic views stretch across the city, Elliot Bay, Cascade Mountains, and the majestic Mount Rainier. Sunset views from here are simply stunning.

Just a short walk away is the Seattle Great Wheel. Take a spin and witness the incredible vistas of the harbour. Afterwards, enjoy the vibrant atmosphere of the Seattle Waterfront with its charming shops and lively fairground rides.

For a burst of colour and creativity, the Chihuly Garden and Glass is a must-see. Wander through the breathtaking display of Dale Chihuly’s enchanting glass sculptures, where vibrant blooms add a touch of nature to the artistic masterpieces.

Seattle is also a haven for pop culture enthusiasts. The Museum of Pop Culture immerses you in the worlds of music, science fiction and more. Be sure to also check out the Museum of Flight, which showcases more than 85 historic aircraft, interactive exhibits and family activities.
US.SEA.leisureActivitiesText:
No trip to Seattle is complete without a trip out to Mount Rainier National Park – a nature lovers’ sanctuary. Here you can hike through scenic trails, mountain climb toward the snow-capped peaks and gaze at the cascading waterfalls.

For a maritime adventure, set sail on a boat right out to Victoria, Vancouver Island. Take a tour to see the orcas – a sight that will leave you in awe. Peak season is between May and October, but it’s possible to see them any time of the year.

Closer to the city, sports fans can join the roar of the crowd at Lumen Field during a Seattle Seahawks football game. Or, watch the Seattle Mariners play a baseball game at T-Mobile Park.
US.SEA.shoppingText:
