This UNESCO-listed treasure trove of Roman ruins is nestled in the rolling hills. Explore its marvelous ancient theatre and temple ruins for a day of adventure.

MA.CMN.touristAttractionsText:
One of the world’s largest mosques is perched on the edge of the ocean in Casablanca. The majestic Hassan II Mosque is adorned with intricate mosaics and a towering minaret that presents a sense of awe and peace.

Venture into the unique art deco district along Boulevard Mohammed V, where Casablanca’s architectural style shines. Stroll through the streets lined with whitewashed buildings and beautiful patterns.

Mohammed V Square is the city’s cultural hub, where iconic landmarks such as the Palace of Justice, Casablanca Cathedral, and Wilaya of Casablanca are framed by fountains and palm trees – adding to the coastal atmosphere.
MA.CMN.leisureActivitiesText:
Make your way to La Corniche, Casablanca’s scenic waterfront. The kilometres-long promenade hugs the Atlantic Ocean and is dotted with cafés, beach restaurants, and the endless blue horizon.

If you’re craving some sun, head to the beach. Whether it’s a peaceful day lounging on the sands of Ain Diab, or simply admiring the blue waters along the corniche, the city’s coastal beauty calls.

For a taste of Moroccan relaxation and hospitality, spend the afternoon in a traditional hammam. Warm steam, exfoliating scrubs, and scented oils are used in an age-old ritual that leaves you feeling renewed. Pamper yourself further by staying in a local home called a riad. The courtyards and ornate décor are a divine setting to sip mint tea and enjoy the serene surroundings in.
MA.CMN.shoppingText:
Shopping in Casablanca is an experience that immerses you right into the centre of Moroccan culture. In addition to the popular Habous market, Old Medina is a maze of narrow streets winding through stalls of treasures – showcasing spices and vibrant displays of leather goods, jewellery and traditional clothing.

Another shopping hotspot is the Bab Marrakech Market, where bustling shops sell everything from patterned ceramics to colourful Moroccan rugs. There are rows upon rows of handcrafted mosaic lamps and bottles of golden argan oil – all offering a piece of magical Morocco to take home. The city also boasts modern malls which are excellent for some air-conditioned shopping.
MA.CMN.destinationPageIntro: Tradition meets modernity in Casablanca – the city is a melting pot of old-world mosques, contemporary structures and everything in-between.
MA.CMN.overviewText:
The beating heart of Morocco’s Atlantic coast, Casablanca invites you to explore its lively streets. This thriving metropolis evokes true Moroccan culture with its old medinas, aromatic cafés, and the friendly smiles of locals. Exploring the city’s neighbourhoods is a must – beautiful architecture showcases the city’s rich history, and shopkeepers create a vibrant energy on almost every corner.

Boasting lovely beaches such as Ain Diab, the enormous Hassan II Mosque, and a lovely corniche to walk along – Casablanca’s seaside location is the perfect backdrop for leisurely strolls and recreation. 

Whether you are sipping mint tea at a café, engaging with friendly locals, or relaxing in a hammam – each moment in this city is a delightful adventure waiting to unfold.
MA.CMN.destinationHighlightsH1: Casablanca: The vibrant heart of Morocco
MA.CMN.eatingImageText:
Casablanca’s culture shines through its dishes. Indulge in a hearty tagine, slow-cooked with fragrant spices, tender meat, and vegetables that melt in your mouth. Try some couscous, a fluffy bed of semolina that is also considered the country’s national dish. To sample the best local fare, head to Old Medina and Central Market, where you'll find loads of authentic spots serving the most flavourful local dishes.

For a sweet and savoury delight, order a pastilla – a flaky pastry stuffed with spiced meat, dusted with cinnamon and sugar.

Lose yourself in the Habous market, where rows of delicious green, black and spiced olives await.

MA.RAK.touristAttractionsText:
Roam around the Medina and the main square, Jamâa El-Fnaa, for the ultimate souk experience. A labyrinth of alleyways, bazaars and stalls will tempt you, along with entertainers such as traditional snake charmers, acrobats, musicians and soothsayers. After watching a show, head to the Saadian Tombs. Undiscovered for hundreds of years, they’re adorned with zelij (Moroccan tiles) and spectacular decorations.

To immerse yourself in a tranquil setting, take a stroll around Menara Gardens. Once a royal retreat, this beautiful space is home to a spectacular lakeside pavilion. Or visit Marrakech’s oldest monument, the 12th-century Almoravid Koubba.
MA.RAK.leisureActivitiesText:
Escape the hustle and bustle of Marrakech’s busy streets in the small but beautiful Majorelle Gardens. This oasis of calm is also home to the Berber Museum, where you can learn about the native tribes of the region. Or visit the peaceful Koutoubia Mosque with its towering minaret, one of the symbols of Marrakech.

Want to explore the great outdoors? You’ll be glad to know that Marrakech is the starting point for desert and Atlas Mountains treks, including horseback and camel tours. Take a camel ride through the Palmeraie on the outskirts of the city and you’ll be surrounded by forests of palm trees.

For a little pampering, relax in one of the city’s famous hammams. From massages and spa treatments to authentic Moroccan baths, there are plenty of options to choose from.
MA.RAK.shoppingText:
Planning a shopping spree in Marrakech? You have to stop by the markets and souks of the Old Quarter. Clustered around Djemaa El-Fnaa is the city’s largest souk, but wander through the streets and you’ll discover plenty of smaller markets. They all offer a huge selection of items and souvenirs such as polished brass trinkets and jewellery.

The city’s tanneries keep the stalls supplied with high-quality leather goods including camel leather jackets, shoes and bags. For something a little more unusual, look for the local cactus silk. It’s actually a natural rayon product that dyes well and produces vibrantly coloured textiles. To find original Moroccan ceramics, browse through the Potter’s Souk, brimming with brightly coloured bowls, tagines and plates.
MA.RAK.destinationPageIntro: Ancient Marrakech is a truly incredible destination, filled with busy markets, tranquil gardens and exquisite mosques, alongside modern malls and high-end restaurants.
MA.RAK.overviewText:
One of Morocco’s imperial cities, Marrakech is a mesmerising destination boasting archaeological gems, secret gardens and bustling souks. Dusty streets take you on a journey through time, and are filled with fascinating sights, smells and sounds. There are plenty of things to see and do, and the towering Atlas Mountains and Agafay Desert are within easy reach as well.

Shoppers are spoilt for choice, with traditional markets alongside air-conditioned malls and exotic boutiques. Food lovers can go on a culinary adventure with classic Moroccan tagine and spicy, mouth-watering street food on every corner. Marrakech promises a trip to remember and will capture your heart, drawing you back again and again.
MA.RAK.destinationHighlightsH1: Marrakech: A marvel of North Africa
MA.RAK.eatingImageText:
Moroccan dishes are among the most recognisable and widely known in North African cuisine. Distinctive tagine stews are prepared with slow-cooked meat and vegetables served in conical pots, making dining a social occasion. A popular favourite is couscous – a semolina grain that’s steamed and mixed with vegetables and meat (usually lamb). Make sure to also try harira, a rich and hearty tomato-based soup with chickpeas and lentils. Up for something a little more exotic? Get yourself a bowl of babbouche – snails are slowly-cooked in a fragrant broth packed with warm spices like anise, thyme and cloves.

If you have a sweet tooth, the perfect dessert is chebakia – a crispy, honey-drenched pastry flavoured with sesame seeds and anise. Be sure to try ghriba cookies with a cup of tea for an authentic Moroccan experience. These traditional cookies have a nutty, cinnamon-laced base and are topped with powdered sugar.

EG.HBE.touristAttractionsText:
One of the most unusual ruins to visit is Cleopatra’s Palace, but you’ll need to strap on a scuba tank to visit this underwater marvel. PADI-approved dive schools will take you through a beginner’s diving course before you head to see the Egyptian queen’s palace.

Alexandria’s Corniche is a sweeping arc of sand set against an azure sea. Along the way, you’ll come across the multi-domed Abu Abbas al-Mursi Mosque, as well as street vendors selling delicious snacks.

For a cooler introduction to some of Alexandria’s history, explore the underground catacombs of Kom el-Shoqafa, or visit the site of the legendary Pharos lighthouse, now home to the 15th-century Fort Qaitbay.

A stroll around the Kom el-Dikka archaeological park lets you discover Roman amphitheatres and Ptolemaic temples.
EG.HBE.leisureActivitiesText:
Alexandria is one of the best beach destinations in Egypt, and the top beaches for a family break or a lazy day sunbathing are Mamoura Beach and Montazah Beach.

The Montazah Royal Gardens is a tranquil and lush chance to escape the hustle and bustle of the city. You’ll find these landscaped green spaces close to Montazah Beach, with cafés, restaurants and swimming pools where you can cool off.

Take a night time stroll over the Stanley Bridge, one of the most iconic sites in the city and a great spot to get some panoramic photos.

The Great Library may be long gone, but you can capture a sense of the grandeur of that once-famous seat of learning with a visit to the Bibliotheca Alexandria, home to hundreds of thousands of books and fascinating museums, including the Antiquities Museum.
EG.HBE.shoppingText:
For some artisan boutiques including hand-made furniture, Attarine Market is the place to go. A twisting series of alleyways, it’s much less touristy than other locations.

Close by you’ll find Manshiya Market, also known as the Downtown market, an eclectic mix of spice stores, textiles and jewellery as well as fresh produce.

The city has plenty of air-conditioned malls including the huge City Centre Mall and the Green Plaza Mall, as well as the upmarket San Stefano Mall, home to international designer stores.
EG.HBE.destinationPageIntro: From the legendary Pharos lighthouse and the Great Library to the museums, souqs and one of the busiest ports in the world, Alexandria is one of Egypt’s glittering jewels.
EG.HBE.overviewText:
Magnificent, legendary, and one of the true gems of Ancient Egypt, Alexandria is a vibrant and unique summer destination that introduces you to a whole new aspect of travel in Egypt. Once home to the greatest library in the world and one of the Seven wonders of the ancient world, Alexandria is a fascinating blend of old and new, modern and antique.

Food influenced by both the Middle East and the Mediterranean, lively souqs and markets, and tours that will take you on a fabulous journey are all reasons to make Alexandria your next destination with Qatar Airways. 

The lure of this great trading city on the coast is a captivating blend of exotic experiences, luxury accommodation, and the chance to delve deeper into the mysteries of ancient Egypt, and the marvels of the 21st-century city too.
EG.HBE.eatingImageText:
Alexandria is renowned for its fresh fish, landed at the port on a daily basis, and cooked using influences from both North African and Mediterranean cuisine.

You’ll find traditional tajines blended with Greek moussaka and Italian dishes with lots of tomato, basil and cheese. Sayadieh is a seafood rice that’s similar to paella, while fish is often served very simply grilled and lightly seasoned with herbs and spices.

Singari fish is cooked with tomatoes, cilantro, cumin and a dash of chilli to give it a kick. Most meals are served with freshly baked unleavened bread.

Or try Alexandrian fondue, a mouthwatering family meal with a secret seven-cheese mix at its heart.

For food on the go, vendors sell falafel, filled pita bread and the city’s own take on ice cream, sorbets and frozen yoghurts.

IQ.ISU.touristAttractionsText:
Explore a culture that stretches back over 100,000 years at the Slemani Museum, one of Iraq’s most important collections of artefacts. For a more focused look at Kurdish culture, the Kurd’s Heritage Museum on Mawlawi Street is full of metalwork, textiles and items that tell the story of the Kurdish people.

While there are plenty of modern malls in the city, Sulaymaniyah Bazaar has that authentic ambience where everything from local food, to jewellery and perfume is on offer. Look out for fresh almond and pistachio paste, a delicious treat that’s made for you while you wait.

For a great family day out, Chavi Land theme park is popular with locals and tourists alike. It’s also home to Iraq’s largest Ferris wheel. Take the cable car to the top of the mountain for a spectacular sunset view.
IQ.ISU.leisureActivitiesText:
For a glimpse into the Sulaymaniyah’s recent past, a visit to the Amna Suraka Museum is a fascinating way to learn about the region’s history.

The city’s hammams are a chance to pamper yourself for an afternoon. The Mufti Hammam is a cultural icon and the only women-only hammam in the city. It’s a fascinating relic that has remained unchanged for over 200 years. 

Sulaymaniyah has plenty of open spaces and parks to explore, the largest of which is Azadi Park, just a short stroll from the Bazaar. It’s a tranquil, relaxing space that’s very family-focused.

Trade the hustle and bustle of the city for the calming charm of Iraq’s countryside. With a network of hiking trails, you’ll find yourself on some wonderful mountain adventures. It’s advisable to hire a local guide to help you traverse the many trails.
IQ.ISU.shoppingText:
At the heart of the city is its central market and while it’s a busy, bustling place, you’ll get a real sense of how it feels to live like a local. There are the usual tourist trinkets on offer, as well as plenty of fresh fruit and delicious local food. 

The city has plenty of malls to explore too, with the City Star Mall and the Majidi Mall being two of the best. You’ll find everything from antique boutiques to department stores and international brands, as well as family entertainment options and food courts.

The Old Town is home to the main Bazaar, but around its side streets, you’ll find smaller stores, boutiques and shops selling artisan crafts and jewellery. As the shopping areas are very central, it’s easy to go exploring without having to go too far from the hotels and restaurants downtown.
IQ.ISU.destinationPageIntro: Surrounded by natural beauty, Sulaymaniyah is a young city with an ancient heart. Busy, vibrant and energetic, it’s a welcoming place full of things to see, do and experience.
IQ.ISU.overviewText:
Sulaymaniyah is a fascinating city with a charming mix of old and new architecture. Its rich cultural heritage and friendly and welcoming nature immediately make you feel at home. Whether it’s bargain hunters in the souqs or families enjoying some time together, life in Sulaymaniyah is always busy.

Set against the dramatic backdrop of the Goizha and Glazarda mountain ranges, the city is a vibrant metropolis that embraces visitors and introduces them to the ancient Kurdish culture. A centre for agriculture as well as commerce, the newer aspects of the city provide visitors with modern galleries, malls, shopping and dining, all surrounded by magnificent mountain scenery. Sulaymaniyah is one of Iraq’s true jewels and is popular with travellers who want to discover the essence of Kurdish life.
IQ.ISU.destinationHighlightsH1: Sulaymaniyah: A jewel of the Middle East
IQ.ISU.eatingImageText:
Food and beverages are a key part of Kurdish culture, and throughout the city you’ll find tea houses, restaurants, and street food on offer. The tea houses in particular are well worth a visit, but bear in mind that some of them are for men only. For a more international dining experience, check out the city’s malls food halls and restaurants. 

If you want to try traditional Kurdish food, look for dishes like yaprakh (stuffed vine leaves), masgouf (roasted freshwater fish with tamarind and spices) or shorbat rumman (a soup made with pomegranate juice, split peas and ground beef).

Explore the area between Ali Naji and Salim Street and you can sample some of the region’s local street food including pitta bread stuffed with meat and vegetables, warm and spicy soups and shawarma.

SA.MED.touristAttractionsText:
The second holiest site in Islam, Medina is home to renowned mosques and plenty of spiritual wonders. Al-Masjid an-Nabawi, the Prophet’s Mosque, is located at the heart of the city. Its towering green domes and spectacular architecture can be admired from the outside.

Nearby stands the Quba Mosque, with its gleaming white exterior that radiates purity and serenity, it’s the first mosque in Islamic history. From here, visit the Al-Baqi Cemetery, the resting place of the Prophet’s family members and other significant Islamic figures.  Another must-see is the Qiblatain Mosque, recognised for its distinctive story about shifting the qibla (direction of prayer) to Mecca.
SA.MED.leisureActivitiesText:
The Dar Al Madina Museum tells the story of Islam in Medina. It displays detailed models, artefacts, and fascinating pieces that unveil the city’s rich history. Not far away, the Al Madina Museum in the old Hejaz Railway Station, draws you back to the time of steam engines. Its original tracks and carriages recall Saudi Arabia’s heritage as a crossroad of cultures.

To relish Medina’s bustling community, make your way to Quba Square. Soak up the energy of traditional shops or cafés as you sip tea and people-watch. After downing a hot drink, go for a stroll along Quba Walkway Park.

For a breathtaking view, head to Uhud Mountain and Mount Uhud Park, a site revered for its historical importance in the Battle of Uhud. It’s a picturesque setting that’s ideal for small hikes, picnics and simply reflecting on your journey.
SA.MED.shoppingText:
Begin your retail adventure at Taiba Market, where you can discover crafts, jewellery, and souvenirs that capture Medina’s essence. Browse colourful handwoven rugs, intricate prayer beads, and calligraphy artwork that make beautiful keepsakes.

Take a step back in time as you wander through Souk Al-Madina, where vendors cheerfully announce what they have on offer. You’ll find everything from oud and sandalwood to handmade pottery. For a truly classical experience, go to the Old Bazaar, featuring narrow lanes filled with interesting stalls. The highlight? The famed Madinah dates – sweet, luscious, and available in varieties that are all bespoke to the region.
SA.MED.destinationPageIntro: Renowned as one of the most spiritual and peaceful places in the Middle East, Medina is abundant in mosques to admire and tranquil sites to put your mind at ease.
SA.MED.overviewText:
Medina, known as the enlightened city, holds a unique charm that echoes through its ancient streets and landmarks. It’s a peaceful place that touches all those who leave their footprints behind. There are tales of travellers, scholars and poets who have all found solace and inspiration within Medina’s walls.

However, the city also exudes a vibrant ambience that’ll lift your spirit. Immerse yourself in lively marketplaces brimming with local flavours, crafts and joyful conversations. Keep walking along, and you’ll come across architectural masterpieces of deep spiritual significance. 

Medina is not just a destination, but an experience, ready to be embraced and remembered.
SA.MED.eatingImageText:
Savour the city’s quintessential dish, kabsa, a fragrant rice pilaf topped with tender chicken or camel meat. A special treat in the region, camel meat is a delicacy with texture and flavour that evokes Medina’s desert heritage. Kabsa is infused with spices like cardamom, cloves and cinnamon. As you take your first bite, you can smell the aroma of spice routes that passed through Medina, leaving their mark on this tasty dish.

Then there’s mutabbaq, a street food favourite that can be found all across the city. This delectable flatbread is stuffed with spiced minced meat, vegetables, or sometimes even sweet treats. Watching vendors expertly prepare mutabbaq, flipping it with swift hands, is an absolute delight.

CN.PVG.businessClassSummary:
Fly to Shanghai in Business or First Class with Qatar Airways and travel to one of Asia’s most dynamic cities in style. Every element of your journey is designed to bring you a world-class experience from start to finish. 

Begin your trip with priority check-in, followed by a soothing break in one of our Business Class lounges. Sit back in a calm space to work or read, enjoy drinks and light snacks, or take a shower to refresh before your flight.  

On board, our attentive crew show you to your spacious seat, where you can unwind in supreme comfort thanks to its ergonomic design and ample legroom. Connect to the high-speed Wi-Fi, available on our A380, A350, B787 and select B777 aircraft, to finalise business or keep in touch with loved ones. 

With Dine Anytime, you can savour cuisine from our à la carte menu whenever it fits your schedule. After your meal, watch the latest movies and TV shows, or prepare for rest on a lie-flat bed with premium linen. CN.PVG.touristAttractionsText:
Shanghai is a megacity filled with impressive structures – from the Oriental Pearl TV Tower and the 128-storey Shanghai Tower, to the renowned Shanghai World Financial Centre.  

A walk along The Bund feels like stepping into an open-air gallery. Architectural styles of all kinds are visible in the surrounding structures – Roman, Classical and Renaissance buildings line the embankment of the Huangpu River. It’s the city’s most iconic riverside, with a spectacular view of the whole cityscape (from both sides).

For a glimpse of Shanghai’s old-world charm, head down Wukang Road with its mix of architectural gems that narrate the city’s diverse past. Or, explore the former French Concession area of Tianzifang. Its maze-like alleys are abundant with Shikumen houses, galleries, and artisanal shops and trendy cafés.
CN.PVG.leisureActivitiesText:
For a leisurely day that still ticks things off your bucket list, stroll through the Yu Garden. There are ornate pavilions, delicate bridges, the Spring Hall, and the enchanting Lotus Pool to admire. The garden will transport you back to the Ming Dynasty, and there’s a vibrant bazaar connected to the park too.

Art and history enthusiasts can head to Shanghai Museum, located in People’s Square. The museum houses over 120,000 ancient artefacts, from jade carvings to bronzeware – telling the story of China’s complex heritage.

For something a little different, venture to the ancient water town of Zhujiajiao, a short journey from the city. A boat cruise through its quiet canals reveals quaint, stone bridges and historic houses representing old Shanghai.
CN.PVG.shoppingText:
Nanjing Road is the beating heart of Shanghai’s retail world. The atmosphere of this vast neon-lit stretch is truly electric. Here, you can scout everything from luxury brands and high-street department stores, to unique souvenirs.

For quirky finds, Tianzifang’s historic alleyways are filled to the brim with craft shops, antique stores and art galleries. Hunt for handmade crafts, or one-of-a-kind pieces that speak to Shanghai’s artistic soul.

If sewing or custom-made garments are your vibe, the South Bund Soft Spinning Material Market is your hidden gem. Rows of luxurious silks and dazzling cottons invite you to craft your dream wardrobe with the help of skilled tailors.
CN.PVG.destinationPageIntro: Shanghai is the centre of China’s economy and a buzzing city to explore – from futuristic skyscrapers and historic quarters to endless shopping and dining.
CN.PVG.overviewText:
Shanghai, a city of futuristic skylines and the centre of China’s economy, is a melting pot of cultures from past and present. Prepare to be swept up into a world of contrasts as you step onto its streets, where soaring skyscrapers reflect in the waterways, and entire neighbourhoods have been preserved as historic landmarks.

From Michelin-starred restaurants and luxury shopping, to historic markets and an ultra-modern metro system, Shanghai isn’t just a city to see, it’s a city to experience. Shanghai’s fascinating blend of diverse sights and never-ending options makes it an exciting travel destination for just about any traveller.
CN.PVG.eatingImageText:
The stylish district of Xintiandi is known for its eateries, from traditional delicacies to modern fusion. 

The street food is certainly a winner in Shanghai. One popular dish is simple yet comforting – made up of crispy, fried dumplings, and noodles tossed with fragrant spring onions and soy sauce. For authentic street food, head to Wujiang Road where the tantalising aroma of xiao long bao fills the air. These soup dumplings are filled with a rich, savoury broth and tender meat.

With its quirky trunk stalls filled with a variety of trinkets and a plethora of street eats, the famous Wisdom Bay Night Market offers a lively evening of indulging. Another must-visit is Changli Road Street Food Market, where sizzling woks and bustling crowds promise an unforgettable feast.

US.ORD.businessClassSummary:
Fly to Chicago in Business or First Class with Qatar Airways and embark on a journey where every detail has been carefully designed to meet your unique needs. 

Start your trip with fast, priority check-in at a dedicated counter, before spending time in one of our sophisticated Business Class lounges. Snack on light refreshments, get down to business in one of the private workstations, or take a revitalising shower before jetting off. 

Once on board, our professional cabin crew guide you to your seat, featuring an ergonomic design and generous legroom for exceptional comfort. Stay connected easily using the high-speed Wi-Fi, available on our A380, A350, B787 and select B777 aircraft. 

Choose when your meals are served with Dine Anytime. Savour gourmet dishes from our à la carte menu, freshly prepared by award-winning chefs. Then explore an abundance of entertainment options, with films, series and games to enjoy throughout your flight. When you wish to rest, settle into a lie-flat bed with premium linen, and gently adapt to your destination’s time zone thanks to ambient lighting.  

Book a Business or First Class flight to Chicago with Qatar Airways and indulge in a luxurious experience like none other.
US.ORD.touristAttractionsText:
Step onto the Skydeck Chicago’s glass balcony and live the thrill of floating above the city. If you’re feeling a little adventurous, you can even step onto the all glass floor for a truly breathtaking, 360-degree panoramic view.

Millennium Park in downtown Chicago is a hub for bold architecture and public art. Marvel at the iconic Cloud Gate, lovingly dubbed as ‘The Bean’ by locals. This must-see landmark stands as a hallmark of Chicago’s artistic character, with its gleaming surface reflecting the city’s skyline. In summer, the park hosts concerts and events to enjoy too – all free of charge.

Visit the Chicago Cultural Centre to discover the Tiffany glass dome – the largest in the world of its kind. Architecture enthusiasts won’t want to miss Robie House, a UNESCO World Heritage Site designed by Frank Lloyd Wright, or the Tribune Tower, a testament to Chicago’s legacy as the birthplace of the skyscraper.
US.ORD.leisureActivitiesText:
You certainly won’t be short of activities to undertake in Chicago. Dive into its soulful roots by listening to a Chicago-style blues gig. The sound of guitars and husky vocals will transport you back to a whimsical era.

Delve into the city’s intriguing past at the Chicago History Museum. The museum features a number of exhibitions, including one dedicated to Abraham Lincoln’s life. The installation highlights Lincoln’s election in 1860, his leadership during the Civil War and his tragic assassination.  

For a more leisurely adventure, head to Navy Pier – a playground by the water where rides, restaurants, and theatres meet with stunning lake views. Up for some water fun? Take up a kayak tour down the Chicago River and paddle through the famed waterways, learning about the city’s architectural wonders from a unique perspective.
US.ORD.shoppingText:
For a shopping encounter like no other, make your way to the aptly named Magnificent Mile. High-end boutiques, luxury retailers, and well-known department stores line the streets with the finest fashion, jewellery and lifestyle items – all against the backdrop of Chicago’s spectacular skyline. 

Wander down State Street, a historic shopping destination that has long been the pulse of Chicago’s retail scene. From classic department stores to specialty shops, State Street offers a blend of nostalgia and modernity.

For a more intimate shopping trip, venture to Andersonville. Locally-owned boutiques display handcrafted jewellery and one-of-a-kind home décor pieces. It’s a place to indulge in the eclectic spirit of the city, where friendly shopkeepers are eager to share their curated collections.
US.ORD.destinationPageIntro: The city of skyscrapers, Chicago, awaits your arrival. Discover landmarks such as The Bean, indulge in delicious deep-dish pizza, and immerse yourself in the hip atmosphere.
US.ORD.overviewText:
Chicago is a city that reaches for the sky – literally and figuratively. It’s a sprawling, ever-buzzing mosaic of life and stories, with the rhythm of jazz and blues weaving through the air. 

Stroll through lively neighbourhoods with artisanal coffee shops to get a taste of the city’s hip atmosphere. There’s no argument that Chicago’s energy is infectious – whether you’re dancing to live music, savouring a deep-dish pizza or simply taking in its soulful culture.
US.ORD.eatingImageText:
Naturally, you must sink your teeth into a deep-dish pizza when in Chicago – a masterpiece of gooey mozzarella, rich tomato sauce and a buttery crust that will leave you craving more. This hearty, cheesy concoction is a quintessential taste of Chicago’s extravagant food scene. Lincoln Park is the perfect neighbourhood to indulge in this local favourite, plus much more. 

For a glimpse into Chicago’s cultural roots and culinary creativity, order an Italian beef sandwich. This delectable mix of tender, spiced beef stuffed in a crusty roll, drenched in a savoury au jus and often adorned with peppers, is a true Chicago classic.

Settle in and stretch out with generous legroom, as ambient lighting gently adjusts your body to your destination’s time zone. Book a Business or First Class flight to Houston with Qatar Airways and experience unrivalled luxury.
US.IAH.touristAttractionsText:
Walk in the footsteps of astronauts and touch a piece of the moon at the Space Centre Houston. The official NASA Johnson Space Centre is fascinating for all ages. It’s not just a visit – it’s a journey through the cosmos.

Travel back in time at the Houston Museum of Natural Science. Here, dinosaurs come to life and ancient artefacts whisper tales of long-lost civilisations – it makes for a great family activity.

Ascend the JPMorgan Chase Tower to enjoy Houston’s skyline from the observation deck. For the opposite effect, venture below the sea at the Downtown Aquarium to a world of coral reefs and underwater creatures.

Explore outside of the city centre in local neighbourhoods like Montrose, Midtown and The Heights. You can find unique boutiques, quirky cafés and local Texan vibes here.
US.IAH.leisureActivitiesText:
Houston is a playground for discovery, abundant with interactive things to see and do, such as the Houston Zoo. With animals from around the world, it’s an international safari in the heart of the city.

Hop on a bike and explore the Houston Museum District. With its cluster of museums, you can pedal your way from one exhibit to another. The Museum of Fine Arts is a highlight, as it features classic and contemporary works. For families, the Children’s Museum is perfect for a fun day out.

Continue your expedition in Buffalo Bayou Park, for breathtaking views of the city. This is just one of the many parks in Houston. Alternatively, explore Market Square Park and Tranquility Park. Stop for a well-deserved picnic to enjoy Houston’s iconic street food – Tex-Mex tacos.
US.IAH.shoppingText:
Houston is home to many malls catering to all kinds of styles and budgets, making it a treasure trove for avid shoppers. In Uptown Houston, there are even malls for the hippest of audiences, with stores stocked with homegrown brands and handicrafts. There are numerous trunk shows and events, allowing you to capture a first glimpse of collections.

Discover the local shopping atmosphere in Rice Village. Streets are lined with bespoke boutiques where you can uncover one-of-a-kind pieces created by Houston designers.

If you adore crafts, antiques and eclectic items, pop by Traders Village. This bustling open-air market has handmade jewellery, vintage homewares and collectibles.
US.IAH.destinationPageIntro: Home to NASA’s official Space Centre, Houston is home to all the action. Explore its museums, bike around parks and don’t forget to sink your teeth into tasty Texas barbecue.
US.IAH.overviewText:
Houston is a sprawling metropolis of spaghetti highways and world-famous activities. It is an energetic city filled with life and entertainment. Home to inspiring institutions like the Houston Space Centre, the city embraces the future with open arms, all while honouring its roots.

Whether you’re a cowboy visiting the Houston Livestock Show and Rodeo or a food enthusiast coming to devour Texas barbecue, Houston has something special for everybody. The adventure starts the moment you step out the door. Buckle up and get ready for a whirlwind of fun and inspiration in Houston.
US.IAH.eatingImageText:
Enjoy authentic Tex-Mex cuisine, a fusion of Texan and Mexican flavours. Order breakfast tacos brimming with eggs, cheese and spicy chorizo.

When you think of Houston, it’s hard not to imagine the delectable aroma of Texas barbecue. Sink your teeth into tender, smoky beef brisket that falls off the bone. Some of these recipes have been perfected over generations.

Surprisingly, Vietnamese restaurants are popping up all over the city – due to Houston having one of the largest Vietnamese populations in the country. Enjoy a comforting bowl of phở to warm up after a day of adventures.

Hit up The Heights for some of the trendiest dining spots for innovative and creative dishes distinctive to Houston.

IQ.NJF.touristAttractionsText:
The main reason most people travel to Najaf is to visit Imam Ali Mosque, the shrine of the first imam and the prophet Muhammad's cousin and son-in-law. With its glittering golden dome and intricate tile work, it’s a feast for the senses as well as a deeply spiritual place.

To see one of the oldest mosques, visit the Great Mosque of Kufa, a 7th century masterpiece that today features 28 semi-circular towers supporting the huge exterior wall. Recent excavations indicate there may have been an even older mosque on the site, making this a hugely significant historical site as well as an important religious one.

You can discover more about the city’s history at the Najaf Museum, which is filled with fascinating exhibits and artefacts dating back to the city’s beginnings.
IQ.NJF.leisureActivitiesText:
Immerse yourself in literature at the Najaf Seminary, one of the most important learning centres in the Islamic world. Lectures, seminars and discussions explore Islamic culture, as well as more in-depth examinations of the Qur’an.

For a family-friendly day out, the Al Sheraa Complex for Entertainment is a combination of great shopping, dining and entertainment for all ages, as well as peaceful gardens. Or visit the Najaf Amusements Park, with thrilling rides for adults, and more age-appropriate rides for younger children.

Escape the city with a day trip to the Najaf Sea. This huge salt lake covering over 100 square miles is a unique ecosystem surrounded by a desert landscape. It’s a chance to see how traditional life is lived in the towns and villages on its shoreline.
IQ.NJF.shoppingText:
The sheer number of visitors flocking to Najaf has led to a boom in retail outlets, and you’ll see new stores and malls springing up across the city. For an authentic shopping experience, the Al Sooq Al Kabeer is the city’s largest market and is packed with everything you can imagine, from herbs and spices to textiles, jewellery and religious artefacts.

For some air-conditioned comfort, Najaf has some exceptional modern malls, including the Najaf City Mall and the Al Najaf Great Mall Hypermarket, both of which have department stores, boutiques and booths selling jewellery, clothing and electronics.

For a more intimate shopping experience, there are lots of small local shops tucked away behind the Shrine of Imam Ali selling headscarves, religious artefacts and souvenirs.
IQ.NJF.destinationPageIntro: Najaf is a fulfilling and enriching experience for the mind, body and spirit. This holy city is a vibrant, dynamic destination filled with busy markets and tranquil holy sites.
IQ.NJF.overviewText:
Known as Iraq’s holiest city, Najaf is a spectacular combination of ornate architecture and spiritual tranquillity. A deeply traditional destination with a strong sense of identity, Najaf welcomes visitors from around the world.

Bustling markets immerse you in the everyday life of the locals as well as a chance to buy beautifully handcrafted souvenirs and the most expensive of spices, saffron. The food is spicy, flavoursome and delicious, and the tea is plentiful and very sweet!

At the top of the list of places to see is the 10th-century Imam Ali Shrine, a place of devotion for millions of pilgrims. This centre for learning and study retains its scholarly character today, and debating is a lively pastime in the cafés and tea houses throughout the city.
IQ.NJF.eatingImageText:
Traditional food in Iraq is bursting with flavour, with herbs and spices, including saffron, playing a key role in its cuisine. One of the most popular is Qeimeh Najafi, a spicy dish made from meat, lentils and chickpeas, served with rice.

Street food revolves around kebabs and the most famous of Middle Eastern dishes, falafel. Najafi lamb kebabs are spicy and succulent, usually served with bread or rice.

During religious occasions, look out for Dabasiyah Halwa, made with date syrup, sugar and cardamon powder mixed into a melt-in-the-mouth flaky pastry.

For a sweet treat that’ll give you a burst of energy try daheen, made from flour, ghee, walnuts, sugar and buffalo cream. Or go for something a little spicier with beef and lamb kebabs with a sprinkle of purple sumac for a kick of flavour.

US.BOS.businessClassSummary:
Fly to Boston in Business or First Class with Qatar Airways and enjoy an exceptional journey to one of America’s most historic cities. From the moment you arrive at the airport to the moment you land; our team is dedicated to creating an experience you will remember. 

After fast, stress-free check-in at an exclusive counter, you can unwind in one of our sophisticated Business Class lounges. Step into a welcoming, peaceful setting with private workstations to check your emails, refreshments to snack on, and quiet areas to recharge before your flight. 

On board, professional cabin crew guide you to your seat with extra legroom and an ergonomic design. Sit back as soft lighting creates a relaxing environment and adjusts your body to your destination’s time zone. Use the high-speed Wi-Fi, available on our A380, A350, B787 and select B777 aircraft, to join a video call or stay in touch with family and colleagues. 

With Dine Anytime, you can savour meals whenever it suits your schedule. Book a Business or First Class flight to Boston with Qatar Airways and indulge in superior comfort.
US.BOS.touristAttractionsText:
Explore Boston by walking along the Freedom Trail. It leads you through 16 historically significant attractions. Visit the Old North Historic Site, where Paul Revere’s midnight ride began, followed by Paul Revere’s house to see where the revolutionary lived.

Head to Boston Common, the oldest public park in America. Previously, this green oasis was the base for colonial protests. These days, it is typically used for relaxing picnics, picturesque walks and more. To embark on another trip along history’s path, climb the Bunker Hill Monument, standing tall as a reminder of the first major battle of the American Revolution.

Cross the river to browse the famed Harvard University campus. Wander through its grounds and explore where some of the brightest minds have studied.
US.BOS.leisureActivitiesText:
Step into the world of baseball at Fenway Park and watch the Red Sox play beneath the iconic Green Monster. More than just a game for the people of Boston, it’s an experience that defines their sports culture.

Discover Boston from the water on a sunset cruise. Admire the city’s skyline glow as you float around the harbour. For a different kind of boat ride, this time out of town, hop on a ferry to Martha’s Vineyard. This spot makes for the perfect getaway from the hustle and bustle of Boston. Enjoy peaceful coastlines, quaint cottages and a laidback vibe.

For little ones, make your way to the New England Aquarium, which offers an underwater journey with fascinating marine life. Get up close to playful sea lions, and marvel at the enormous tank of sharks, turtles and rays.
US.BOS.shoppingText:
Faneuil Hall Marketplace is where the city’s past meets modern retail. Stroll down cobblestone paths dotted with boutiques and souvenir shops. Pick up a locally crafted piece of Boston, like a vintage-style baseball cap.

A trip to Newbury Street is a must for fashion enthusiasts. This renowned street is home to chic boutiques, luxury brands and rustic cafés. Whether you’re looking for a designer handbag, a bespoke outfit or unique jewellery, Newbury Street is likely the place that has it.

In Harvard Square, historic charm greets you with independent bookstores, street musicians and one-of-a-kind boutiques. As the birthplace of academia, you can probably score yourself a rare first edition here – it’s certainly the destination to purchase something that speaks to your intellectual side.
US.BOS.destinationPageIntro: The cultural hub of New England, Boston is known for attractions of historical and modern heritage. Don’t forget to tuck into a lobster roll while you’re there.
US.BOS.overviewText:
Boston, New England’s hub, is like a storybook coming to life. One minute you’re wandering down a charming alley filled with historical landmarks and the next, you’re surrounded by the buzz of modern life, where start-ups and students are in abundance.

Each season brings its own personality – vibrant autumn reds, cosy winter nights and sunny, spring days where you can enjoy the parks and the waterfront. Enjoy a comforting warm drink at local cafés or stroll through the city for quirky stores. Whatever you find yourself doing, Boston welcomes you with an energy that invites exploration and discovery.
US.BOS.destinationHighlightsH1: Boston: A city of history and possibilities
US.BOS.eatingImageText:
Don’t leave Boston without trying a lobster roll. Tender lobster meat is piled into a toasted bun, served with a drizzle of warm butter. It’s the ultimate taste of New England’s shores in the summer. Then, there’s the famous clam chowder. Thick and creamy, this soup is packed with clams and potatoes. It’s particularly comforting on a winter’s day.

Venture to the North End, where Italian eateries serve up homemade pasta and desserts like cannoli, crispy pastry shells filled with sweet ricotta and chocolate chips. Down by Seaport, seafood reigns supreme. Whether its grilled swordfish, fresh oysters or scallops, you’re in for a treat.

At Quincy Market and the Boston Public Market, you can find an array of local specialties, from seafood to farm-fresh produce.

After swift check-in at a dedicated counter, unwind in one of our elegant Business Class lounges. Head to one of the private workstations to finish a few last-minute tasks, take a shower to freshen up, or retreat to a quiet area and recharge before your flight.

Spacious seats boasting an ergonomic design, combined with ambient lighting, create the ideal environment for relaxation. Book a Business or First Class flight to Philadelphia with Qatar Airways and bask in unmatched comfort.
US.PHL.touristAttractionsText:
If you know of one attraction to see in Philadelphia, it’s likely the Liberty Bell – a symbol of freedom, with its famous crack that’s echoed through centuries of American history. Continue the historical journey and step into the footsteps of revolutionaries at the Independence Hall, where the Declaration of Independence was signed.

Embrace Philly’s spirit of grit and resilience at the Rocky Statue and the iconic Rocky Steps. Join the masses jogging up the steps, recreating that legendary moment. When you reach the top, the sweeping views of the city are a reward of their own.

Meander through Love Park, where the picturesque LOVE sculpture stands tall. End your day along the Delaware River waterfront, with its lively boardwalk, restaurants and scenic views.
US.PHL.leisureActivitiesText:
Philadelphia’s artsy heart beats along Benjamin Franklin Parkway. Culture fills every corner, starting with the Barnes Foundation, where walls are bursting with masterpieces by Renoir, Cézanne and Matisse. Around the corner, the Franklin Institute is abundant with interactive exhibits and the colossal Benjamin Franklin National Memorial.

For a hidden gem, explore the Philadelphia Magic Gardens on South Street. It’s an outdoor mosaic wonderland crafted by a local artist. Every inch of wall and ground is covered in vibrant tiles and mirror fragments.

For an escape about an hour outside the city, head to Chester County and visit the Longwood Gardens. It’s a floral fantasy, spread over 1,000 acres with exotic plants, fountains and woodlands. If you are lucky, you may catch a flower show or live concert.
US.PHL.shoppingText:
South Street and Baltimore Avenue are dotted with quirky boutiques and vintage finds. Uncover one-of-a-kind art pieces, handmade jewellery and trendy clothing that captures Philly’s eclectic vibe.

On 52nd Street, delve into art galleries, bookstores and locally owned shops. Known as West Philly’s Main Street, it’s a haven for unique and independent stores. Not far away, Chinatown brims with shops selling traditional wares, Asian groceries and bright red lanterns.

If you’re drawn to sparkle, Jewellers’ Row is America’s oldest diamond district, with generations-old jewellers crafting everything from engagement rings to custom creations. Upscale shopping is not hard to find either in Rittenhouse Square. The brownstones and high-rises surround you with a mix of luxury retailers.
US.PHL.destinationPageIntro: Discover Philadelphia, rich with history and art. Snap a photo with the Liberty Bell and indulge in a Philly cheesesteak. There’s lots to explore in the City of Brotherly Love.
US.PHL.overviewText:
Known as the City of Brotherly Love, there’s no doubt you can feel right at home in Philadelphia. It’s the birthplace of America, where the ideals of freedom and independence took root and you can find echoes of its revolutionary past at every turn.

However, Philadelphia, or Philly as it’s playfully referred to, is more than just its storied past. Its neighbourhoods buzz with creativity, art and energy. Wander down streets decorated with colourful murals or head to the scenic waterfront for an idyllic evening stroll. Culinary enthusiasts are also in for a treat with internationally-acclaimed dishes and bustling markets that tempt you to savour every flavour the city has to offer.

Whether you’re here for the museums, the cheesesteaks or the historical landmarks, Philly will draw you in.
US.PHL.eatingImageText:
A trip to Philadelphia wouldn’t be complete without a world-famous Philly cheesesteak. This mouth-watering combo of thinly sliced steak, melted cheese, and onions are packed into a soft roll. There’s an art to ordering it too. You can say, “I want a philly cheesesteak whiz wit”, for cheese whiz and onions – the classic way to go.

The Reading Terminal Market is a must-visit, where you can order soft Philly pretzels – golden and chewy, with just the right amount of salt. Over at the Italian Market, vendors serve up hoagies, loaded with meats, cheese and vegetables tucked into a long, Italian roll. Try tomato pie too – a Sicilian-style pizza with thick, focaccia-like dough topped with tomato sauce and a sprinkle of parmesan.

Finally, for a sweet treat, try water ice. This smooth, refreshing dessert is made from Italian ice and comes in a variety of fruity flavours. You get also get it topped with custard, which is called a gelati.

CN.HGH.touristAttractionsText:
West Lake lies at the heart of Hangzhou – a peaceful expanse of water fringed by parks, pathways and viewpoints. Take a boat ride or stay after dark to watch the Impression West Lake light show, a magical fusion of light, music and performance.

For a deeper cultural experience, visit Lingyin and wander round the majestic pagodas and grottos. Nearby, the hills are lined with the Longjing Tea Plantation, the birthplace of the region’s famed Dragon Well tea.

Step into the elegant world of Qing Dynasty merchants at the Former Residence of Hu Xueyan, a wonderfully preserved historic home. For panoramic views over the Qiantang River, climb to the top of the Liuhe (Six Harmonies) Pagoda before ending your day with a lakeside dinner.
CN.HGH.leisureActivitiesText:
A walk around West Lake is a perfect way to experience Hangzhou’s natural beauty, with leafy paths leading past Lingyin Road and the city’s Botanical Gardens. The route winds through bamboo groves and landscaped gardens, or you can hire a boat to explore the lake’s two scenic islands.

Just outside the city, hiking trails lead into the hills. The path from Baochu Pagoda is a gentle climb with rewarding views over Hangzhou’s rooftops. 
Tea culture is central to local life. For an authentic experience, head to Meijiawu Village to watch Longjing tea being picked and enjoy a fresh brew in a hillside teahouse.

As evening falls, take a Grand Canal Night Cruise and see the city illuminated from the water – a serene way to end the day.
CN.HGH.shoppingText:
Begin your shopping experience at Wulin Square, the centre of Hangzhou’s commercial district. Here, sleek malls and designer boutiques offer everything from global fashion brands to Chinese couture, electronics and luxury souvenirs.

For a more traditional atmosphere, stroll along Hefang Street, a charming pedestrian area known for its heritage architecture and stalls selling silk, tea, calligraphy sets and porcelain.

As the sun sets, head to Wushan Night Market, where the air fills with the scent of street food spices and stalls display handcrafted goods, jewellery and keepsakes.

For something truly special, visit Wushan Square or the eastern edge of West Lake to find local artists selling watercolour landscapes and traditional paintings – the perfect way to take home a piece of Hangzhou’s cultural charm.
CN.HGH.destinationPageIntro: Hangzhou weaves together centuries of culture, history, and trade, offering a timeless Chinese experience amid the tranquil beauty of the Zhejiang countryside.
CN.HGH.overviewText:
Nestled on the banks of the iconic West Lake, Hangzhou is where Chinese history, culture, and natural wonders unite. Once the largest city in the medieval world and now a UNESCO World Heritage Site, it offers an immersive tapestry of experiences. 

At its heart lies the shimmering lake that has inspired poets and artists for centuries. Bustling marketplaces reflect its past as a Silk Road trading hub, while leafy streets reveal the multi-layered character Marco Polo called ‘the finest and noblest in the world’.

The surrounding landscape is breathtaking, with classical pagodas and terraced tea plantations where the scent of Longjing tea fills the air. Fly to Hangzhou with Qatar Airways and discover a city shaped by legend, nature, and timeless elegance.
CN.HGH.destinationHighlightsH1: Hangzhou: Centuries of trade and culture
CN.HGH.eatingImageText:
Hefang Street is the best place to discover Hangzhou’s local tea houses and eateries. Start with a cup of Longjing tea, served with delicate Chinese pastries and savoury snacks. For a taste of tradition, try West Lake fish in sweet and sour sauce – a bold yet refined local favourite. Another signature dish is shelled shrimp stewed with Longjing tea, pairing the region’s prized brew with fresh seafood.

For a non-seafood option, Beggar’s Chicken – marinated, wrapped in lotus leaves, and slow-baked – delivers a fragrant, hearty meal.

Tofu is a staple here, often prepared with a signature blend of eight herbs and spices. For dessert, look out for Victory Cake, made with rice flour and filled with red bean or lotus seed paste – best enjoyed fresh at the Wushan Night Market.

PH.DVO.touristAttractionsText:
The Philippines is renowned for its natural wonders. One of its rarest is the Philippine eagle or monkey-eating eagle. This endangered species has its home in the forests around Mount Apo, and you can visit the Philippine Eagle Centre to meet this magnificent bird.

Experienced hikers can admire more of the country’s wildlife during a challenging climb up Mount Apo’s trails, and be rewarded with stunning views. If you prefer something more relaxing, stop by Samal Island, a tropical paradise that’s just a short distance off the coast.

Urbanites will love shopping and dining in the city, as well as the entertainment options showcasing the Philippines' rich cultural heritage through captivating music and dance. And if you love chocolate, a visit to the Malagos Chocolate Museum is a must!
PH.DVO.leisureActivitiesText:
This region of the Philippines has been inhabited for centuries. A trip to Kadayawan Village lets you see how the indigenous Lumad and Muslim Moro people lived. You’ll also get a glimpse of the region’s architecture in Magsaysay Park, downtown Davao.

To explore flora and fauna, head to Eden Nature Park, which has plenty of activities including the Sky Rider and Sky Swing attractions. The park is also home to accessible and gentle hiking trails for all ages.

For an authentic Filipino experience, go island hopping to Malipano Island or Taklobo Sanctuary. Here, you can snorkel in the crystal-clear water and visit attractions like the Samal Coral Garden or the Starfish Sanctuary.
PH.DVO.shoppingText:
Davao is a shopper’s delight, especially its night markets. The Roxas Night Market is a vibrant spot frequented by locals and the best place in the city to try mouth-watering street food.

For a luxurious shopping spree, make your way to downtown Davao, also known as the Poblacion District. It’s home to several large malls where you can enjoy some well-deserved retail therapy. You’ll come across plenty of global brands at electronics stores, fashion outlets and more. Abreeza Mall is the most popular, offering exciting entertainment and an extensive food hall.

As you roam around the city, you’ll stumble upon more artisan shops, boutiques and galleries selling handmade artwork. It’s worth venturing away from the main downtown zone to relish a more unique experience in the side streets.
PH.DVO.destinationPageIntro: Davao combines breath-taking natural beauty and vibrant urban excitement. Surrounded by lush forests, it’s a warm, friendly and welcoming destination all year round.
PH.DVO.overviewText:
With the majestic and mysterious Mount Apo towering in the distance and the white-sand beaches of the Pacific coast just a few minutes away, Davao boasts a fascinating combination of seaside wonders and urban marvels. Buzzing with energy, it welcomes you with irresistible cuisine, high-end shopping and warm Filipino hospitality wherever you go.

Stroll through markets selling exotic fruits and handmade crafts, explore the forested slopes of the mountain, or go on a serene boat ride along the river. After discovering new flavours and places, find your own peaceful hideaway next to the sea in beach huts that reach out over the clear blue water.

Davao is an intimate destination with all the convenience of modern life at your fingertips.
PH.DVO.eatingImageText:
Davao is renowned for its exotic array of fruits and vegetables, the most famous of which has to be the durian. This delicious fruit may be pungent, but its flesh has a creamy, custard-like texture. It has inspired many of the local dishes including durian candy, ice cream and even a cake!

The city definitely indulges your sweet tooth because its other claim to culinary fame is Malagos chocolate, made from cacao only grown in this region. Its distinctive flavour is famous around the world.

Filipino cuisine features a blend of Asian influences, so expect delectable dishes infused with spices. Given the city’s large Muslim population, there are plenty of halal restaurants too, many of which are found in the downtown area.

PH.CRK.touristAttractionsText:
Trek to the summit of Nabuclod Mountain for panoramic views of the lush landscapes that the Philippines is known for. Admire the breathtaking vista of rolling hills, rivers and faraway towns. Adventure calls again at Mount Pinatubo, with its famous crater lake – a serene, turquoise gem surrounded by rugged terrain. After the volcano erupted in 1991, the dramatic scenes around the lake include rocky valleys and lava fields.

If you’re a history buff, make your way to the Clark Museum, where vibrant exhibits showcase the rich cultural heritage of the city. There are ancient artefacts and modern aviation stories – a plethora of exhibitions that perfectly summarise the city of Clark.
PH.CRK.leisureActivitiesText:
Clark is a playground for those seeking a blend of fun, relaxation and a dash of history. Take advantage of the surroundings and indulge in a volcanic sand spa treatment. Sinking into the warm, molten sand will melt away any tension – it’s rejuvenation courtesy of nature.

For family-friendly thrills, take your pick of the water parks and amusement parks on offer in the area – sure to keep all ages entertained. 

For a touch of the city's aviation history, head to Air Force City Park, where vintage planes stand proudly on display. It’s a fascinating glimpse of the Philippines’ aviation heritage, providing a chance to marvel at these sky warriors up close.
PH.CRK.shoppingText:
Flock to the bustling duty-free shops for international goods of designer labels, luxury perfumes and fine chocolates.

Some of Clark’s traditional markets offer a slice of Filipino culture, where you can stroll around colourful stalls of handicrafts, woven textiles, and handmade jewellery. For an upscale experience, there are numerous sleek shopping malls filled with trendy boutiques, electronics stores, and high-end dining spots.
PH.CRK.destinationPageIntro: Discover the quiet side of the Philippines in Clark and explore volcanic landscapes, relax at unique spas, play in adventure parks and indulge in local, Filipino cuisine.
PH.CRK.overviewText:
Nestled in the heart of Pampanga, Clark offers a quiet, laid-back getaway in the Philippines. It’s the perfect place for travellers looking to escape the busy cities and enjoy a slower, more peaceful atmosphere. With its tree-lined streets and wide-open spaces, Clark feels worlds away from any chaos, yet it’s only a three-hour drive from Manila.

The town’s suburban charm blends natural and contemporary comforts. Mountains and volcanic landscapes surround the area, offering endless opportunities for outdoor enthusiasts. Whether you are exploring local Kapampangan cuisine, wandering through duty-free shops, or simply enjoying the calm, Clark is poised for discovery. Venture off-the-beaten-path and discover the hidden gems of Clark.
PH.CRK.destinationHighlightsH1: Clark: Hidden gem of the Philippines
PH.CRK.eatingImageText:
At the centre of Clark’s food scene is Kapampangan cuisine. Renowned for its bold dishes, each meal is prepared with recipes passed down through generations. Delve into a plate of kare-kare – tender oxtail and vegetables stewed in a velvety, peanut sauce, and served with a side of prawn paste called bagoong.

Enjoy more Filipino meals, from the comforting chicken adobo to the irresistible sweetness of halo-halo on a hot day (a mix of crushed ice, fruit, and coconut or evaporated milk). 

Visit some of the farm-to-table establishments that are popular in Clark. Savour organic produce harvested from nearby farms and taste local flavours.

Those with an international palate, Clark has plenty for indulgence. From premium cuts at one of the city’s steak houses, to cafés with a European flair.

PK.LHE.touristAttractionsText:
The cultural heart of Pakistan is packed with attractions, most conveniently located near the city centre. Begin your sightseeing journey at the Badshahi Mosque, where the stunning red sandstone façade and surrounding lush gardens offer a glimpse into the Mughal era. Adjacent to the mosque lies the Lahore Fort, home to the Sheesh Mahal, or the Palace of Mirrors, one of the fort’s most cherished treasures.

As you exit, stroll through the Raushnai Gate, a symbol of Lahore’s spirit and the historic entrance to the fort. And, don’t miss the Wazir Khan Mosque, renowned for its exquisite tile work and mesmerising, intricate designs.
PK.LHE.leisureActivitiesText:
Immerse yourself into Lahore’s rich cultural scene by visiting the Lahore Museum, which houses an impressive collection of historical and artistic artefacts from the Mughal era and beyond.

For an outdoor adventure, head to the Lahore Wildlife Park on the city’s outskirts, perfect for families and animal enthusiasts. To experience more of Pakistan’s natural beauty, venture to the Changa Manga Forest, one of the largest and oldest man-made forests, complete with a wildlife preserve.

A day trip to witness the Wagah Border Ceremony is also a must. This spectacular military ritual features a display of synchronised marching that showcases their national pride. The ritual attracts large crowds daily, with many tours departing from the city centre.
PK.LHE.shoppingText:
Lahore’s shopping scene is a vibrant mix, but it’s the traditional markets that truly stand out, offering a treasure trove of handcrafted items and unique souvenirs.

Delhi Gate, located in the heart of the Old City, is renowned for its jewellery, handwoven fabrics, and beautiful pottery and ceramics. The historic setting adds to the charm of wandering through its bustling streets.

Anarkali Bazaar is another must-visit. This bustling market offers a sensory feast with authentic clothing, aromatic spices and colourful textiles. Be sure to check out the khussa shoes – these locally made footwear pieces blend comfort with intricate designs, making them a perfect souvenir.

Liberty Market is another gem, known for its bespoke handicrafts and eclectic array of shops and boutiques.
PK.LHE.destinationPageIntro: Start with Lahore Fort and Badshahi Mosque in the famous Walled City, then capture memories at Raushnai Gate. For a nature escape, venture to Changa Manga Forest.
PK.LHE.overviewText:
Lahore, a city rich in Pakistani history and culture, offers an immersive experience filled with a mix of vibrant sights, sounds, and aromas. Each corner of this lively city bursts with life and colour, inviting you to explore its many facets. From the bustling bazaars brimming with artisanal crafts and street food, to the ancient traditions and religious landmarks, Lahore caters to every traveller’s interests, providing a diverse array of experiences.

The city’s warmth and hospitality will make you feel right at home, while its dynamic atmosphere ensures there’s always something new to discover. Whether you’re here for a short visit or an extended stay, Lahore is sure to impress.
PK.LHE.destinationHighlightsH1: Lahore: The cultural heart of Pakistan
PK.LHE.eatingImageText:
Lahore is a street food haven, with food streets scattered throughout the city. Start your adventure at Gawalmandi Food Street, where traditional and contemporary delights blend seamlessly. Enjoy modern restaurants that reinterpret classic recipes, or browse the menu in an old dhaba (a traditional roadside eatery) and try paya – a slow-cooked, flavourful stew made from the hooves of cow, goat or sheep.

Lahore Fort Food Street offers several rooftop restaurants with historical charm, while Lakshmi Chowk Food Street serves up the true flavours of Pakistan with spicy chaat and crispy samosas.

Don’t forget to treat yourself to the Lahore speciality, halwa puri. This beloved dish combines sweet and savoury flavours with fried bread, sweet semolina pudding, and chickpea gravy or potato curry.

PK.ISB.touristAttractionsText:
The Faisal Mosque is Islamabad’s most iconic landmark. As the fifth largest mosque in the world, its impressive contemporary architecture and serene ambiance make it a must-visit attraction. Next, explore the Pakistan Monument, a national symbol that represents the provinces and territories of Pakistan. The adjoining museum details rich stories of the country’s history and heritage.

For an educational family activity, visit the Pakistan Museum of Natural History, which houses exhibits on the country’s diverse natural past.

Travel outside of the city to Shah Allah Ditta Caves, nestled in the Margalla Hills. These prehistoric limestone caves are an absolute marvel and the surrounding trails are incredible hiking locations.
PK.ISB.leisureActivitiesText:
Outdoor activities are abundant in Islamabad, with the majestic Margalla Hills situated just a few kilometres from the city centre. It provides an ideal setting for rock climbing and hiking, including the Dara Janglan – otherwise known as Hiking Trail 5. This scenic nature walk is also popular for bird watching. The nearby Bruti Waterfall is a hidden gem and typical rest stop for hikers.

Take a car out of the city to Rawal Lake for water-based activities. It is an idyllic spot for boating, fishing and a picnic by the waters.

For a more relaxing encounter, head to Fatima Jinnah Park, also known as F-9 Park. It’s a great space for picnics and leisurely walks. Shakarparian National Park is another recreational place that offers panoramic views of Islamabad and Rawalpindi.
PK.ISB.shoppingText:
Whether you’re looking for modern convenience or traditional marketplaces, Islamabad has it all.

The city has numerous malls filled with international brands, homegrown boutiques, dining and entertainment. For a more local experience, browse the Sunday Bazaar. Held weekly, you can purchase anything from fresh produce to handmade crafts.

Jinnah Market is renowned for its unique offerings and bespoke souvenirs. Find the Jinnah cap, made of local sheep wool, or intricately designed Sindhi topi, which is a cultural accessory. You can also find pottery with intricate designs and Pashmina shawls.
PK.ISB.destinationPageIntro: Islamabad is lush with greenery and the Margalla Hills are great for rock-climbing. Complete your trip to Pakistan’s capital by exploring the Faisal Mosque.
PK.ISB.overviewText:
Islamabad, the capital city of Pakistan, is not only a city of culture and history but it’s also a place of distinct natural beauty. Picturesque hills and vast lakes are located just minutes from the city centre, making it a destination of adventure, relaxation and culture.

The city itself is renowned for its stunning architecture, and thriving food and arts scene. Discover modern landmarks, explore the old parts of town and embrace the tranquillity of its natural surroundings.

With its extensive historical past, diversity and beautiful landscapes, Islamabad invites visitors to experience the best of Pakistan.
PK.ISB.eatingImageText:
Head to Saidpur Village for authentic Pakistani street food. Indulge in pani puri (hollow, fried dough balls filled with potatoes), crispy samosas, flavourful fritters called pakoras, and tangy chaat – crispy, fried dough wafers. F-10 Markaz is also an area filled with international street food, serving everything from burgers to samosas.

Pakistani barbecue is another must-try, with juicy kebabs and spicy tikka demonstrating the country’s grilling traditions. Make sure to try a traditional breakfast, featuring halwa puri – fried flatbread served with a semolina pudding, nihari – a spiced beef stew, and parathas – flaky flatbread.

Islamabad Food Street is a hotspot for even more local foods, but also international cuisine. Be sure to taste Pakistan’s most favoured dish, biryani, which consists of layers of spiced rice and tender meat.

PK.SKT.touristAttractionsText:
Start your journey at the Iqbal Manzil, the birthplace of Allama Iqbal, Pakistan’s beloved philosopher-poet. You can wander through its beautifully preserved rooms and browse all sorts of interesting artefacts. 

The Allama Iqbal Library is an absolute must-visit for book lovers and history buffs. Housed in a grand building, it offers a serene space to reflect on the legacy of knowledge and wisdom that has shaped the city.

If you’re interested in architecture, check out the Sialkot Cathedral and admire its soaring spires, stained-glass windows and distinct Gothic feel. Just a short walk from there, you’ll find the Shawala Teja Singh Temple, which also stands as a testament to Sialkot’s multicultural past with its intricate carvings. Don’t miss the Sialkot Fort – an ancient stronghold with mesmerising views of the city.
PK.SKT.leisureActivitiesText:
Start your day with a refreshing stroll through Gulshan-e-Iqbal Park. This lush haven is bursting with vibrant flowerbeds and tree-lined paths – it’s the perfect spot for a morning walk, a family picnic, or unwinding amongst nature. 

Calling all sports fans – Jinnah Stadium is a landmark you won’t want to miss. Once a proud host of international cricket matches, this iconic venue now buzzes with local events and sports gatherings.

Make your way to Fatima Jinnah Garrison Park for a little break from the city’s hustle and bustle. This sprawling green space is ideal for a night out. Here, you’ll find well-maintained walking tracks, playgrounds for kids, and plenty of quiet nooks to relax and unwind.
PK.SKT.shoppingText:
You simply can’t talk about Sialkot shopping without mentioning its world-renowned sporting goods. If you’re a sports enthusiast, then you’re in for a treat – you’ll find a wide variety of high-quality items, from cricket bats to footballs and boxing gear.

Prepare to be amazed by Sialkot’s exquisite leather goods. The city’s talented artisans have mastered the art of transforming leather into stylish handbags and jackets, unique accessories and more. Their quality rivals global brands, but with a distinctive Sialkot touch.

Looking for something special? The Sarafa Bazaar is a glittering maze of gold, silver and jewellery shops – the ideal spot to pick out a sparkling keepsake. And if you’re after vibrant fabrics or traditional attire, a visit to Shahabpura Bazaar is a must. Finally, Anarkali Bazaar is where you’ll find handcrafted trinkets and indulge in some delectable street food.
PK.SKT.destinationPageIntro: Sialkot, Pakistan’s historical gem, is known for its innovative industry, rich cultural heritage and one-of-a-kind Punjab charm.
PK.SKT.overviewText:
Nestled right in the heart of Punjab, you’ll find Sialkot, often called the Birmingham of Pakistan – and for good reason. It’s a buzzing hub of craftsmanship and industry, celebrated across the globe for its production of sporting goods and leatherware. But Sialkot is much more than its industrious reputation – it’s a city brimming with culture, history and charm.

The city proudly carries the legacy of Pakistan’s national poet Allama Iqbal, who serves as a beacon of inspiration. As you wander around, you’ll discover the city is filled with historic landmarks, unique artisanal treasures, vibrant parks and delicious cuisine.

Whether you’re here to explore its heritage or marvel at its innovative spirit, Sialkot invites you to experience a city like no other.
PK.SKT.eatingImageText:
When it comes to food, Pakistan truly knows how to please the palate, and Sialkot is no exception. Indulge in their traditional tandoori chicken. It’s marinated in a medley of spices and cooked to perfection in a clay oven for a tender, charred and absolutely delicious flavour.

For something heartier, try bhuna gosht – a rich and flavourful dish that embodies the essence of Pakistani cuisine. Meat is slowly cooked in aromatic spices and paired with warm, fluffy naan.

No visit to Sialkot is complete without tasting nihari, the ultimate comfort food. This slow-cooked stew of beef or mutton is a beloved breakfast tradition here. Another classic favourite you must try is biryani – basmati rice layered with spiced chicken or beef.

PK.MUX.touristAttractionsText:
The Shrine of Bahauddin Zakariya is one of the top things to do in Multan while you’re here. Built in the early-mid 13th century, it is one of the earliest examples of Multan’s distinctive architecture. The beauty of its blue tiles and serene ambience gives you a respite from the hustle and bustle of the city. The Urs Bahauddin Zakariya festival is held yearly here. 

Multan has always been a strategically important location, and its fort is a reminder of its history. The impressive Damdama is the main surviving gateway, offering spectacular panoramic views over the city.

Another prominent landmark to visit is Ghanta Ghar, the Clock Tower of Multan. A central point around which urban life revolves in Multan, it houses the city’s municipal offices and council hall, as well as souqs.
PK.MUX.leisureActivitiesText:
Cricket culture is big in Pakistan, making it an integral sport in the country. The Multan Cricket Stadium, home to the Multan Sultans, is a destination not to be missed. Catch a game to experience the vibrant and passionate atmosphere – a fun activity when you’re in town. 

To escape the summer heat, explore the banks of the Chenab River. It’s a wonderfully relaxing way to experience the natural wonder of the Punjab and its lush landscape.

For some peace and serenity, visit Shahi Eid Gah Mosque. Explore its breathtaking classical Islamic design. During Eid, it’s a focal point for the Muslim community.

Cultural festivals are also abundant throughout the year. If you happen be in town, it’s not something to miss. From live performances, exhibitions, dancing and music, to street food vendors and special menus in the city’s restaurants, it’s a celebration of Multan’s rich heritage and traditions.
PK.MUX.shoppingText:
Shopping in Multan ranges from traditional souqs and markets to air-conditioned malls. The top destination is the Mall of Multan on Bosan Road, filled with national and international brands, a food hall, and entertainment options. If you love malls, United Mall near the Multan Cantt commercial district is another favourite and a great family-friendly location.

To live like a local, Hussain Agahi Bazar is the place to head for an authentic souq experience. Look out for the Landa Bazar, one of the oldest flea markets in the city and a great place to find something unique. The city is famous for its artisan leatherwork, stunning textiles and distinctive blue pottery, all of which you’ll find in its galleries, shops and markets.
PK.MUX.destinationPageIntro: From ancient mausoleums to busy markets, fine dining and serene scenes, Multan is one of Pakistan’s true gems that takes you on a journey through time.
PK.MUX.overviewText:
Ancient and mysterious yet playful and welcoming, Multan is a hidden gem in the heart of the Punjab region. This is a city of stories and culture, fabulous architecture and a deep history. 

Known also as the City of Saints, Multan’s history stretches back over 5,000 years. Here, you’ll find tales of history’s greats as you walk along its cobbled streets and busy souqs.

A stroll through the city streets is a journey through the ages, with beauty at every corner. From the blue tiles of the Mausoleum of Shah Rukn-e-Alam to the vibrant markets that have welcomed traders and merchants for thousands of years, Multan is a feast for the senses. Sample exotic and delicious food and experience the warm and friendly welcome from locals who make you feel a part of this legendary city.
PK.MUX.eatingImageText:
Multan’s foodscape is a revelation for even the most refined palate, offering rich flavours and delicious delights. Multan has been at the centre of so many civilisations over the course of its history that the various culinary influences make its cuisine complex and interesting. 

Local dishes represent its place as an important trading post close to the spice routes that intertwine across southern Asia. Combine this with the plentiful citrus fruits that grow in the area and you have the tangy, zesty flavor of Multani Sohan Halwa, a sweet treat.

Multani Sajji will make your mouth water. Enjoy a combination of succulent lamb or chicken marinated in a unique blend of herbs and spices, cooked over an open fire on skewers. Then, indulge in a sweet ending to your meal, with a refreshing mango.

IN.DEL.businessClassSummary:
Fly to Delhi in Business or First Class with Qatar Airways and enjoy a seamless experience from the moment you arrive at the airport. Thanks to dedicated check-in counters and swift immigration processing, you can handle all the formalities easily. 

For a calm start to your trip, relax in one of our Business Class lounges before departure. Nibble on a freshly made snack, take a refreshing shower, or use a private workstation to prepare for meetings. If you’re in the mood to unwind, simply recline and relish a few quiet minutes to yourself before boarding. 

Once on board, settle into an ergonomically designed seat with ample space. Ambient lighting supports your body clock, and highspeed WiFi on our A380, A350, B787 and select B777 aircraft, keeps you connected. Dine on your own schedule by choosing a meal from our à la carte menu whenever you like, before browsing our extensive entertainment selection. When it’s time to rest, convert your seat into a fully lie-flat bed and drift off to sleep. Touch down feeling refreshed and ready to explore an energetic city. 

Book your Business or First Class flight to Delhi with Qatar Airways and travel in unparalleled luxury.
IN.DEL.touristAttractionsText:
Start your Delhi expedition with a visit to Humayun’s Tomb. This UNESCO World Heritage site, and precursor to the Taj Mahal, is a sight of magnificence with its symmetrical design and Persian-inspired architecture.

Make your way to the Red Fort, another UNESCO World Heritage site, to experience the grandeur of India’s rich Mughal heritage. Spend some time analysing the intricate carvings and majestic structures that narrate the city’s past.

Naturally, a trip to Delhi must include a tour to Jama Masjid, India’s largest mosque. Climb the steps of its minaret and be rewarded with a panoramic view of Old Delhi.
