For a moment of peace, head to the Lotus Temple. Known for its stunning lotus-shaped design, the temple is architecturally spectacular and evokes a peaceful ambiance away from the bustling city.
IN.DEL.leisureActivitiesText:
Take a morning stroll through Lodhi Gardens, a flourishing oasis located in the heart of the city. Enjoy manicured gardens and uncover historic tombs, found throughout this tranquil retreat.

Witness the Change of Guard ceremony at Rashtrapati Bhavan, the official residence of the President of India. The spectacle of precision and tradition offers a unique glimpse into India’s ceremonial customs.

Dive into the world of Indian Art at the National Museum, home to an extensive collection that spans over 5,000 years of history. From paintings to sculptures and everything in between, this museum showcases a journey through time.

For a taste of modern Delhi, explore the eclectic mix of galleries, chic boutiques and colourful cafés in Hauz Khas Village.
IN.DEL.shoppingText:
For an authentic shopping experience, wander through the hidden nooks of Old Delhi. Discover all kinds of markets, including the spice bazaar where the air is thick with aromas of cardamom, cinnamon and saffron.

Connaught Place has numerous government emporiums that sell high-quality Indian handicrafts, textiles and traditional art. If you’re a bargain hunter, the flea market stalls on Janpath are a must-visit, stocking everything from clothing to quirky souvenirs. For a more upscale atmosphere, go to Khan Market, renowned for its high-end boutiques.

Dilli Haat is another must-do. It’s abundant with artisans that travelled across India to showcase their crafts. From handmade jewellery to pottery, it’s the perfect place to source an authentic and unique souvenir.
IN.DEL.destinationPageIntro: The heart of India is rich with ancient heritage and diversity. Delhi locals welcome you with their festive and vibrant culture.
IN.DEL.overviewText:
Delhi, the heart of India, is a vibrant blend of diversity in cultures, traditions and lifestyles. The streets pulse with life, from the bustling markets of Old Delhi to the tree-lined avenues of New Delhi. Marvel at ancient monuments and admire contemporary buildings – every corner of this city tells a story of its evolution.

Discover festivals, multifaceted neighbourhoods, and artistic expressions – there is no part of Delhi that won’t delight the senses. Whether you’re a history enthusiast looking to explore Delhi’s storied past, or a passionate foodie wanting to savour the world-renowned culinary scene, Delhi’s atmosphere will leave you inspired and longing for more.
IN.DEL.destinationHighlightsH1: Delhi: The vibrant heart of India
IN.DEL.eatingImageText:
Embark on a gastronomic adventure in the busy streets of Old Delhi, where street food reigns supreme. Indulge in golgappa or spicy papdi chaat – fried savoury snacks made with a mix of chickpeas, potatoes, spices and chutneys – great to enjoy on the go. If you’re craving something sweet, try jalebi rabdi – crispy deep-fried flat spirals, soaked in thickened milk and topped with cardamom and pistachios.

Hop on a rickshaw to take a food tour through Chandni Chowk to sample an array of delicacies in a lively atmosphere. Try masala dosa – a South Indian specialty of crispy crepes filled with spiced potatoes. Whether you’re indulging in street food or savouring classic favourites, Delhi’s flavours will leave you craving more.

IN.BLR.touristAttractionsText:
Begin your Bengaluru trip with a visit to the ISKCON Temple, located just outside the city centre. The temple’s stunning design is something to marvel at and the atmosphere is often alive with spiritual activities. 

Drop in to the historic Bull Temple which is dedicated to Nandi (the bull) and showcases impressive Dravidian architecture. For another deep dive into Bengaluru’s ancient history and royal heritage, check out the majestic Bangalore Palace with its Tudor-style designs, luscious gardens and opulent interiors. Nearby, Tipu Sultan’s Summer Palace provides an example of Indo-Islamic architecture. 

If you’re visiting with your little ones, take a short train or bus ride away from the city to an amusement park. It has rides, water play and entertainment that the whole family will enjoy.
IN.BLR.leisureActivitiesText:
Take a morning stroll through the Lalbagh Botanical Garden, a flourishing sanctuary renowned for its exotic plant species and a glasshouse. Cubbon Park is another ideal spot for nature lovers and those seeking a calm and relaxing atmosphere – it’s perfect for afternoon picnics and sightseeing.

For a glimpse of Bengaluru’s wildlife, head out of the city to Bannerghatta Biological Park. Home to tigers, lions, elephants, a butterfly park and more, it’s a great destination for a day well spent outdoors.

If you’re an art enthusiast, don’t miss the National Gallery of Modern Art. Housed in a colonial-era mansion, this gallery showcases the country’s dynamic creative scene in a superior setting.
IN.BLR.shoppingText:
The array of shopping in Bengaluru matches the variety of food destinations in this Indian city, with plenty of shopping encounters to cater to every taste and style. Browse Vittal Mallya Road, dotted with upscale shopping complexes featuring high-end brands and designer boutiques.

The Erstwhile South Parade – once a grand avenue – is still lined with landmarks and multifaceted shops that are abundant with authentic Indian textiles, handcrafted jewellery and unique souvenirs. Bring home sandalwood products, silk textiles or even their cherished coffee powder as souvenirs.

Commercial Street is another must-do retail location. This bustling market is a treasure trove of fashionable clothing, accessories, trinkets and even electronics.
IN.BLR.destinationPageIntro: Explore an Indian capital city with a thriving art scene, vibrant culinary landscape, and eclectic shopping choices. There’s something for everyone to enjoy in Bengaluru.
IN.BLR.overviewText:
Known as the ‘Silicon Valley of India’, Bengaluru is a hub of innovation that offers a variety of both modern and traditional experiences. Karnataka’s urban capital is busy with professionals from near and far, as well as families and solo travellers. The city landscape is dotted with lush greenery creating a refreshing atmosphere in a majorly cosmopolitan city. Its thriving art scene, vibrant culinary experiences and eclectic shopping options ensure that there’s something for everyone to enjoy.

Whether you are attracted to its entrepreneurial spirit, its rich cultural tapestry or welcoming ambience, Bengaluru promises an enriching holiday.
IN.BLR.destinationHighlightsH1: Bengaluru: The Silicon Valley of India
IN.BLR.eatingImageText:
Begin your gastronomic journey at Bengaluru’s most iconic food spot, Thindi Beedi in VV Puram. The road is alive with dining and festivities in the evenings, providing a plethora of mouth-watering Indian treats to savour. Taste your way through the many popular crepes and flatbreads including dosas (a savoury crepe), akki rotti (a vegetable and spice flatbread) and sweet holige (a sweet flatbread). The variety of flavours in this street food market is unmatched.

Be sure to indulge in a classic Indian breakfast, idli vada. Soft steamed rice cakes, paired with crispy lentil doughnuts, are served with chutneys and sambar. For something hearty, try bisi bele bath, a quintessential Karnataka dish made of a rice base, lentils, vegetables and spices. Wash it all down with a cup of fresh, local coffee.

IN.MAA.touristAttractionsText:
Begin your expedition in a city overflowing with history at Fort St. George, the first British fortress in India. This historical site now serves as a museum showcasing artefacts from the colonial period. To go deeper into India’s past, explore the Government Museum. As one of the oldest museums in India, it features an extensive collection of archaeological artefacts and Roman antiques.

Visit the spiritual landmark and architectural wonder of Kapaleeshwarar Temple. Dedicated to Lord Shiva, this Dravidian-style temple is adorned with intricate carvings. Finally, uncover the magnificence of San Thome Basilica. This neo-Gothic building is a design beauty and of great religious significance, having been built over the tomb of Saint Thomas the Apostle.
IN.MAA.leisureActivitiesText:
Hit the slopes in Chennai at Snow Kingdom. This indoor snow theme park provides a delightful escape from Chennai’s tropical climate and is perfect for families to enjoy.

If you’d prefer peace and tranquility, seek spiritual solace at Sri Ramakrishna Math. The serene environment and stunning gardens offer an unsurpassed day retreat. 

No getaway to Chennai is complete without experiencing one of its breathtaking beaches. Marina Beach, one of the world’s longest urban beaches, has radiant sunrise views and a vibrant atmosphere. If you’re hoping for a more laidback ambience, travel to Besant Nagar Beach.

Discover the wonders of Guindy National Park, situated in the middle of Chennai city. The park is home to the endangered Blackbuck, fourteen other species of mammals, several birds and more.
IN.MAA.shoppingText:
For those seeking contemporary retail therapy, there are numerous malls in Chennai that house a range of international and local brands.

Pangal Road and Ranganthan Street are bustling shopping hubs that stock everything from electronics and textiles to souvenirs and spices.

Look for a beautiful piece of artistic jewellery, presenting a timeless souvenir that also celebrates the region’s legacy. Local artisans create leaf handicrafts too, which make unique home décor pieces. Other craftwork to consider taking home with you include a pattamara mat, metal works and stone carvings. If you are an artisan yourself, you can’t leave Chennai without touring Cotton Alley to browse the vast selection of high-quality cottons.
IN.MAA.destinationPageIntro: Explore India’s extensive past, admire the architectural wonders of spiritual temples and relax on one of the longest beaches in the world. Experience the best of Chennai.
IN.MAA.overviewText:
As the thriving capital of Tamil Nadu in India, Chennai offers a captivating blend of tradition and modernity, making it an exceptional destination for a holiday or business trip. Despite its rapid modernisation, Chennai has retained its traditional charm.

Nestled along the Coromandel Coast, this dynamic city boasts a rich tapestry of cultural heritage, unique experiences and an incredible gastronomic and shopping landscape. Marvel at remarkable temples, discover awe-inspiring green spaces or relax on a magnificent beach.

Embark on a journey to Chennai – a city that promises an enriching and unforgettable experience.
IN.MAA.eatingImageText:
Chennai is a true foodie haven – everywhere you look provides a sensory feast that reflects the city’s lively spirit. In George Town and Sowcarpet Market, the street food scene is alive with vendors offering an array of snacks. Try a crispy vada – a doughnut shaped lentil fritter, or a masala dosa – a crunchy crepe filled with spiced potatoes. 

Savour the taste of idiyappam – rice flour noodles pressed into a shape and steamed, and chaat – a crispy fried savoury snack served with a jumble of chickpeas, potatoes, yoghurt sauce and chutney. Wash it all down with a hot cup of chai (spiced tea), typically presented in a clay pot which enhances the flavour and adds an earthy aroma.

IN.HYD.touristAttractionsText:
Start your Hyderabad adventure at Golconda Fort, which stands as a testament to the city’s royal past. Visit the fort in the evening to witness the sound and light show that showcases the history of the Deccan region. Near the fort, the Qutub Shahi Tombs and Paigah Tombs provide a glimpse into the opulent lifestyles of the families that once resided there.

Charminar Mosque must make your itinerary, standing as one of the most famous buildings in India. Not far away is the Mecca Masjid, one of the oldest mosques in Hyderabad.

You’ll be transported back in time as you explore the narrow lanes of Hyderabad’s Old City, one of India’s most evocative traditional quarters. Tour Chowmahalla Palace and admire its courtly halls, luscious gardens, and exquisite craftmanship.
IN.HYD.leisureActivitiesText:
A visit to Falaknuma Palace is a must. Whether you experience a luxurious stay or a delicious high tea, get ready to be treated like royalty while you marvel at the magnificent architecture and mesmerising views across the city.

Escape the bustle of the city for an afternoon at Hussain Sagar Lake, a serene oasis that provides an ideal setting for picnics and leisurely strolls. The lake is shaped like a heart, making it a beautiful setting for couples. There is also a Buddha statue in the middle of the lake, which can be visited by boat.

Explore the vibrant cultural landscape of Hyderabad at Shilparamam, an arts and crafts village that demonstrates the rich nature of Telangana. Mosey through its winding pathways with traditional huts where local artisans craft pottery, weaving and woodcarving. Be captivated by live folk performances, dance recitals and musical concerts that celebrate the region's diversity.
IN.HYD.shoppingText:
It’s time to roll out your rupees, as there are many shopping locations around Hyderabad. Immerse yourself in the lively energy of Hyderabad’s bazaars in the streets of Charminar. The stalls offer a treasure trove of souvenirs and mementos to take back home. 

Step into a world of glittering splendour at Laad Bazaar, renowned for its extravagant jewellery, especially bangles. Adorned with intricate designs and embellishments, they are the perfect Hyderabad keepsake. Next, indulge your senses in the fragrances of the Hyderabad perfume market. Artisans craft customised scents on the spot, using exotic and native ingredients.

For high-end shopping, stroll Hyderabad’s Golden Mile. This is where you will find an array of designer stores, jewellery boutiques and several malls.
IN.HYD.destinationPageIntro: The proud minarets of the 16th-century Charminar Palace and mosque, with the even older Golconda Fortress, will welcome you to Hyderabad – southern India’s jewel.
IN.HYD.overviewText:
Nestled in the heart of Southern India, Hyderabad will charm you with its history, culture and flavours. 

Also known as the City of Pearls, Hyderabad once flourished as a global centre for rare gems, diamonds and pearls. In current times, it retells this story through its monuments and ancient sites.

Discover its royal heritage firsthand in one of tje many palaces and temples. Discover the street culture as you shop in bustling bazaars and devour delectable Indian dishes.

Uncover the hidden gems of Hyderabad and embark on a historical expedition in Telangana’s capital.
IN.HYD.destinationHighlightsH1: Hyderabad: a rich tapestry of culture
IN.HYD.eatingImageText:
Delight your taste buds in Hyderabad’s Old City where the streets are lined with eateries offering a variety of Indian flavours. For a snack on the go, try a keema samosa, a baked or fried pastry filled with meat and spices. Tantalise your taste buds and order dosa with boti kebab – a savoury crepe with a skewer of lamb, served with spiced yoghurt. Be sure to quench your thirst with an Irani chai, a Hyderabad special with Persian influence. 

No trip to Hyderabad is complete without trying the city’s signature dish: biryani. Prepared with aromatic spices, fragrant rice and meat – each bite is a culinary journey to remember.

IN.COK.touristAttractionsText:
Explore Kochi’s colonial past at Fort Kochi, an area that exudes old-world allure. Explore the charming streets and marvel at the historic St. Francis Church. A short distance away stands the Dutch Palace. Donned with intricate Kerala murals and royal artefact exhibits, the palace offers a unique glimpse into the life of Kochi Rajas – the Kingdom of Cochin.

Take a break from the bustling city and stroll down Marina Drive. This beachfront promenade offers beautiful sunset views with the popular Rainbow Hanging Bridge in the backdrop.

Venture into the heart of rural Kerala at the Kumbalangi Integrated Tourism Village where you can immerse yourself in village life, undertaking activities such as crab farming, canoeing and traditional fishing.
IN.COK.leisureActivitiesText:
Uncover Kerala’s cultural background at the Kerala Folklore Museum, housing a treasure trove of artefacts, costumes and artworks that narrate the state’s colourful traditions. After this, discover the grandeur of the Hill Palace Museum in Tripunithura. It is Kerala’s first heritage museum and was once residence to the Kochi royal family.

For a dose of vitamin D, Cherai Beach is an idyllic retreat. This highly regarded beach is frequented for its golden sands and tranquil waters. It’s also a great spot for enjoying fresh seafood at nearby beachside cafés.

If you’re visiting Kochi with the whole family, plan an exhilarating theme park outing packed with thrill-seeking rides and water attractions.
IN.COK.shoppingText:
With Kochi being a spice trading hub, one of the recommended things to buy in the city is of course, spices. Explore spice markets, where the air is filled with thick aromas of cardamom, cloves, cinnamon and pepper. Take home a memorable souvenir of bottled spices to share with family and friends.

Visit the markets in Mattancherry for a unique shopping experience, where you can find antique shops brimming with treasures. Scout for ancient artefacts, exquisite jewellery and locally handcrafted items. Nearby, Mattancherry Palace also has markets to browse for classic Kerala souvenirs.
IN.COK.destinationPageIntro: In Kochi, treat your senses with rich cuisine, spice-scented markets and sights that reflect a vibrant mix of cultures.
IN.COK.overviewText:
Kochi, also known as ‘The Queen of the Arabian Sea’, is a scenic city on the southwest coast of India. Located in the state of Kerala, Kochi is renowned for its rich and diverse cultural heritage and stunning seafront location.

Travel through time at the local markets, a testament to the city’s major trading port history. Indulge in culinary delights that combine the flavours of its international influences or embark on a quest to enjoy the natural, pristine beaches. Every corner of Kochi reveals a unique experience for every traveller to enjoy.
IN.COK.destinationHighlightsH1: Kochi: The Queen of the Arabian Sea
IN.COK.eatingImageText:
Kochi presents an assorted gastronomic experience that reflects its past. The city is abundant with delectable offerings, drawing inspiration from the Portuguese, Dutch and English, along with traditional Indian influence. Begin your food discovery with fish molly, a mild, creamy fish curry that pays tribute to the fisherman legacy of the city. To further take advantage of Kochi’s coastal cuisine, delight in a fish fry – freshly caught fish marinated and fried in local spices.

Savour appam and stew, a classic breakfast dish that includes a rice pancake paired with an aromatic coconut milk stew. No visit to Kochi is complete without a trip to a toddy shop – a café serving its namesake refreshment: a fermented palm drink. Snack on some Kerala delicacies such as crab masala or banana chips, and you have the perfect accompaniment to this unique drink.

IN.CCJ.touristAttractionsText:
Mananchira Square is a peaceful oasis where manicured lawns and traditional architecture surround the Mananchira Lake. Here, visitors can relish in its charm and history. Speaking of history, venture to Beypore, one of India’s oldest ports. This famous harbour once welcomed merchants travelling through the ancient maritime silk route. Today, its shipyard still crafts traditional wooden dhow boats.

The banks of the Kallayi River should be on your Kozhikode bucket list, as the river has long been a hub for India’s timber trade. Another iconic river is the Chalippuzha River, which hosts the annual Malabar River Festival. 

Catch a glimpse of Tali Maha Shiva Kshetram for its architecture and historical significance. For a taste of Keralan tranquillity, catch the sunset and watch the dolphins at Dolphin’s Point.
IN.CCJ.leisureActivitiesText:
It wouldn’t be a holiday to Kerala without a trip to the beach. Golden sands stretch for miles at Kozhikode Beach, where locals serve up a variety of snacks. Walk further along the coastline to the historic Kappad Beach, where Vasco da Gama once set foot in India, adding a touch of history to your trip.

Alternatively, immerse yourself in the stars at the Kozhikode Planetarium. This unexpected journey brings distant galaxies to life. However, if nature is more your style, the Kadalundi Bird Sanctuary is a must-see. The serene estuary setting is where migratory birds gather.

For a little more adventure, explore the Thusharagiri and Kozhippara Waterfalls. Cascading down rugged hills, these waterfalls are surrounded by forest, mist and the cool mountain breeze.
IN.CCJ.shoppingText:
For shopping, head to Sweet Meat Street. Its stalls and shops are not only full of food but also bursting with colourful fabrics and souvenirs. If you’re looking to take home something truly local, there is a wholesale spice market filled with cinnamon, cardamom, pepper and more – a treat for culinary enthusiasts.

A shop along Town Hall Road should be on the agenda for textiles. Here, beautifully woven handloom fabrics capture the authentic elegance of Kerala, while cottons and delicate calicos make for thoughtful keepsakes. You can also find distinctive souvenirs like coir products, made from coconut fibres, and miniature models of snake boats – an ode to Kerala’s river races. For a piece of local artistry, shop for unique rosewood or buffalo horn carvings.
IN.CCJ.destinationPageIntro: With picturesque beaches, traditional architecture and riveting river rapids, Kozhikode offers the perfect combination of history and nature.
IN.CCJ.overviewText:
Nestled between rivers, rolling hills and sun-kissed beaches, Kozhikode is a city where the spirit of Malabar thrives. Often called the City of Spices, Kozhikode holds centuries of history as a bustling port and gateway to the East. Traders and travellers arrived here, leaving traces of their culture that blended well into the local vibes of today.

The beauty of Kozhikode lies in its contrasts as you stroll through its busy streets or escape to the countryside of rice paddies. Pristine beaches invite you to witness mesmerising sunsets, and rivers wind through the city lined by dense greenery.

Despite its deep-rooted traditions, Kozhikode is one of Kerala’s most developed cities, balancing modernity and a rustic atmosphere. Experience the vibrant soul of Kerala for yourself.
IN.CCJ.destinationHighlightsH1: Kozhikode: A heritage jewel in the Malabar Coast
IN.CCJ.eatingImageText:
Start your day with a classic Kerala-style breakfast of soft idiyappam – a steamed rice or noodle dish with creamy coconut milk. The entirety of Kozhikode’s food scene is a sensory marvel, like the tantalising options along Sweet Meat Street. This old lane overflows with bakeries and stalls. Make sure to try Kozhikode’s legendary halwa. For a sensory experience, explore Palayam Market, abundant with vegetables and local spices.

An unmissable delight is mussels fry, known as kallumakkaya. Freshly caught mussels are coated in spices and fried to perfection. For something heartier, indulge in pathal, a rice bread filled with coconut-infused chicken or beef. But nothing compares to the Malabar dum biriyani, a mildly spiced version layered with chicken, lamb or mutton.

IN.AMD.touristAttractionsText:
A tour of Mahatma Gandhi’s Sabarmati Ashram is a must. What once was a home to Mahatma Gandhi and Kasturba Bai, is now a museum that preserves their legacy. Learn about India’s freedom struggle as you read through his personal letters and marvel at his spinning wheel, the iconic charkha.

Explore the Jhulta Minara Sidi Bashir Mosque, famous for its shaking minarets. These 15th-century architectural enigmas defy logic. They vibrate when shaken, yet the mystery behind this marvel remains unsolved. For an architectural contrast, visit the Bai Harir Vav, a stunning sandstone stepwell with detailed carvings and underground chambers. Then make your way to Hutheesing Jain Temple, an exquisite white marble structure that radiates peace. 

For a family-friendly day out, visit Lokmanya Tilak Garden, formerly known as Victoria Garden. The park boasts scenic greenery, walkways, a children’s play area and more.
IN.AMD.leisureActivitiesText:
With so many attractions to discover, set foot on the Ahmedabad Heritage Walk. You have the option to start at the Swaminarayan Temple for the morning walk or the Siddi Saiyad Mosque for the night walk.

The journey is just over 2-kilometres long and reveals 20 of the city’s most significant cultural landmarks. Meander through ancient havelis (traditional townhouses), secret shrines, and colourful markets that eventually lead you to the majestic wonder of Jama Masjid.

After soaking up the history, head to Kankaria Lake. Hop on the toy train that circles the lake, enjoy the thrill of water rides, or get on a hot air balloon.
IN.AMD.shoppingText:
The city’s rich culture comes to life through its markets. The Law Garden Night Market is tucked away inside a lush park, providing a relaxing yet lively pedestrian-only atmosphere. It’s filled with stalls stocked with authentic Gujarati outfits, intricately embroidered chaniya cholis, and mirror-adorned kurtas. There’s also handcrafted jewellery and home décor that epitomises Indian artistry.

The Lal Darwaza Market is another must-visit, offering an array of hidden gems. You can find outfits, accessories and trinkets of all kinds. At Sindhi Market, textiles reign supreme. It is known for its cotton textile works, where you can shop for fabrics, saris and dress materials in any pattern and colour.
IN.AMD.destinationPageIntro: Ahmedabad has a special place in Mahatma Gandhi's legacy. It’s also home to India’s premier textile museum, the Calico Museum of Textiles and the magnificent Bai Harir Stepwell.
IN.AMD.overviewText:
Feel the heartbeat of Gujarat in Ahmedabad. The air is thick with stories of dynasties, revolutions, and the vibrant spirit of its people. There is a culture of craft, with artisans busy at work, weavers spinning fabric, and chefs serving up dishes with delicious, complex flavours out of quaint food stalls.

The markets hum with life, bursting with divine textiles, intricate handicrafts and welcoming personalities. The aroma of street food draws you in, while the sound of honking rickshaws is simply part of the background noise. Ahmedabad has pockets of peace too, with shady trees, serene lakes and alleyways hiding quiet cafés. Explore this wonderful city and everything Ahmedabad has to offer.
IN.AMD.destinationHighlightsH1: Ahmedabad: A city of heritage and artisans
IN.AMD.eatingImageText:
Dive into the world of Gujarati street food, where khakhra (crisp wheat crackers) melt in your mouth and fafda (crunchy, chickpea-flour papadams) are a delectable snack. For something a little heartier, try tikkichaat pakora – a crispy, savoury delight topped with chutney, creating the perfect balance of sweet and spicy with every bite.

No trip to Ahmedabad is complete without a traditional Gujarati thali, consisting of a variety of dishes on a single platter such as dal lentil stew, kadhi (yoghurt-based curry), rice and more. Shrikhand (a sweet, flavoured yoghurt) and jalebi (a crunchy, deep-fried dessert) are often served as part of a thali, to top it off.

The square of Manek Chowk in Old Ahmedabad transforms into a dessert and street food paradise in the evenings – it’s a feast for the senses. Make sure to try a kulfi, a creamy frozen dessert that comes in a variety of flavours. You’ll be spoilt for choice.

IN.ATQ.touristAttractionsText:
Begin your journey at the awe-inspiring Sri Darbar Sahib Amritsar to admire its impeccable golden exterior and traditional architecture. Don’t miss the Digital Sikh Museum beneath it, which presents a glimpse into Sikh history.

For something truly magnificent, head to the Attari-Wagah Border at sunset. The daily flag-lowering ceremony between India and Pakistan is a magnificent show of patriotism.

Make your way to Sri Akal Takht Sahib, the highest seat of Sikh authority. This grand building isn’t just beautiful to look at, it is also a place of important significance for Sikhs. If you’re lucky enough to be there for festivals like Lohri, Hola Mohalla or Baisakhi, you may be swept in by the vibrant rituals, folksongs and the infectious energy of bhangra dancing.
IN.ATQ.leisureActivitiesText:
Immerse yourself in personal stories, artefacts and multimedia exhibits about Amritsar’s past at the Partition Museum. Watch how the poignant history of the 1947 Partition is brought to life. Each corner helps develop a deep understanding of this defining and monumental event.

Admire the Gandhi Gate, also known as Hall Gate, where you can soak in the architectural diversity – an intriguing blend of Mughal, Colonial and Sikh designs. The vibrant atmosphere buzzes with life, serving as the gateway between the old and new parts of the city’s streets and culture.

To experience what local life is like, head to Saada Pind, a living museum and charming replica of a traditional Punjabi village. Explore old traditions, immerse in the culture and sample authentic Punjabi dishes.
IN.ATQ.shoppingText:
Each market in Amritsar has its own unique charm. For traditional wear, head to Katra Jaimal Singh Bazaar, where colourful sarees and exquisite pashmina shawls catch your eye. The intricate jewellery here reflects Punjab’s deep-rooted craftmanship – it’s a prime souvenir for those seeking timeless treasures.

If you are in search of another wholesome shopping experience, Hall Bazaar is a go-to as it’s stocked with everything from handicrafts to embroidered fabrics. The Mughal-style entrance, with its grand arch, sets the tone for an authentic Amritsar shopping spree.

Looking for something a bit more relaxing? Lawrence Road Market blends shopping and food seamlessly. Browse through contemporary stores before grabbing a street snack or sip Amritsari coffee at one of the cosy cafés.
IN.ATQ.destinationPageIntro: Experience the culturally rich Amritsar. Discover the Sri Darbar Sahib, mouthwatering food, historic landmarks, bustling bazaars and more.
IN.ATQ.overviewText:
Explore the lively streets of Amritsar, a city with an unmistakable charm. Known amongst locals as the cultural heartland of Punjab, the clatter of rickshaws fill the air – bridging age-old traditions to the modern day. The scent of irresistible street food is everywhere, with all kinds of delicious delicacies to devour and hot cups of chai to drink.

Whether you are savouring Punjabi cuisine, discovering incredible landmarks, attending one of the many cultural festivals or simply soaking in the city’s warmth, Amritsar provides an experience that is both soul-stirring and inviting. It’s an explosion of sights, sounds and flavours just waiting to be explored.
IN.ATQ.destinationHighlightsH1: Amritsar: The cultural hub of Punjab
IN.ATQ.eatingImageText:
Food is more than just a meal in Amritsar, it’s a celebration of flavours. Sink your teeth into Punjabi cuisine, where every bite is a burst of spice and hearty ingredients. Order the famous Amritsar kulcha which originated in the city. This crispy flatbread stuffed with spicy potato, paneer, cauliflower or onion is absolutely delectable.

Visit the Guru ka Langar, where a simple yet fulfilling thali of lentils, vegetables and fresh raita is served to thousands each day. It’s a good place to dine in a communal setting. The streets nearby are also filled with food, with stalls offering smoked eggplant called baingan bharta and fresh palak paneer.

Of course, no meal in Amritsar is complete without lassi. Thick, and creamy, this yogurt-based drink is a beloved refreshment. Enjoy it plain or flavoured with fresh fruits.

IN.GOX.touristAttractionsText:
Begin with beach-hopping by travelling to Palolem Beach, where the shore is lined with coconut trees and kayaking is a popular choice amongst locals. Come evening, the surrounding areas are filled with energy, from beachside barbecues to live music. Further south, you can find Agonda Beach, which is a top location for dolphin spotting and tranquil boat rides.

For a change of scenery, travel to Dudhsagar Falls, nestled in the Goan jungle. You can hike through the forest or take a jeep ride to reach this natural wonder.

Explore Goa’s cultural history in its capital Panaji. Set off on a walking tour of the impressive Portuguese architecture – a window into the region’s colonial past. While there, stop by Madragoa, a cultural space that showcases Goa’s Indo-Portuguese heritage through live performances of Mando and Fado music.
IN.GOX.leisureActivitiesText:
Goa’s coastlines offer incredible surfing spots as well as relaxing beach vibes. After catching some waves, head out on a boat trip to spot dancing dolphins or kayak through backwaters and mangroves.

A visit to Mollem National Park is a journey into Goa’s rich biodiversity. Visit the Flame-throated Bulbul sanctuary, Goa’s state bird, and admire the state tree, the Matti or Indian Laurel.

Goa is alive with greenery and life during the monsoon season, from June to September. If you are lucky enough to be there throughout the season, monsoon festivals fill the streets with music, dance and celebration. If you are visiting outside of monsoon season, head to the submerged village of Curdi as it only re-emerges from the waters once a year.
IN.GOX.shoppingText:
The iconic Anjuna Market is adorned with colourful stalls set along the coastline, stocked with everything from handcrafted jewellery to flowing boho dresses. As the sun sets, the market buzzes with chatter and the delight of finding items you never knew you needed.

For an evening expedition, make your way to the Arpora Saturday Night Market where you can listen to live music, enjoy street food and wander through stalls of artisanal goods, quirky fashion and vintage pieces.

At the heart of Goan life is the Mapusa Market, where locals come to buy fresh produce, spices and handmade goods. It’s a great destination to pick up home decor or homewares made from unique materials like bamboo and seashells – they’re ideal souvenirs from your Goan adventure.
IN.GOX.destinationPageIntro: Pristine beaches, lush natural landscapes and wildlife, a mosaic of Indian and Portuguese culture in its cuisine and heritage – a trip to the tropical haven of Goa boasts all of this and then some.
IN.GOX.overviewText:
Goa awaits you with its golden sands and crystal-clear waters lapping at your feet. Rainbow-coloured houses peek out from swaying palm trees and life here moves at a slower pace than the rest of India. The essence of Goa is a blend of Indo-Portuguese tradition with laidback, beachside vibes.

Whether you’re exploring the coastal marketplaces, tasting local seafood or losing yourself in the charm of the lush landscapes, Goa’s energy is infectious. Surf the waves by morning, hike the dense jungle in the afternoon and dance under the stars at night. Goa invites you to explore, unwind and savour the beauty of life’s simple pleasures.
IN.GOX.eatingImageText:
When you think of food in Goa, you think of delectable, fresh seafood, seasoned to perfection with different kinds of masala. Fish curry and rice is a popular meal in Goa – it’s a must-try for all visitors. A traditional Goan thali, as locals call it, offers an authentic taste of this coastal enclave. Each bite bursts with the tang of tamarind, the heat of local spices and the freshness of the day’s catch.

Goa’s bustling markets – Mapusa, Panjim and Margao – are the perfect places to buy food souvenirs. Pick up crunchy cashews, freshly baked local bread and irresistible Goan sweets like dodol (a toffee-like, palm sugar-based confectionary) or bebinca (a layer cake).

IN.NAG.touristAttractionsText:
Nagpur offers a myriad of temples and forts to uncover. Visit the majestic Dhamma Chakra Stupa, a stunning monument symbolising peace and harmony. Ascend to Ramtek Fort Temple, perched atop a hill that provides breathtaking panoramic views of the countryside. This ancient temple, steeped in legends, invites you to marvel at its intricately carved stonework and soak in the tranquility of the landscape.

No holiday to Nagpur would be complete without a hike up Shree Ganesh Mandir Tekdi, where the lively atmosphere and lush surroundings create an idyllic escape from the city’s hustle and bustle.

Treat your senses at Lata Mangeshkar Musical Garden, where whimsical musical fountains dance to enchanting melodies. As the sun sets, the gardens are a spectacle of light and sound.
IN.NAG.leisureActivitiesText:
Nagpur is one of the best places to embark on a wildlife safari in India. Here, you can witness the beauty of leopards, tigers, and birdlife in their natural habitats.

For a little relaxation, unwind at Ambazari Lake, a picturesque haven surrounded by mango trees. There is a fountain, walking trails, and many boats and watercrafts to hire for a jaunt on the water.

For a dash of adventure, travel out of the city to Amba Khori waterfalls. The journey leads you through thick greenery where you’ll be welcomed by the sight and sound of cascading water. Take a dip, or simply admire the view. Continue your adventure with some glamping at Waki Woods. Enjoy Nagpur’s magnificent outdoors from the comfort of a furnished tent.
IN.NAG.shoppingText:
Make your way through Dharampeth Shopping Street, where the colourful shops overflow with everything from hip apparel to exquisite handicrafts. With much the same vibe, Sitabuildi Main Road presents a mix of street vendors and shopfronts, stocked with goods of every kind.

Browse the Sarafa Bazaar, where vendors proudly showcase fresh oranges, reflecting the region’s agricultural legacy. As you walk through the market, be sure to pick up some melt-in-your-mouth besan ladoo – sweet dough balls with a cardamom twist, or kachoris – crispy, deep fried, savoury stuffed pastries named.
IN.NAG.destinationPageIntro: Visit Nagpur, a city of oranges and symbolic wonders. Venture through its streets of bazaars, discover impressive temples and forts, and trek to the Central Indian jungle.
IN.NAG.overviewText:
Affectionately known as Orange City due to its abundant orange blooms, Nagpur bursts with life, culture and energy. Aside from its citrus crown, there is much to discover in Nagpur – it’s a city of rich history, diverse cultures, and welcoming hospitality.

Explore the impressive temples and forts, wander through the vibrant streets and sample local delicacies that tell a story of culinary heritage. The city is a melting pot of art and music too, with attractions offering a glimpse into the creative soul of India.

Whether you’re here to savour its flavours, immerse yourself in its culture, or simply enjoy its warm climate, Nagpur promises an unforgettable experience that will stay with you long after you’ve left.
IN.NAG.destinationHighlightsH1: Nagpur: The city of orange blossoms
IN.NAG.eatingImageText:
Begin your days with a big bowl of tarri poha. This comforting breakfast bowl is made from flattened rice cooked with spices, coriander, onion, and a hint of lemon – often served with a spicy curry called tarri.

Much like the rest of India, Nagpur is renowned for its street food, especially samosas. These delightful golden pastries are typically filled with spiced potatoes and peas.

Your Nagpur palate would not be complete without dining on Saoji food – a culinary tradition of intense spicy flavours. With its origins in the region, the cuisine is characterised by its fiery curries, aromatic spices, and slow-cooked meats.

Let’s not forget Nagpur’s claim to fame either – oranges. Grown locally, they are juicy, sweet, and bursting with flavour.

IN.TRV.touristAttractionsText:
Padmanabhaswamy Temple is a sight to behold, with its gold-adorned architecture that almost feels ethereal. Legends say that hidden treasures still lie beneath its floors. Continue exploring the grandeur of India’s building designs at Kanakakunnu Palace, there the grand halls narrate Kerala’s regal past. The palace often hosts cultural events under its majestic ceilings.

Art enthusiasts will enjoy a day in the Napier Museum, filled with relics and sculptures that bring Kerala’s rich heritage to life. Venture towards the coast to Vizhinjam Lighthouse, and climb to the top for breathtaking vistas of the Arabian Sea. For a tranquil escape, head out to Meenmutty Waterfalls, a hidden gem surrounded by lush forest. Located just under 50 kilometres from the city centre, it’s a great spot for trekking.
IN.TRV.leisureActivitiesText:
Get ready for a fun adventure at the Neyyar Wildlife Sanctuary. You can witness elephants at the rehabilitation centre and spot leopards roaming the sanctuary. Plus, you can visit the crocodile farm for a close encounter. 

Looking for some relaxation? Head over to the Neyyar Dam for a peaceful boat ride. Enjoy the serene scenery and maybe even cast a line from the boat to reel in a Thiruvananthapuram catch. 

Longing for a relaxing beach day? Then, make your way to Samudra Beach – a gem on Kerala’s coastline that’s perfect for a day in the sun. Watch the fishermen cast their nets, stroll along the shore and admire the Kerala sunset.
IN.TRV.shoppingText:
The bustling Chalai Market is a 100-year-old shopping haven. The narrow lanes feel like a vibrant maze, where the aroma of freshly ground spices mingles with the chatter of vendors selling everything from local fruits to handmade jewellery.

No shopping trip here is complete without exploring the stunning selection of sarees. Whether it’s the luxurious silk varieties or the elegant cotton handlooms, each garment tells a tale of Kerala’s weaving tradition. And don’t forget the spices – Thiruvananthapuram is the land of cardamom, pepper and cinnamon. Pick up a variety of samples to take home as gifts for the special cooks in your life.
IN.TRV.destinationPageIntro: Welcome to Thiruvananthapuram – where you can visit Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple with its tranquil Padmatheertham Pond, the stunning Padmanabhapuram Palace, and a variety of museums, beaches and zoos.
IN.TRV.overviewText:
Known as one of Kerala’s coastal gems, Thiruvananthapuram is a city of history and nature. The air is filled with the sweet scent of fresh coconut and spices, creating an idyllic setting for your Indian adventure. 

Start your mornings with a steaming cup of Indian coffee – a tradition as old and timeless as the city itself. Explore the vibrant markets overflowing with colourful fabrics and fragrant spices and indulge in some delectable Kerala street food. 

Tradition is woven into every corner of Thiruvananthapuram, from the bustling markets to the quaint eateries serving up coconut-based dishes. Lose yourself in the picturesque beauty of this ancient city and discover its charm for yourself.
IN.TRV.eatingImageText:
Start your day at the iconic Indian Coffee House. This café is not just a coffee shop, but a landmark of the city. The spiral-shaped building is as famous for its architecture as for its coffee. Sip on a warm, aromatic brew while admiring this work of art.

For breakfast, try the puttu with kadala curry – a soft, steamed rice cake, paired with spicy black chickpea curry. You’ll find the best versions in quaint, family-run restaurants.

In the evening, the city streets come alive with the sizzle of street food stalls. Don’t miss the Thattu dosa – a mini crepe-like bread made with rice or lentil, and often served with chutney or tangy sambar (a stew made with lentils, mixed vegetables and spices). Grab some from a busy stall near Palayam Market and savour it like a local.

TZ.ZNZ.businessClassSummary:
Book a flight to Zanzibar with Qatar Airways in Business or First Class, and get ready to embark on your African odyssey in style. Exquisite cabins and unrivalled technology ensure that every moment of your travel experience is a true pleasure. 

Begin in one of our elegant Business lounges, a peaceful haven where you can relax while sipping on a refreshing drink, checking your emails or reading a book. Take a hot shower to prepare for the rest of your journey, or watch the world go by as you wait for your flight to be called. When reaching the aircraft, our professional cabin crew will show you to your spacious seat. It’s ergonomically designed to bring you maximum comfort and offers ample legroom.  

During the flight, you can select a delicious meal from our exclusive à la carte menu, created by award-winning chefs. Then immerse yourself in a blockbuster film from our vast entertainment selection, or join that important video conference. Connect quickly and seamlessly courtesy of the complimentary Wi-Fi, available on our A380, A350, B787 and select B777 aircraft. 

Set off on a delightful trip to Zanzibar when flying in Business or First Class on board Qatar Airways.
TZ.ZNZ.touristAttractionsText:
Begin your sightseeing adventure in the capital, Stone Town – a living testament to the island’s multicultural past. Explore its maze-like streets, dive into the lively energy of the markets and just soak up that relaxed island vibe.  

Most sites in Stone Town are all within walking distance and you can take a guided tour of the city. Delve into the regal history at the Palace Museum, where tales of former Sultans come to live. Then head to the Old Fort, a significant historical site that offers a glimpse into Zanzibar’s past. Today, it’s a vibrant cultural hub with souvenir shops selling paintings, sculptures and traditional clothes. 

Top off your exploration with a touch of rock ‘n’ roll at the Freddie Mercury Museum and connect with Zanzibar’s very own legendary music icon.
TZ.ZNZ.leisureActivitiesText:
Zanzibar is a playground for underwater adventurers and nature enthusiast. Snorkelling here is unmatched. Dive right in to see a kaleidoscope of tropical fish and breathtaking coral gardens – an experience you won’t forget. Nungwi Beach is a great option for snorkelling and deep-sea fishing. Here you can also set sail on a traditional dhow cruise, dine in chic restaurants and stay in overwater bungalows.

Just a quick boat hop away lies Changuu Island, a sanctuary where ancient Seychelles tortoises roam freely – some are almost 200 years old. It’s an amazing opportunity to get up close with these gentle giants. For the nature lovers, Jozani Chwaka Bay National Park is another must-see. Spot the rare and playful colobus monkeys swinging through the trees and explore the serene beauty of the mangrove forests. 

Take a day to unwind on Nakupenda Beach – an absolute gem with crystal-clear waters, powdery-white sands and a serene atmosphere that makes it the perfect escape.
TZ.ZNZ.shoppingText:
Zanzibar’s markets are the perfect place to find local treasures and souvenirs. The historic Old Slave Market is abundant with handmade trinkets, while Shimoni Market is the go-to spot for beachwear and other textiles ideal for the sunny shores. 

Stone Town’s winding alleys are dotted with stalls of dazzling tanzanite jewellery – a deep-blue gemstone that is unique to East Africa. You’ll find artisans busy crafting delicate beaded necklaces and earrings that make stunning souvenirs.

Handwoven baskets are another lovely keepsake that can be found on almost every corner, along with seaweed-infused soaps, aromatic lotions and paintings.
TZ.ZNZ.destinationPageIntro: Take in the centuries-old marvels of Stone Town and Old Fort, before relaxing on the shore, communing with beach turtles, or trying some of the world’s best snorkelling in beautiful Zanzibar.
TZ.ZNZ.overviewText:
Ready for a real reset? Zanzibar is the answer – you’ll feel like you’ve stepped right into a daydream. Picture turquoise waters, powder-white sands and palms swaying in the breeze. 

What will your days look like? Probably spent lounging on beaches that look like they belong on a postcard. Let the island’s laid-back charm simply wash over you, and keep an eye out because you might spot some adorable beach turtles. As the sun sets, the beaches glow with a golden hue and the aroma of grilled seafood fills the air – yum!

But Zanzibar is more than just stunning scenery. It boasts a rich history that’s a vibrant blend of African, Arab, Indian and European influences. You’ll see this fascinating mix in the local traditions and unique architecture.

Zanzibar is much more than a getaway – it’s pure tropical bliss waiting to discovered.
TZ.ZNZ.eatingImageText:
Kick off your Zanzibar mornings the local way with a comforting cup of chai, a spiced tea infused with hints of cardamom and cinnamon – the perfect introduction to an island that specialises in spices. And speaking of which, if you’re up for a spiced-up sensory adventure, then a tour through Tangawizi Spice Farm is a must. You can touch, smell, and taste the spices that define Swahili cooking.

As evening approaches, let your nose guide you to Forodhani Market, where the tantalising scent of fish laced with sweet coconut hangs in the air. This is the place to get the best local treats like crispy potato balls, savoury samosas, and fresh seafood. 

Another street food favourite is Mishkaki. This smoky barbeque-flavoured meat is grilled to perfection and served on a stick (kebab-style). Pizza anyone? Zanzibar pizza is a delicious take on a classic dish. And despite the name, it’s nothing like a traditional pizza. It’s made with a crepe-like base and filled with a variety of ingredients.

SC.SEZ.businessClassSummary:
Book a flight to the Seychelles with Qatar Airways in Business or First Class and reach one of the most beguiling destinations on the globe in complete comfort. With a world-renowned team to take care of your every need and state-of-the-art aircraft, our flights represent the pinnacle of luxury travel. 

Begin your trip by relaxing in one of our Business Class lounges. Quiet zones are ideal for escaping the hustle and bustle of the airport with a good book, or checking your emails in peace. To freshen up for the next leg of your journey, take a shower or sip on an ice-cold beverage. When it's time for your flight, our welcoming cabin crew will show you to your seat on board one of our premium aircraft. Wherever you’re going, you’ll experience unmatched comfort in a spacious seat with plenty of legroom.  

During the flight, join a video call when connecting to the high-speed Wi-Fi, available on our A380, A350, B787, and select B777 aircraft. After the call, indulge in a delicious meal courtesy of our award-winning chefs, then watch a film from our extensive entertainment variety. To arrive invigorated, enjoy a restful sleep on a lie-flat bed, while ambient lighting helps you adjust to your destination’s time zone.  

Prepare for an extraordinary Business or First Class experience when flying to the Seychelles with Qatar Airways.
SC.SEZ.touristAttractionsText:
While beach getaways are undoubtedly the star attraction here, there’s plenty more to do and see in the Seychelles. Island-hopping is going to be your new favourite hobby. 

Take a ferry to Vallée de Mai Reserve in Praslin Island to enjoy nature at its best. This ancient forest – a UNESCO World Heritage site – is home to the iconic Coco de Mer palm, as well as many exotic birds, reptiles and wild vegetations.

Next up is the idyllic Anse Source d’Argent on La Digue, one of the Seychelles’ most breathtaking beaches. Famous for its crystal-clear waters and granite boulders, it’s one of the most photographed beaches in the world – you’ll probably recognise its backdrop from popular Hollywood films. The waters of this beach teem with marine life and you could easily spot tropical fish and turtles in their natural habitat. 

For a unique once-in-a-lifetime experience, take a short flight from Mahé Island to Aldabra Atoll to see the giant tortoises as they roam freely.
SC.SEZ.leisureActivitiesText:
Naturally, the water is where the majority of the activities happen in the Seychelles. Set sail across the blue waters and discover the many secluded beaches and uninhabited islets.

Beneath the waves, snorkelling and diving is truly unforgettable. The shallow, clear waters also make for an excellent place for first-timers to try scuba diving. Swim alongside sharks, rays, and a dazzling array of marine life. If fishing is more your passion, you can take a fishing tour or hire a boat. Cast a line for wahoo, dorado, and barracuda, just to name a few.

Up for a good hike? Head to the Copolia Trail in the Morne Seychellois National Park for stunning, panoramic views over the islands. A trip to Seychelles Tea Factory on Mahé Island is also worth a visit to discover the art behind the local beverage that’s enjoyed as much as water.
SC.SEZ.shoppingText:
Peek into the Seychellois way of life as you wander through the bustling streets of Sir Selwyn Clarke Market in Victoria. Here, you can shop for one-of-a-kind souvenirs like coconut shell artefacts and figurines carved from the Coco de Mer nut. You can also find stylish home décor pieces that capture the natural character and impressive craftsmanship of Seychelles.

Did you know? The Seychelles is home to a variety of spices, including top-quality vanilla. This cherished local commodity is a popular buy to take home. Pick up some fragrant vanilla pods, vanilla essence, or creamy vanilla-infused treats. 

If you’re looking for something a little more high-end, the Seychelles is known for its exquisite local black pearls, available in upscale boutiques and malls.
SC.SEZ.destinationPageIntro: From the Vallee de Mai Nature Reserve to the stunning Aldabra Atoll, in the Seychelles, each island is a tropical jewel waiting to be explored.
SC.SEZ.overviewText:
Say hello to the Seychelles – a pristine archipelago of 115 islands scattered across the turquoise water of the Indian Ocean. This idyllic destination boasts breathtaking scenery, white-sand beaches, lush rainforests and a vibrant underwater world filled with coral reefs and marine life. 

Whether you’re seeking relaxation, adventure or cultural immersion in the charming Creole villages, the Seychelles offers an unforgettable blend of natural beauty and authentic island charm. You’re ‘shore’ to love it here!
SC.SEZ.eatingImageText:
Creole food takes centre stage in Seychelles, blending traditions of Africa, France, India and China. For a Seychelles twist, fish is typically incorporated in most of the dishes. Enjoy freshly caught snapper, tuna, or kingfish marinated in Creole spices and grilled to perfection. Be sure to also sample some succulent langoustines – grilled to perfection and often served with fragrant local spices, they’re a true delicacy.

A local favourite to try is octopus curry. Slow-cooked in coconut milk and infused with fragrant spices like cinnamon, cloves, and nutmeg, it delivers a unique fusion of sweet and spicy.

For a taste of locally grown fruits, try the starfruit – accurately named for its shape. Often found in salads, or served as a garnish, this juicy, sweet and sour fruit adds a burst of flavour to any dish.

No meal in the Seychelles is complete without rice accompanied by ladob, a traditional dessert made from sweet potatoes, coconut milk, vanilla and sugar.

GB.LGW.overviewTabHeading: Book your visit to London Gatwick
GB.LGW.touristAttractionsText:
For something quintessentially British, journey to the charming town of Horsham. Its picturesque streets and quaint cafés invite you to relax with a cup of tea and a shortbread biscuit.

Venture a bit further to Tunbridge Wells. This historic spa town boasts elegant Georgian architecture, lush parks, and the Royal Tunbridge Wells High Street. Visit the Calverley Grounds while you’re there, a perfectly manicured park abundant with history.

Arundel Castle is not far away, perched above the River Arun. The grand halls and pristine grounds will make you feel royalty as you take a glimpse into England’s medieval past.

For a taste of Britain’s seaside, cruise over to Hastings. Brimming with character, this quirky old town is a breath of fresh air. It’s home to eclectic shops and has an artsy vibe you won’t want to leave.
GB.LGW.leisureActivitiesText:
Step into a wildlife wonderland at the British Wildlife Centre, just 16 kilometres from London Gatwick. Become David Attenborough for the day and spot red squirrels, owls and much more.

Hit the trails a little further out in Surrey to pedal or hike the rolling hills of Box Hill. The reward is worth the trek, with breathtaking views across the hills and beyond.

For a relaxing seaside escape, travel 30 minutes by car to Brighton. It’s a town that’s forever on holiday – with street performers, beachside stores, and a pier that’s perfect for a stroll with an ice cream.

Further afield, but a true hidden gem, is New Forest National Park. A couple of hours from London Gatwick, you can witness wild horses roaming free in ancient woodlands – it’s truly exceptional.
GB.LGW.shoppingText:
The surrounding area of Gatwick is a prime destination for shopping. The High Street in Horley is dotted with small boutiques and independent shops. Scout fashionable finds and unexpected gifts that capture the essence of British flair – it’s a treasure trove of extraordinary shopping experiences.

There’s a collection of malls within a few miles of London Gatwick too. Explore the expansive world of British shopping centres and shop to your heart’s content.

For some souvenir shopping, Martlets Hall in Crawley provides an array of British goods and local craftmanship. These lively markets and pop-up stalls are stocked with artisanal products, handmade crafts, and a variety of British goodies. Choose yourself an ornate tea set, shortbread biscuits, or Union Jack memorabilia.
GB.LGW.touristAttractionsTabHeading: Things to do in London Gatwick
GB.LGW.destinationPageIntro: A central hub for the best of Britain, London Gatwick is close to the countryside, the seaside, quaint towns and shopping high streets.
GB.LGW.overviewText:
Just a stone's throw from London Gatwick, an entire world of adventure and charm awaits.

Discover quaint British towns that are home to unique shops and cosy cafés, and enjoy the serene beauty of the countryside, where picturesque landscapes await your exploration. Head to the seaside, where the coastal charm and vibes promise a refreshing getaway.

The areas surrounding Gatwick are brimming with captivating experiences that are both enriching and unforgettable.
GB.LGW.destinationHighlightsH1: London Gatwick: A central hub for the best of Britain
GB.LGW.eatingImageText:
The great thing about England is the sheer number of traditional British eateries you can stumble upon in a day. No matter which town or district you end up venturing to, you’re guaranteed to come across ‘the local’ where you can tuck into a delectable, hearty meal. Savour the crisp perfection of classic fish and chips – don’t forget the mushy peas and curry sauce on the side. Or indulge in a Sunday roast of succulent meats, crispy potatoes, and all the trimmings.

If you have a chance, head to Horley High Street, just 5 minutes from London Gatwick, where you can find a delightful mix of British fare and international cuisine. Whether you’re looking for a big English breakfast of eggs, meat, baked beans and all the sides, or seeking a deep bowl of Italian pasta – you’ll find it in Horley.

GB.BHX.touristAttractionsText:
Birmingham and large swathes of the West Midlands were once referred to as the Black Country due to the thick smoke from factories that filled the air during the industrial revolution. 

For the history buffs, there’s plenty to uncover and explore in Birmingham and its surrounding areas. Take a trip to the Black Country Living Museum in Dudley, just a 45-minute drive from the city centre, to learn what it was like when ironworking foundries were in their golden era. Titanic’s anchor was forged there and more recently was the set of a popular television series.

For a countryside landmark, only a 15-minute drive from the city centre, head to Sarehole Mill. This picturesque watermill was the inspiration for a renowned author’s novel. For a day trip to a nearby town, venture on to discover Warwick Castle, a medieval masterpiece with fortified towers and exciting events for all ages.

Finally, bring your Birmingham trip to a close by visiting Soho House Museum, the former home of the Lunar Society and Matthew Boulton – inventor and industrialist. Its Georgian architecture is something to marvel at.
GB.BHX.leisureActivitiesText:
Wander through the Birmingham Museum and Art Gallery, abundant with Renaissance masterpieces and the infamous Pre-Raphaelite collection. 

For the literature lovers, go to Shakespeare’s Schoolroom and Guildhall in nearby Stratford-upon-Avon. It’s about an hour away by car or train but worth the journey. Walk in the footsteps of the Bard, in the medieval building that shaped the world’s greatest playwright.

Adventure calls once you’re back in Birmingham. Embark on a canal boat or canoe tour to glide through Birmingham’s waterways, uncovering stories about the city’s heritage along the way. Take a breath of fresh countryside air at Winterbourne House and Garden, a peaceful oasis of landscaped gardens and an enchanting Edwardian home.
GB.BHX.shoppingText:
At the heart of Birmingham’s shopping district lies New Street, where a shopping centre anchors one end, and the grand Town Hall greets you at the other. Between them you can find a vibrant stretch of high-street icons and quirky independent boutiques for some retail therapy, along with cafés for much-needed refreshments once you’re done.

For something a little different, explore Birmingham’s unique shopping arcades. Tucked away from the main street, these elegant, smaller arcades are home to specialty stores, vintage finds and bespoke crafts. Make sure to wander beyond the big names to the quaint side streets, where local designers showcase their wares and offer something truly special.
GB.BHX.destinationPageIntro: Shaped by Britain’s industrial revolution, Birmingham is a cultural delight in the heart of the UK. It’s abundant with historical attractions, Balti houses and shopping destinations.
GB.BHX.overviewText:
Birmingham is a lively city with a treasure trove of history, culture and metropolitan energy. Once the centre of the Industrial Revolution, Birmingham’s story is one of transformation and regeneration. You can feel the pulse of history as you stroll through the streets – it’s where the first steam engines roared to life and Britain’s industry thrived.

Today, Birmingham has become a dynamic blend of old and new, with classical buildings standing alongside contemporary marvels. Its rich industrial past has influenced a city filled with creative spirit, diverse communities and a promising future. From its canals to the charming markets and cutting-edge museums, Birmingham is always evolving yet rooted in its fascinating past.
GB.BHX.eatingImageText:
The most iconic food area of Birmingham is the Balti Triangle in the Sparkhill and Sparkbrook neighbourhoods, where the city’s renowned Balti houses reign supreme. These bustling spots are the birthplace of the ‘Birmingham Balti’. The origin of this dish can be traced back to the city’s large Pakistani community and has become a symbol of the cultural melting pot Birmingham is today. This sizzling, aromatic dish is packed with flavour and served in a stainless-steel pot – a ‘balti’ – alongside fluffy rice and a sharing portion of naan bread. You can’t leave Birmingham without trying it.

If you’re craving other British classics, the Bullring Open Market has traditional fish and chips: flaky fish, covered in a crisp, golden batter, served with chunky chips, finished off with salt and a splash of vinegar. If you're on the go, grab a Cornish pasty – a buttery pastry filled with tender meat and vegetables.

Indulge in an afternoon tea filled with dainty delights including Shrewsbury cakes. These regional favourites are crumbly biscuits flavoured with lemon zest and nutmeg.

GB.EDI.businessClassSummary:
Fly to Edinburgh in Business or First Class with Qatar Airways to discover the iconic landmarks and hidden gems of Scotland’s capital. From boarding to landing, our world-renowned team are here to customise your journey to suit your unique needs. 

Begin with effortless check-in, followed by a leisurely break in one of our Business Class lounges, where you can sip a cool beverage or enjoy a light snack while you wait. Make the most of the private workstations to catch up on emails, or take a rejuvenating shower before your flight. 

On board our modern aircraft, you’re shown to your seat, where you can stretch out in complete comfort thanks to the spacious design and extra legroom. Connect to the fast Wi-Fi (available on our A380, A350, B787 and select B777 aircraft) for that important work conference or video call with family and friends.  

To delight your taste buds, savour the exceptional range of dishes on our à la carte menu, freshly prepared by our award-winning chefs. Then settle back and relax with a film or TV show from our vast entertainment library, or rest on a lie-flat bed while ambient lighting gently resets your body to your destination’s time zone. Arrive feeling refreshed and ready to explore the ancient city or seal that important business deal. 

Book a flight to Edinburgh in First Class or Business Class with Qatar Airways and experience unparalleled luxury.
GB.EDI.touristAttractionsText:
Begin your sightseeing adventure at the majestic Edinburgh Castle, perched high on Castle Rock. This historic fortress is a treasure trove of Scotland’s heritage, housing the Crown Jewels and the Stone of Destiny.

Next, stroll down the Royal Mile to the Palace of Holyroodhouse, the King’s official residence. Continue your journey to Calton Hill, where the National Monument, inspired by Athens’ Parthenon, stands in tribute to Scottish soldiers who died in the Napoleonic Wars.

For a change of scenery, take a day trip to the legendary Loch Ness. Accessible by train or car, this famous loch is steeped in mystery, with incredible sights to see. Make sure to hop on a boat tour to learn about the elusive Nessie.

Another must-do is a day trip to the Scottish Highlands. This rugged landscape is ideal for trekking and exploring the charming rural villages, offering a true taste of Scotland’s nature.
GB.EDI.leisureActivitiesText:
Because it is so steeped in history, Edinburgh offers a wealth of activities for travellers. Start your journey at the National Museum of Scotland, where vast collections tell the stories of Scotland’s rich heritage, natural wonders and cultural treasures. If you’re seeking adventure, a hike up Arthur’s Seat is a must. Featured in many films, this ancient volcano rewards climbers with stunning panoramic views of the city below.

Take a leisurely stroll along the Water of Leith, a picturesque riverwalk that winds through the heart of Edinburgh. You can opt for a short or long route depending on how much you’d like to walk.

Don’t miss the Camera Obscura and World of Illusions, where optical illusions and interactive exhibits provide fun for the whole family.
GB.EDI.shoppingText:
Head back to the Royal Mile for a shopping extravaganza, where the street is lined with eclectic shops offering authentic Scottish items such as cashmere, tweed and tartan, reflecting Scotland’s textile heritage.

Meander down Princes Street to explore high-end boutiques, department stores and well-known brands. On Victoria Street, you’ll find bespoke and independent shops perfect for scouting artisanal goods and quirky gifts.

For a vibrant market experience, make your way to Waverley Market, brimming with handcrafted jewellery, local art and distinctive fashion items. Looking for a souvenir to take home? Pick up some Scottish shortbread or oatcakes, and a CD or vinyl of bagpipe music.
GB.EDI.destinationPageIntro: Take in Edinburgh Castle and the royal residence at the Palace of Holyroodhouse, before taking a trip to experience the Scottish Highlands and the elusive, Loch Ness Monster.
GB.EDI.overviewText:
Edinburgh is a captivating blend of ancient history and modern charm, promising an unforgettable adventure for every traveller.

Wander along cobblestone streets, explore vibrant neighbourhoods and marvel at impressive landmarks. The city boasts a rich tapestry of culture, with world-class festivals, theatres and galleries. To truly savour the essence of Edinburgh, there’s nothing quite like indulging in its unique and hearty local dishes. Each bite offers a taste of the city’s culinary heritage, turning your visit into a gastronomic adventure.

Whether you’re seeking a short escape or a longer stay, Edinburgh’s allure will make you feel right at home.
GB.EDI.eatingImageText:
From traditional Scottish fare to exquisite dining at Michelin-starred establishments, Edinburgh stands as a culinary capital. Wander down the Royal Mile for a taste of local delicacies and contemporary eats. Order the traditional Scottish dish, haggis – a savoury pudding made from sheep’s offal, mixed with oats and spices. It’s typically served with neeps and tatties (i.e., mashed turnips and potatoes).

Take a walk down Princes Street and Rose Street to discover cosy eateries and charming Scottish nooks. Treat yourself to a hearty plate of stovies, a comforting dish of potatoes, onions and meat. If you’re out for breakfast, try haddock or kippers – local fish dishes often served with poached eggs.

IT.FCO.businessClassSummary:
Fly to Rome in Business or First Class with Qatar Airways and begin a journey designed to suit your needs. When you arrive at the airport, check in at a dedicated counter and enjoy fasttracked immigration procedures, so you complete all the formalities effortlessly. 

Before boarding, luxuriate in one of our Business Class lounges. Settle into comfortable seating, savour freshly prepared light dishes, or use a private workstation to finish a few tasks. If you prefer to recharge, take a restorative shower or relish a quiet moment to reset. 

On board, your seat provides generous personal space and optimal comfort, while ambient lighting helps you adjust to a new time zone. Highspeed WiFi on our A380, A350, B787 and select B777 aircraft keeps you connected in the air. Indulge in a meal from our à la carte menu whenever you choose to, or explore a wide selection of films, series and games. Then transform your seat into a fully lie-flat bed for deep, uninterrupted rest. Arrive at your destination refreshed and ready to make the most of the ‘Eternal City’.  

Book your Business or First Class flight to Rome with Qatar Airways for an impeccable travel experience.
IT.FCO.touristAttractionsText:
Start your Roman adventure by tossing a coin into the Trevi Fountain to wish your return to this charming city. Explore Rome’s gladiator past at the Colosseum, a giant amphitheatre built during the reign of Rome’s Flavian Emperors. Close by is the Roman Forum (Foro Romano), the ruins of Ancient Rome’s social and political hub.

The Pantheon is an architectural wonder, with its majestic dome and oculus. When you’re done admiring its beauty, explore the Piazza Navona, known for its fountains, Baroque influence and vibrant street life.

Across the Tiber River is Castel Sant’Angelo. Uncover its deep history or enjoy panoramic views of the city. Nearby is St. Peter’s Basilica, which is a breathtaking sight and top destination for pilgrims from all over the world.
IT.FCO.leisureActivitiesText:
Begin your sightseeing at Vatican City – visit the Vatican Museums to admire its extensive collection of art and artefacts. Michelangelo’s painting on the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel is a magnificent sight. The Vatican Gardens are also worth exploring, with landscaped gardens and an incredible view of St. Peter’s Basilica.

The Galleria Borghese presents a serene, green escape from the hustle of the city. Housed in the former Villa Borghese Pinciana, it features many sculptures and artworks.

Discover Rome’s artistic and aristocratic heritage by visiting the Galleria Doria Pamphilj for its vast art collection or Baroque masterpieces at Palazzo Barberini.

A fun way to get around Rome is by bike. Cycle through charming neighbourhoods and past iconic landmarks while discovering hidden nooks of the city.
IT.FCO.shoppingText:
When in Rome, experience an Italian rite of passage –shopping. Explore the Tridente, a complex of roads formed by three straight streets. Via del Corso is the main shopping street, abundant with popular international brands and local boutiques. In the other two streets, Via del Babuino and Via di Ripetta, discover exquisite pieces by Italian designers and jewellers.

For luxury brands, head to Via Condotti, home to the latest haute couture. On the other hand, Via Cola di Rienzo in Prati has a more relaxed shopping vibe.

For budget-friendly options, make your way to Campo de’ Fiori. Shop for local produce, souvenirs and Italian-made goods. The Monti district is a Bohemian neighbourhood in Rome known for its independent stores, vintage shops and little cafés.
IT.FCO.destinationPageIntro: Let the magnificence of Rome captivate you. Marvel at architectural wonders, toss a coin into the legendary Trevi Fountain or indulge in its world-famous gelato.
IT.FCO.overviewText:
Visit Rome, a captivating Italian city of charm and romance. As you wander through its cobblestone streets, discover a place where very corner tells a story. Take in the grandeur of its ancient ruins and the elegance of its Renaissance and Baroque architecture.

Step back in time while admiring remnants of the Roman Empire and marvel in cultural heritage at its world-class museums. People-watch and soak up the atmosphere at picturesque piazzas and shop your way through each retail district. Indulge in the finest Italian cuisine, from traditional trattorias to modern eateries.

Whether you’re tucking in to a slice of pizza bianca or exploring the Colosseum, Rome captivates with endless discoveries.
IT.FCO.eatingImageText:
Italian food is world-renowned so it’s no surprise that Rome is a gastronomic hub. Head to the neighbourhood of Trastevere for an authentic trattoria experience.

Savour the delicate flavours of carpaccio – thinly sliced raw meat or fish drizzled in olive oil and lemon juice, or a hearty Roman pizza bianca. As for pasta dishes, opt for cacio e pepe and carbonara. For a refreshing starter, try insalata caprese – a salad made with tomato, mozzarella and basil. Naturally, conclude any meal with Rome’s famous gelato.

Coffee in Rome is more than a drink, it’s an experience. Enjoy a perfectly brewed caffé (espresso with crema on top) at one of the city’s many cafés.

A great way to immerse yourself in Rome’s food scene is to embark on a food tour to sample a range of Roman delicacies.

IT.VCE.touristAttractionsText:
The heart of Venice is the Piazza San Marco or St Mark’s Square. This iconic location has been used in countless films, and its cafés sitting beneath the porticoes and the huge bell tower are just some of the delights on display. Don’t miss the glittering gold icons and mosaics on display in the Basilica de San Marco.

Sail down the Grand Canal in style with a gondolier, or travel like the locals on one of the vaporetti (water buses) that take you past sights like the Fondaco dei Turchi or the carved marble façade of the 15th-century Ca’ d’Oro.

The Rialto Bridge is one of Venice’s most famous landmarks and if you’ve chosen this city as a city break destination, one of the must-sees during your stay. The market on the western side of the bridge has been operating for over a thousand years.
IT.VCE.leisureActivitiesText:
Visit the Murano glassmaking island in the lagoon to see highly skilled craftspeople creating the most exquisite glassware. The island is just a ten-minute water taxi ride from Venice and is the home of glassmaking in Europe. A visit to the Museo del Vetro will introduce you to the craft and its history.

Another island to visit is Burano, with its brightly-coloured cottages and authentic ambience. This fishing community has managed to hold onto its cultural heritage and is a fascinating glimpse into life in Venice, the traditions such as lacemaking and a chance to try some Venetian food.

The best way to see Venice is to get lost! This compact city is easy to explore on foot and a few steps away from the busy tourist locations you’ll find the old Venice, with its piazzas and tiny streets.
IT.VCE.shoppingText:
Venice has always been a trade hub, so shopping here is a delight. Calle Larga XXII Marzo is the city’s most famous shopping street, lined with luxury boutiques and restaurants.

The area around Piazza San Marco is the place to go for high-end international brands, or browse around Campo Santo Stefano and Calle de la Mandola for more quirky boutiques and some great vintage stores. For a truly luxurious shopping experience, visit the Fondaco dei Tedeschi, in front of the Grand Canal.

The Rialto market has been a bustling hive of activity for 1000 years, and it’s still a place to buy trinkets and souvenirs today, especially masks and enamel jewellery.

And for some authentic Murano glass, head over to the island of Murano to ensure you buy authentic pieces made by the island’s artisans.
IT.VCE.destinationPageIntro: Venice is a true bucket-list location and one of the great city break destinations in the world. Unique, colourful, and utterly beautiful, one visit is never enough.
IT.VCE.overviewText:
Venice is, arguably, the most beautiful city in the world. This incredible fairytale location set in a blue lagoon and surrounded by tiny islands is stunning and has inspired artists, musicians and poets for hundreds of years. Famous for its canals, its imposing buildings and its 400 bridges, it’s a destination that will call you back again and again.

From Murano glass to exquisite masked balls, espresso bars and the iconic gondoliers that ply their trade along the canals, everything about Venice is unique. While the sublime beauty of St Mark’s Square and the Renaissance-inspired church interiors are dazzling and can be seen in a weekend, a longer city break will give you the chance to explore its side streets and secret piazzas. This is where the true heart of Venice can be found.
IT.VCE.destinationHighlightsH1: Venice: The queen of the Adriatic
IT.VCE.eatingImageText:
Thanks to its location and importance as a trade centre, Venice is a food lover’s delight. From the restaurants and cafés that line St Mark’s Square to fine dining and stand-up coffee bars, there’s lots to experience.

Fish plays a big role on the menus, especially cuttlefish. One of the city’s trademark dishes is seppie al nero, where black cuttlefish ink is used to create a rich sauce. Or try sarde in saor, fried sardines dipped in fried onions, raisins and pine nuts.

For a light lunch, try the Venetian version of tapas, cicchetti. Most traditional cicchetti dishes involve seafood including anchovies and tuna. Or try the local pizza.

For something more substantial, one of Venice’s favourite dishes is risotto, and risi e bisi is one of the most popular, a mix of rice and fresh peas.

FR.NCE.touristAttractionsText:
Perched on the Côte d’Azur lies the iconic Promenade des Anglais, where you’ll discover Nice’s stunning beaches.
