While access to loungers and shade is available for a fee, it ensures a relaxing experience. Venture a little further to Villefranche-sur-Mer, where a collection of colourful villas dot the coastline. Amongst them is the breathtaking Villa Ephrussi de Rothschild – a rose-hued masterpiece set amidst lush gardens.

For a dose of history, climb up to Parc de la Colline du Château, the former site of Nice’s ancient castle. From its summit, a panoramic scene of red rooftops and the azure bay stretches below. Stop by Port Lympia for a quintessential Mediterranean experience with its brightly coloured boats and lively cafés.

Don’t miss the vibrancy of Place Masséna – Nice’s main square – where striking modern sculptures harmoniously meet the grandeur of neoclassical facades.
FR.NCE.leisureActivitiesText:
Dive into Nice’s vibrant art scene, beginning with the Musée Matisse. Here, Henri Matisse’s vivid colours and striking patterns are sure to inspire. Just a short distance away, the Musée National Marc Chagall offers a captivating experience, where Chagall’s renowned work brings scenes to life with poetic grace.

Take a refreshing jog along the Promenade des Anglais to truly experience the charm of the French Riveriera. Or, hop on a bike to explore Nice’s scenic surroundings – a brief picturesque ride will lead you into the tranquil countryside, adorned with rows of grapevines and rolling hills.

For a touch of luxury and glamour, take a day trip to neighbouring Monaco. The winding coastal roads take you to an exclusive enclave of yachts, luxury establishments and high fashion.
FR.NCE.shoppingText:
Shopping in Nice is as refined and radiant as the city itself, and it’s bursting with an array of incredible luxury labels and designer brands. Head to Avenue Jean Médecin, Nice’s main shopping artery, for all things fashion – the perfect place for renowned French brands. 

For something a little different, embark on a treasure hunt at Cours Saleya Market. Here, you’ll find stalls brimming with lavender sachets, handmade soaps, and delicious tapenade. Among the fresh blooms and fragrant herbs, you’ll feel the flavours and colours of the Côte d’Azur come alive.

And don’t forget to visit Nice’s charming Old Town. Stroll through the cobbled streets and explore boutique stores selling local Biot glassware and handcrafted souvenirs.
FR.NCE.destinationPageIntro: Resting on the fabled French Riviera, Nice is among the world's most relaxing and indulgent vacation spots, with its luxurious shopping outlets and unique ‘Cuisine Nissarde’.
FR.NCE.overviewText:
Nestled just moments from the Italian border, Nice is a sunlit gem on the French Riviera. Wander through the pastel streets lined with palm trees, where the scent of fresh lavender and sea salt lingers in the air. With each step, you’ll find yourself surrounded by historic beauty and the relaxed charm of this coastal town.

Waves sparkle under the shimmering sun, inviting you to slow down and take in Nice’s natural beauty. Renowned for its French finesse with a hint of Italian flair, Nice boasts grand architecture, a vibrant bohemian art scene, gourmet delights and luxurious boutiques.

Whether you’re basking on the beach, exploring bustling old-world markets or gazing out over the bay, Nice promises an escape so enchanting, it’s unforgettable.
FR.NCE.destinationHighlightsH1: Nice: Delight of the French Riviera
FR.NCE.eatingImageText:
In Nice, every meal is a vibrant celebration of Cuisine Nissarde – a Mediterranean flavour palate that’s as sun-drenched as the city itself. 

To kick things off, why not snack on some socca? This beloved dish of chickpea flour pancakes cooked on a traditional wood-fired oven, is humble, yet delicious.

For something heartier, try pissaladière. Often compared to pizza, it’s a savoury delight with caramelised onions, anchovies and olives layered on a thin, crispy dough. Make sure to try petits farcis niçois – another local specialty that puts a tasty twist on vegetables. Picture plump tomatoes, courgettes or peppers generously stuffed with a seasoned filling of minced meat, garlic and fragrant herbs, then roasted to perfection.

No trip to France would be complete without a sweet treat. Indulge in a delicate macaron – the Niçois sure know how to make these, especially in lemon and lavender flavours.

GR.JMK.touristAttractionsText: The famed windmills of Mykonos, dating back to the 16th century, are a defining feature of the island. Found in the enchanting Little Venice district, they overlook the sea and boast one of the best sunset views on the island. Nearby, the Castle of Chora is surrounded by narrow alleyways where you can take a leisurely stroll to discover Greek history. For a deeper look into the island’s past, hop on a boat to Delos –  a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It’s known for its ancient ruins, including temples, sculptures, and a remarkably preserved amphitheatre.
GR.JMK.leisureActivitiesText: From the quiet allure of Agios Sostis in the north to the bustling energy of Elia Beach in the south, Mykonos offers something for every beachgoer. Families will enjoy the gentle waters and nearby facilities at Kalo Livadi Beach. For a change of pace, take a horseback ride through the island’s tranquil interior or wander along scenic trails by bike or on foot. Want to see marine life without getting wet? Join a glass-bottom boat tour for an alternative view of the underwater world around Mykonos.
GR.JMK.shoppingText: Treat yourself to some retail therapy at elegant boutiques or stores filled with fine jewellery, designer fashion and unique souvenirs. In Mykonos Town, art galleries display pieces by local and international artists, many inspired by the island’s impressive sunsets. Go beyond the main Matogianni Street and you’ll find picturesque lanes lined with shops selling handmade crafts, antiques and rare books. For everyday essentials, the island also has mini-marts and small supermarkets dotted throughout the towns and villages.
GR.JMK.destinationPageIntro: Whitewashed houses, golden beaches and delicious island cuisine make Mykonos a picture-perfect retreat – ideal for a relaxed escape for couples, families and sunseekers alike.
GR.JMK.overviewText: Famous for its whitewashed houses, blue-domed buildings and iconic windmills, Mykonos is one of Greece’s most beloved islands. Just a short journey from the mainland, it blends traditional charm with natural beauty, creating a serene pace of life. Mykonos is ideal for a luxury holiday, with sun-drenched beaches, peaceful coves and lively coastal towns to explore. It’s a destination where you can enjoy everything from abundant local seafood and high-end shopping, to enticing waters and spectacular sunsets. Solo travellers, couples, families and groups of friends will all experience premium hospitality during a classic Aegean holiday.
GR.JMK.eatingImageText: Indulge in a rich variety of dining experiences at spots all over Mykonos, from harbourside restaurants in Little Venice to laid-back tavernas by the beach. Fresh seafood is a staple, with typical Greek dishes served across the island. Mykonos bread is traditionally made with barley and features in many meals, especially kouvaroti – a local favourite paired with salads, cheese or soup. For a light lunch, try a pie stuffed with sweet onions and trivolia, a cheese made exclusively on the island. End on a sweet note with kalathakia – almond cakes shaped like little baskets.

Then savour the exquisite dishes on our à la carte menu, freshly prepared by our exceptional chefs, followed a blockbuster film from our selection of entertainment options. After the film, catch some rest in a lie-flat bed, while ambient lighting adjusts your body to your destination’s time zone.

Book a flight to Barcelona with Qatar Airways in Business or First Class and arrive in one of Europe’s most dynamic cities in style.
ES.BCN.touristAttractionsText:
Begin sightseeing in Barcelona at the renowned Basilica de Sagrada Familia, Antoni Gaudi’s masterpiece. Despite the fact that this edifice has been under construction since 1882, its architecture and towering spires are both awe-inspiring and one-of-a kind. Continue to the Casa Batlló, a UNESCO World Heritage site renowned for its whimsical interiors and stunning façade. Nearby, Casa Milà is another example of Barcelona’s incredible architecture, with its innovative design and rooftop chimneys.

If you are a sports enthusiast, take a tour of Camp Nou Stadium, home to FC Barcelona. The stadium houses a museum which dives into the rich history of one of the world’s most popular football clubs.

Spend an afternoon exploring the gardens and museums within Parc de Montjuïc. By night, the Magic Fountain inside the park displays a mesmerising light and music show.
ES.BCN.leisureActivitiesText:
See the sights around Barcelona by bicycle, weaving through the city’s quaint streets, historic sites and beautiful beachfronts on two wheels. Ride the cable car to Montjuïc Castle for some stunning panoramic views of the city and the Mediterranean Sea. 

Enjoy nature with a dash of art at the impressive Park Güell, fully designed by Gaudi. 

Explore deeper into Barcelona’s art scene at the Picasso Museum, housing an extensive collection of the artist’s work. Or find some of Salvador Dali’s work in Museu Nacional d’Art de Catalunya.

Attend a concert at the Palau de la Música Catalana for a show of a lifetime in an architectural gem. The spectacular stained glass and ornate décor is something to marvel at.
ES.BCN.shoppingText:
Much like the rest of Europe, Barcelona is a paradise for shoppers, from high-end retail stores and plazas to traditional local markets. Las Ramblas is a popular place to shop for souvenirs, crafts and locally made trinkets. There is also an abundance of entertainment within the marketplace, with street performers at every corner. Next, uncover the winding alleyways of the Gothic Quarter – this striking part of Barcelona is not only full of places to eat, but it also has many boutiques that tell the story of Barcelona’s heritage. 

For a taste of true Spanish luxury, head to Barcelona’s Golden Mile – a stretch of high-end boutiques and designer stores along Passeig de Gràcia.
ES.BCN.destinationPageIntro: Home to the architectural and artistic masterpieces of many famous artists, the beautiful city of Barcelona is a melting pot of creativity, food and music.
ES.BCN.overviewText:
Explore Barcelona, the Spanish city along the Mediterranean coast that is celebrated for its jaw-dropping architecture and rich heritage. Discover the many iconic sights that the city is known for and immerse yourself in the thriving art and culture scene. Barcelona is home to many famous artists and architects, with works dotted all over the city – ensuring plenty of sights to see and things to do. 

The city’s coastal location adds to Barcelona’s allure, with picturesque beaches to relax on, scenic promenades to stroll down and waterfront restaurants to dine at. The culinary landscape is a delight from local markets and tapas bars to fine dining establishments. Whether you’re attracted to the city’s art, history, food or natural beauty, Barcelona promises a refreshing and inspiring holiday.
ES.BCN.eatingImageText:
Barcelona is a feast for the senses and there are plenty of local Catalan dishes to savour, from the classical streets in the Gothic Quarter to the lively Boqueria Market, where you can purchase fresh produce and local delicacies. 

Try fideuà – a meal similar to paella but prepared with noodles, and canelons – a Catalan adaptation of Italian cannelloni filled with meat or seafood. Conclude your gastronomic adventure with a delectable créme Catalana. Resembling créme brulee, this creamy dessert has a crunchy, caramelised sugar top.

ES.AGP.touristAttractionsText:
Malaga’s skyline is crowned by the majestic Moorish Alcazaba – a twin citadel dating back to the 8th century. Wander its ancient walls and enjoy panoramic views of the city and stunning sunset vistas that turn the citadel’s sandstone walls to a glowing amber. Within the inner citadel, you’ll find three palace gardens with sparkling fountains. 

History buffs will also enjoy the Roman amphitheatre, beautifully preserved and still alive with performances today. Catching a concert here is an unforgettable experience – like time-traveling with a soundtrack.

If you’re a lover of the arts, then you’re in for a treat. Head to Plaza de la Merced, where you’ll find the birthplace of Pablo Picasso. Explore the museum dedicated to his legacy and discover how his influence shaped the art world of the 20th century. 

For something a little different, hop on the Malaga Ferris Wheel near the port. It offers panoramic views of the city, the sea, and the mountains beyond – it’s especially nice at sunset.
ES.AGP.leisureActivitiesText:
No trip to Malaga is complete without soaking up the sun on its iconic beaches. The city’s coastline is famous for a reason – soft golden sand and crystal-clear waters that have earned Blue Flag status. Head to La Misericordia Beach for laid-back vibes and sun-soaked relaxation, or try Los Alamos Beach for a family-friendly day packed with beachside concerts and water sports.

For culinary enthusiasts, tapas tours and espetos are a delicious way to savour the city’s flavours and soak in the culture. You’ll learn about the history and traditions of the locals and enjoy the social atmosphere.

Up for some adventure? Take a day trip to El Caminito del Rey, a dramatic cliffside walkway – thrilling, scenic, and a fantastic way to experience southern Spain. Or, head east along the coast to discover Nerja, with its cliffside views, charming old town and the breathtaking Nerja Caves.

Whether you're chasing mountain air or coastal charm, Malaga is the perfect starting point.
ES.AGP.shoppingText:
Malaga offers a shopping experience as stylish and varied as the city itself. Start with Calle Larios, the city’s most iconic shopping street. This elegant marble-paved boulevard is lined with international brands, designer boutiques, and charming cafés – perfect for browsing and people-watching.

Just a short stroll away is Calle Nueva, a hub for eco-conscious fashion and wellness products. It’s an ideal spot to discover local designers and sustainable finds.

To shop like a local, a visit to the vibrant Atarazanas Market is a must. This bustling marketplace is a feast for the senses, with fresh local produce, sizzling street food and a kaleidoscope of colour thanks to its stunning stained-glass windows and Mudéjar-style architecture. It’s where Malaga’s soul comes alive.

For a truly authentic Spanish shopping experience, wander down Calle Especería. This charming street is dotted with Spanish fashion boutiques and cosy tapas – perfect for mixing retail therapy with a taste of local flavour.
ES.AGP.destinationPageIntro: Malaga is a cultural feast with youthful energy, and it’s the ideal base for a family-friendly beach holiday along the Costa del Sol.
ES.AGP.overviewText:
When you think of Malaga, you instantly picture golden beaches and sparkling blue waters – and for good reason. This gem on Spain’s southern coast is a favourite family destination – the perfect launchpad for exploring the sun-drenched Costa del Sol. But there’s so much more to discover beyond the shoreline.

Malaga is a city that blends history and energy in the most captivating way. Its streets are lined with stunning architecture, centuries-old landmarks and a vibrant spirit that keeps things fresh and exciting. As the birthplace of Picasso, it’s no surprise that art, music, and theatre pulse through the city, offering a true taste of Andalucía’s creative soul.

From cultural treasures to family-friendly adventures, Malaga offers a whole new way to experience Spain.
ES.AGP.eatingImageText:
Food in Malaga is rich, flavourful and unmistakably Andalusian. Be sure to try the local favourite, espeto – fresh sardines skewered and grilled over open flames at beachfront restaurants. It’s smoky, simple, and best enjoyed with a squeeze of lemon and a sea breeze. 

For something sweet, treat yourself to churros dipped in thick, velvety hot chocolate. Or, opt for some ColaCao – a beloved Spanish chocolate drink, often mixed with milk for a quick pick-me-up. Craving a snack? Grab a handful of fried, salted almonds from a local vendor – they’re crunchy, salty and utterly delicious.

Dining in Malaga is full of character. Along the coast, you’ll find lively restaurants where waiters sing out the dishes they’re carrying – just wave when something catches your ear! For a more refined experience, the region also boasts Michelin-starred restaurants, with the finest three-star spots located in nearby Marbella.

CH.GVA.touristAttractionsText:
Geneva’s iconic water fountain, Jet d’Eau has become a symbol of the city. What began as an accidental water release in the 19th century is now a famous landmark for locals and visitors alike, shooting a plume of water over 140 metres high.

A short walk from Jet d’Eau and at the foot of Old Town, sits Parc des Bastions. Home to the city’s first botanical garden and plenty of historic monuments – walking along the tree-lined streets is like taking a tour through history.

For a glimpse into global diplomacy at work, head to the Palais des Nations, the headquarters of the United Nations Office.
CH.GVA.leisureActivitiesText:
From watchmaking history at the Patek Philippe Museum and nuclear research at the CERN Science Gateway, to an immersive humanitarian experience at the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Museum – Geneva is a museum-hopper’s paradise.

If art is more your scene, make your way to Quartier des Bains, a vibrant neighbourhood teeming with galleries and exhibitions. Another museum worth a mention here is Geneva’s largest art museum, Musée d'Art et d'Histoire.

Geneva’s beauty isn’t just within its city limits either. Hike up La Saléve for stunning, panoramic views of the city and Lake Geneva. In winter, the mountainscape transforms into a cross-country skiing wonderland for those with a taste for adventure (and views).
CH.GVA.shoppingText:
As the birthplace of watchmaking, the city is a paradise for timepiece enthusiasts. From world-renowned brands to independent boutiques, most corners of Geneva demonstrate the intricate craftmanship that’s been honed for centuries. If you are in the market for more locally-made items, Swiss army knives and boxes of chocolates are must-have souvenirs.

Geneva is known for its refined, luxurious products, so shopping is a truly indulgent experience. The elegant shopping street of Rue de Marché is the ultimate retail destination, lined with high-end boutiques, luxury fashion houses, jewellers and haute couture.
CH.GVA.destinationPageIntro: The Alpine city of Geneva is rich in sophistication and charm. Experience life at its finest – from the quaint atmosphere and famous Swiss chocolate, to luxury shopping and captivating museums.
CH.GVA.overviewText:
Geneva is a city where every turn reveals a new layer of elegance. Nestled amidst a breathtaking Alpine setting, with its expansive lake framed by snow-capped peaks, visitors will feel like they’ve stepped into a postcard. 

While Geneva boasts historical monuments, it also pulses with a vibrant international energy. The city streets hum with a quiet sophistication – think high-end boutiques, gourmet cafés, and cultural treasures around every corner.

Lose yourself wandering down the cobblestone streets, exploring quirky neighbourhoods, enjoying the serene parks, and savouring the Swiss-French culinary scene.
CH.GVA.destinationHighlightsH1: Geneva: Discover the finer things in life
CH.GVA.eatingImageText:
Often overshadowed by its glamorous European neighbours, Geneva is an underrated foodie city with a delightful mix of culinary influences. 

First up is Swiss chocolate – of course. Geneva boasts world-class chocolatiers known for their high-quality, melt-in-your-mouth masterpieces. 

A stroll through the city streets reveal gourmand surprises at every turn. Venture to Carouge, a bohemian neighbourhood that feels like a small, Italian village. Here, you’ll find an array of cosy cafés and artisanal food spots that reflect the area’s Mediterranean flair.

For a true taste of Switzerland, try rösti, a crispy potato dish that’s the perfect comfort food, or tuck in to the gooey delight of raclette and fondue. Whether it’s dipping bread into molten cheese, or scraping melted raclette from your plate, these dishes are quite the experience and will leave you wanting more.

BA.SJJ.touristAttractionsText:
Sarajevo’s Old Town is the heart of the city – a maze of cobbled streets lined with mosques, restaurants and enticing cafés. Visit the historic Latin Bridge, where Archduke Franz Ferdinand’s assassination took place – a pivotal event that triggered World War I. For a deeper understanding of the city’s past, explore its many museums.

Just a short tram ride away, Vrelo Bosne offers a tranquil escape from the city. Nestled at the source of the Bosna River, this scenic park is perfect for strolls or an afternoon picnic, especially during springtime.
BA.SJJ.leisureActivitiesText:
Take the cable car from the city centre to the top of Mount Trebević for sweeping views across Sarajevo and the surrounding countryside. On the way down, stop at the abandoned bobsleigh track from the 1984 Winter Olympics – now a striking open-air gallery of local street art. Sarajevo also hosts year-round festivals celebrating music, dance, and Balkan life, as well as food festivals that highlight the region’s varied and delicious cuisine.

Visiting in winter? Then make sure to travel to the nearby mountains of Bjelašnica and Jahorina, where excellent snow conditions and challenging runs attract skiers from across the region.
BA.SJJ.shoppingText:
Sarajevo is renowned for its copper craftsmanship, and the best place to encounter it is Kazandžiluk. You’ll find narrow lanes lined with artisan shops offering hand-hammered coffee sets, jewellery and souvenirs.

Gazi Husrev-beg’s Bezistan is a historic covered market from the Ottoman era, filled with stalls selling textiles, leather goods and handicrafts. You’ll also find antique bookshops and Fair-Trade boutiques nestled beside cosy cafés and tea houses.

For a more contemporary experience, head to the modern city centre, where large malls offer air-conditioned comfort and a wide range of national and international brands.
BA.SJJ.destinationPageIntro: A melting pot of influences, Sarajevo is bubbling with fascinating history, bustling markets, and diverse cuisine, offering an exciting mix of arts, shopping and sights.
BA.SJJ.overviewText:
Sarajevo is where East meets West, a city shaped by its complex past and vibrant cultural diversity. Wander through lively streets lined with cafés that echo a European charm, then turn a corner to discover Ottoman-era mosques and traditional bazaars. From ancient architecture to modern shopping streets, Sarajevo offers a unique blend of cultures in one compact, walkable city.

A short journey beyond the city reveals alpine meadows and peaceful rural retreats. Engaging, hospitable, and full of character, Sarajevo is one of Eastern Europe’s most intriguing destinations.
BA.SJJ.eatingImageText:
Bosnian cuisine is a rich blend of Middle Eastern, European and Balkan flavours. Expect subtle spices, hearty portions, and the warm, smoky flavour of paprika in many dishes. 

Ćevapi – small grilled sausages made from minced beef and lamb – are a national favourite, typically served on flatbread with chopped onions, sour cream and ajvar relish. Be sure to also try bey’s soup, or begova čorba. This comforting, hearty meal made with chicken and okra is often served on special occasions.

For a light snack, grab a burek – filo pastry filled with meat, cheese or spinach. End your meal with Bosnian baklava – these sweet filo treats layered with pistachios and honey, are sure to make your day.

MT.MLA.touristAttractionsText:
Malta has some great beaches, and thanks to the onshore breezes, it’s a fabulous spot for surfing and windsurfing. The clear waters around the coast also make it a diver’s dream and there are ancient wrecks to explore under the waves.

The Megalithic Temples are UNESCO World Heritage Sites and some of the oldest structures in the world. The two ancient temples of Ggantija on Gozo hint at the secrets of a lost civilization, while the temples on Malta are incredibly well preserved.

Malta has plenty of festivals throughout the year, with the Valletta Carnival in February and March being one of the best. The Malta Folk Festival celebrates the music and culture of the islands, while the Arts Festival embraces new artists and shows why the islands have inspired generations of painters and sculptors alike.
MT.MLA.leisureActivitiesText:
If you love tennis, you’ll love Malta. The game is hugely popular throughout the island and thanks to the warm climate, the game is played all year round. There are plenty of courts available if you want to play a few sets before breakfast.

Explore the natural beauty of the islands, especially Gozo, by hiking the coastal paths. Or sail into the Blue Lagoon, dive into the crystal-clear waters and swim with the turtles and brightly coloured fish.

History lovers can take a guided tour of the Silent City of Mdina and find out about the legendary Crusader Knights of St John.

If you’re travelling with children, a trip to the Malta National Aquarium lets them get up close to some of the island’s marine species. And for younger ones, there are play areas and parks for all ages.
MT.MLA.shoppingText:
Malta offers all types of shopping experiences from open-air markets and street fairs, to premium malls and boutiques.

Monti Open Air Market in Floriana is one of the most popular for its unique crafts. Spend the day exploring Ta’ Qali Crafts Village in H’attard for handmade filigree jewellery, leather goods, and speciality Mdina glassware. If you want a unique reminder of Malta, look for delicate handmade lace.

If you love truffles and chocolates, Mosta is the place to go to browse shops selling tempting treats. For a taste of old Malta, a visit to the bustling Marsaxlokk market on a Sunday is a delightful experience.

Looking for something a little more modern? Valletta offers the cool comfort of air-conditioned malls and familiar international brands. Or, lose yourself in the delightful maze of Birkirkara’s boutiques, where the thrill of discovering vintage treasures fills the air.
MT.MLA.destinationPageIntro: Malta is a glistening jewel in the Mediterranean, a fascinating combination of Italian and African cultures, and home to some of the oldest structures on the planet.
MT.MLA.overviewText:
Made up of three islands, Malta is an archipelago in the middle of the Mediterranean Sea. Its position between Sicily and North Africa gives it a distinctive heritage and a historically important role, resulting in a group of islands covered in historical monuments and sites. Popular for water sports such as diving, it’s also ideal as a beach destination. Its warm, welcoming ambience makes it an excellent family destination too.

Culturally diverse – with incredible ancient cities, Megalithic temples, busy markets and fine dining – Malta is a thriving holiday location that has so much to offer adventurous travellers. The islands are a dream for anyone interested in history, while beach lovers and especially surfers may have just found their new favourite place in the world.
MT.MLA.destinationHighlightsH1: Malta: A fusion of ancient and modern
MT.MLA.eatingImageText:
Although influenced by Italian and African cooking, Maltese cuisine has developed its own distinct identity. Rabbit is one of the most commonly eaten meats on the island, with fenkata (a marinated stew) eaten on special occasions.

For a quick snack, look out for small savoury pastries called pastizzi, filled with ricotta cheese or an amazingly tasty pea paste.

Fish is a cornerstone in Maltese gastronomy, reflecting the island’s close relationship with the sea. Lampuka (also known as mahi-mahi) is served either fried or in a pie. Other dishes to try are pixxispad mixwi (grilled swordfish steak cooked with lemon and olive oil) and grilled seabass with a simple seasoning.

For light snacks, a plate of cheese and locally grown olives with the local Maltese bread is simple and delicious.

CY.LCA.touristAttractionsText:
Marvel at the Byzantine structures and architecture around Larnaca, often featuring domes, frescoes, and intricate iconography dating back centuries. Browse the Ecclesiastical Museum nearby, a treasure trove of Cypriot heritage, where ancient relics and artefacts are housed.

Then set off to the Hala Sultan Tekke Mosque, a peaceful haven with its whitewashed dome framed by palm trees on the banks of Salt Lake. You can also venture to Larnaca Medieval Castle, a Byzantine-era fortress on the seafront. To go even further back in time, take a trip to the Choirokoitia Neolithic Settlement, a UNESCO World Heritage site. Walk through this village of stone huts that were built thousands of years ago.
CY.LCA.leisureActivitiesText:
Larnaca’s coastline will take your breath away. Finikoudes Beach has a palm-fringed promenade bursting with energy, day and night. Pervolia Beach is a kite surfer’s haven, and McKenzie Beach adds a unique edge to laidback ocean vibes with planes swooping low overhead.

To discover more natural beauty, visit the Larnaca Salt Lake and watch pink flamingos gathering in winter. Want to get a glimpse of the underwater world? Stop by Zenobia Wreck, one of the region’s top dive sites that lies below the Mediterranean waves. Brace a dive to see it up close, or opt for a glass-bottom boat tour.

For a slice of Cyprus’ rustic atmosphere, head to the Larnaca Villages where you’ll be warmly welcomed. These scenic spots are located on rolling hills and filled with local crafts and quaint eateries.
CY.LCA.shoppingText:
Ermou Street, Larnaca’s most popular retail strip, is a lively hub in the centre of the city where high-end boutiques meet artisan stores. Stroll along the colourful pavement and shop distinctive local designs, trendy accessories, and chic clothing. 

You’ll also find Lefkaritika lace, a highlight of Cypriot craftsmanship. This handmade treasure is renowned for its delicate, detailed patterns and stories woven into each piece. Known as an heirloom, the lace is something you can cherish as a piece of Cyprus wherever you go.
CY.LCA.destinationPageIntro: Larnaca boasts sandy beaches, a lively promenade lined with restaurants and shops, and ancient landmarks to explore.
CY.LCA.overviewText:
Nestled on the southern coast of Cyprus, Larnaca invites you to explore its charming culture and storied past. Whether you’re strolling the famed palm-lined promenade or wandering through its ancient streets, every corner tells a tale of bygone eras.

Immerse yourself in its rich tapestry of designs at some of the historic landmarks, or feel the tranquil ambience of its old spiritual sites. Alternatively, uncover the contemporary side of the city by sipping on a Cypriot coffee in a beachside café, or losing yourself in its bustling marketplaces.

Larnaca captures the spirit of Cyprus – sun-drenched, welcoming and timeless. Whether you’re here to relax, shop or dine, memories of this seaside gem will stay with you long after you have left its shores.
CY.LCA.eatingImageText:
Savour the Mediterranean’s freshest flavours at seaside restaurants along Piale Pasha Street. Taste the national dish of grilled souvlakia – succulent skewers of marinated meat. Or, satisfy your taste buds with a platter of Cyprus’ beloved halloumi, fried to perfection or served with pitta bread.

After indulging in traditional cuisine, make your way to the Larnaca Municipal Market, where stalls brim with vibrant dried fruits and earthy olives. Look out for delectable Cypriot sweets too, like the local sugared delights or loukoumades – honey-soaked dough balls that melt in your mouth.

What’s more, you’ll stumble upon goods that portray the heart of Cyprus. Whether it’s a jar of local honey or a bag of aromatic herbs, the market has plenty souvenirs to bring home.

TR.AYT.touristAttractionsText:
Explore the winding streets of Antalya’s Old Quarter and pass through Hadrian’s Gate, a Roman-era triumphal arch. Along the way, browse artisan boutiques, the Fluted Minaret and the historic Broken Minaret mosque. Then, wander downhill to explore Yat Limani, the city’s original Roman harbour. 

For family-friendly fun, spend a day at Konyaaltı Beach and the renowned Antalya Aquarium, featuring one of the world’s longest tunnel aquariums. Or, take a boat trip to the scenic Düden Falls, where the upper cascades offer shaded walking trails and the lower falls spill dramatically into the sea.
TR.AYT.leisureActivitiesText: Spend an evening under the stars at the Roman-era Aspendos Amphitheatre, where plays, concerts and dance performances bring history to life. For panoramic views of the coastline, ride the Olympos Cable Car or take hot air balloon flight over the countryside (it’s particularly beautiful at sunrise!). Antalya’s warm waters are ideal for snorkelling and diving, with PADI-certified schools offering guided experiences for all levels. Families can enjoy paddleboarding along quiet coves, or deep-sea fishing on a private boat trip.
TR.AYT.shoppingText: Shopping in Antalya offers something for every taste — from timeless craftsmanship to sleek up-to-date malls. In the Old Quarter, explore traditional shops tucked down narrow streets for exquisite handmade crafts and souvenirs. Visit Lara Street Market on Saturdays for a lively, authentic experience, or explore Manavgat Bazaar for Turkish carpets, leather goods, and copperware. Haggling is part of the fun, so don’t be shy. For more contemporary shopping, Antalya’s air-conditioned malls and Konyaaltı Street’s stylish outlets offer everything from designer labels to homegrown fashion.
TR.AYT.destinationPageIntro: From sun-soaked sands to fascinating ruins and vibrant markets, Antalya blends history, culture, and cuisine into an unforgettable escape for families and couples alike.
TR.AYT.overviewText: Antalya is one of Türkiye’s most popular destinations, with its golden beaches, incredible nature and that genuinely warm Mediterranean charm. Here, ancient monuments sit alongside modern shopping malls, offering the perfect blend of past and present. And the coast’s crystal-clear waters are perfect for diving, sailing or paddleboarding under the blue skies. With over 300 days of sunshine each year, Antalya creates the most idyllic setting for relaxed family holidays and sunset strolls by the sea. Embrace an easy pace of life and discover the best of Antalya on your next holiday.
TR.AYT.eatingImageText:
Antalya’s cuisine reflects the rich flavours of the region, with dishes that showcase fresh produce, fragrant spices and coastal ingredients. A local favourite is tahini piyaz – a white bean salad topped with a sesame and garlic tarator sauce, often served with warm bread. For a heartier meal, try stuffed lamb ribs, slow-cooked with spiced rice. Fresh seafood is a must, with grouper, sea bass and swordfish often on the menu. 

For dessert, be sure to try arap kadayıf – crisp pastries filled with walnuts and cinnamon, and topped with a honey lemon syrup.

TR.BJV.touristAttractionsText: Step back in time at Bodrum Castle, a 15th-century fortress that’s now home to the Museum of Underwater Archaeology and filled with artefacts from shipwrecks off the Aegean coast. Just outside the city, the well-preserved Roman amphitheatre hosts open-air performances during summer – a unique setting for evening entertainment. Follow the road to Gümbet to spot the region’s historic windmills, once part of daily life in Bodrum. Closer to town, the Myndos Gate marks the ancient city entrance and the site of a battle during Alexander the Great’s siege of Halicarnassus.
TR.BJV.leisureActivitiesText: Bodrum’s beaches are a natural highlight, with clear waters, nearby restaurants and water sports for all ages. The stretch between the castle and Halikarnas is excellent for swimming, and features plenty of free loungers and beachside cafés. Hire a boat from the marina to explore the coast, or visit Vass for windsurfing and a relaxed, bohemian atmosphere. Diving is popular too, with PADI-certified schools offering guided sessions. For something a little different, take a bus to Camel Beach – a peaceful spot where you can go for an exhilarating camel ride along the shore.
TR.BJV.shoppingText: Bodrum offers a diverse shopping scene, from bustling bazaars to elegant marinas and modern malls. In the city centre, browse markets and boutiques for handmade leather sandals, wood carvings, and the region’s famous mandarin jam. Bodrum Bazaar, stretching from the castle to the seafront, is ideal for souvenirs and local crafts. For high-end shopping, head to the designer boutiques at Yalıkavak and Bodrum marinas, where jewellery, art and fashion are on display. Prefer air-conditioned comfort? Bodrum’s malls offer a mix of Turkish and international brands.
TR.BJV.destinationPageIntro: Remarkable history meets coastal charm in Bodrum, where golden beaches, colourful markets, and bold Mediterranean flavours create a memorable escape for both couples and families.
TR.BJV.overviewText: A lively destination on Türkiye’s Aegean coast, Bodrum is a beautiful blend of sun-soaked beaches, abundant history and contemporary style. Once home to the Mausoleum of Halicarnassus – one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World – it now welcomes visitors to its attractive marina, stylish shops and cobbled lanes. Explore the charming Old Quarter, browse bustling markets or enjoy world-class dining along the promenade. From luxury yachts to fascinating ruins, Bodrum offers an engaging mix of relaxation and discovery for an unforgettable summer holiday.
TR.BJV.eatingImageText: Bodrum’s dining scene offers something for everyone – from upscale restaurants to welcoming family-run taverns. For a true taste of the region, try Çökertme kebab – crisp matchstick potatoes topped with tender lamb or beef, finished with garlic yoghurt and tomato sauce. Local menus often feature seasonal vegetables, including delicately stuffed zucchini flowers. With its coastal location, Bodrum is known for fresh seafood dishes. Red mullet, sea bass and bream are popular, while lobster, octopus and crab are prepared simply with lemon and herbs.

NG.ABV.touristAttractionsText:
The Abuja National Mosque is one of the top landmarks to visit. The striking architecture is a testament to Abuja’s religious and cultural heritage. Its golden dome, towering minarets and intricate interior are a symbol of unity and spirituality.

When it comes to natural attractions, the Usama Dam offers a tranquil escape, with sparkling waters and green hills to marvel at. It’s also a lovely place to enjoy a picnic. A little further off the beaten path is Gurara Waterfalls, a cascading beauty surrounded by greenery. Feel the thrill of adventure at Wonderland Mountain with its diverse landscapes, perfect for hikes or a quiet stroll.
NG.ABV.leisureActivitiesText:
Take a trip to Nike Art Gallery, a treasure trove of Nigerian creativity. The gallery brims with bold, colourful artwork and detailed sculptures that showcase the city’s cultural heritage. For a family fun day, Sunrise Waterpark is worth a visit. Kids and adults alike will love cooling off in the pools and racing down the slides and water rides. The National Children’s Park and Zoo is another family-friendly place to visit to see native wildlife and exotic animals.

A holiday to Abuja wouldn’t be complete without a deep dive into Nigeria’s wilderness. Take a day trip to the Yankari Game Reserve, a wildlife park like no other. Here, you can spot African bush elephants, African buffaloes, Olive baboons, countless bird species and more.
NG.ABV.shoppingText:
Wuse Market is a buzz of activity where you can find fresh produce, spices and a variety of souvenirs to take home with you. Think traditional fabrics in bold prints and colours, beaded jewellery and beautiful leatherworks.

For those with an eye for unique finds, the market’s bronze carvings are a must-see. Each piece, from delicate figurines to larger-than-life sculptures, showcases Nigeria’s exceptional craftmanship.
NG.ABV.destinationPageIntro: From natural wonders to unusual museums and beautiful mosques, you’ll discover that there’s plenty to see and do in Nigeria’s capital, Abuja.
NG.ABV.overviewText:
Built in the 1980’s and named the capital of Nigeria in 1991, Abuja is a city that boasts modern infrastructure and natural wonder. Its charm extends far beyond the city centre. Just a short drive away from the hustle and bustle, nature thrives with landscapes of lush greenery and stunning waterfalls.

Explore Abuja’s natural beauty and cultural diversity through galleries, markets and city landmarks. From city dwellings to the quiet hills, the city invites you to adventure and unwind.
NG.ABV.eatingImageText:
There are a few regional favourites in Abuja that you have to try. First is masa, a fluffy rice cake with a hint of sweetness – delicious on its own or dipped in soup.

Next, make sure to try the popular street food, suya – grilled meat skewers seasoned with a peanut-based spice blend and topped with thinly sliced onions. Looking for a light bite? Try dambu nama, sometimes referred to as meat floss – it’s shredded beef or chicken, seasoned with ground spices and dried. Another popular dried meat snack across Northern Nigeria is kilishi, a spicy beef or sometimes lamb jerky.

And of course, no trip to Nigeria is complete without trying jollof rice, a West African staple that’s as vibrant in taste as it is in colour. This moreish rice dish is cooked in a spicy tomato sauce, typically served with fried plantain and meat, chicken or fish.

Indulge in these city flavours at the Street Food Park in Wuse, where local vendors serve up an array of cultural dishes and desserts. Finally, take a trip to Maitama Farmers’ Market to sample Abuja’s fresh produce.

SY.ALP.touristAttractionsText:
No visit to Aleppo is complete without exploring the Citadel, an imposing fortress that has stood at the heart of the city since the third millennium BC. Take in sweeping views across the ancient skyline from its formidable walls.

Wander through the al-Jalloum district to discover the Great Mosque of Aleppo, a remarkable 11th-century monument surrounded by peaceful courtyards. Admire intricate stonework and graceful minarets that evoke centuries past.

To uncover Aleppo’s storied past, visit the National Museum, home to extraordinary artefacts unveiling Syria’s vivid history. Nearby, the elegant Popular Traditions Museum reveals life inside a traditional Aleppine mansion.
SY.ALP.leisureActivitiesText:
Step into one of the world’s oldest hammams and experience the rejuvenating warmth of traditional steam baths, surrounded by exquisite qashani-tiled walls and floors.

Visit the Cultural Village on the outskirts of Aleppo to discover beautifully restored historic homes and artisans showcasing authentic Syrian crafts.

Throughout the year, vibrant festivals bring Aleppo’s spirit to life. Celebrate local traditions at the Cotton Festival, or admire the elegance of Arabian horses at the Al-Asala Festival.

Take time to stroll through the winding alleys of Aleppo’s historic Old City, where hidden courtyards and bustling markets await, as well as tempting street vendors offering cool drinks and savoury treats.
SY.ALP.shoppingText:
Aleppo’s traditional crafts are a delight waiting to be discovered. Start with the city’s famous soap, hand-crafted from olive and laurel oil at an 800-year-old soap factory.

Explore exciting souqs, where gold jewellery glitters under vaulted ceilings. Look out for the distinctive Aleppo weave, a unique chain design crafted only in this historic city.

To store your new treasures, pick up a hand-made wooden box, delicately inlaid with classic Arab patterns.

The Al-Madina Souq, once one of the longest covered markets in the world, offers an absorbing journey through leather goods, sparkling jewellery and, of course, fresh pistachios.

For a more modern shopping experience, Aleppo’s malls offer high-end international brands, stylish local boutiques, family-friendly entertainment, and inviting restaurants.
SY.ALP.destinationPageIntro: A timeless metropolis of winding souqs, ancient citadels, and fascinating traditions – Aleppo invites you to explore over five millennia of captivating history.
SY.ALP.overviewText:
One of the world's oldest continuously inhabited cities, Aleppo blends layers of ancient history with bustling modern life. At its heart lies the Old City, a UNESCO World Heritage Site where winding streets reveal stunning Arabic architecture and beguiling hidden courtyards. Let us guide you through this enchanting destination, where every corner tells a story spanning over 5,000 years.

Today, Aleppo is reclaiming its place as a cultural and commercial centre in the Middle East. Bustling souqs offer a complex tapestry of spices, textiles, and crafts, while new malls bring exclusive shopping opportunities. Savour traditional Syrian cuisine at local markets, where bold flavours and time-honoured recipes abound. With a warm, welcoming spirit and a deep pride in its history, Aleppo invites you to experience a destination where the past and present come together in unforgettable ways.
SY.ALP.eatingImageText:
Aleppo’s cuisine is known for its bold flavours and traditional techniques. A must-try is fuul (a hearty bean stew infused with onions and mint), or shawarma (spicy marinated chicken wrapped in warm bread with pickled cucumber and garlic cream).

For a lighter meal, sample mujaddara, a savoury blend of brown lentils, rice and caramelised onions. Yabraq, tender vine leaves stuffed with minced lamb and slow-cooked in lemon juice, offers an authentic taste of Aleppo.

Sweet-lovers will enjoy basbousa (a sticky semolina cake soaked in syrup), or tulumba (golden dough balls drenched in syrup). Aleppo’s famous pistachios also feature in delicate, flaky baklava.

AE.AUH.overviewTabHeading: Book your visit to Abu Dhabi

AE.AUH.touristAttractionsText:
Begin your Abu Dhabi holiday at the country’s largest mosque, Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque. Take a tour to learn what went into building this architectural marvel. 

For more opulence, make your way to the Emirates Palace. This hotel is covered in over 6,000 square metres of gold leaf, making it a popular choice for the world’s most affluent. Taste the grandeur with a 24-carat gold leaf cappuccino at the lobby café. Nearby, the Presidential Palace awaits where Emirati leadership often meet with delegates. The buildings and grounds are spectacular to explore.

To get your bearings, go up to the Etihad Towers Skydeck for a 360-degree view of the city – take the opportunity to enjoy high tea there, too. Opposite the towers lies the Abu Dhabi Corniche, an 8-kilometre recreational path perfect for a walk, scooter or bike ride.
AE.AUH.leisureActivitiesText:
Spend a day at the Louvre Abu Dhabi. This floating dome museum is magnificent from the inside out. You can even kayak around it, which is stunning at sunset. Further immerse yourself in what the city has to offer and kayak in the Eastern Mangroves too.

Take a few days to explore Yas Island and its four iconic theme parks to enjoy water slides and the world’s fastest rollercoaster. It’s a playground for both the young and young at heart. Similarly, the National Aquarium is a wonderful place to witness some of the planet’s most colourful marine life, while learning more about the country’s conservation efforts.

Beaches surround the city of Abu Dhabi. Sink your toes into the white sands of Saadiyat Island’s Soul Beach.
AE.AUH.businessClassTitle: Business Class flights to Abu Dhabi
AE.AUH.shoppingText:
The city’s plethora of malls are more than just a shopping destination – they are an experience. Browse designer boutiques, play in an indoor snow park or head straight to a theme park. In the heat of summer, the malls are where to be!

For a glimpse of local culture, make your way to the Old Souk for a modern take on the old marketplaces. It’s perfect to buy ceramics, traditional dress, cashmere scarves and decorative wares as souvenirs.

Visit the Gold Souk for a lasting memory of your trip. As one of the best places in the world to buy gold, it’s almost essential.

The date market, located near the fish market, is worth a visit too – sample some of the world’s finest dates and grab yourself a few edible treats to take home.
AE.AUH.touristAttractionsTabHeading: Things to do in Abu Dhabi
AE.AUH.destinationPageIntro: Go for white-knuckle rides at theme parks and water parks, or head to sandy beaches to relax. Abu Dhabi awaits.
AE.AUH.overviewText:
Step into the unique city of Abu Dhabi, where modernity truly converges with tradition. The city’s atmosphere is rooted in its Arabic heritage mixed with futuristic architecture and world-leading technology. Skyscrapers rise into the sky amidst the bustling souks wafting aromas of exotic spices.

Find yourself embracing a sun-soaked beach on the Arabian Gulf by morning and on the world’s fastest rollercoaster in the evening. There is an activity for every kind of traveller with a cultural district, entertainment district, incredible dining, pristine beaches and water sports. 

In Abu Dhabi, every moment is an invitation to discover something new.
AE.AUH.eatingImageText:
The culinary scene is as diverse as the city, with an amalgamation of cultures and flavours. Abu Dhabi is home to many world-class dining experiences and Michelin-starred restaurants.

For a local favourite, venture down Hamdan Street for a self-guided food tour. Sink your teeth into a shawarma and sip on a piping hot cup of karak tea, spiced with cinnamon, ginger and cardamom, to name a few.

Seafood lovers, head to the Fish Market at Mina Zayed for an experience like no other. Spend the day fishing on the Gulf, or choose a freshly caught fish from the market. Then take it to one of the restaurants on the edge of the market where they gut it, cook it to perfection, and serve it to you – what a treat.

DE.BER.businessClassSummary:
Fly to Berlin in Business or First Class with Qatar Airways and discover a vibrant destination known for its rich history. From start to finish, every element of your voyage is meticulously taken care of by our world-renowned team. 

Begin your trip to Germany’s capital with frictionless check-in before unwinding in one of our deluxe Business Class lounges. Here, you can freshen up with a shower or use one of the private workstations to catch up on your emails. To enjoy a quiet moment, indulge in some reading while sipping a cool beverage or tucking into a light snack before your flight.  

Once on board our state-of-the-art aircraft, you’re shown to a spacious, ergonomically designed seat with generous legroom. Settle in and take advantage of the high-speed Wi-Fi (available on our A380, A350, B787 and select B777 aircraft) for those essential video calls. Then delight your tastebuds with the dishes on our à la carte menu, prepared for you by our award-winning chefs.  

After your meal, relax with a film or TV show from our entertainment library, or get some rest on a lie-flat bed with soft linen and ambient lighting to help your body reset to your destination’s time zone. Arrive feeling revived and ready for business or exploring the city’s cultural attractions.  

Book a flight to Berlin in First or Business Class with Qatar Airways and experience luxury travel at its finest.
DE.BER.touristAttractionsText:
One must experience the iconic piece of history that is the Berlin Wall. Start at the Visitor Centre to understand its history and significance, then venture to admire the wall's remnants. The largest section of the wall runs for just under one and a half kilometres, now named the East Side Gallery. It’s been painted by 118 international artists, creating the longest open-air gallery in the world.

Head over to Brandenburg Gate, another portal to Berlin’s storied past. Then, take a breather at the Berlin Cathedral. For a monumental Berlin city view, climb the spiral staircase in the futuristic glass dome of the Reichstag Building – an architectural marvel that is far from just a regular government building.

For something a little different, head to the Berlin Story Bunker. A bit like Berlin itself, this underground museum is gritty, intriguing and packed with interesting facts.
DE.BER.leisureActivitiesText:
Explore the heart of Berlin’s cultural scene at Museum Island, where five museums await you. Designated as a UNESCO World Heritage Site, this museum complex showcases all sorts of exhibitions from art and cultural, to historical and archeological.

After museum-hopping, make your way to Tiergarten Park. The lush park is idyllic for leisurely strolls and picnics, or you can rent a bike if you’re feeling active.

Ready for a thrill? The Berlin Dungeon is a spine-tingling adventure you can’t miss. This immersive attraction with live actors uncovers Berlin’s history in the most entertaining way possible.

If you’re visiting with family, Zoo Berlin is a hit with all ages. Dating back to 1844, this zoo has evolved over the years as the home to a huge variety of species – a must-see for animal enthusiasts.
DE.BER.shoppingText:
Shopping in Berlin is a journey through the eras. Charlottenburg Palace becomes lively with market stalls every December and should not be missed. Once a royal residence, these magnificent grounds transform into a winter wonderland, with twinkling lights and handcrafted gifts.

For a renowned favourite that has stood the test of time, visit Kurfürstendamm. Doubling as an attraction, the Champs-Élysées of Berlin is not only dotted with luxury boutiques, but also houses gourmet restaurants, concert halls and opera houses.

If the modern-day chic in you is calling, browse Friedrichstraße. The mix of contemporary and classic gives you plenty of options to fill your suitcase. For the laid-back shopper, Bergmannstraße and Oranienstraße are your go-to. They even hold weekly markets for vintage treasures and upcycled good
DE.BER.destinationPageIntro: Journey through time in the city of Berlin. Discover the remnants of the Berlin Wall contrasted with modern-day art. Immerse yourself in local eateries and cafés.
DE.BER.overviewText:
Berlin, a place where every corner tells a story. From the cobblestone streets echoing footsteps of the past, to the colourful graffiti murals shouting the voices of today. It’s a blend of cultures, with a creative energy that influences everyone who visits. Dive into hip neighbourhoods with arty districts filled with unique shops and independent galleries. Socialise with friendly locals in lively outdoor spaces and enjoy the comforting aromas of Berlin’s delicacies.

Berlin isn’t just a destination, it’s an experience – a living tapestry of stories waiting to be discovered. Pack your curiosity and come see what adventures await in this captivating city.
DE.BER.destinationHighlightsH1: Berlin: History with a contemporary twist
DE.BER.eatingImageText:
One of the best parts about Berlin is dining outdoors – it’s the quintessential Berlin thing to do. While you’re there, sink your teeth into currywurst. This popular sausage dish is smothered in a tangy, curry ketchup sauce. Much like this, meals in Berlin are typically of the hearty kind, such as Königsberger Klopse – a bowl of meatballs in a creamy, caper sauce.

Treat your taste buds to a late-night street food snack. The doner kebab (bread wrapped around sliced meats and vegetables, drizzled with creamy sauces) is quite a hit with the locals.

For a taste of the market halls, Markthalle Neun is a favourite – abundant with everything from artisanal cheeses to exotic spices. Don’t miss Street Food Thursday where you can sample food from all over the world.

IN.CCU.touristAttractionsText:
Kolkata’s most popular tourist attraction is the Queen Victoria Memorial and it’s easy to see why. The past whispers through its majestic marble halls and the tranquil gardens provide a relaxing retreat from the liveliness of the city. 

Venture south to Kalighat Mandir, a sacred structure that is not only stunning in appearance but also home to a wealth of Indian history and significance.

Depending on the time of year, you may see workers extracting clay from the banks of the Ganga, also known as the Hooghly River, if you travel out of the city to Kumartuli. Between August and October, they are particularly busy preparing for rituals.

Cricket lovers must not miss visiting the Eden Gardens – the oldest cricket stadium in the whole of India.
IN.CCU.leisureActivitiesText:
For a truly unique activity, attend a tea auction at Nilhat House. Catch a tram there for a quintessential Kolkata experience. Watch the passionate spirit of Kolkata’s commerce, and enjoy the sight and aroma of fresh, local tea leaves. 

Looking for green spaces? Explore Bidhannagar, also known as Salt Lake City. Head to Salt Lake Central Park for bird watching or Nicco Park for fun activities the whole family will enjoy. 

For an unforgettable adventure, take a day trip out of the city to the Sundarbans, where the majestic Bengal tiger roams the mangroves. Listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site, the Sundarbans is known as the largest mangrove forest in the world. It’s certainly worth a trip out of the city centre to marvel at its beauty.
IN.CCU.shoppingText:
Shopping in Kolkata is a treasure hunt through time-honoured traditions. The textiles and crafts are second to none – browse silks, saris and intricate handwoven fabrics that tell stories of generations.

Bookworms will also find delight in Kolkata, a city famed for its intellectual side. Explore College Street, where book merchants line its sidewalks, offering rare editions and the latest bestsellers.

Park Street is where Kolkata’s past and present collide, with chic boutiques lined alongside colonial architecture. Shop for clothing, crafts and everything in between. For a local shopping experience, go to New Market – a bustling maze of stalls where you can find conch shell jewellery, vibrant bangles and hand-moulded terracotta sculptures.
IN.CCU.destinationPageIntro: From the beauty of the Queen Victoria Market to tiger spotting in the Sundarbans, Kolkata is a vibrant city of culture and adventure.
IN.CCU.overviewText:
Explore Kolkata, a city rich in culture and history. Discover a bustling destination where the aroma of spices and chai fill the air as you wander through the vibrant streets. Immerse yourself in the atmosphere of colourful rickshaws, friendly street vendors and lively chatter that create a symphony that is unmistakably Kolkata.

Old-world charm is ever-present as art, literature and food aren’t just appreciated – they are celebrated. Whether you are savouring a street-side snack, getting lost in a hidden alleyway or Bengal tiger spotting, Kolkata has a way of drawing you in.
IN.CCU.eatingImageText:
Begin your culinary journey with a steaming cup of chai, the city’s lifeblood. Then discover local cuisine, where macher jhol (a fish curry) takes centre stage. Tender fish swims in a spicy, tangy gravy that dances on your taste buds – it’s the heartbeat of every Bengali kitchen.

Dacres Lane is a foodie’s playground, as street vendors whip up everything from crispy pakora (fritters) to juicy kebabs. For those with a sweet tooth, the rasgulla is a must try. These soft, spongy dumplings soaked in a sweet syrup are not to be missed in Kolkata.

For the early birds, Terreti Bazaar is the place to be. Arrive at dawn and you will be rewarded with a feast of Chinese dumplings, fresh fish and flavourful breakfast dishes – all prepared right before your eyes.

CN.CKG.touristAttractionsText:
Immerse yourself in the character of the city with a visit to the Hongya Cave Cultural Centre. It’s a glimpse into the heart of Chongqing and is beautiful when lit up at night. The riverfront location means you get a spectacular view of the Yangtze as it flows past.

Take a cable car across the river and stroll along Nanbin Road. This is the place to stop and get that perfect picture of the Chongqing skyline in all its splendour. A little further along you’ll find the night food market at Haitang Yanyu Park.

The region is famous for its hot springs, so a tour bus trip out of the city to one of the nearby parks will let you experience them for yourself. It’s a great way to soothe tired muscles, or check into one of the many spas and wellness centres in the city for a traditional massage.
CN.CKG.leisureActivitiesText:
With the Yangtze right on your doorstep, it’s a perfect opportunity to take a leisurely river tour to see some of China’s most incredible scenery, including the Three Gorges. A visit to the Three Gorges Museum is a chance to learn about the Ba-Yu culture before your cruise.

While Chongqing is full of skyscrapers, some parts are much older. A stroll around Ciqikou Ancient Town gives you a chance to see the original heart of the Mountain City and browse for handmade crafts.

Chongqing embraces its natural beauty, and a visit to one of its many parks and gardens is well worth the time. A short journey out of the centre of the city brings you to the Huayan Tourist Park, one of the city’s most charming and tranquil retreats. Or visit the Jinyun Mountain Natural Reserve for hiking trails.
CN.CKG.shoppingText:
This ultra-modern city has plenty of shopping malls to choose from, with a major mall located in each downtown district. These are filled with high-end stores, designer labels and smaller shops offering clothing, cosmetics and accessories.

You’ll also find plenty of food courts and entertainment options in all of the city’s larger malls.

The region is famous for its delicate Shu embroidery, filled with intricate details and graceful designs. If you’re looking for a distinctive memento of your visit, a piece of Shu embroidery is ideal and you’ll find plenty of craftspeople in the markets selling examples.

The city’s main commercial districts include Jiefangbei and the Shapingba Three Square Walking Street, where you’ll find a wealth of retail outlets, shops and boutiques.
CN.CKG.destinationPageIntro: Chongqing, the beautiful Mountain City, welcomes visitors with a beguiling combination of modern and traditional, with delicious food, river cruises, and bustling markets.
CN.CKG.overviewText:
One of the world’s fastest-growing tourist destinations, Chongqing is an enthralling city sitting alongside the Yangtze River. Famous for its vibrant arts scene, spicy food, and stunning scenery, the ‘Mountain City’ is a fast-paced, lively city break destination.

Chongqing is often shrouded in an ethereal mist, thanks to the mountainous landscape, giving it a fairytale-like atmosphere. But at street level, you’ll find everything from air-conditioned malls (a welcome escape from the summer heat) to traditional markets, temples and winding alleyways full of tiny shops.

If you love browsing for bargains, Chongqing is an ideal shopping destination. From UNESCO World Heritage Sites to roadside cafés, Chongqing is a truly remarkable city that’s well worth adding to your bucket list.
CN.CKG.eatingImageText:
At the heart of Chongqing cuisine is hot pot - basically a broth that’s simmered with a variety of herbs and spices. This is the city’s most popular dish and falls into three categories – mild, medium or spicy. Beware – the latter can be challenging for those not used to chili!

Diners are given a variety of thinly sliced meats, fresh seafood, leafy greens, mushrooms, tofu, and noodles, which are then added to the broth. It’s a perfect way to discover the variety of flavours on offer in Chongqing.

Street food is extremely popular and you’ll find plenty of night markets where you can try noodles and dumplings. Chongqing has several night markets, such as Jiaochangkou,  Guanyinqiao and Nanbin Road.

SY.DAM.touristAttractionsText:
For one of the best panoramic views of the city, take the trek up to the top of Mount Qasioun, especially in the evening when the city sparkles below. You’ll also be rewarded with some excellent restaurants at the top, as well as street food vendors, before you make the walk back down.

The city’s hammams are famous for their authentic Turkish baths, especially Nur-al-Din Bath (men only) and Bakri Bath (open to women every day except Friday).

The Old City is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and is filled with wonderfully atmospheric narrow streets and souqs. Another historically important site to add to your itinerary is the Narcissus Palace, where evening performances of Arabic music in the traditional eateries immerse visitors in the culture of the city.
SY.DAM.leisureActivitiesText:
Visit Umayyad Mosque, one of the largest and oldest in the world, and a major cultural landmark with impressive architecture. Inside you’ll find tombs and shrines of historical figures. 

Stroll down Souq al-Hamidiyah until you come to the Citadel or walk along Straight Street. This ancient Roman road is lined with historic buildings and boutiques selling silks, jewellery and trinkets. 

To understand more about Damascus, a visit to the Al-Azm Palace Museum is one of the best ways to immerse yourself in its culture. The tranquil courtyard and gardens give visitors a chance to appreciate the palace’s exquisite architecture too.

For a taste of modern Damascus, visit the Opera House. This contemporary performance space has excellent acoustics and hosts performances from world-renowned musicians and singers.
SY.DAM.shoppingText:
From souqs to malls, Damascus is a shopper’s dream. For budget shopping, take a wander through Souq al-Hamidiyah, Damascus’ main covered market. Or visit the Midhat Pasha Souq for traditional market stalls and plenty of bargains. 

If you love browsing independent stores, Straight Street is lined with handicraft stalls, antiques shops and galleries. Explore the Bab Sharqi area for high-end boutiques. 

In the Old City, the alleyways are home to some more unusual stores where you can really experience a genuinely friendly and welcoming ambience and plenty of beautiful, handcrafted items on display. 

For some luxury shopping, the Four Seasons Hotel Shopping Arcade is filled with international brands, or take a walk down Salhiyeh Street for some exclusive outlets.
SY.DAM.destinationPageIntro: Damascus is where the old and the new sit side by side. Wander through endless bazaars, dine on delicious food, and savour the sights and sounds of this ancient metropolis.
SY.DAM.overviewText:
Damascus is a truly incredible destination. The world’s oldest continually inhabited city is a maze of cobbled streets and alleyways, bustling bazaars and peaceful parks. Its remarkable history is on display on every street corner, with golden-domed mosques and brooding citadels that beg to be explored. Its people are warm, friendly and incredibly welcoming.

With an array of world-class restaurants, simple coffee shops, and deliciously spicy street food, it’s a foodie’s dream. 

From the UNESCO World Heritage Old City to the extraordinary Umayyad Mosque, there’s so much to see in this lovely city that just one visit will not be enough.
SY.DAM.eatingImageText:
Syrian cuisine is flavoursome, spicy, and delicious. There are plenty of international restaurants in Damascus but if you want to eat like a local, look out for dishes such as kibbeh – a mix of bulgur, minced onions and ground meat with a distinctive mix of spices. 

Share a mezze with family and friends, where you can all try a selection of dishes. Or choose a hearty meal of lamb served with fatteh (soaked bread, chickpeas and yogurt).

The best place to find authentic Syrian food is in the Midan area of the city, just south of the Old City. For the best shawarma and falafel stands, and pastry shops with sweet pastries piled high, visit Jazmatiya Street.

DE.DUS.touristAttractionsText:
Ready to explore? Your first stop has to be the Rhine Tower. You’ll get a bird’s-eye view of the whole city, including the gorgeous Rhine River Promenade (which is perfect for a relaxing stroll, by the way). For something a little different, check out the Media Harbour, where cutting-edge architecture creates a striking contrast against the backdrop of the calm Rhine. 

Step back in time in Düsseldorf Old Town. You’ll find a delightful mix of traditional restaurants and taverns lining the historic cobblestone streets. As you explore, you’ll come across the unique St Lambertus Cathedral, a landmark that holds centuries of history. 

For a royal escape, make your way to Benrath Palace. This stunning Rococo palace with grand gardens will make you feel like you’ve stepped into a fairytale.
DE.DUS.leisureActivitiesText:
Whether you’re into art, thrills or family fun, this city has something for you. 

The Museum Kunstpalast houses a vast collection of European masterpieces, modern art, and delicate glassworks that are sure to inspire you. If you’re looking for something a little more adventurous, head to Alpenpark Neuss, just a short trip outside the city. This indoor ski resort is a skiing and snowboarding wonderland, open year-round for that perfect adrenaline rush.

Car enthusiasts, prepare to be wowed at the Classic Remise Düsseldorf. This place will ignite your admiration for vintage automobiles. There’s a showroom and museum filled with classic cars, each with its own story of design, speed and history.

Travelling with little ones? Sea Life is a must-do. Explore the wonders of the ocean and get up close with amazing marine creatures.
DE.DUS.shoppingText:
No trip to Düsseldorf is complete without a day shopping on the prestigious Königsallee, otherwise named King’s Alley. This isn’t your average street – think high-end boutiques, designer stores and a serious dose of glamour. It’s no wonder Düsseldorf is known as Germany’s fashion capital – the Kö, as locals call it, is where style come to life! From couture gowns to intricate watches and more, you’ll find it all here. 

Head to Radschlägermarkt for a glimpse of something more eclectic. This vibrant flea market held on Sundays, is filled with vintage finds, antiques and trinkets. Searching for a retro piece to spice up your wardrobe? Or maybe a one-of-a-kind painting to take back home?  This is the place to be.
DE.DUS.destinationPageIntro: Düsseldorf is full of cultural intrigue in every corner, from contemporary art collections and artisan eateries, to grand historic architecture.
DE.DUS.overviewText:
Step into the vibrant heart of Düsseldorf, Germany’s fashion capital. The city has an energetic atmosphere that’s constantly buzzing with creativity and modern style. And when it comes to retail, you’ll find an experience that’s second to none. 

But it’s much more than just a place to shop – Düsseldorf embodies style in every aspect of daily life. Art, music, and cuisine culture come together to create a quintessentially German experience. Explore the city’s diverse neighbourhoods, each with its own unique character. You’ll stumble upon charming little cafés tucked away on quiet streets and one-of-a-kind treasures in stylish boutiques. Düsseldorf has a way of sparking your curiosity and leaving you with unforgettable memories.
DE.DUS.eatingImageText:
In Düsseldorf’s Altstadt (Old Town), food is more than just tasting – it’s a whole experience. Start off at Carlsplatz Market, a thriving hub where stalls overflow with fresh fish, artisanal cheeses, and local delicacies. The aromas filling the air will have you wanting to grab a bite of everything. 

If you’re craving a hearty local meal, then try Düsseldorf's beloved Halve Hahn – a rye roll layered with thick slices of creamy gouda cheese, and served with a dollop of tangy mustard. Speaking of mustard, it’s a really big deal here. Düsseldorf’s known for its spicy mustard, and it’s best sampled with juicy roast chicken or tender beef – a classic Rhineland favourite that you can’t miss.

TR.ESB.touristAttractionsText:
Discover the history of the Hammam with a visit to the Roman Baths of Ankara, complete with an open-air museum. Then head into the old part of the city for your own Hamman experience. Or deep dive into the culture of Türkiye with a visit to the Ethnography Museum.

To marvel at traditional architecture, make your way to Antikabir, the huge mausoleum of Mustafa Kemal Ataturk, the founder of modern Türkiye. It’s at the heart of not just the city but the entire country, and is a magnificent building with a fascinating museum attached. The daily Changing of the Guard ceremony is a wonderfully photogenic event.

Creativity is a key aspect of life in Ankara, and the CerModern Contemporary Art Gallery offers a stunning showcase of modern art. Exhibiting both national and international artists, it always has plenty to see.
TR.ESB.leisureActivitiesText:
There are several great family attractions, including the Club Watercity Aquapark, enchanting Ankara Toy Museum, and immersive Aqua Vega Aquarium. Here, you can walk through an acrylic tunnel just inches from sharks swimming over your head! You can also go on a family outing to Gençlik Parkı, with cafés and fun-filled amusement park rides for everyone.

For a tranquil break from all the action, admire panoramic views from Atakule, the 125m-high observation tower. While you’re there, indulge in a meal at the revolving restaurant. Or venture outside the city during a day trip to the Eymir Lake, a calming setting where you can relax. Take a boat trip or pack a picnic and enjoy the picturesque scenery.
TR.ESB.shoppingText:
The most popular areas for retail therapy in Ankara include Kizilay, Tunali Street, Kavaklidere, Ulus and Izmir Street. In Kizilay, treat yourself to the ultimate boutique shopping experience, especially on the tree-lined Atatürk Boulevard. This district is also known for its premium malls, including the Karum Mall. To see a mall loved by locals, stop by Gordion Shopping Center, offering dining, entertainment and an abundance of fashion outlets.

Tunali Hilmi is an ideal bazaar for genuine Turkish handicrafts. Ulus is one of the best spots for bags, textiles and artwork, while Izmir Street is home to some of the highest quality leather goods, including belts and handmade shoes. For upmarket shopping and art galleries, go to the Çankaya district and browse unique independent stores as well as artisan shops.
TR.ESB.destinationPageIntro: Ankara is one of Türkiye’s true gems. Lively, exciting and energetic, it’s the perfect destination for a city break in summer or winter.
TR.ESB.overviewText:
Once just a small town famous for its Angora wool, Ankara has grown into Türkiye’s modern capital. It’s a bustling place that embraces both its ancient history and youthful vibrancy, making it an ideal city break destination for families and couples.

Ankara has a charm of its own, shaped by its past and present. Roman monuments and museums stocked with captivating relics, sit alongside sleek boutiques, designer stores and exclusive restaurants. 

The city is a feast for the senses in both summer and winter. Savour local cuisine, with street vendors selling mouth-watering treats, and spoil yourself while shopping in any of the busy markets or air-conditioned, contemporary malls.
TR.ESB.destinationHighlightsH1: Ankara: A historic city filled with life
TR.ESB.eatingImageText:
Turkish cuisine is packed with flavour yet pleasantly mild, making it perfect for families and adventurous foodies. Wander around Ankara’s older districts and look for meyhanes, restaurants where you can sample fresh seafood dishes and authentic Turkish delicacies such as meze. You’ll also find street vendors selling on-the-go treats like halka tatlisi, a deep-fried dough drenched in sugar syrup.

Besides this, feast on the popular doner kebab or lahmacun, also known as ‘Turkish pizza’. Don’t forget to try Ankara tava, a dish made with lamb, orzo pasta, tomatoes and hot peppers. If you’re craving international cuisine, explore a variety of options including Chinese, Indian and Thai. Tunalı Hilmi Street and the area around Kuğul Park have some excellent restaurants.

DE.FRA.businessClassSummary:
Fly to Frankfurt in Business or First Class with Qatar Airways for a luxurious travel experience. From the moment you arrive at the airport to the moment you land at your destination; you’ll enjoy unrivalled service tailored to your needs.

Begin your journey with hassle-free, priority check-in, followed by a peaceful break in one of our exclusive Business Class lounges. Here, you can sip on a beverage, savour a light snack, use state-of-the-art workstations, or take a revitalising shower before your flight.

On board our modern, spacious aircraft, you’re greeted by our professional cabin crew and shown to your seat. With ample legroom and plenty of personal space, you can just stretch out and relax. Stay connected to colleagues and friends using the fast Wi-Fi, available on our A380, A350, B787 and select B777 aircraft.

Indulge your love of gourmet cuisine with dishes from our à la carte menu, freshly prepared by our award-winning chefs. After your meal, watch a film or TV show from our extensive entertainment selection. Then rest a on a lie-flat bed with soft linen, while the ambient lighting gently adjusts your body to your destination’s time zone. Arrive in Germany’s commercial capital feeling refreshed and ready to immerse yourself in its dynamic business sector and lively cultural scene.

Book a flight to Frankfurt in Business or First Class with Qatar Airways and bask in unmatched comfort.
DE.FRA.touristAttractionsText:
In a city where history and modernity blend seamlessly, start your journey at Frankfurt’s most historic landmark, The Römer. This medieval gem is a must-see, especially in winter when it transforms into a festive wonderland with markets and the aroma of roasted chestnuts filling the air.

Just a stone’s throw away is the DomRömer Quarter, teeming with cafés, boutiques, and museums. Grab a coffee and watch the world go by. Next up, the Cathedral of St. Bartholomew awaits with its soaring spire, its Gothic architecture and serene interior.

Gain a new perspective after exploring the city and ascend to the top of Main Tower. From here, you can spot the city's sights and see the River Main winding through it all.
DE.FRA.leisureActivitiesText:
For a cultural feast, head to the Museum Embankment, a boulevard lined with museums. Whether you’re an art lover or a history enthusiast, there’s something to pique your interest.

Nature enthusiasts can explore Frankfurt’s unique urban oasis within its city limits. The Frankfurt City Forest is perfect for hiking, running, and cycling. In fact, the entire city is a cyclist’s paradise. After exploring the forest, enjoy a scenic ride along the Main River for stunning views of the skyline.

For a unique experience, visit the Kultur-und Kongresszentrum Jahrhunderthalle. Known for its diverse events, you might catch a thrilling concert, an inspiring lecture, or a theatrical performance. The best part? Each visit offers something new and exciting!
DE.FRA.shoppingText:
