Shopping in Frankfurt offers a myriad of experiences, from flea markets to malls and bustling shopping streets. In winter, the festive markets are a must-visit, perfect for treating yourself to a handcrafted nutcracker or decoration.

Year-round, the Schaumainkai flea market is full of action. Sip on a traditional German apple beverage as you browse through vintage treasures and quirky antiques.

No trip to Frankfurt would be complete without exploring the Zeil, the city's true shopping gem. This boulevard is lined with both local and international brands, and street performers add even more charm to your shopping spree.
DE.FRA.destinationPageIntro: In bustling Frankfurt, cosmopolitan charm meets old-world wonders along the banks of the River Main.
DE.FRA.overviewText:
Frankfurt, often dubbed “Mainhattan” for its impressive skyline and location on the River Main, is a city where gleaming skyscrapers stand alongside picturesque classical buildings – exemplifying the blend of old and new. The city hums with vibrant energy, from bustling marketplaces to serene riverside promenades.

Stroll through the centre enjoying the delightful scent of freshly baked bread. Admire cultural landmarks, including numerous museums and Gothic cathedrals. Relax in urban gardens and embrace the warmth of the magical winter season. Frankfurt's spirit is captivating, promising an unforgettable trip that combines excitement with German charm
DE.FRA.eatingImageText:
Every bite in Frankfurt tells a story. Begin your foodie exploration on Upper Berger Straße, where German café culture thrives. On Wednesdays and Saturdays, the street buzzes with markets offering everything from hearty German specialties to creative delights like spaghetti ice cream.

For a quintessentially German experience, visit the Erzeugermarkt Konstablerwache farmers market. Try Grüne Soße, a tangy green sauce typically served with potatoes and eggs, or Handkäse mit Musik, a sour milk cheese marinated in vinegar and onions – don’t knock it until you’ve tried it! For gourmet Frankfurter sausages and other delicacies, stop by the Kleinmarkthalle market.

In the evenings, stroll down Kaiserstraße in the Station District for international cuisine and a lively atmosphere.

DE.HAM.touristAttractionsText:
At the top of any itinerary should be a visit to Speicherstadt, a UNESCO Heritage Site and a fascinating glimpse into Hamburg’s maritime past. This huge warehouse comes alive at night with a dazzling light show illuminating the red brick buildings and steel bridges.

Young visitors will love the charm of Miniatur Wunderland, a tour around the world in miniature from Patagonia to Antarctica.

Hamburg’s waterfront is iconic, and the floating dock of Landungsbrücken is a must-see. Or take a tour of the city’s imposing town hall, an ornate example of Hanseatic design.

Escape the urban delights of Hamburg in the city’s various parks and green spaces. Alsterpark sits on the northwest shore of the Außenalster lakes and is popular with visitors and locals, especially on a lazy Sunday afternoon.
DE.HAM.leisureActivitiesText:
Famous for its connection to the Beatles, the music scene in Hamburg is still as energetic, with Große Freiheit 36 at the center of entertainment.

For a more cultural experience and to hear the music of Hamburg’s beloved son Brahms, the incredible acoustics of the Elbphilharmonie are home to the Hamburg Symphony.

One of the best ways to get to know the real Hamburg is to explore its cycle paths. Safe, level, and suitable for all ages and abilities, cycle tours take you along the Alster. Or set off and discover the city’s parks and cafés. Hamburg is a truly cycle-focused city.

For photographers, Hamburg is an architectural and visual delight. Old and new sit alongside one another, and the afternoon light lets you capture the city’s ever-changing moods.
DE.HAM.shoppingText:
Alsterarkaden is a charming waterfront parade of exclusive shops and boutiques, some excellent Arabic food at Saliba, and some of the most opulent interiors in the city.

Gänsemarkt is a cluster of malls and parades around a public square, creating a relaxed shopping experience filled with stores and independent boutiques. For some trendy European fashion shopping, stop off at Gerhofstrasse.

Hamburg’s markets are a chance for some serious bargain hunting, and they don’t get much better than the Flohschanze flea market every Saturday for all things vintage, retro and chic.

While the Europa Passage may give you that quintessential mall experience, the Hamburger Hof is a far more authentic Hanseatic shopping arcade with a charming mix of independent stores and excellent eateries too.
DE.HAM.destinationPageIntro: Explore the charm and energy of Hamburg. From its historic port to its impressive architecture, fine dining and year-round festivals, Hamburg is a feast for the senses.
DE.HAM.overviewText:
Hamburg is a wonderful surprise. A sparkling harbor introduces you to the city’s maritime legacy, where cargo ships and the occasional tall ship traverse the calm waters. This is a cultural city, where music, art and theatre are celebrated in iconic constructions like the Elbphilharmonie, and historic buildings sit alongside the dazzling skyscrapers of the commercial district.

Go in search of traditional German food in the city’s restaurants or explore the UNESCO Heritage Speicherstadt district. In the evening, the city comes alive to the sound of music. Whether you love a bit of German rock or some classical opera, Hamburg is ready to entertain you. Warm, welcoming, and with an ambience that immediately makes you feel at home, travel to Hamburg to discover a true German gem.
DE.HAM.eatingImageText:
One of Hamburg’s culinary surprises is the Portuguese Quarter, where you can take a break from hearty German food and grab a mid-morning galão (espresso with steamed milk) and pastel de nata (a custard tart).

For a very special meal, book a table at the inspiring Literaturhauscafé, where you can try a German specialty, Pflaumenknödel. These sweet soft dumplings filled with plum and smothered in vanilla sauce are a fabulously indulgent treat after a day’s cycling around the city.

Franzbrötchen, a cinnamon pastry, is a Hamburg specialty and ideal for a mid-morning snack. Or grab a tasty Fischbrötchen for lunch – a crusty bread roll filled with delicious, fresh fish such as herring. You’ll find the best versions in the Hamburg Fish Market in the Altonaer Fischmarkt down by the docks.

DJ.JIB.touristAttractionsText:
While much of Djibouti may be desert, its coastline is the perfect place for exploring the underwater world. Scuba diving in the clear blue water will take you to coral reefs that teem with brightly coloured fish, turtles and marine creatures.

If you prefer to stay on top of the water, you can kayak in the calm waters of the Gulf of Tadjoura and discover your own isolated beach or snorkel in pristine waters.

Explore Lac’ Assal, the second-lowest point on earth, where huge flocks of pink flamingos congregate and steam from towering limestone chimneys hint at the volcanic activity below the surface.

Or head to Lac Abbé to see an astonishing contrast between white salt shores and vivid blue waters. This is the perfect destination for wildlife and landscape photography.
DJ.JIB.leisureActivitiesText:
Djibouti City is it’s one of Africa’s most rapidly expanding communities, and is the administrative centre for the entire country. Head to the national library where you can find out more about the history and culture of this unique enclave through a series of exhibitions.

The country’s Tropical Aquarium is well worth a visit in Djibouti City, as is the Presidential Palace, a grand building with European influences.

For some spectacular views, lace up your hiking boots and take a guided climb of the dormant Ardoukoba volcano. Or book a place on a snorkelling trip to the Bay of Ghoubbet to see the majestic splendour of the huge yet gentle whale sharks.
DJ.JIB.shoppingText:
The main shopping centre is Djibouti City, where you’ll find bustling markets such as Les Caisses Market, selling everything from fresh fruit and vegetables to handicrafts, textiles and bead jewellery.

For boutique shopping, head to Grand Marche in the city centre. Here you’ll find plenty of both local and international shops selling traditional African clothes as well as spices, electrical goods, souvenirs and crafts.

The city also has a good selection of upscale malls selling high-quality international brands and well-known labels. But for that authentic shopping experience, the hectic and exciting markets are hard to beat. Just be sure to practice your haggling skills first.
DJ.JIB.destinationPageIntro: Djibouti is a charmingly authentic slice of East African life, surrounded by natural beauty and an untouched landscape. An enchanting destination for true adventurers.
DJ.JIB.overviewText:
Djibouti may be tiny in comparison to its neighbours, but what it lacks in size it more than makes up with personality, a warm welcome, and spectacular natural beauty. Bordered by Ethiopia, Somalia and Eritrea, it’s one of Africa’s least-known destinations and as such is a true unexplored and unspoilt gem.

From turquoise-blue ocean waters that caress deserted sandy beaches to the raw and wild beauty of the volcanic plateau and the towering mountain ranges to the north, Djibouti has more than its fair share of natural wonders.

The small but busy capital is home to authentic market shopping experiences and a unique cuisine that’s an inspiring combination of African, Middle Eastern and European influences. Take the path less travelled and discover Djibouti with Qatar Airways.
DJ.JIB.eatingImageText:
Djibouti food is a delightful mix of influences from neighbouring countries such as Yemen, Ethiopia and Somalia, as well as Arabic and French cuisines. Spices such as cinnamon, cardamom and saffron play a key role in adding depth and flavour to dishes, and the most common meats used in traditional Djibouti cooking are beef, goat or lamb, as well as fish closer to the coast.

Try marake kaloune, a spicy fish stew made with tilapia or sea bass, rice, onions, okra, eggplants and tomatoes.

Fah-fah is a traditional dish in the south of the country, made with goat meat, vegetables and a dash of green chillies to give it a kick.

And if you have a sweet tooth, xalwo (also known as halwa) is a chewy sweet made with brown sugar, cardamom, cloves and saffron.

TZ.JRO.touristAttractionsText:
While summitting Kilimanjaro is a bucket-list achievement, the mountain offers far more than its peak. In a town named Moshi, the view of Kilimanjaro’s snow-capped summit is arguably the best from the ground. 

Beyond the mountain, immerse yourself in the green landscapes surrounding Materuni Waterfall – just a short hike through native banana plantations. A dip in the Kikuletwa Hot Springs is a relaxing contrast to the ruggedness of the forestry, with the warm waters inviting you to unwind. If you’re a coffee lover, a visit to a plantation is a must – you can savour the process from bean to cup.

For a taste of local life, explore Olpopongi Maasai Cultural Village, where the traditions of the Maasai come to fruition through stories, dance and crafts.
TZ.JRO.leisureActivitiesText:
Climbing Kilimanjaro will likely be the highlight of your trip but the city is an adventurer’s playground brimming with all kinds of activities. Bike through the Rau Forest Reserve, with trails that wind through towering trees and undergrowth. If taking to the water is more your pace, canoe on the serene Momela Lake. Views of the mountain can be seen from the lake and you can take it as fast or as slow as you like.

If you are a thrill seeker, soar to the skies on a paraglider. There are not many incredible destinations that match the endless vistas and majesty of Kilimanjaro. If you’d rather marvel at the natural fliers, bird watching is another popular activity to take up. Sunbirds and raptors can be spotted on the treetops, giving you a glimpse of the mountain’s biodiversity.
TZ.JRO.shoppingText:
The Central Market is a prime destination to find a souvenir from your enchanting holiday in Tanzania. Colourful stalls overflow with fresh produce, fragrant spices, beautiful textiles and much more.

For those preparing to take on the summit, there are trekking stores dotted throughout Moshi that’ll have you covered for all seasons. They’re stocked with everything from sturdy hiking boots to thermal layers, ensuring you’re ready for whatever the mountain throws your way. 

Beyond practicality, there are street markets filled with trinkets such as Maasai beads, handcrafted by Maasai artisans – making them a meaningful souvenir from your travels.
TZ.JRO.destinationPageIntro: With the highest mountain in Africa, Tanzania's breathtaking Kilimanjaro is likely on any adventurer’s bucket-list. But, there’s so much more to see than climbing to the summit.
TZ.JRO.overviewText:
Journey to Kilimanjaro, the heart of Tanzania, where adventure soars. The allure of the Kilimanjaro climb is undeniable, as the magnificent giant is visible from almost everywhere in the city. However, to think of Kilimanjaro solely as a place to conquer would be to miss the richness that lies at its base.

Kilimanjaro is a land of bustling markets, coffee plantations, friendly communities and stunning natural wonders. Every corner of the city reveals a new facet of culture and nature intertwined. Whether you are summiting the mountain, wandering through the lush forestland, savouring local flavours or retreating to a hot spring, each path leads to a wondrous discovery.
TZ.JRO.eatingImageText:
Naturally, you must indulge in the variety of bananas native to the region throughout your stay in Kilimanjaro, whether it’s straight off the tree, roasted, fried or simmered in a stew. 

Tanzania’s national dish, nyama choma, is another must-try. This is simply grilled meat, often paired with a side of ugali, a hearty maize-based staple with a texture similar to a stiff polenta. It provides the ideal sustenance required for your Kilimanjaro adventures.

The culinary scene isn’t just limited to local flavours, Moshi boasts an array of international cuisine too. Indian food is particularly popular, as there is a large Indian community in the area. While you are in Moshi, be sure to stop at one of the charming coffee houses. Taste the coffee of the region and enjoy a cosy dining space at the bottom of the mountain.

KH.KTI.overviewTabHeading: Book your visit to Phnom Penh
KH.KTI.touristAttractionsText:
To learn more about the country, visit the National Museum of Cambodia to gain a deeper understanding of its history, culture and people. The Royal Palace is also a key stop on your Cambodia itinerary, with two pagodas to see – the Silver Pagoda and the Temple of the Emerald Buddha.

Take a sunset cruise at the Tonlé Sap for a different perspective of the city. Then stop at one of Cambodia’s night markets for a unique shopping experience. One of the best is located at the northern end of the docks at Sisowath Quay.

For an interesting mix of Asian and European culture, a visit to the French Quarter is a chance to see grand buildings alongside the white chedi of Wat Phnom. To enjoy an Art Deco-inspired shopping experience, stroll around Phsar Thmei market, close to the modern Sorya Shopping Centre.
KH.KTI.leisureActivitiesText:
A Mekong cruise takes you along the river and lets you watch the sun set on the horizon behind the Royal Palace. If you prefer, it’s also possible to hire your own boat with a local captain so you can explore a little further.

For something unique, cooking schools offer lessons where you can learn about local ingredients and create your own Cambodian dishes. 

To find out more about the wildlife of Cambodia, take an interactive tour at Phnom Tamao Wildlife Rescue Centre, where elephants and some of Cambodia’s last surviving tigers are rehabilitated. Interactions are closely monitored to ensure the animal’s welfare is never compromised.

Phnom Penh’s art scene is thriving, and Meta House offers exhibitions, events, and lectures about the history of art and culture in Cambodia. It’s your chance to see the country’s up-and-coming artists’ work.
KH.KTI.shoppingText:
As a shopping destination, Phnom Penh offers a huge selection of malls and markets. Central Market is a Cambodian landmark with its striking golden dome which houses jewellery stores, electronics, paintings and crafts. 

A quirky place to shop is the Russian Market, where you can explore and buy local batik scarves and handicrafts, jewellery and clothes. 

If you prefer shopping in an air-conditioned atmosphere, there are three Aeon Malls – family-friendly destinations with children’s entertainment and food halls selling a wide selection of cuisine.

For something unique, tucked away behind the Royal Palace is Street 240 – a destination lined with artisan stores. When the sun goes down, Phnom Penh’s night markets are a wonderfully relaxed shopping experience. Enjoy the night breeze as you browse.
KH.KTI.touristAttractionsTabHeading: Things to do in Phnom Penh
KH.KTI.destinationPageIntro: Phnom Penh is a stunning destination rich in culture and history. Fly there via the new Techo International Airport from 9 September 2025.
KH.KTI.overviewText:
Starting 9 September 2025, fly to Techo International Airport – the new airport servicing Phnom Penh.

A wonderful destination that welcomes everyone, Phnom Penh mixes ancient Cambodian culture with a dynamic youthfulness. Experience the vibrant energy of its people and the scent of spices in the air.

Street food vendors sell hot and spicy snacks, while new shopping malls offer an air-conditioned escape from the tropical heat. Temples provide restful spaces where you can embrace peace and serenity amid a bustling city.

With its thriving art scene and spectacular architecture, you can immerse yourself in the energy of the capital, making this a great city break destination with a difference. From palaces to parks, stalls to statues, Phnom Penh is a trip of a lifetime.
KH.KTI.destinationHighlightsH1: Phnom Penh: An exotic Cambodian escape
KH.KTI.eatingImageText:
Phnom Penh’s cuisine is an exciting combination of traditional dishes and influences from around the world, including French, Portuguese, Thai, Vietnamese and Chinese. To try some of the more exotic flavours, a stroll along the Riverfront introduces you to Cambodian street food as well as fine dining experiences. Noodles such as num banh chok are particularly popular, as are fruit and vegetarian dishes. Fish is also a fantastic option. Try amok trey, a spicy steamed fish curry.

If you really want to challenge your palate, you’ll find vendors along the Riverfront and Sisowath Quay selling fried insects, which are a common part of Cambodian street food.

For a relaxed dining experience, Boeng Keng Kang has plenty of cafés and restaurants to explore.

SO.MGQ.touristAttractionsText:
Mogadishu is a great beach destination, with powder-soft sand and clear blue water. Jazeera Beach is a white sand beach that’s tranquil and uncrowded. Take a boat ride out to the island or just spend the day lazing on the sand. Lido Beach, (nicknamed Mogadishu Miami Beach) is another popular family-friendly beach with safe swimming and plenty of restaurants.

Embrace the complex culture of Somalia with a visit to the National Theatre, or explore the ancient ruins of Garesa Palace, a once-grand symbol of the city’s strategic position as a trading post.

Mogadishu’s mosques are peaceful places for contemplation away from the buzz of the city. The Arba’a Rukun mosque sits in the heart of the city’s medieval district, or spend a couple of hours at the modern Mosque of Islamic Solidarity.
SO.MGQ.leisureActivitiesText:
Mogadishu’s beaches offer plenty of water sports to enjoy including swimming, snorkelling, and diving. Hire a boat and go deep-sea fishing off the coast, or join a guided dive to explore some of the Indian Ocean’s aquatic treasures.

You can delve deeper into the country’s history with a guided tour of the National Museum of Somalia, or a walking tour of some of the city’s ancient attractions, including the 10th century Fakhr al-Din Mosque and the striking ruins of Mogadishu Cathedral. One of the city’s main attractions is the 15th century Almnara Tower.

Take a tour of the Karaan District, one of the city’s oldest neighbourhoods and full of interesting buildings, mosques and busy street markets.
SO.MGQ.shoppingText:
Mogadishu’s markets are lively, busy and very noisy! The largest in Somalia is the city’s Bakaara Market, where you’ll find stalls selling local crafts, fresh food and textiles. The Fish Market is famous for its freshly caught seafood and authentic atmosphere.

The city’s malls offer air-conditioned relief from the midday heat as well as an excellent modern shopping experience. Bin Arif is packed with busy shops including the country’s first Korean retail outlet, while LC Waikiki mall is another popular mall with locals. For the best mall shopping experience, Banaadir Mall offers plenty of shops, a food court and easy parking.

If you want to go street shopping, it’s wise to book a guide who can lead you through the labyrinthine side streets and squares to avoid getting lost!
SO.MGQ.destinationPageIntro: As a city break destination, Mogadishu is one of the most exciting North African destinations. Millennia of history is on display within a modern, thriving metropolis.
SO.MGQ.overviewText:
Somalia’s capital city sits on the Indian Ocean and is an incredible legacy of four thousand years of history. Towering citadels and ancient city walls take you on a journey through centuries of different influences, cultural diversity and trade.

Its location on the coast makes Mogadishu a major port, with busy markets and stores selling their wares. Archaeological digs are constantly turning up new information about the city’s past, while local artists and craftspeople are keeping artisan traditions alive.

As the city enters its next stage, the 21st century is starting to make its mark with new shopping malls and trendy restaurants. But a stroll through the Old City immediately transports you back in time, allowing you to immerse yourself in the history and character of North Africa.
SO.MGQ.eatingImageText:
Somali food is delicious, with rich stews, rice dishes and one of the most famous of Somalia’s street foods, sambusas, which are similar to samosas and are crispy fried pastries filled with meat or vegetables.

Bariis iskukaris is a rice dish full of spices, or try suqaar, a tasty and filling meat stew. A refreshing glass of shaah cadays goes down well on a hot afternoon; it’s a fragrant and delicately spiced tea drunk by locals and visitors alike.

Mogadishu’s proximity to the sea means that seafood is a popular addition to restaurant menus. You’ll find the best close to Lido Beach. International food includes Indian and Turkish cuisine, or grab some hot sambusas from the street vendors in the markets.

NG.PHC.overviewTabHeading: Book your visit to Port Harcourt
NG.PHC.touristAttractionsText:
If you’re here with the family and fancy a day away from the beach, Port Harcourt Pleasure Park has an amusement park that younger travellers will love. Isaac Boro Park is focused more on eco-friendly tourism, with scenic trails to explore that are suitable for all ages and abilities.

If you want to see a selection of exotic animals without travelling into the bush on safari, Port Harcourt Zoo focuses on conservation and education in a fun and family-friendly environment.

If you can’t resist the call of the fairway, Port Harcourt Golf Club is open to non-members and has some challenging holes. And after all that excitement, a stroll down to the beach gives you incredible views of the sunset and the chance to find a local restaurant selling fresh fish and spicy Nigerian culinary specialities.
NG.PHC.leisureActivitiesText:
If you’re in Port Harcourt just before Christmas, you’ll get the chance to join in with the festivities of the Carniriv Festival. This week-long celebration embraces the cultural diversity and heritage of Nigeria with parades, music and dance.

If you’ve never experienced the sheer exuberance of an African football match, book some tickets for a match at the Adokiye Amiesimaka Stadium along with 38,000 other supporters. The Stadium also hosts music concerts and events.

Immerse yourself in the art of Nigeria at the Delaroke Art Gallery, which showcases the work of up-and-coming young creatives as well as internationally renowned artists.

Treat yourself to a little pampering at one of the city’s luxurious spas, or take a guided cultural tour of the city’s trendiest locations.
NG.PHC.shoppingText:
The most popular souvenirs to buy in Port Harcourt include brightly-coloured fabrics and textiles, bead jewellery and hand-tooled leather boxes. Take a stroll down Mile One or Mile Three market. Slightly chaotic, noisy and great fun, this is the place to grab a bargain. Be prepared to haggle.

If you prefer the comfort of air-conditioned retail, Port Harcourt Mall is the place to go with a large food court, entertainment and outlets selling electrical goods, fashion and accessories.

In the downtown area you’ll also come across several large art galleries selling work by local artists.

Explore the side streets off Market Three and you’ll find local sellers offering all sorts of trinkets. For fresh produce, the city’s malls have plenty of fruit and delicious local treats on offer.
NG.PHC.touristAttractionsTabHeading: Things to do in Port Harcourt
NG.PHC.destinationPageIntro: Vibrant and energetic, Port Harcourt is perfect for sunkissed beach holidays. Delicious food and excellent shopping also make this an attractive city break destination.
NG.PHC.overviewText:
Prosperous, welcoming, and lively, Port Harcourt is one of Nigeria’s best-kept secrets. This city may have been built on the wealth of its rich oil fields, but it still retains that authenticity and friendly atmosphere that makes it such a great city break destination. Its stunning sandy beaches also make it one of Nigeria’s best beach destinations.

Bustling markets sit beside modern malls, and fine dining competes with street food vendors for the attention of gastronomes. Tranquil parks let you take a break from the hustle and bustle of the city, while Port Harcourt’s location in the southeast region of Nigeria makes it a starting point for exploring the coast.

Add in that it’s a budget-friendly city and you have one of the most interesting and affordable travel destinations in Africa.
NG.PHC.eatingImageText:
Southern Nigerian food is filled with soups, stews, and fish dishes, all carefully prepared with a unique range of herbs and spices. One of the most popular is Boli and fish. Boli is roasted plantain served with smoked or roasted fish with a tangy pepper sauce.

For a quick snack on the go, suya is the Nigerian version of kebabs, with grilled chicken or beef skewers marinated in spices and grilled over an open fire.

Soups play a big part in Nigerian cuisine, such as Banga soup made from palm fruit or afang soup, made from afang leaves and meat such as beef or mutton. If you prefer something lighter, try jollof rice cooked with tomatoes and spices.

In the downtown area of the city you’ll find international cuisine from around the world with a particular emphasis on Chinese and Asian food.

CN.PKX.touristAttractionsText:
A trip to China wouldn’t be complete without seeing the Great Wall, where the views are mesmerising. Marvel at the Mutianyu section, just a two-hour drive from the city. Its stone traces the curves of rugged hills, making every step feel monumental.

Then retreat to the Summer Palace, otherwise known as Yiheyuan, a sprawling oasis of calm lakes, marble bridges, and the iconic Longevity Hill. Once reserved for royalty, this scenic garden is now open to the public and features ornate, timeless pavilions. 

You can also meander through the parklands at Tian Tan, the Temple of Heaven, one of Beijing’s most revered landmarks. Another spectacle is Yonghe Temple, where Tibetan Buddhist art, red-lacquered halls, and the scent of incense evokes a sense of peace.
CN.PKX.leisureActivitiesText:
Chaoyang Park is a lush sanctuary that’s even larger than New York’s Central Park. Watch locals practicing tai chi in the morning, or paddle through the serene lake. Discover the outdoors even further at Houhai Lake, where you can take a boat ride or ice skate.

After heading out onto the waters, wander through the famous hutongs. These narrow alleyways were once abundant across the city and now preserve an authentic slice of Beijing. Walk the winding lanes filled with courtyard homes and quirky shops, or look for a cosy eatery – especially near Gulou.

Once you’ve indulged in a delicious meal, you’ll be ready to step into the Forbidden City. This golden-roofed labyrinth of palaces and halls once hosted emperors. It forms a stark contrast with Tiananmen Square, a symbol of modern China.
CN.PKX.shoppingText:
Journey through the Panjiayuan Antique Market, where age-old traditions meet present-day luxury. This open-air treasure trove has over 4,000 stalls overflowing with Chinese antiques, vintage calligraphy, jade jewellery and carved wooden ornaments. If you’re looking for pearls, electronics or souvenirs, make your way to Hongqiao Pearl Market. 

In the historic hutongs, Nanluoguxiang shopping street combines classical appeal with a contemporary vibe. Boutiques are stocked with everything from silk scarves to Chinese-inspired home décor. To uncover the latest collections by high-end and global brands, browse the stores in Taikoo Li. This sophisticated complex is ideal for window shopping too, with elegant architecture and chic cafés.
CN.PKX.destinationPageIntro: Beijing, the lively capital of China, is teeming with things to do from dining on delectable Chinese delicacies, to walking the Great Wall and marveling at stunning temples.
CN.PKX.overviewText:
The capital of China is full of surprises thanks to the contrast between ancient secrets and ultra-modern charm. Wander through buzzing alleys where the aroma of sizzling dumplings mingles with bursts of laughter and chatter from hidden tea houses, or roam around tranquil gardens where locals do morning tai chi. 

Beijing brims with wonders that span centuries. Delve right in and explore sleek high-rises, fascinating temples, and neon lights that glow over traditional rooftops. Find yourself haggling in bustling markets one minute, and admiring a sunset over a beautiful lake the next. With its larger-than-life personality, Beijing is the perfect stop for a thrilling adventure.
CN.PKX.destinationHighlightsH1: Beijing: An ancient yet modern city
CN.PKX.eatingImageText:
To get a taste of Beijing, try the city's favourite street breakfast, jianbing, a savoury pancake filled with eggs, spring onions and crunchy wonton. Spot vendors selling this delicacy on Wangfujing Snack Street, where you can also sample bing tanghulu – candied tofu drizzled in sauces. Dumpling lovers can rejoice too, as jiaozi (dough wrapped around a succulent filling) is found on every corner.

For a sit-down dining experience, head to the vibrant 798 Art District, featuring edgy restaurants blending Eastern and Western cuisine. Visit one of them and dive into Beijing's popular hot pot of meat and vegetables cooking in an aromatic broth. Savour even more flavours by tucking into crispy, golden Peking duck. This sumptuous dish is served with pancakes, hoisin sauce and green onions.

SA.RSI.overviewTabHeading: Book your visit to The Red Sea
SA.RSI.touristAttractionsText:
Saudi Arabia’s Red Sea region offers a rare blend of cultural heritage and untouched natural beauty. Peaceful and still largely undiscovered, this region is emerging as a luxury destination, with deserted beaches and pristine oases to explore. Umm Sahar Island is a wonderful escape near Umluj, offering powder-soft sand and crystal-clear waters perfect for diving and snorkelling.

Discover the region’s rich biodiversity at The Red Sea Marine Life Institute, or journey north along the coast to King Abdulaziz’s Castle in Duba – a striking fortress overlooking the sea and a testament to the area’s strategic legacy. The surrounding coastline is dotted with immaculate beaches and world-class dive sites, where vibrant coral reefs and serene waters await.
SA.RSI.leisureActivitiesText:
Along Saudi Arabia’s Red Sea coast is where ancient traditions meet thrilling adventure. Dive into the region’s extraordinary marine world, with one of the longest barrier reef systems on the planet. The vibrant coral reefs and crystal-clear waters offer unforgettable underwater adventures – get ready to snap some photos!

Back on land, hike or bike across dramatic volcanic plains and rugged mountain foothills. Guided trails suit all levels, and e-bikes offer a relaxed way to explore this untamed terrain and enjoy the panoramic views. For a truly memorable moment, hike into the mountains and watch the sun set. 

For an authentic experience, take a guided tour to explore the art of falconry and learn about the deep cultural significance of these majestic birds.
SA.RSI.shoppingText:
Whether you’re after high-end fashion or something uniquely handcrafted, shopping along Saudi Arabia’s Red Sea coast offers a captivating blend of heritage and modern luxury. It’s a perfect way to discover the richness of the region – explored one boutique, market or souq at a time.

You can begin your retail experience even before your journey begins – right at The Red Sea International Airport. Here, you’ll find a curated selection of upscale boutiques and designer shops to peruse. 

For a more traditional experience, head to Umluj, where relaxed malls and a laid-back atmosphere invite you to browse for souvenirs and locally made goods at your own pace. Further north, Al Wajh offers a classic souq experience, with bustling markets filled with aromatic spices, handmade textiles and artisanal crafts. Specialty shops showcase regional pottery and traditional wares, offering a deeper connection to the local culture.

From luxury labels to authentic keepsakes, The Red Sea coast delivers a shopping experience as diverse and vibrant as the region itself.
SA.RSI.touristAttractionsTabHeading: Things to do in The Red Sea
SA.RSI.destinationPageIntro: The Red Sea is famed for its world-class diving, pristine beaches and luxurious resorts. Plus, a rich culture and history for those willing to venture off the beaten path.
SA.RSI.overviewText:
Tucked away on Saudi Arabia’s pristine western coastline, The Red Sea is a breathtaking destination where nature takes center stage. Picture vibrant coral reefs teeming with marine life, soft sandy beaches that feel like your own private sanctuary and dramatic landscapes where golden desert meets the shimmering sea.

The Red Sea is a visionary development introducing luxurious resorts, conservation-led diving and unforgettable cultural experiences. Whether you’re snorkelling colourful reefs, kayaking through turquoise waters, or unwinding in the sunset, The Red Sea offers a serene escape in the heart of the Middle East.

Fly to The Red Sea with Qatar Airways and be one of the first to discover this remarkable new destination.
SA.RSI.socialProofQuote: Book flights to The Red Sea (RSI)
SA.RSI.destinationHighlightsH1: The Red Sea: Nature, culture, adventure
SA.RSI.eatingImageText:
Saudi Arabia’s Red Sea coast is a haven for seafood lovers, where the day’s catch is transformed into dishes that celebrate both tradition and flavour. Local specialties include grilled najel (coral grouper), delicately seasoned with garlic and lemon, and sayadieh – a fragrant medley of rice, snapper or sea bass, caramelised onions and toasted pine nuts. 

Another local favourite is kabsa – this national dish blends aromatic rice with lamb, chicken or seafood to make for a warm and hearty meal. Make sure to also try saleeg – a creamy rice dish served with slow-roasted meat, that’s beloved for its comforting richness.

For those craving global flavours, Jeddah’s vibrant dining scene offers an eclectic mix – from Japanese sushi and Levantine street food to international fusion and upscale fine dining, all just a few steps from the sea.

AE.SHJ.touristAttractionsText:
Take a trip to the Mleiha Archaeological Centre, located in the deserts of Sharjah, where you can learn about ancient Bedouin culture in the region. For those seeking a thrill, there are plenty of recreational activities for you to take part in. You may even spot an oryx on your adventure.

Visit the Sharjah Art Museum, where modern artworks and old-age masterpieces are housed.

For a slice of serenity, stroll along the Buhaira Corniche, revealing panoramic views of the city-side lagoon. While there, visit Al Noor Island, which has the dreamlike Butterfly House in its centre.

Sharjah is a prime location for a beach getaway and it’s certainly not short of beautiful shores – one of the best being Khorfakkan Beach. It boasts crystal clear waters and excellent conditions for swimming, snorkelling and even fishing.
AE.SHJ.leisureActivitiesText:
Trek or kayak through the Khor Kalba Mangroves, abundant with rare bird species, crabs and sea turtles. For more wildlife encounters, visit Arabia’s Wildlife Centre in Sharjah Desert Park. The diverse fauna of the Arabian Peninsula are on full display in their natural habitats.

For a unique experience that epitomises the ingenuity of the United Arab Emirates, step into the Rain Room. You can walk through a downpour without getting wet – it’s an artistic, sensory journey.

Travel a few hours North to set sail on a Musandam Dibba boat tour in a traditional-style dhow, where the dramatic fjords of the Arabian Peninsula meet turquoise waters. As you sail along, watch dolphins dance beside your boat and take a plunge in the refreshing waters.
AE.SHJ.shoppingText:
The Central Souk, otherwise known as the Blue Souk – because of its blue tile-trimmed exterior – houses an array of treasures. Sift through stalls of handcrafted jewellery, intricate carpets and authentic Arab garments for a taste of old Arabia.

For a deeper sense of history, Souk Al Arsah is one of the oldest marketplaces the United Arab Emirates. With its ancient walls and wooden doors, this souk exudes timeless charm. Look for antiques, pearls and homemade souvenirs.

Sharjah’s modern side shines through its malls, with many to choose from. You can shop for global brands, local designers and everything in between.
AE.SHJ.destinationPageIntro: Sharjah is the historic soul of the United Arab Emirates. Relax in the coastal region, experience old Arabia in the city or venture further out to the golden desert.
AE.SHJ.overviewText:
Sharjah has earned the title of UNESCO Cultural Capital of the Arab Region. It’s a place where every effort has been made to preserve Emirati history. Wander through the colourful souks, marvel at the old architecture and explore the archeological sites. Sharjah is also home to sleek waterfronts, contemporary galleries and cultural spaces.

Whether you tour the coffee shops of Sharjah tasting local delicacies, manoeuvre through untamed deserts, or simply unwind by the sea – there’s so much to enjoy in this unique city in the United Arab Emirates.
AE.SHJ.eatingImageText:
Coffee is a rite of passage in most of the United Arab Emirates, and Sharjah is no different. Relax in one of the many coffee shops throughout the city where you can savour a cup of strong Arabic coffee, spiced with cardamom and paired with sweet, succulent dates.

Craving something more substantial? Sink your teeth into a shawarma, Sharjah’s beloved street food. Tender, spiced meat is slow-cooked on a rotisserie and wrapped in soft bread with a healthy dollop of garlic sauce, pickles and crisp vegetables.

For something more refined, dine at one of the many Middle Eastern restaurants. From creamy hummus to grilled lamb and aromatic rice, every bite is packed with flavour. Don’t miss out on a visit to Souk Al Jubail, a bustling market brimming with fresh produce, seafood and spices.

RU.SVO.touristAttractionsText:
The iconic Kremlin is the heart of Moscow and holds much history – back to a time when emperors ruled and legends were born. Just outside of Kremlin, the Red Square awaits – a UNESCO World Heritage site home to many impressive landmarks. Stand before Lenin’s Mausoleum, where the revolutionary leader was laid to rest.

Take a moment to soak up the energy of the square before gazing up at the awe-inspiring domes of Saint Basil’s Cathedral. Its candy-coloured towers are a masterpiece of Russian architecture.

For panoramic views, head to Sparrow Hills, a hill on the Moskva River where the city unfolds beneath you. Then, visit the Ostankino TV Tower. It’s one of the tallest structures in Europe and features a glass floor – if you dare walk on it.
RU.SVO.leisureActivitiesText:
The Pushkin Museum hosts centuries of art from all over the globe, from ancient treasures to modern marvels. For even more history, step into the State Historical Museum. It is one of the largest museums in the world and its vast halls tell Russia’s story in vivid detail, from royal crowns to Soviet-era relics.

For a glimpse of local art, the State Tretyakov Gallery is a must. Here, Russian artists showcase their paintings and sculptures.

Catch a ballet or an opera at the legendary Bolshoi Theatre – where world-class performances are staged in one of the most beautiful theatres on earth. 

For some fun with the little ones, visit one of the largest indoor amusement parks in Europe.
RU.SVO.shoppingText:
The pedestrian street, Arbat Street, is where history and art meet modern chic. Stroll down the lively boulevard where souvenir shops mingle with galleries and cafés. It’s an idyllic spot to browse local crafts and sip on a coffee in Moscow’s artistic hub.

For an upscale retail experience, go to Tverskaya Street, Moscow’s answer to Fifth Avenue. Lined with high-end boutiques, flagship stores, and luxury brands – it’s where the fashion-forward Muscovites shop.

For something truly unique, head to Izmailovo Market. This sprawling flea market is abundant with antiques, hand-painted Russian matryoshka dolls, intricate crafts, and timeless art. You can spend hours exploring its labyrinth of stalls.
RU.SVO.destinationPageIntro: Moscow, the majestic capital of Russia, is abundant with landmarks and sights to see. From the impressive colours of Saint Basil’s Cathedral to the iconic Kremlin.
RU.SVO.overviewText:
Moscow, Europe’s biggest city, is a bustling metropolis that offers fascinating Russian architecture, impressive history and a rich cultural tapestry. The city’s wide, pedestrian-friendly boulevards lead the way to bustling markets serving up local delicacies, iconic architectural landmarks, amazing museums, great shopping and so much more.  

The skyline is full of contrasts, from the colourful domes of the cathedrals to the contemporary towers that are among the tallest in the world. As the seasons change in Moscow, as does the atmosphere. In winter, it’s a glittering wonderland of snow and ice, while in summer the parks and riversides are dotted with picnics and locals enjoying the sun.

Book a trip to Moscow and get lost in the many layers of Russia’s capital.
RU.SVO.eatingImageText:
Russian food is steeped in tradition and bold flavours. Try a steaming bowl of borscht, a popular and comforting Russian soup made with beetroot, cabbage, and a swirl of sour cream. It’s rich and hearty – ideal for Moscow’s chilly days.

Dig into Olivier salad, a festive favourite that involves potatoes, peas, carrots, and pickles tossed with mayonnaise. But for a real taste of Moscow’s culinary soul, try pelmeni – delicate dumplings filled with meat or vegetables – a staple across Russia.

If you‘d like to sample some of these classics or explore more of Moscow’s contemporary food scene, make your way to Usachevsky Market. Dating back to 1932, what was once a humble street market is now a bustling indoor space brimming with stalls of local and international delicacies.

CN.TFU.touristAttractionsText:
Chengdu is the home of the Giant Panda, so a visit to see these adorable creatures is a must. There are nearly 200 Giant Pandas at the Chengdu Panda Base, where incredible conservation efforts are bringing these gentle and distinctive bears back from the brink of extinction.

Immerse yourself in Chengdu Old Town with a walk down Jinli Ancient Street. It’s located next to the Wuhou temple and is a busy street lined with restaurants, stalls and street vendors.

Learn about the recent history of Chengdu at the Anren Ancient Town, a 60-minute bus ride from the city centre and home to the Jianchuan Museum. Or embrace the tranquillity of the Wuhou Temple and learn about the famous Three Kingdom period of Chinese history.

A trip to the Zhaojue Monastery introduces you to the concepts of Buddhism.
CN.TFU.leisureActivitiesText:
Take in a Sichuan opera performance, a unique type of Chinese opera dating back hundreds of years that includes unusual elements such as comedy, magic tricks and dancing, as well as fire-breathing.

Spend the day in the People’s Park, a wonderfully lush open space and a great opportunity to meet the local people and try an authentic tea house. 

If you’re fascinated by fashion, a visit to the Shu Brocade and Embroidery Museum is a stunning glimpse into the intricacies of Chinese textiles and silks dating back to the early emperors and their royal courts.

If you feel a little more energetic, Chengdu has miles of cycle paths to explore. Hire a bike and take the family on a ride through the parks and squares of the city and its suburbs.
CN.TFU.shoppingText:
One of the top places to shop in Chengdu is the Chunxi Road area, where you’ll find hundreds of independent stores, boutiques, modern malls and street markets. If you want to go antique hunting then the Song Xian Qiao Antique market is the place to go, where you might even find the odd Tibetan artefact or two, as well as ceramics and jewellery.

If you prefer a more modern shopping experience in air-conditioned comfort, the Galleria International Shopping Mall is home to around 200 stores including high-end brands.

For trendy clothes shops, Imperial Examination Lane beside the Chunxi Road shopping centre is the place to go.

And for art and handmade crafts, Song Xian Qiao Art City’s Antique Art Market is one of the largest art markets in Southwest China and packed with beautiful items and paintings.
CN.TFU.destinationPageIntro: Meet China’s most famous wildlife, Giant Pandas, hunt for bargains in busy markets, and explore the diverse culture and history in Chengdu, Sichuan’s glittering capital.
CN.TFU.overviewText:
Lush, affluent and laid-back, Chengdu is Sichuan’s capital and one of the most popular tourist destinations in China. Renowned as the home of the Giant Panda and famed for its beauty and robust economy, the city has been an important cultural and trade centre for over 4,000 years, and today is a wonderful shopping destination for high-quality goods and handicrafts.

The city has a distinctive character that feels much more relaxed. The diversity of the city’s culture embraces Buddhism and Taoism, making Chengdu a fascinating and multi-layered city break destination to explore. With spicy, flavoursome Sichuan cuisine and natural beauty all around, a trip to Chengdu with Qatar Airways is a chance to create memories that will last a lifetime.
CN.TFU.eatingImageText:
Sichuan cuisine is uniquely spicy and delicious. Before you try an authentic meal, start your culinary journey with a visit to the Sichuan Cuisine Museum. It’s a great place to understand the culture of Sichuan food and how it differs from Cantonese cuisine.

Chilli features heavily in Sichuan cooking, so expect the food to be fiery! Dishes such as spiced steamed beef or Sichuan dumplings come with a feisty chilli dressing. There are also more familiar dishes on offer such as Kung Pow chicken and Mapo Tofu. But look out for regional specialities like Cold Chicken in Chili Oil, and wood-fire chicken cooked with ginger and Sichuan pepper, then stewed in fermented bean paste, with extra chillis!

The best place to try some street food is in the Old City, especially along Jinli Ancient Street.

FR.TLS.touristAttractionsText: Visit La Capitole, known as the city hall of Toulouse. Its grand facade and square brims with life, making it the perfect spot to sit and watch the street performers while sipping on a coffee. Then take a walk along Quai de la Daurade, where the Garonne River shimmers and the city sparkles at sunset. In summer, your evenings are best spent aboard a guinguette, a lively open-air bistro often perched on a péniche – otherwise known as a houseboat.
FR.TLS.leisureActivitiesText:
Meander through Cité de l’Espace, where you can explore interactive exhibits and experience galaxies far away. Curious minds will love the Muséum de Toulouse, where natural history springs to life with fossils, flora and fauna. Wrap up your museum visits at the Fondation Bemburg, housed in a stunning Renaissance mansion. Here, you can marvel at masterpieces from Monet and Bonnard.

To enjoy a more serene ambience, head to the Jardin Japonais, a haven of koi ponds, stone bridges and zen-like calm in the heart of the city. Roam around the park with a leisurely bike ride along the Canal du Midi – a path shaded by trees where you can admire the charming houseboats. For a touch of elegance, attend the opera or ballet at the Théâtre du Capitole, and indulge in an evening of enchantment.
FR.TLS.shoppingText:
Elevate your wardrobe with some retail therapy in Toulouse. Streetwear is popular and best found in Rue Peyras and Rue Temponières. Go to Rue des Arts, Rue Boulbonne and Rue Croix-Baragnon for boutiques brimming with sophisticated couture pieces. If vintage is more your vibe, Rue Cujas is a hub of retro finds, offering everything from bohemian accessories to pre-loved designer gems.

Consider yourself a sports fan? Browse rugby jerseys and keepsakes that show pride in Toulouse’s beloved team. Before you leave, shop violet and pastel-themed products that celebrate the city’s emblematic flower, the Toulouse violet.
FR.TLS.destinationPageIntro: Toulouse is a city where ancient meets modern, delicious food tempts you at every corner, and architectural wonders are waiting to be discovered.
FR.TLS.overviewText:
Nestled along the banks of the Garonne River, Toulouse is a tapestry of history, culture and innovation. It was nicknamed the ‘Pink City’ of France, with buildings in hues of rose and coral, and terracotta bricks not found anywhere else.

A stroll through Toulouse feels like stepping into a live painting, displaying a seamless blend of the past and future. Ancient basilicas stand proud alongside aerospace marvels, earning the city its dual reputation as a cultural gem and the European capital of space exploration.

It’s charm doesn’t stop with the architecture though, as Toulouse is home to many culinary delights, and bustling markets filled with local flavours. This French city celebrates art and gastronomy – the ultimate ‘joie de vivre’.
FR.TLS.eatingImageText:
In Toulouse, every bite tells a story steeped in tradition and flavour. For cheese lovers, the city’s fromageries are irresistible. Wander into artisan shops to discover wheels of creamy brie, tangy Roquefort and nutty tomme. You could even bring some home as an edible souvenir.

If you’re planning to whip up a decadent meal, head to Marché des Carmes and scout a treasure trove of fresh produce, aromatic herbs and regional products. Pick up a few ingredients at Marché Victor Hugo too, where you’ll be tempted by busy stalls with charcuterie and pastries. Don’t forget to stop by the vibrant Marché Saint-Cyprien, which captures the spirit of French living with its colourful, locally-made offerings.

TR.TZX.touristAttractionsText: Wander the imposing citadel walls of Trabzon Castle and take in sweeping vistas of the Black Sea coastline. At the modern Trabzon Aquarium, journey through a 200-metre tunnel beneath the waves, where around 80 species of marine life – including sharks and colourful fish – swim all around you. For a tranquil escape into nature, head into the mountains to discover Uzungöl Lake. Surrounded by forests, it’s a serene spot to take a boat trip, go on a scenic hike or simply soak up the breathtaking alpine landscape.
TR.TZX.leisureActivitiesText: For the best views in Trabzon, take the Boztepe Cable Car to the top of Boztepe Hill and watch the sun dip into the Black Sea from above the rooftops. Dine at one of the hilltop restaurants, or for a thrill, book a paragliding experience for a rapid return to sea level. Step into Trabzon’s rich past at the Trabzon Museum, where interactive exhibits bring to life the stories of famous travellers like Marco Polo. Along the coast, boat trips offer an alternative perspective of the city, while lush inland parks urge you to unwind with a picnic and a moment of tranquillity.
TR.TZX.shoppingText: Step into Bedesten Bazaar, a traditional market dating back to the Ottoman Empire. Here you’ll find high-quality fabrics, hand-tooled leather goods, and glittering jewellery that reflects the area’s proud cultural heritage, with a dedicated section of unique products made by local makers. For a more relaxed shopping experience, Trabzon Meydan Market attracts residents and visitors alike, with everything from souvenirs to spices. Moloz Popular Market stands out as a women-led market specialising in handmade crafts and enticing produce, including honey and cheeses. If you prefer modern comforts, Trabzon has several large, air-conditioned malls offering Turkish and international brands – perfect for an afternoon of relaxed browsing.
TR.TZX.destinationPageIntro: Revel in a different side of Türkiye in Trabzon – where ancient streets meet Black Sea views, magnificent scenery and evocative Ottoman influences in the city.
TR.TZX.overviewText:
Located on Türkiye’s Black Sea coast, Trabzon blends alpine scenery, Ottoman history and exceptional hospitality. Trabzon invites you to wander its charming cobbled streets, explore its ancient walled quarter and step back in time.

Once an essential stop on the Silk Road and the birthplace of Suleiman the Magnificent, Trabzon offers a captivating mix of heritage and culture. Explore Byzantine landmarks, enjoy delicious seafood by the harbour, and taste local dishes featuring the region’s prized hazelnuts. With mountains on one side and the sea on the other, this enigmatic city is a fantastic year-round escape.
TR.TZX.destinationHighlightsH1: Trabzon: Where mountains meet the sea
TR.TZX.eatingImageText:
Food in Trabzon showcases the unique flavours of Türkiye’s Black Sea coast. Because of its location, fresh fish dishes are heavily popular here. Try anchovies known as hamsi – they’re lightly fried and served with lemon and garlic for a simple, tasty snack. 

Another regional favourite is kuymak, an indulgent, cheesy fondue-style dish served with crispy bread. For a classic, hearty meal, order akçaabat köftesi – spiced veal meatballs served with yoghurt and salad. The area is also known for its black cabbage, used in soups and mouthwatering salads. 

Craving something sweet? Try laz böreği – a creamy, custard-filled pastry similar to baklava.

SA.ULH.touristAttractionsText:
Take a tour of Hegra, Saudi Arabia’s first UNESCO World Heritage Site. A combination of natural and man-made rock formations and carvings, it’s also home to ancient Nabataean tombs. A guided tour with a local Rawi or storyteller will add even more colour to this incredible site.

The ancient site of Dadan was home to the Dadanite Royal Family. High above the tombs are ancient carvings of lions and other figures dating back over 3,000 years.

The incredible AlUla Old Town is a sensitively restored site where both ancient and new homes sit side by side. The new constructions have been mindfully created to blend in with the original buildings, immersing you in the culture and lifestyle of the people. Climb the Citadel for a bird-eye view of the city’s 900 mud brick houses and town squares.
SA.ULH.leisureActivitiesText:
Rest in the shade of the enchanting Oasis of AlUla, filled with over two million date palms, a wealth of citrus fruit trees and still key to the food produced in this region.

Elephant Mountain (known as Jabal al Fil), is a must-see, especially at sunrise or sunset when the surfaces of this distinctive site change colour. 

The surrounding desert is free of light pollution, making it one of the best places in the region to see the night sky. If you love astronomy, a stargazing trip to Gharameel is highly recommended for a clear view of the Milky Way.

To see the whole region from a unique perspective, take a helicopter tour that includes views of Jabal al Fil, Hegra, Jabal Ikmah, Dadan and AlUla Old Town. It’s a fabulous way to see so much in one incredible experience.
SA.ULH.shoppingText:
The best place to go shopping in AlUla is Market Street, in the heart of the Old Town. Filled with a wide selection of stalls and shops selling souvenirs including textiles, jewellery and handicrafts, the market feels as if you’ve stepped back in time to when this historic trading centre was filled with caravans.

You’ll find stores selling traditional local dress, which is brightly coloured in rich reds, golds and oranges that reflect the colours of the landscape. Other shops celebrate the Arabic art of calligraphy with exquisite Arabic Scripts embellished with the finest examples of ‘Khatt’ created by skilled artists who have spent years learning the techniques of this craft.

If you love jewellery, AlUla has some exceptional shops selling 24k gold in both modern and traditional designs.
SA.ULH.destinationPageIntro: AlUla is truly special. It is Saudi Arabia’s hidden gem, a monumental celebration of ancient cultures in one of the country’s most breathtakingly beautiful locations.
SA.ULH.overviewText:
On the northern tip of the Hejaz is the ancient oasis of AlUla. With a history stretching back thousands of years, it’s a truly incredible location originally built by those who also constructed the famous Jordanian city of Petra.

Filled with Nabatean historical sites, AlUla is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site and internationally important in the story of life in the Middle East and beyond.

The awe-inspiring desert scenery coupled with a region that is effectively an outdoor museum makes it one of the must-see places not just in Saudi Arabia, but the world. Modern facilities sit alongside ancient monuments, a perfect juxtaposition of old and new.

The cuisine is as unique as the landscape, and the welcome is as warm as the desert sun. AlUla is unique and a once-in-a-lifetime experience.
SA.ULH.eatingImageText:
Thanks to the incredible AlUla oasis, there is an abundance of fresh fruit and vegetables on offer. Traditional dishes are influenced by thousands of years of civilization and use a wide range of spices and flavours.

Must-try food includes mutabbaq, a delicious stuffed pancake filled with vegetables and spices, and is ideal if you prefer vegetarian food. For a hearty meal, al harees is a meat and wheat dish seasoned with spices and with a creamy texture.

Kasba is a classic rice dish flavoured with cardamom, bay, saffron and cinnamon and served with chicken.

With nearly 30 different types of citrus fruit available, you’ll find fresh, zesty salads such as tabbouleh that add an extra dimension to meals. And for on-the-go snacks, plenty of street vendors offer treats such as falafel and hummus.
